Validation Determination Basis & Result Qualification Module (VDBRQM)
Validation Determination Basis & Result Qualification Module (VDBRQM)
Architecture Ecosystem: Structured Reality Standards™
Architecture Family: VALIDOS® — Validation Governance Architecture
Parent Standard: Validation Determination Standard (VDTS)
Operational Layer: Validation Determination Governance Layer
Category: AI & Interpretation
Subcategory: Validation Governance
Type: Parent Standard Module
Governed Space: Validation Determination Basis &
Result Qualification
Version: 1.0
Status: Canonical · Open Module
Effective Date: 11 August 2026
Compatibility: OOF® Methodology OS™ · GOA™ · OBIDENITY® · INTEGROS®
· ORA™ · AGA™ · AIG® · CLIA® · MGIA™ · ASGA™ · RIS™
AI-Readable: Yes
Authority: OOF®
Protection: MIP® — Methodological Intellectual Property
Canonical Language: English (UCL™)
Governed Space
Validation Determination Basis & Result Qualification
Canonical Definition
Validation Determination Basis & Result Qualification Module
(VDBRQM) defines the governance framework for assembling, verifying,
bounding, qualifying, and preserving the complete governed
information basis from which Validation Determination may
legitimately proceed and for determining which Validation Execution
Results are methodologically eligible, conditionally eligible,
restricted, superseded, or ineligible to contribute to
that determination.
It establishes the transition from a completed Validation Execution

Record into an identifiable and governed Validation
Determination Basis.
Operational Role
VDBRQM serves as the first internal governance space of the
Validation Determination Standard.
The preceding Validation Execution Standard establishes:
what was actually executed,
what outputs were generated,
whether execution was complete,
whether execution was conformant,
which deviations occurred,
which limitations remain,
and whether execution is Determination Ready.
VDBRQM asks: Which parts of that governed execution record may
legitimately participate in Validation Determination, under what
conditions, and within which determination boundaries?
The governed progression is:
Validation Execution Record → Determination Readiness Verification →
Determination Basis Assembly → Result Identification → Result
Qualification → Result Restriction → Determination Basis Freeze →
Qualified Validation Determination Basis
VDBRQM does not determine whether a Validation Criterion
is satisfied.
It establishes the legitimate information basis from which criterion
determination may begin.
Module Operational Space
VDBRQM governs:
Validation Determination Basis,
determination-basis identity,
determination-basis assembly,
Determination Readiness verification,
Validation Object continuity,
determination-purpose continuity,
determination-scope continuity,
Validation Depth continuity,
criteria-set continuity,
execution-result identification,
execution-result qualification,
result eligibility,

conditional result eligibility,
result restriction,
result exclusion,
result supersession,
duplicate-result control,
result comparability,
result provenance,
result-to-execution linkage,
evidence-condition propagation,
source-condition propagation,
execution-limitation propagation,
residual-deviation propagation,
uncertainty propagation,
result completeness,
determination-basis completeness,
determination-basis consistency,
determination-basis conflict,
determination-basis versioning,
determination-basis freeze,
and determination-basis traceability.
Module Function
VDBRQM applies after Validation Execution has reached a
Determination Ready or Conditionally Ready condition.
Its function is to prevent:
every generated output automatically entering determination,
invalid execution results being mixed with legitimate results,
superseded results being counted twice,
duplicate measurements distorting interpretation,
results being detached from their object version,
results being interpreted outside their executed scope,
conditionally usable results losing their conditions,
evidence limitations disappearing,
source restrictions disappearing,
execution deviations being forgotten,
incomparable results being aggregated,
partial execution being represented as a complete determination basis,
and later criterion determinations relying upon information whose methodological eligibility was never established.
Validation Determination Basis

The Validation Determination Basis is the governed collection of
information from which formal Validation Determination is permitted
to proceed.
It may include:
Validation Object reference,
object version or state,
Validation Purpose,
actual Validation Scope,
achieved Validation Depth,
applicable Validation Criteria,
applicable thresholds,
acceptance conditions,
rejection conditions,
approved Validation Method,
Evidence Fitness information,
Source Reliability information,
Validation Execution Record,
Execution Completeness status,
Execution Conformity status,
qualified execution results,
residual deviations,
unresolved exceptions,
execution limitations,
evidence limitations,
source limitations,
uncertainty,
and applicable determination restrictions.
Determination Basis Is Not the Entire Execution Record
The complete Validation Execution Record may contain information
that should not participate equally in determination.
For example, it may contain:
failed test attempts,
invalid measurements,
superseded outputs,
diagnostic data,
repeated tests,
outputs generated during control loss,
results produced against the wrong configuration,
exploratory observations,
or records retained only for traceability.
VDBRQM therefore distinguishes:
Validation Execution Record
from: Validation Determination Basis
The first records what occurred.
The second establishes what may legitimately support the conclusion.
Determination Readiness Verification

Before assembling the Determination Basis, VDBRQM verifies the
Determination Readiness status produced by VEXS.
Possible incoming conditions include:
Determination Ready
Determination Conditionally Ready
Determination Readiness Undetermined
Determination Not Ready
or:
Determination Blocked
VDBRQM must preserve this status rather than bypass it.
Determination Ready
Where execution is Determination Ready, the execution record may
proceed into result qualification subject to normal
determination governance.
Determination Conditionally Ready
Where execution is Conditionally Ready, VDBRQM must propagate the
applicable conditions into the Determination Basis.
For example:
reduced scope,
restricted criterion set,
unresolved minor limitation,
conditionally usable execution portion,
or another explicit boundary.
Determination Not Ready
Where execution is Not Ready, VDBRQM should not construct a
substantive determination basis as though execution were complete.
The process may require:
additional execution,
corrective execution,
missing records,
deviation resolution,
or another remediation.
Determination Blocked
Where VEXS establishes a Determination Block, VDBRQM preserves
that block.
VALIDOS® establishes:
A determination layer cannot repair an execution layer that lacks
legitimate determination basis.
Validation Object Continuity
The Determination Basis must remain bound to the exact Validation
Object established and executed against.
VDBRQM therefore verifies continuity across:

Validation Object → Execution Object → Determination Object
A material mismatch may block or restrict determination.
Object Version Continuity
Where version matters, the determination basis must identify
the exact:
version,
configuration,
release,
state,
temporal instance,
dataset edition,
model checkpoint,
or other relevant object representation.
Results from materially different versions should not be
silently merged.
Determination Purpose Continuity
The purpose of determination must remain within the governed
Validation Purpose.
A result generated for one validation purpose should not
automatically be repurposed to support another materially
different determination.
Therefore:
Result Relevance to Purpose Must Be Established
Determination Scope Continuity
VDBRQM establishes the maximum scope within which results may
contribute to determination.
The actual determination scope cannot legitimately exceed the
execution scope supporting it.
Where execution was reduced, the Determination Basis must inherit
that reduction.
Validation Depth Continuity
The achieved Validation Depth is carried into the
Determination Basis.
A result generated under limited validation depth cannot
automatically support a high-assurance determination.
VDBRQM therefore preserves: Achieved Validation Depth → Permissible
Determination Strength
Criteria Set Continuity
The applicable Validation Criteria should remain identifiable before
result qualification begins.
VDBRQM preserves:
criterion identity,

criterion version,
criterion hierarchy,
mandatory status,
critical status,
thresholds,
acceptance conditions,
rejection conditions,
and applicable criterion dependencies.
Validation Execution Result
A Validation Execution Result is an output generated through a
validation activity that may potentially contribute to
Validation Determination.
Results may include:
measurements,
observations,
classifications,
comparisons,
statistical outputs,
simulation outputs,
test outcomes,
detected behaviors,
expert assessments,
AI-generated analytical outputs,
system responses,
or other execution-derived information.
Generation does not establish eligibility.
Result Identity
A material Validation Execution Result should be
sufficiently identifiable.
A Result Record may contain:
Result Identifier,
Execution Instance,
Validation Object,
object state,
method step,
applicable criterion,
generating activity,
evidence used,
source used,
time,
environment,
configuration,
control state,
and applicable deviation relationship.
Result Qualification
Result Qualification determines whether an execution result
possesses sufficient methodological standing to contribute to
Validation Determination.
Qualification asks:
Was the result generated by legitimate execution?
Is it connected to the correct Validation Object?
Was the correct method used?
Is it relevant to the applicable criterion?
Were required controls active?
Are evidence conditions satisfied?
Are source conditions satisfied?

Is the result within scope?
Is the result sufficiently traceable?
Is it superseded?
Is it duplicated?
Is it affected by unresolved deviation?
Can it be meaningfully interpreted?
Result Qualification Status
VDBRQM may classify results as:
Determination Eligible
The result may legitimately contribute to Validation Determination
within its governed scope.
Conditionally Determination Eligible
The result may contribute only under explicit conditions,
limitations, restrictions, corroboration requirements, or
interpretive boundaries.
Determination Restricted
The result is legitimate only for a narrower purpose, criterion,
scope, population, environment, or analytical role.
Determination Ineligible
The result should not contribute substantively to the
Validation Determination.
Eligibility Undetermined
Available information is insufficient to establish the result's
methodological eligibility.
Eligibility Is Not Favorability
Result Qualification must remain independent of whether the result
supports the desired outcome.
A favorable result should not receive easier qualification.
An unfavorable result should not receive stricter qualification.
VALIDOS® establishes:
Result Eligibility Must Be Determined by Methodological Fitness, Not
Outcome Preference
Conditional Result Eligibility
A result may be conditionally eligible where:
corroboration is required,
a source has limited reliability,
execution was conditionally conformant,
environmental conditions restrict interpretation,

a measurement has known uncertainty,
scope is limited,
or another governed condition applies.
The condition must remain attached to the result
throughout determination.
Result Restriction
A valid result may have a narrower legitimate role than
originally intended.
For example, a result may be usable:
descriptively but not conclusively,
for one criterion but not another,
for one population only,
for one environment,
as supporting evidence only,
or within a defined time period.
VDBRQM makes such restrictions explicit.
Result Exclusion
A result may require exclusion where it is:
generated by invalid execution,
connected to the wrong object,
methodologically corrupted,
produced during critical control loss,
insufficiently traceable,
outside scope,
based upon unusable evidence,
dependent upon a disqualified source,
or otherwise incapable of legitimately supporting determination.
Exclusion must remain recorded.
Excluded Results Must Not Disappear
An excluded result should not simply be deleted from
validation history.
VALIDOS® preserves:
Result Generated → Qualification Assessment → Result Excluded
→ Reason
This prevents selective removal of inconvenient findings.
Result Supersession
A result may be replaced by a later legitimate result.
Examples include:
corrected measurement,
repeated test,
corrected calculation,
re-executed activity,
or newer governed output.
VDBRQM may classify the earlier result as:
Superseded
rather than deleting it.
Superseded Does Not Mean Erased

Historical traceability should preserve:
Original Result → Reason for Re-Execution or Correction → New Result
→ Supersession Relationship
Duplicate Result Control
Validation processes may unintentionally count the same underlying
observation multiple times.
For example:
one event appears in multiple logs,
one dataset is represented by several derived metrics,
the same source is repeated through multiple channels,
or one measurement is copied into several reports.
VDBRQM prevents duplicated information from artificially increasing
determination strength.
Result Independence
Where multiple results are treated as independent support, their
actual independence should be considered.
Ten outputs derived from the same underlying source are not
necessarily equivalent to ten independent observations.
This is particularly important for corroboration and confidence.
Result Comparability
Results may be methodologically valid individually but not
directly comparable.
Differences may include:
method,
units,
population,
environment,
configuration,
object state,
time,
sampling,
or measurement basis.
VDBRQM determines whether comparison or aggregation is legitimate.
Comparable Results
Results may be considered sufficiently comparable where material
differences do not undermine the intended analytical relationship.
Conditionally Comparable Results
Results may be compared only after:
normalization,
scope restriction,
adjustment,
explicit caveat,
or another governed treatment.

Non-Comparable Results
Results that cannot legitimately support direct comparison should
remain separate.
VALIDOS® establishes:
Available Together ≠ Methodologically Comparable
Result Provenance
Every material result should remain traceable to its origin within
validation execution.
Result provenance may include:
Execution Instance → Activity → Method Step → Evidence → Source →
Object State → Result
This allows later determination to understand how the result came
into existence.
Evidence Condition Propagation
Evidence conditions established earlier in VALIDOS® must remain
connected to results derived from that evidence.
If evidence was:
Conditionally Fit
then a dependent result may inherit relevant limitations.
VDBRQM prevents evidence restrictions from disappearing during
determination preparation.
Source Condition Propagation
Source Reliability conditions also propagate where
materially relevant.
For example:
If a source required corroboration, a result depending upon that
source may remain conditionally eligible until corroboration
is established.
Execution Limitation Propagation
Execution limitations identified by VEXS must remain visible in the
Determination Basis.
These may include:
reduced scope,
incomplete activity,
partial conformity,
environmental limitation,
configuration limitation,
traceability limitation,
or another execution condition.
Residual Deviation Propagation
A deviation may have been closed operationally while leaving
residual methodological effects.

VDBRQM attaches those residual effects to affected results.
This prevents deviation closure from being mistaken for restoration
of unrestricted result eligibility.
Uncertainty Propagation
Known uncertainty associated with:
measurement,
method,
evidence,
source,
execution,
sampling,
or object behavior
should remain connected to affected results.
Uncertainty should not first appear only at the final
determination stage.
Result Conflict Awareness
VDBRQM may identify preliminary conflicts between qualified results.
At this stage, it does not resolve the conflict.
It records that:
Result A and Result B may support materially
different interpretations.
Formal conflict governance occurs later within VDTS.
Result Completeness
Result Completeness asks whether the execution record contains the
expected material results necessary for criterion determination.
A result set may be:
Complete Conditionally Complete
Partially Complete
Incomplete
or:
Completeness Undetermined
This is distinct from Execution Completeness.
Execution may have occurred while one expected result was not
successfully generated.
Missing Result
A Missing Result exists where an expected material output
is unavailable.
A missing result may arise from:
execution failure,
recording failure,
corrupted output,
unavailable measurement,
system failure,
or another cause.
VALIDOS® establishes:
Missing Result ≠ Negative Result
Determination Basis Completeness
The complete Determination Basis should contain sufficient

legitimate information to support criterion-level determination.
Possible conditions include:
Basis Complete
Basis Conditionally Complete
Basis Partially Complete
Basis Incomplete
or:
Basis Completeness Undetermined
Determination Basis Consistency
A complete Determination Basis may still contain
incompatible information.
VDBRQM therefore assesses consistency across:
object identity,
versions,
scope,
criteria,
methods,
results,
evidence,
sources,
execution conditions,
and limitations.
Determination Basis Conflict
A Determination Basis Conflict exists where two or more components
of the basis impose materially incompatible interpretations or
conditions before criterion determination begins.
Examples include:
two valid results generated against materially different object states,
incompatible method outputs,
contradictory evidence conditions,
incompatible source restrictions,
or conflicting execution scopes.
Such conflicts must remain explicit.
Basis Freeze
Before criterion-level determination begins, the material
Determination Basis should be version-fixed.
A Determination Basis Freeze establishes which:
results,
criteria,
evidence,
sources,
execution records,
limitations,
deviations,
and uncertainty conditions
were available to the determination process.
Why Determination Basis Freeze Matters
Without a Basis Freeze, information may be added, removed, or
replaced while determination is being performed without preserving
which information actually supported the conclusion.

VALIDOS® therefore establishes:
A Validation Determination must be traceable to the information
basis from which it was actually derived.
Determination Basis Versioning
Material changes should create distinguishable basis versions.
For example:
Determination Basis 1.0
Determination Basis 1.1
Determination Basis 2.0
The implementation may choose its own versioning mechanism.
The governance requirement is preservation of material change.
Basis Change
After freeze, material changes may include:
newly discovered result,
excluded result,
corrected result,
evidence reassessment,
source reassessment,
execution reassessment,
newly discovered deviation,
uncertainty revision,
or scope correction.
Such changes may require determination restart or reassessment.
Qualification Reassessment
A result's qualification may change when new information emerges.
Possible transitions include:
Eligible → Conditionally Eligible
Eligible → Ineligible
Conditionally Eligible → Eligible
Undetermined → Eligible
or another governed transition.
Earlier qualification should remain historically visible.
Determination Basis Integrity Awareness
VDBRQM depends upon the integrity of the records it consumes.
It does not replace INTEGROS® or specialized
evidence-integrity governance.
Where record integrity is materially uncertain, that condition
becomes part of the Determination Basis.
Minimum Implementation Framework
1. Verify Determination Readiness
Confirm whether execution is permitted to enter determination.

2. Establish Validation Object Continuity
Bind determination to the correct Validation Object, version,
configuration, and state.
3. Establish Determination Boundaries
Preserve:
Validation Purpose,
actual Validation Scope,
achieved Validation Depth,
and applicable Criteria Set.
4. Assemble Execution Results
Identify all material outputs potentially relevant to determination.
5. Qualify Results
Classify each material result according to its
methodological eligibility.
6. Propagate Conditions
Attach relevant:
Evidence Fitness conditions,
Source Reliability conditions,
execution limitations,
residual deviations,
and uncertainty.
7. Control Duplicates, Supersession, and Comparability
Prevent artificial inflation or invalid aggregation of results.
8. Assess Result-Set Completeness
Determine whether required material results are available.
9. Assess Determination Basis Completeness & Consistency
Identify missing information, contradictions, or Basis Conflicts.
10. Freeze and Version the Determination Basis
Preserve the exact governed information basis entering
criterion determination.
11. Preserve Lifecycle Traceability
Maintain:
Determination Basis Identifier,
Validation Object reference,
object version,
Purpose,
Scope,
Depth,
Criteria Set,
Execution Instance,
results,
Result Qualification Status,
restrictions,
exclusions,
supersession relationships,
comparability status,
Evidence Fitness conditions,
Source Reliability conditions,
execution limitations,
deviations,
uncertainty,

completeness,
conflicts,
Basis version,
Basis Freeze,
changes,
reassessments,
and sufficient lifecycle continuity.
Governance Outputs
VDBRQM may produce:
Validation Determination Basis,
Validation Determination Basis Identifier,
Determination Readiness Verification Record,
Determination Boundary Record,
Validation Execution Result Register,
Validation Result Qualification Record,
Result Eligibility Status,
Conditional Result Eligibility Record,
Result Restriction Record,
Result Exclusion Record,
Result Supersession Record,
Duplicate Result Record,
Result Independence Assessment,
Result Comparability Assessment,
Result Provenance Record,
Evidence Condition Propagation Record,
Source Condition Propagation Record,
Execution Limitation Propagation Record,
Residual Deviation Propagation Record,
Result Uncertainty Record,
Result Conflict Signal,
Result Completeness Assessment,
Missing Result Record,
Determination Basis Completeness Assessment,
Determination Basis Consistency Assessment,
Determination Basis Conflict Record,
Determination Basis Version,
Determination Basis Freeze Record,
Determination Basis Change Record,
and Result Qualification Reassessment Record.
Use Case 1 — AI Model Validation
Scenario
An AI model produces 1,000 validation outputs.
Thirty were generated during a period when a required execution
control was unavailable, and fifty were later repeated under
restored conditions.
Application
VDBRQM does not treat all 1,050 recorded outputs as equivalent

determination evidence.
It identifies:
affected original outputs,
corrected repetitions,
supersession relationships,
control-loss conditions,
duplicate relationships,
and result eligibility.
Result
Only the methodologically qualified result set enters
criterion determination.
The larger raw output count cannot artificially increase
validation confidence.
Use Case 2 — Industrial Validation
Scenario
Two measurement systems produce results for the same
Validation Criterion.
Both systems are individually valid, but they use different
measurement scales and environmental conditions.
Application
VDBRQM assesses result comparability before the outputs
are aggregated.
Result
The results may be classified as:
Conditionally Comparable
and require normalization or separate interpretation rather than
being directly averaged.
Use Case 3 — Autonomous Validation System
Scenario
An autonomous validation agent generates thousands of test outputs,
including failed attempts, retries, diagnostic outputs, and final
successful executions.
Application
VDBRQM distinguishes:
diagnostic outputs,
failed attempts,
superseded results,
final eligible results,
duplicate information,
and results affected by execution deviations.
Result
Automated scale does not become methodological weight by itself.
The Validation Determination Basis contains only results
legitimately capable of supporting determination.
Architectural Position
Validation Determination Basis & Result Qualification is the first

internal governance space of the Validation Determination
Standard (VDTS).
The transition is:
Validation Execution → Validation Determination Basis
VDBRQM establishes:
Which governed validation results may legitimately
enter determination?
The next VDTS governance stage can then ask:
What does each qualified result set demonstrate relative to each
applicable Validation Criterion?
The VDTS internal progression therefore begins:
Determination Basis & Result Qualification → Criterion Determination
→ Conflict & Uncertainty Governance → Cross-Criterion Integration →
Overall Validation Determination
Foundational Principle
A validation conclusion can be no more legitimate than the results
permitted to participate in its determination.
Canonical Closing Statement
Validation Determination Basis & Result Qualification Module
establishes the governed entry layer of Validation Determination
within VALIDOS® by transforming the complete Validation Execution
Record into an identifiable, bounded, qualified, versioned, and
traceable Validation Determination Basis. Through readiness
verification, object and scope continuity, result qualification,
eligibility, restriction, exclusion, supersession, duplicate
control, comparability, provenance, condition propagation,
uncertainty preservation, completeness assessment, consistency
assessment, conflict identification, basis freezing, and
reassessment, VDBRQM ensures that criterion-level and overall

Validation Determinations can be derived only from results
possessing legitimate methodological standing rather than from the
undifferentiated outputs of validation execution.

Validation Determination Conflict & Uncertainty Governance Module (VDCUGM)
Validation Determination Conflict & Uncertainty Governance Module (VDCUGM)
Architecture Ecosystem: Structured Reality Standards™
Architecture Family: VALIDOS® — Validation Governance Architecture
Parent Standard: Validation Determination Standard (VDTS)
Operational Layer: Validation Determination Governance Layer
Category: AI & Interpretation
Subcategory: Validation Governance
Type: Parent Standard Module
Governed Space: Validation Determination Conflict &
Uncertainty Governance
Version: 1.0
Status: Canonical · Open Module
Effective Date: 11 August 2026
Compatibility: OOF® Methodology OS™ · GOA™ · OBIDENITY® · INTEGROS®
· ORA™ · AGA™ · AIG® · CLIA® · MGIA™ · ASGA™ · RIS™
AI-Readable: Yes
Authority: OOF®
Protection: MIP® — Methodological Intellectual Property
Canonical Language: English (UCL™)
Governed Space
Validation Determination Conflict & Uncertainty Governance
Canonical Definition
Validation Determination Conflict & Uncertainty Governance Module
(VDCUGM) defines the governance framework for identifying,
classifying, preserving, analyzing, contextualizing, escalating,
constraining, and where methodologically possible resolving material
conflicts, contradictory findings, incompatible criterion signals,
uncertainty, ambiguity, incomplete knowledge, and determination
instability arising within the governed Validation
Determination Basis.
It establishes the conditions under which disagreement and

uncertainty become explicit determination-governance inputs rather
than hidden, averaged, discarded, or prematurely converted
into certainty.
Operational Role
VDCUGM serves as the third internal governance space of the
Validation Determination Standard.
The preceding modules establish:
VDBRQM — Which results may legitimately participate
in determination?
VCDM — What does the qualified result set demonstrate about each
individual Validation Criterion?
VDCUGM asks:
Where do legitimate findings conflict, where does uncertainty
materially affect interpretation, and what must happen before
criterion outcomes can be integrated into an overall
Validation Determination?
The governed progression is:
Criterion Determinations & Conflict Signals → Conflict
Identification → Conflict Classification → Uncertainty
Identification → Materiality Assessment → Cause & Scope Analysis →
Resolution or Preservation → Determination Constraint → Conflict &
Uncertainty Record
VDCUGM does not perform final cross-criterion aggregation.
It governs the interpretive instability that must be understood
before aggregation can legitimately occur.
Module Operational Space
VDCUGM governs:
determination conflict,
criterion conflict,
result conflict,
evidence conflict,
source-related determination conflict,
method-related determination conflict,
execution-related determination conflict,
scope conflict,
threshold conflict,
temporal conflict,
contextual conflict,
contradiction,
inconsistency,
unresolved disagreement,

determination uncertainty,
measurement uncertainty,
methodological uncertainty,
evidentiary uncertainty,
source uncertainty,
execution uncertainty,
sampling uncertainty,
contextual uncertainty,
model uncertainty,
object-state uncertainty,
uncertainty materiality,
uncertainty propagation,
conflict materiality,
conflict causation,
conflict localization,
conflict escalation,
conflict resolution,
unresolved conflict preservation,
conditional determination constraints,
indeterminacy triggers,
and conflict-and-uncertainty traceability.
Module Function
VDCUGM applies after criterion-level determinations and material
conflict signals have been established.
Its function is to prevent:
contradictory findings being silently averaged,
unfavorable evidence being discarded as noise,
uncertainty being hidden behind point estimates,
disagreements between methods being resolved by preference,
disagreements between sources being resolved by reputation alone,
scope differences being mistaken for factual contradiction,
temporal changes being treated as inconsistent evidence,
missing information being converted into certainty,
one dominant criterion result suppressing legitimate contrary evidence,
and overall determination being constructed before material conflict and uncertainty are governably understood.
Conflict Is Not Automatically Error
VALIDOS® establishes:
Conflict ≠ Methodological Failure
Two legitimate results may disagree because they describe:
different operating conditions,

different populations,
different times,
different system states,
different methodological sensitivities,
or genuinely unstable object behavior.
Conflict may therefore contain important validation information.
The first governance task is not to eliminate conflict.
It is to understand what the conflict represents.
Validation Determination Conflict
A Validation Determination Conflict exists where two or more
legitimate findings, criterion outcomes, or interpretive pathways
support materially incompatible conclusions within an overlapping
determination space.
The overlap requirement matters.
Two different conclusions are not necessarily conflicting if they
apply to different valid scopes.
Result Conflict
A Result Conflict exists where qualified Validation Results
materially disagree about the same validation-relevant condition.
Examples include:
repeated measurements producing incompatible values,
two tests producing different classifications,
simulation and operational testing diverging,
or different time periods showing materially different behavior.
Criterion Conflict
A Criterion Conflict exists where one criterion-level determination
contains legitimate internal inconsistency or where materially
related criteria support incompatible implications.
For example:
Criterion A: Satisfied
while:
Criterion B: Not Satisfied
may or may not constitute a conflict.
It becomes a determination conflict only if the approved criteria

structure expects those outcomes to be mutually compatible or
causally related.
Evidence Conflict
Evidence Conflict occurs where legitimate evidence supports
materially different interpretations.
This may arise from:
different datasets,
different populations,
different observations,
different time periods,
or different environments.
Evidence Conflict is not automatically Source Conflict.
Source-Related Determination Conflict
Two sufficiently reliable sources may disagree.
VDCUGM preserves the disagreement and examines whether it
arises from:
different source roles,
different observations,
different access,
different time periods,
different methodologies,
or genuine factual incompatibility.
A more authoritative source should not automatically win merely
because of status.
Method-Related Determination Conflict
Different suitable Validation Methods may produce materially
different findings.
This may reveal:
different sensitivity,
different assumptions,
different scope,
hidden methodological limitations,
or object behavior that varies by measurement method.
Method conflict may require methodological comparison rather than
numerical averaging.
Execution-Related Conflict
Execution differences may explain apparent determination conflict.
For example:
Two valid test results may differ because:
one occurred under nominal operation,
one under degraded operation,
one used a different configuration,
or one followed a different sequence.
VDCUGM distinguishes factual disagreement from

execution-context difference.
Scope Conflict
A Scope Conflict exists where two determinations appear
contradictory but actually apply to materially different scopes.
For example:
Satisfied for Population A
and:
Not Satisfied for Population B
are not necessarily contradictory.
The conflict may disappear once scope is correctly represented.
Temporal Conflict
A Validation Object may change over time.
A criterion may be satisfied at Time 1 and not satisfied at Time 2.
This is not necessarily inconsistent validation.
It may represent:
State Change
Drift
Degradation
Improvement
or:
Context Change VDCUGM preserves time as part of
conflict interpretation.
Contextual Conflict
A system may behave differently across:
jurisdictions,
languages,
environments,
user groups,
hardware,
software configurations,
or operating modes.
Contextual differences must not be compressed into one universal
conclusion if the underlying behavior is genuinely conditional.
Threshold Conflict
Different thresholds may produce apparently conflicting conclusions.
VDCUGM identifies whether:
different criterion versions were used,
different jurisdictions apply different thresholds,
different Validation Depths use different acceptance levels,
or an unauthorized threshold change occurred.
Threshold differences must remain explicit.
Conflict Classification
A material conflict may be classified as:
Apparent Conflict
The disagreement disappears when scope, time, context, or definition
is clarified.
Resolvable Conflict

The conflict can be methodologically resolved using existing
governed information.
Conditionally Resolvable Conflict
The conflict can be resolved only under explicit assumptions,
boundaries, or additional controls.
Unresolved Conflict
Legitimate incompatible findings remain after reasonable
governance analysis.
Critical Conflict
The unresolved conflict materially prevents a reliable criterion or
overall determination.
These classifications support downstream determination governance.
Conflict Materiality
Not every disagreement matters equally.
Conflict materiality may depend upon:
affected criterion,
mandatory or critical status,
Validation Purpose,
Validation Depth,
scope,
consequence of error,
persistence,
strength of competing findings,
and whether the conflict can change the overall determination.
Conflict Localization
VDCUGM seeks to determine where the conflict actually exists.
Possible localization levels include:
one result,
one criterion,
one subgroup,
one environment,
one time period,
one subsystem,
one object state,
or the complete Validation Object.
Localization prevents narrow conflicts from unnecessarily
contaminating the entire determination.
Conflict Cause Analysis
Possible causes may include:
measurement variation,
evidence limitations,
source differences,
method differences,
execution differences,
sampling effects,
data drift,
object instability,
context dependence,
threshold mismatch,
hidden dependency,
or genuine unresolved reality.

Cause analysis informs whether conflict can be resolved, bounded, or
must remain explicit.
Conflict Resolution
Where methodologically justified, conflict may be resolved through:
scope clarification,
corrected threshold application,
removal of ineligible result,
corrected result qualification,
method comparison,
additional analysis,
additional validation,
source clarification,
evidence clarification,
temporal separation,
contextual separation,
or another governed mechanism.
Resolution Must Not Mean Preference
VALIDOS® establishes:
Conflict Resolution ≠ Choosing the Preferred Result
Resolution must be based upon governed methodological reasons.
A favorable conclusion does not gain priority merely because it
supports deployment, approval, reputation, or business objectives.
Unresolved Conflict
An unresolved conflict is a legitimate determination condition.
Possible downstream effects include:
Criterion Not Determinable,
Conditional Determination,
Partial Determination,
reduced determination scope,
additional validation requirement,
or Indeterminate Validation Determination.
Conflict Preservation
Where conflict cannot be legitimately resolved, both sides of the
conflict should remain traceable.
The record should preserve:
conflicting findings,
their basis,
relevant scope,
evidence,
sources,
methods,
uncertainty,
and reason resolution was not possible.
Uncertainty Governance
Validation uncertainty represents the degree to which available

governed information leaves material doubt concerning interpretation
or determination.
Uncertainty is not one single phenomenon.
VDCUGM separates uncertainty by source and function.
Measurement Uncertainty
Measurement uncertainty concerns uncertainty inherent in observed or
measured values.
This may include:
instrument tolerance,
noise,
repeatability,
precision,
resolution,
or another measurement limitation.
Methodological Uncertainty
Methodological uncertainty concerns uncertainty arising from:
method assumptions,
model choice,
analytical design,
simulation limitations,
sampling method,
or methodological approximation.
Evidentiary Uncertainty
Evidentiary uncertainty concerns:
incomplete evidence,
limited representativeness,
sparse observations,
missing scenarios,
temporal limitations,
or Evidence Fitness restrictions.
Source Uncertainty
Source uncertainty concerns unresolved conditions involving:
identity,
provenance,
capability,
competence,
independence,
conflicts,
or reliability.
Execution Uncertainty
Execution uncertainty concerns uncertainty about:
what happened,
whether a procedure was followed,
whether a control remained active,
whether object state changed,
or whether critical execution details can be reconstructed.
Sampling Uncertainty
Sampling may produce uncertainty concerning whether observed results
represent the wider population, environment, or state space.
Contextual Uncertainty
Contextual uncertainty arises where applicability across:
environments,

populations,
jurisdictions,
languages,
system states,
or operating conditions
cannot be fully established.
Object-State Uncertainty
The Validation Object itself may exhibit:
stochastic behavior,
adaptive behavior,
dynamic behavior,
drift,
emergent behavior,
or poorly understood state transitions.
This may create uncertainty that is not reducible to
measurement error.
Uncertainty Is Not Ignorance
Some uncertainty can be characterized quantitatively
or qualitatively.
Other uncertainty reflects lack of knowledge.
VDCUGM permits distinctions such as:
Known Quantified Uncertainty
Known Qualitative Uncertainty
Known Unknown
and:
Uncharacterized Uncertainty
where useful.
Uncertainty Materiality
Uncertainty becomes material where it can reasonably affect:
criterion status,
determination scope,
determination conditions,
overall Validation Determination,
or later reliance.
Not every uncertainty requires the same governance response.
Uncertainty Tolerance
The acceptable degree of uncertainty may depend upon:
Validation Purpose,
Validation Depth,
criterion criticality,
risk,
reversibility,
consequence of error,
and intended reliance.
A research context may tolerate uncertainty unacceptable in
high-consequence autonomous deployment.
Uncertainty-Compatible Determination
A determination may remain legitimate where uncertainty is
sufficiently bounded and compatible with the applicable
governance requirements.
Perfect certainty is not required.
Uncertainty-Driven Conditionality

Where uncertainty restricts applicability but does not prevent a
conclusion, downstream determination may become conditional.
For example:
Positive only within tested operating conditions.
Uncertainty-Driven Indeterminacy
Where uncertainty prevents legitimate distinction between
satisfaction and non-satisfaction, the correct outcome
is indeterminacy.
VALIDOS® establishes:
When uncertainty materially prevents knowing, the architecture
should preserve not knowing.
Uncertainty Propagation
Uncertainty should remain attached to the findings that depend
upon it.
The conceptual chain may be:
Evidence Uncertainty → Result Uncertainty → Criterion Uncertainty →
Overall Determination Constraint
This prevents uncertainty from disappearing during aggregation.
Uncertainty Amplification
Several individually modest uncertainties may combine into a larger
determination problem.
For example:
moderate evidence uncertainty,
moderate source uncertainty,
and moderate execution uncertainty
may collectively create substantial criterion uncertainty.
VDCUGM therefore considers cumulative uncertainty.
Uncertainty Reduction
Uncertainty may be reduced through:
additional evidence,
additional validation,
better measurement,
independent corroboration,
narrower scope,
improved source qualification,
repeated testing,
or clearer methodological boundaries.
Uncertainty reduction should remain traceable.
Residual Uncertainty
Uncertainty remaining after reasonable reduction efforts becomes
Residual Uncertainty.

Residual Uncertainty must propagate into later determination
governance where material.
Conflict and Uncertainty Interaction
Conflict and uncertainty often interact.
A conflict may increase uncertainty.
Uncertainty may make apparent conflict impossible to resolve.
VDCUGM therefore governs them together while preserving their
conceptual distinction.
Conflict Without High Uncertainty
Two strong findings may genuinely conflict.
In such cases, the conflict may be clear even though each finding is
individually well-supported.
High Uncertainty Without Conflict
A single criterion may have no contradictory result but still remain
highly uncertain because the evidence basis is weak.
Therefore:
Conflict ≠ Uncertainty
and: Uncertainty ≠ Conflict
Determination Constraint
VDCUGM may create a formal Determination Constraint.
A Determination Constraint defines how identified conflict or
uncertainty must affect later cross-criterion integration.
Possible constraints include:
reduced scope,
conditional interpretation,
no aggregation across specified results,
additional validation required,
criterion remains Not Determinable,
partial determination only,
or overall indeterminacy required.
Critical Determination Constraint
A critical conflict or uncertainty may prevent legitimate
overall determination.
Such a condition may create:
Overall Determination Blocked by Conflict
or:
Overall Determination Blocked by Uncertainty
where appropriate.
Conflict Escalation

Material conflicts may require escalation where resolution exceeds
the authority or capability of the current determination process.
Escalation may involve:
methodology review,
independent review,
specialized expert review,
governance authority,
additional validation,
or another defined pathway.
Uncertainty Escalation
High-consequence uncertainty may likewise require:
deeper Validation Depth,
additional evidence,
broader testing,
more reliable sources,
or independent confirmation.
Conflict Status
VDCUGM may establish:
Conflict Resolved
Conflict Conditionally Resolved
Conflict Bounded
Conflict Unresolved
Critical Conflict
or:
Conflict Status Undetermined
Uncertainty Status
Uncertainty may be characterized as:
Uncertainty Acceptable
Uncertainty Conditionally Acceptable
Uncertainty Material
Uncertainty Determination-Limiting
Uncertainty Determination-Blocking
or:
Uncertainty Undetermined
These statuses inform later integration rather than becoming
Validation States.
Conflict & Uncertainty Record
A formal record may preserve:
Conflict or Uncertainty Identifier,
affected Validation Object,
affected criteria,
affected results,
scope,
time,
context,
evidence,
sources,
methods,
execution references,
materiality,
cause,
uncertainty type,
competing interpretations,
analysis,
resolution attempt,
resolution status,
residual uncertainty,
Determination Constraints,
escalation,
and sufficient traceability.
Human Conflict Resolution
Human expert judgment may assist conflict resolution where

interpretation is complex.
Where used, it should remain:
attributable,
bounded,
competence-aware,
conflict-of-interest aware,
evidence-based,
and traceable.
Automated Conflict Detection
Automated systems may identify:
inconsistent results,
threshold disagreement,
cross-method divergence,
duplicate contradictions,
or statistical anomalies.
Detection can be automated even where resolution requires human or
governed methodological review.
AI-Assisted Conflict & Uncertainty Analysis
AI may assist with:
clustering conflicting findings,
tracing sources,
identifying contextual differences,
mapping uncertainty,
detecting hidden assumptions,
and proposing resolution pathways.
AI assistance should not silently resolve a material conflict by
preference or opaque reasoning.
Conflict Reassessment
Conflict status may change when:
new results appear,
evidence is corrected,
scope is clarified,
source reliability changes,
a method error is identified,
or additional validation is performed.
Uncertainty Reassessment
Uncertainty may change because of:
new evidence,
additional observation,
improved measurement,
model change,
environmental change,
or improved methodological understanding.
Historical uncertainty assessments should remain visible.
Minimum Implementation Framework
1. Identify Material Conflicts
Detect incompatible findings, criterion signals, or interpretations
within overlapping determination scope.
2. Classify Conflict Type
Determine whether conflict is:
result-based,

criterion-based,
evidence-based,
source-related,
method-related,
execution-related,
scope-related,
temporal,
contextual,
or threshold-related.
3. Identify Uncertainty
Map relevant uncertainty sources affecting criterion or
overall interpretation.
4. Assess Materiality
Determine whether conflict or uncertainty is:
immaterial,
tolerable,
material,
determination-limiting,
or determination-blocking.
5. Analyze Cause and Scope
Determine whether the issue reflects:
actual contradiction,
scope difference,
time difference,
context difference,
methodological limitation,
source difference,
execution difference,
or genuine object instability.
6. Attempt Governed Resolution Where Legitimate
Use methodologically defensible resolution pathways.
7. Preserve Unresolved Conflict and Residual Uncertainty
Do not force closure where the governed basis does not support it.
8. Establish Determination Constraints
Define how conflict and uncertainty must affect later
cross-criterion integration.
9. Establish Escalation Where Required
Trigger additional review or validation where materiality
demands it.
10. Preserve Lifecycle Traceability
Maintain:
conflict records,
uncertainty records,
affected criteria,
affected results,
evidence,
sources,
methods,
execution references,
scope,
context,
time,
materiality,
cause,
analysis,
resolution status,
residual uncertainty,
Determination Constraints,
reassessment triggers,
changes,
and sufficient lifecycle continuity.
Governance Outputs
VDCUGM may produce:

Validation Determination Conflict Register,
Result Conflict Record,
Criterion Conflict Record,
Evidence Conflict Record,
Source-Related Conflict Record,
Method-Related Conflict Record,
Execution-Related Conflict Record,
Scope Conflict Record,
Temporal Conflict Record,
Contextual Conflict Record,
Threshold Conflict Record,
Conflict Classification,
Conflict Materiality Assessment,
Conflict Cause Assessment,
Conflict Localization Record,
Conflict Resolution Record,
Unresolved Conflict Record,
Validation Uncertainty Register,
Measurement Uncertainty Record,
Methodological Uncertainty Record,
Evidentiary Uncertainty Record,
Source Uncertainty Record,
Execution Uncertainty Record,
Sampling Uncertainty Record,
Contextual Uncertainty Record,
Object-State Uncertainty Record,
Residual Uncertainty Record,
Cumulative Uncertainty Assessment,
Determination Constraint,
Critical Determination Constraint,
Conflict Escalation Record,
Uncertainty Escalation Record,
Conflict Status,
Uncertainty Status,
and Conflict & Uncertainty Reassessment Record.
Use Case 1 — AI Model Validation
Scenario
An AI model satisfies a safety criterion in simulation but produces
materially different behavior during controlled real-world testing.
Both validation methods were suitable and both executions
were conformant.
Application
VDCUGM does not select the more favorable result.
It examines:
method differences,
environmental differences,
scope,
execution conditions,
object state,
and remaining uncertainty.
Result

The conflict may be localized to simulation-to-reality transfer and
produce a Determination Constraint preventing unrestricted criterion
satisfaction until the divergence is resolved or bounded.
Use Case 2 — Healthcare AI
Scenario
A diagnostic AI system meets the required performance threshold
across the overall validation population but shows materially lower
performance in a small subgroup with limited sample size.
Application
VDCUGM distinguishes:
subgroup conflict,
sampling uncertainty,
population scope,
and evidence limitations.
Result
Rather than averaging the subgroup away, the module may preserve
conditionality or require the subgroup criterion to remain Not
Determinable pending additional validation.
Use Case 3 — Autonomous System
Scenario
Repeated validation of an autonomous system produces stable results
under normal conditions but inconsistent outcomes under a rare
degraded-state scenario.
Application
VDCUGM determines whether the inconsistency reflects:
stochastic system behavior,
insufficient sample size,
environment variation,
execution differences,
or genuine unstable behavior.
Result
Where the conflict cannot be resolved, the residual uncertainty
remains attached to the affected criterion and may constrain later
overall determination.
Architectural Position
Validation Determination Conflict & Uncertainty Governance is the
third internal governance space of the Validation Determination
Standard (VDTS).
The progression now becomes:

Determination Basis & Result Qualification → Criterion Determination
→ Conflict & Uncertainty Governance
VDBRQM establishes:
Which results may participate?
VCDM establishes:
What does each qualified result set demonstrate about
each criterion?
VDCUGM establishes:
Where do those findings conflict, where does uncertainty remain, and
what interpretive constraints must survive?
The next VDTS governance stage can then ask:
How should the now-governed criterion outcomes be combined across
mandatory, critical, dependent, conditional, and
hierarchical criteria?
The VDTS progression therefore continues:
Determination Basis & Result Qualification → Criterion Determination
→ Conflict & Uncertainty Governance → Cross-Criterion Integration →
Overall Validation Determination
Foundational Principle
Conflict and uncertainty should not be eliminated for the sake of a
cleaner conclusion; they should remain visible until the validation
record legitimately supports resolution, limitation,
or indeterminacy.
Canonical Closing Statement
Validation Determination Conflict & Uncertainty Governance Module
establishes the interpretive stability layer of VALIDOS® by
governing contradictory findings, criterion conflict, evidence and
source disagreement, method and execution divergence, scope and
temporal differences, uncertainty, materiality, causation,
localization, resolution, residual uncertainty, escalation, and
Determination Constraints. VDCUGM ensures that cross-criterion

integration cannot convert unresolved disagreement, methodological
ambiguity, or incomplete knowledge into artificial certainty and
that every later Validation Determination remains bounded by the
conflicts and uncertainties the governed validation record is
actually capable of resolving.
