Canonical Definition
Value Nullification Condition Module (VNCM) is the first Core Module of the Value Nullification Standard (VNS) within VFM® — Value Flow Mechanisms Architecture.
VNCM governs the identification, definition, qualification, contextualization, and recording of conditions capable of causing or enabling previously existing positive value to enter a legitimate Value Nullification pathway.

The Module establishes whether a condition relevant to potential nullification exists and whether that condition is materially connected to the governed value within its defined Value Context.
VNCM does not determine that value has reached zero.
It establishes the conditions under which such a determination may become possible.
Its foundational function is:
to identify whether a legitimate nullification condition exists before any zero-value threshold, DeMonet™ mechanism, nullification determination, or ZVA™ transition is considered.
Architectural Position
VNCM is the first module within VNS.
It receives governed value information from the preceding VFM® lifecycle, particularly:
VSS — Value State Standard
VCS — Value Change Standard
and, where progressive decline has occurred:
VDGS — Value Degradation Standard.
It precedes:
VNTM — Value Nullification Threshold Module.
Its architectural role is therefore to establish:
what condition may place existing positive value on a legitimate nullification pathway
before VNTM determines:
whether the applicable zero-value threshold has actually been reached.
VFM® Governance Flow Position
Value Context → Value Origin → Value Emergence → Value Recognition → Value State → Value Change → Value Development → Value Degradation → Value Nullification → Value Restoration
VNCM operates at the entry point into:
Value Nullification.
Internal Module Flow

Existing Positive Value → Potential Nullification Condition Identification → Value Context Alignment → Affected Value Dimension Identification → Condition Qualification
→ Condition Materiality Assessment → Temporal Status Definition → Nullification Condition State → Governed Nullification Condition → VNTM — Value Nullification Threshold Module
The internal logic is:
What condition exists → which value it affects → whether the condition is relevant to nullification → whether it is materially capable of eliminating the governed positive value → whether threshold assessment should begin.
Operational Space
VNCM governs the space between:
existing positive value
and
a qualified condition capable of placing that value on a nullification pathway.
This operational space includes:
nullification condition identification; condition definition; condition classification; Value Context linkage; affected Value Object identification; affected value dimension identification; condition materiality; condition applicability; condition activation; condition persistence; condition duration; condition reversibility; condition recurrence; condition dependency; compound nullification conditions; deliberate value withdrawal conditions; progressive degradation conditions; immediate nullification conditions; temporal nullification conditions; contextual nullification conditions; condition uncertainty; condition evidence linkage; nullification condition recording.
Existing Value Requirement

VNCM may govern a Value Nullification Condition only where the relevant positive value previously existed.
This requirement prevents VNS from being applied to potential value that never emerged.
The minimum logic is:
Positive Value Exists
→ Potential Nullification Condition Appears
→ VNCM Assessment.
Where no positive value previously existed:
Value Never Emerged
and the condition cannot legitimately be treated as nullification of that value.
Therefore:
Absence of Value ≠ Nullification Condition.
Nullification Condition Principle
A Value Nullification Condition is a governed condition capable of materially contributing to or enabling the transition of previously existing positive value toward a zero-value condition.
A condition may be:
necessary
without being sufficient.
It may also become sufficient only when combined with:
another condition; a threshold crossing; a temporal requirement; an external event; loss of a required capability; exhaustion of remaining utility; another governed dependency.
VNCM therefore separates:
Condition Exists
from
Value Is Nullified.
Condition ≠ Threshold
VNCM governs the condition.
VNTM governs the threshold.
For example:
A critical component of an industrial machine becomes unavailable.
That may constitute a:
Potential Nullification Condition.
But if the machine can continue functioning through alternative components, repair, substitution, or another viable configuration, the zero-value threshold may not have been reached.
Therefore:

Nullification Condition ≠ Nullification Threshold Reached.
This boundary is essential to prevent premature zero-value determinations.
Condition ≠ Cause
A nullification condition must also remain distinguishable from the external event that produced it.
For example:
Regulatory Event
may produce:
Loss of Permitted Operational Use
which may become:
Value Nullification Condition.
VNCM governs the condition affecting value.
It does not need to govern the external regulatory system that caused the condition.
Similarly:
Physical Damage
may create:
Loss of Required Functionality.
The physical event and the value condition are related but methodologically distinct.
Condition Classification
VNCM may classify Nullification Conditions according to their nature.
Relevant classes may include:
Functional Condition
A required value-conferring function becomes unavailable.
Operational Condition
The Value Object can no longer operate within the defined Value Context.
Temporal Condition
A time-dependent source of value reaches expiry or another defined temporal boundary.
Contextual Condition
A change in the governed context removes the basis under which positive value existed.
Capability Condition
A required capability is lost or withdrawn.
Access Condition
Access necessary for the relevant value becomes unavailable.
Technological Condition
Technological change eliminates the relevant usefulness or applicability of existing value.
Structural Condition

A structural property required to sustain value ceases to exist.
Deliberate Withdrawal Condition
An authorized actor deliberately removes a value-conferring property, function, access right, or capability.
Exhaustion Condition
The value-bearing capacity has been consumed or exhausted.
Destruction Condition
A value-conferring property is destroyed.
Compound Condition
Multiple conditions jointly create a potential nullification pathway even though no individual condition would be sufficient alone.
These classes are not intended to limit future forms of Value Nullification.
Value Context Alignment
A condition can qualify as a Nullification Condition only relative to the applicable Value Context.
For example:
A machine becomes legally prohibited from operating in Jurisdiction A.
This may create:
Operational Value Nullification Condition — Jurisdiction A.
The same machine may remain legally usable and operationally valuable in Jurisdiction B.
VNCM must therefore preserve:
Condition + Value Context
rather than declaring an uncontrolled universal nullification condition.
Value Dimension Identification
VNCM requires identification of the value dimension affected by the condition.
A Value Object may simultaneously possess:
Operational Value
Economic Value
Strategic Value
Knowledge Value
Functional Value
Salvage Value
Historical Value
Informational Value
A condition capable of eliminating one dimension does not automatically threaten every other dimension.
Therefore:

Nullification Condition for Value Dimension A ≠ Nullification Condition for all Value Dimensions.
Condition Materiality
Not every adverse condition is materially relevant to Value Nullification.
VNCM therefore evaluates whether the identified condition is capable of materially affecting the continued existence of the governed positive value.
A condition may be:
Non-Material
Potentially Material
Material
Critical
depending upon the governed methodology.
A minor performance reduction may affect value without creating a meaningful pathway toward zero.
A complete loss of the only required operational capability may represent a critical nullification condition.
Necessary and Sufficient Conditions
VNCM distinguishes between:
Necessary Condition
and
Sufficient Condition.
A necessary condition must exist before nullification can occur but may not independently establish it.
A sufficient condition may, when legitimately established together with the applicable threshold logic, provide the condition basis necessary for nullification determination.
Some Value Nullification pathways may require:
Condition A + Condition B + Condition C
before the pathway becomes materially complete.
Therefore:
One Condition ≠ Complete Nullification Basis.
Compound Nullification Conditions
Complex systems may lose value through combinations of conditions.
For example:
A technology platform may retain positive value while:
maintenance costs increase
or while:
user adoption decreases
or while:

integration support weakens.
But the combination:
No Maintenance Support
No Compatible Infrastructure
No Operational Users
No Viable Migration Path
may create a materially different nullification condition.
VNCM therefore permits conditions to be governed individually and collectively.
Progressive Nullification Condition
A nullification condition may develop progressively.
Example:
Component availability declines
→ maintenance becomes increasingly difficult
→ critical replacement capability disappears
→ continued operation becomes impossible.
VNCM must preserve the evolution of the condition rather than treating the final state as if it appeared instantaneously.
This provides a clean interface from:
Value Degradation
into:
Value Nullification.
Immediate Nullification Condition
Some conditions arise immediately.
Examples may include:
irreversible destruction;
immediate termination of a required right; complete loss of access; instantaneous expiration; sudden removal of essential functionality; abrupt contextual invalidation.
In such cases:
Positive Value
may move directly into a potential nullification pathway without prolonged degradation.
Therefore:
Prior Progressive Degradation Is Not Required.
Deliberate Value Withdrawal Condition
VNCM explicitly recognizes deliberate withdrawal as a possible Nullification Condition.
A value-conferring capability may be intentionally:

disabled; terminated; retired; revoked; withdrawn; decommissioned; made inaccessible; permanently discontinued.
The existence of intentional action does not itself establish Value Nullification.
VNCM determines whether that action creates a condition materially capable of eliminating the relevant positive value.
Temporary Condition
A Nullification Condition may be temporary.
For example:
A system becomes completely inaccessible because a required infrastructure service fails.
The condition may create:
Temporary Loss of Access.
Whether this causes a legitimate zero-value state depends on the applicable threshold and Value Context.
VNCM therefore records whether a condition is:
Temporary
Persistent
Recurring
Indeterminate
or
Permanent where determinable.
Condition Reversibility
A condition may be reversible even where it is capable of causing temporary Value Nullification.
Examples include:
repairable failure; renewable authorization; restorable access; replaceable infrastructure; reversible deactivation.
Reversibility does not prevent the condition from qualifying.
It affects the condition's meaning and potential downstream restoration pathway.
Therefore:
Reversible Condition ≠ Non-Material Condition.
Condition Activation
A potential condition may exist without being active.
For example:
A license has a known expiry date.
Before expiry:
Future Nullification Condition Identified
but:
Condition Not Yet Active.
At expiry:
Condition Activated.
VNCM therefore distinguishes between:

Identified Future Condition
Active Condition
Resolved Condition
and
Expired Condition.
Condition State
VNCM may assign a governed Nullification Condition State.
A minimum model may include:
1. Not Established
No legitimate Nullification Condition has been established.
2. Potential
A condition capable of becoming materially relevant has been identified but is not yet sufficiently established.
3. Active
The condition currently exists and is relevant to the governed value.
4. Critical
The condition materially threatens continued positive value and requires threshold assessment.
5. Resolved
The condition previously existed but has been removed or neutralized before nullification was established.
6. Indeterminate
Available information is insufficient to determine the condition state.
The states remain governance states, not universal physical classifications.
Condition Uncertainty
VNCM requires material uncertainty surrounding a condition to remain visible.
Uncertainty may concern:
whether the condition exists; when it began; whether it persists; what value dimension it affects; its materiality; its reversibility; its dependency upon other conditions; whether it can actually eliminate the governed value.
Uncertainty must not be converted silently into certainty merely because a nullification assessment has begun.
Condition Evidence
A Nullification Condition should be supported by evidence appropriate to the Value Context.
Evidence may include:

operational records; technical records; market information; contractual records; regulatory information; system logs; physical observations; lifecycle records; capability assessments; governed external determinations.
VNCM uses such evidence to establish the condition.
It does not replace the broader evidence integrity, validation, or audit architectures governing that evidence.
Temporal Condition Record
VNCM should preserve the temporal structure of the condition.
Where relevant:
T₀ — Positive Value Exists
→ T₁ — Condition First Appears
→ T₂ — Condition Becomes Material
→ T₃ — Condition Becomes Critical
→ T₄ — Threshold Assessment Begins
This allows later governance to distinguish:
when the condition arose
from
when value actually reached zero.
VNCM Boundary with VDGS
VDGS — Value Degradation Standard governs decline while positive value remains.
VNCM governs conditions capable of moving that positive value toward nullification.
A degradation process may create a Nullification Condition.
But:
Degradation ≠ Nullification Condition automatically.
Only degradation materially capable of placing the relevant value on a zero-value pathway enters VNCM.
VNCM Boundary with VNTM
VNCM determines:
What Nullification Condition exists?
VNTM determines:
Has the applicable Value Nullification Threshold been reached?
Therefore:
Condition ≠ Threshold.
VNCM Boundary with DeMonet™
VNCM does not execute or determine the DeMonet™ mechanism.

It establishes the governed condition basis that may allow the value to proceed toward DeMonet™.
The internal sequence remains:
Condition
→ Threshold
→ DeMonet™
not:
Condition = DeMonet™.
VNCM Boundary with VSS
VSS determines the current governed Value State.
VNCM determines whether a condition exists that may cause the current positive state to enter a Value Nullification pathway.
Therefore:
Current State ≠ Nullification Condition.
VNCM Boundary with VCS
VCS governs what material change occurred to value.
VNCM governs whether a resulting condition is materially capable of eliminating the relevant positive value.
A Value Change may therefore provide an input into VNCM without becoming the Nullification Condition itself.
VNCM Boundary with ORA™
ORA™ may govern the Operational Reality in which a condition occurs.
VNCM governs the value-specific meaning of that condition for potential nullification.
Therefore:
Operational Event ≠ Value Nullification Condition automatically.
VNCM Boundary with VALIDOS®
VALIDOS® may validate evidence, claims, methods, or determinations associated with a Nullification Condition.
VNCM owns the methodological definition and governance of the Value Nullification Condition itself.
VNCM Boundary with INTEGROS®
INTEGROS® may govern the integrity of records, evidence, and condition information.
VNCM governs what those conditions mean within the Value Nullification pathway.
VNCM Boundary with ADIT®

ADIT® may audit whether the condition, evidence, records, and decisions are observable and reconstructable.
VNCM governs whether a legitimate Value Nullification Condition has been established.
Minimum Implementation Framework
A minimum VNCM implementation should establish:
1. Existing Value Confirmation
Confirm that the relevant positive value previously existed.
2. Condition Identification
Identify the potential Value Nullification Condition.
3. Value Context Linkage
Define the Value Context within which the condition is relevant.
4. Value Dimension Identification
Identify which governed value dimension is affected.
5. Condition Classification
Determine the nature and type of the condition.
6. Materiality Assessment
Determine whether the condition is materially capable of threatening continued positive value.
7. Dependency Assessment
Identify whether the condition acts independently or together with other conditions.
8. Temporal Status
Determine whether the condition is future, active, recurring, persistent, resolved, or permanent where determinable.
9. Reversibility Assessment
Record whether the condition appears reversible, conditionally reversible, irreversible, or indeterminate.
10. Condition State Assignment
Assign and document the governed Nullification Condition State.
Governance Outputs
VNCM may produce:

Value Nullification Condition Record Existing Positive Value Confirmation Value Context Link Record Affected Value Dimension Record Nullification Condition Classification Nullification Condition Materiality Assessment Nullification Condition Dependency Record
Compound Condition Record Nullification Condition Temporal Record Nullification Condition Reversibility Status Nullification Condition Evidence Link Nullification Condition State Governed Nullification Condition Object
These outputs provide the governed input for:
VNTM — Value Nullification Threshold Module.
Use Case 1 — Industrial Production Asset Loses
Essential Support
A specialized industrial machine has existing positive operational value.
Its manufacturer progressively discontinues replacement components.
The first reduction in component availability does not nullify the machine's value.
VNCM identifies:
Existing Operational Value
→ Declining Critical Component Availability
→ Potential Nullification Condition.
The company then determines that the final essential control component is no longer manufactured, no compatible substitute exists, and the component is necessary for continued operation.
VNCM can classify:
Loss of Essential Replacement Capability
as an:
Active · Critical Value Nullification Condition.
But VNCM still does not declare:
Operational Value = 0.
The governed condition is transferred to VNTM to determine whether the applicable zero-value threshold has actually been reached.
This prevents:

“The machine is becoming difficult to maintain”
from being prematurely transformed into:
“The machine has zero operational value.”
Use Case 2 — Digital Service Withdraws a Value-
Creating Capability
A digital platform provides customers with a capability that creates measurable functional value.
The platform operator announces that the capability will be permanently discontinued in 90 days.
VNCM first identifies:
Future Deliberate Withdrawal Condition.
During the 90-day period, the capability remains available and positive functional value continues to exist.
The condition therefore exists as a future condition but has not yet produced nullification.
At termination:
Capability Access Withdrawn
→ Condition Activated
→ Functional Value Dimension Affected
→ Critical Nullification Condition Established.
VNCM passes the governed condition to VNTM.
VNTM can then determine whether withdrawal has actually crossed the applicable functional zero-value threshold.
This preserves the difference between:
announced future loss
active loss condition
and
actual Value Nullification.
Enterprise Application
VNCM gives organizations a governed early-stage mechanism for identifying when existing value has entered conditions that could legitimately lead to zero.
It can be applied across:

industrial assets; software; digital platforms; infrastructure; intellectual property; contractual rights; organizational capabilities; technologies; datasets; AI systems; autonomous systems; services; licenses; operational systems.
Its purpose is not to classify adverse events as nullification.
Its purpose is to establish:
which conditions are actually relevant to the possible disappearance of existing positive value.
VNCM therefore creates the first governed gate of the Value Nullification pathway.
Foundational Principles
Value must exist before a Value Nullification Condition can govern its potential loss.
Value Never Emerged ≠ Value Nullification Condition.
Adverse Event ≠ Value Nullification Condition automatically.
Condition ≠ Threshold.
Condition ≠ Nullification Determination.
Condition ≠ DeMonet™.
A condition may be necessary without being sufficient.
Multiple conditions may jointly create a nullification pathway.
A Nullification Condition may be progressive or immediate.
A Nullification Condition may be deliberate or externally caused.
A Nullification Condition may be temporary, persistent, recurring, reversible, or permanent.
A condition affecting one value dimension does not automatically threaten every value dimension.
The existence of a Nullification Condition establishes a reason to assess the zero-value boundary; it does not establish that the boundary has already been crossed.
Canonical Closing Statement

Value Nullification Condition Module establishes the first governed control point of the Value Nullification Standard by identifying, defining, qualifying, contextualizing, and recording conditions capable of placing previously existing positive value on a legitimate pathway toward zero. Through explicit governance of existing- value prerequisites, Value Context, affected value dimensions, condition classification, materiality, dependencies, compound conditions, activation, temporal status, reversibility, uncertainty, and condition states, VNCM prevents adverse events, degradation, future risks, capability changes, or deliberate withdrawals from being prematurely interpreted as completed Value Nullification. By separating the existence of a nullification- relevant condition from threshold crossing, DeMonet™, formal nullification determination, and ZVA™ state transition, VNCM creates the governed entry gate required before VFM® can legitimately determine whether positive value has actually reached its zero-value boundary.

Canonical Definition
Value Nullification Determination Module (VNDM) is the fourth Core Module of the Value Nullification Standard (VNS) within VFM® — Value Flow Mechanisms Architecture.
VNDM governs the formal determination of whether previously existing positive value has legitimately completed a Value Nullification transition and reached a governed zero-value condition within a defined Value Context, value dimension, scope, and temporal basis.

The Module receives the governed nullification conditions, threshold basis, and DeMonet™ transition established through the preceding VNS modules and determines whether the complete available basis supports recognition of the value as nullified.
Its foundational function is:
to prevent zero value from being assumed, declared, or operationally treated as established until the governed basis demonstrates that previously existing positive value has legitimately reached the applicable zero-value condition.
Architectural Position
VNDM is the fourth module within VNS.
It follows:
VDMM — DeMonet™ Mechanism Module
and precedes:
VNZM — Zero-Value State Transition Module.
The preceding modules establish:
the conditions under which nullification may occur
→ the threshold separating positive value from zero value
→ the DeMonet™ mechanism through which positive value crosses that boundary.
VNDM determines:
whether those governed elements collectively establish Value Nullification.
VNZM subsequently governs:
the transition of the determined nullified value into its appropriate zero-value state representation.
The distinction is fundamental:
DeMonet™ Transition ≠ Nullification Determination ≠ Zero-Value State.
Internal Module Flow

Governed Nullification Condition Basis → Governed Nullification Threshold Basis → DeMonet™ Transition Record → Prior Positive Value Confirmation → Affected Value Identification → Context & Dimension Confirmation → Threshold Satisfaction Review → Transition Completion Review → Contradictory Basis Review → Uncertainty Assessment → Nullification Determination → Determination State Assignment → Value Nullification Determination Record → VNZM — Zero-Value State Transition Module
Operational Space
VNDM governs the point between:
evidence of a potential or completed nullification transition
and
formal recognition that Value Nullification has occurred.
Its operational space includes:
prior positive value confirmation; nullified value identification; Value Context confirmation; value-dimension confirmation; nullification-condition review; threshold satisfaction; DeMonet™ transition review; transition completion; temporal determination; scope determination; partial versus complete dimensional nullification; contradictory basis; uncertainty; conditional determination; indeterminate determination; determination reversal or reassessment where materially justified; formal Value Nullification Determination.
Prior Positive Value Requirement
A valid Value Nullification Determination requires a governed basis showing that positive value existed before the alleged nullification.
Therefore:
Prior Positive Value = Required
because:
Value Never Emerged ≠ Value Nullified.

If no positive value can legitimately be established within the relevant governed context, VNDM must not manufacture a nullification event merely because the current value is zero.
The correct result may instead be:
Nullification Not Established.
Determination Object
Every VNDM determination must identify precisely what value has allegedly been nullified.
The Determination Object may relate to:
an entire Value Object; one value dimension; one capability; one function; one right; one economic use; one operational use; one market; one jurisdiction; one configuration; one temporal condition; one component of a compound Value Object.
This prevents a local value loss from becoming an unsupported declaration of total value loss.
Context-Specific Determination
Value Nullification is contextual.
An object may legitimately have:
Zero Operational Value
while retaining:
Positive Economic Value.
It may have:
Zero Value in Jurisdiction A
while retaining:
Positive Value in Jurisdiction B.
It may have:
Zero Current Use Value
while retaining:
Positive Option Value.
VNDM must therefore bind every determination to its relevant:
Value Object
Value Context
Value Dimension
Scope
Time
where materially applicable.
Therefore:
Zero in One Context ≠ Zero Everywhere.
Threshold Satisfaction
VNDM must confirm that the applicable threshold established through VNTM has actually been satisfied.
A value approaching zero is not necessarily zero.
Therefore:
Near-Zero Value ≠ Zero Value.
Likewise:

Severely Degraded Value ≠ Nullified Value.
Where positive value remains above the applicable governed zero-value boundary, VNDM must not issue a positive Value Nullification Determination.
Transition Completion
A DeMonet™ process may be initiated without being complete.
VNDM therefore distinguishes:
DeMonet™ Initiated
from
DeMonet™ Completed.
Where the relevant transition remains incomplete and positive value still exists, Value Nullification has not yet been fully established.
This prevents anticipated future nullification from being recorded as present nullification.
Nullification Determination Basis
A positive determination should establish, where materially relevant:
What positive value existed
→ within what Value Context
→ in which value dimension
→ under what nullification conditions
→ against what threshold
→ through what DeMonet™ transition
→ at what point the zero-value condition was reached
→ what scope of value was affected
→ what uncertainty remains.
The determination must remain reconstructable from its governed basis.
Positive Determination
A Positive Value Nullification Determination establishes that the relevant previously existing positive value has reached the applicable zero-value condition within the defined governed scope.
Canonical result:
Previously Existing Positive Value
→ Applicable Nullification Conditions
→ Applicable Nullification Threshold Reached
→ DeMonet™ Completed
→ Value Nullification Determined.

This determination does not yet establish Value Extinction.
Negative Determination
VNDM may determine that Value Nullification has not occurred.
This may result where:
positive value remains; the threshold has not been reached; DeMonet™ has not completed; the alleged value never existed; the wrong value dimension was assessed; the wrong Value Context was applied; available evidence contradicts nullification; the basis is insufficient; the alleged zero-value condition is merely a measurement or classification error.
A negative determination is itself a governed outcome.
Conditional Determination
In some cases, nullification can legitimately be established only under specified conditions.
For example:
Operational Value Nullified within Configuration C-4 while Dependency D remains unavailable.
This does not necessarily support:
Operational Value permanently nullified under all configurations.
Conditional determination allows VFM® to preserve legitimate zero-value recognition without overstating its scope.
Indeterminate Determination
Where the available governed basis cannot establish whether Value Nullification occurred, VNDM must permit:
Indeterminate.
This is critical.
Governance must not force a binary conclusion where the underlying basis does not support one.
Possible causes include:
incomplete historical value records; uncertain threshold crossing; conflicting evidence; unclear timing; unresolved context; uncertain DeMonet™ completion; insufficient dimensional separation.

Unknown ≠ Zero.
Partial Nullification Determination
A Value Object may contain multiple independently meaningful value components.
VNDM may therefore determine:
Partial Value Nullification
where a defined portion of value reaches zero while other positive value remains.
Example:
A patent portfolio contains ten commercially usable patents.
Two lose all enforceable commercial value in a defined jurisdiction.
VNDM may determine nullification for those governed value components without declaring the entire portfolio valueless.
Dimensional Nullification Determination
A single object may carry several value dimensions simultaneously.
For example:
Operational Value
Economic Value
Strategic Value
Knowledge Value
Salvage Value
Option Value
VNDM may determine:
Operational Value = Nullified
while:
Economic Value > 0
and:
Knowledge Value > 0.
This dimensional separation is essential for preventing false total-value conclusions.
Temporal Determination
VNDM should establish when Value Nullification occurred where the available basis permits.
The temporal state may be:
Exact
where a specific transition point is known.
Bounded
where nullification occurred within a defined interval.
Condition-Dependent
where zero value exists only during specified conditions.
Indeterminate
where the fact of nullification can be established but its exact timing cannot.
The determination should not create false temporal precision.
Temporary Zero Value

A positive Value Nullification Determination does not require that zero value be permanent.
An object may legitimately reach zero value and later recover.
Therefore:
Temporary Zero Value can still be genuine Zero Value.
For example:
A digital capability may become completely unavailable for six months.
During that governed period:
Functional Value = 0.
If restoration later occurs:
Zero Value
→ ReMonet™
→ Restored Value.
The later restoration does not retroactively invalidate the earlier nullification determination.
Nullification ≠ Extinction
VNDM must preserve one of the central VFM® boundaries:
Value Nullification ≠ Value Extinction.
A nullified value may still possess:
restoration potential.
The determination:
Current Value = 0
does not establish:
Recoverable Value No Longer Exists.
The latter belongs to:
VXSS — Value Extinction Standard.
Therefore:
Zero Value ≠ Value Extinction.
Nullification ≠ Object Destruction
A Value Object may physically continue to exist after its relevant value has been nullified.
Likewise, an object may be physically destroyed while some value remains through:
insurance rights; salvage; intellectual property; data; replacement rights; contractual claims; knowledge; residual materials.
Therefore:
Object Destruction ≠ Automatic Value Nullification
and
Value Nullification ≠ Object Destruction.
VFM® governs value, not merely physical existence.
Nullification ≠ Accounting Write-Off
An accounting system may write an asset down to zero.

That accounting action may be relevant evidence.
It does not automatically constitute a VFM® Value Nullification Determination.
Likewise, VFM® may determine that a relevant value dimension has reached zero while accounting systems retain a non-zero carrying amount.
Therefore:
Accounting State ≠ Governed Value State.
External valuation, accounting, tax, regulatory, or financial systems may provide inputs.
VNDM governs the VFM® nullification determination.
Nullification ≠ Market Price Zero
Market price may contribute to the determination of some economic value dimensions.
But:
Market Price = 0
does not automatically mean:
All Value = 0.
An object may retain:
operational value; strategic value; option value; knowledge value; recovery value; salvage value; internal utility.
VNDM must preserve the distinction between the relevant value dimension and the total Value Object.
Contradictory Basis Review
Before issuing a positive determination, VNDM should consider material information contradicting nullification.
Contradictory information may show:
remaining positive use; continuing demand; residual economic value; alternative operational use; active rights; restoration already underway; positive value in another governed dimension; incorrect threshold application; incomplete DeMonet™ transition.
Contradictory evidence must not be removed merely because it complicates the determination.
Uncertainty Preservation

A Value Nullification Determination should preserve material uncertainty affecting its meaning.
Relevant uncertainty may concern:
prior value; measurement; threshold; timing; scope; context; dimensional separation;
transition completion; evidence reliability; future recoverability.
Uncertainty does not necessarily prevent a determination.
It determines how strongly and broadly that determination may legitimately be represented.
Determination States
VNDM may assign a governed Value Nullification Determination State.
1. Not Established
The governed basis does not support Value Nullification.
2. Conditionally Established
Value Nullification is established only within explicitly defined conditions.
3. Established
The governed basis supports a positive Value Nullification Determination within the defined scope.
4. Partially Established
Nullification is established for only a defined component, dimension, context, or portion of the Value Object.
5. Indeterminate
The available basis cannot legitimately establish whether nullification occurred.
6. Under Reassessment
A previous determination is undergoing governed reconsideration following material new information or changed conditions.
7. Superseded
A later governed determination has replaced the earlier determination.
These states prevent a nullification conclusion from being represented more strongly than its basis permits.
Determination Reassessment

A Value Nullification Determination may require reassessment where materially relevant new information appears.
Possible triggers include:
newly discovered positive value; corrected historical information; threshold error; newly available evidence; changed Value Context; incorrect dimensional classification;
revised transition record; evidence of earlier restoration; material data correction.
Reassessment does not mean that governance is unstable.
It means that determinations remain accountable to the governed basis on which they depend.
Boundary with VNCM
VNCM governs:
the conditions under which Value Nullification becomes applicable.
VNDM governs:
whether Value Nullification has actually been established.
Therefore:
Nullification Condition ≠ Nullification Determination.
Boundary with VNTM
VNTM governs:
the threshold separating positive value from the zero-value condition.
VNDM governs:
whether the applicable threshold has been satisfied as part of the complete nullification basis.
Therefore:
Threshold ≠ Determination.
Boundary with VDMM
VDMM governs:
DeMonet™ as the transition mechanism from positive value into zero value.
VNDM governs:
formal determination that the relevant nullification transition has legitimately occurred.
Therefore:
Transition Mechanism ≠ Determination.
Boundary with VNZM
VNDM establishes:
that Value Nullification has occurred.
VNZM governs:
the resulting transition into the appropriate governed zero-value state.
Therefore:

Nullification Determination ≠ Zero-Value State Transition.
Boundary with VSS
VSS governs:
the current governed Value State.
VNDM establishes a specific lifecycle determination that may require the Value State to be updated.
Therefore:
Determination → State Consequence
but:
Determination ≠ State.
Boundary with VDGS
VDGS governs declining value while positive value remains.
VNDM must not classify degradation as nullification until the applicable zero-value threshold has actually been reached.
Therefore:
Degraded Value > 0 ≠ Nullified Value.
Boundary with VRSS
VRSS governs restoration of impaired, dormant, lost, or zero value.
A later ReMonet™ transition may restore value after a valid VNDM nullification determination.
Therefore:
Later Restoration ≠ Earlier Determination Was Invalid.
Boundary with VXSS
VXSS governs the terminal condition where the relevant value no longer exists as recoverable value within the governed lifecycle.
VNDM governs only whether positive value has reached zero.
Therefore:
Nullification Determination ≠ Extinction Determination.
Boundary with ORA™
ORA™ may establish the Operational Reality surrounding an event that affected value.
VNDM determines the resulting value condition within VFM®.
Therefore:
Operational Reality Determination ≠ Value Nullification Determination.
Boundary with VALIDOS®
VALIDOS® may validate claims, evidence, methods, or determinations used in establishing nullification.

VNDM owns the methodological determination of Value Nullification within VFM®.
Boundary with INTEGROS®
INTEGROS® may govern integrity properties of the information and evidence supporting the determination.
VNDM governs what that governed basis means for Value Nullification.
Boundary with ADIT®
ADIT® may audit whether the determination basis, evidence, transition history, and records are observable and reconstructable.
VNDM owns the Value Nullification Determination itself.
Minimum Implementation Framework
1. Prior Value Confirmation
Confirm that positive value previously existed within the relevant governed context.
2. Determination Object Identification
Identify the exact value, dimension, component, capability, right, or context being assessed.
3. Condition Review
Confirm the applicable Value Nullification Conditions.
4. Threshold Review
Confirm the applicable Value Nullification Threshold and whether it has been satisfied.
5. DeMonet™ Review
Confirm whether the governed DeMonet™ transition has been completed.
6. Scope & Context Review
Determine the exact scope, dimension, context, and temporal basis of the alleged nullification.
7. Contradictory Basis Review
Identify material information inconsistent with the proposed determination.
8. Uncertainty Assessment
Preserve material uncertainty affecting the determination.
9. Determination State Assignment
Assign the appropriate Value Nullification Determination State.
10. Determination Record

Create a traceable record of the determination and its governed basis.
Governance Outputs
VNDM may produce:
Value Nullification Determination Value Nullification Determination Record Prior Positive Value Confirmation Nullified Value Identification Record Value Dimension Determination Value Context Determination Nullification Scope Record Threshold Satisfaction Record DeMonet™ Completion Record Nullification Temporal Record Contradictory Basis Record Nullification Uncertainty Record Value Nullification Determination State Governed Nullification Determination Object
These outputs provide the governed basis for:
VNZM — Zero-Value State Transition Module.
Use Case 1 — Industrial Technology Loses One
Value Dimension but Retains Others
A manufacturing company operates a specialized production machine.
A new production architecture makes the machine technically incompatible with the company's manufacturing environment.
The machine can no longer perform any operational function within that environment.
VNDM receives the preceding governed basis establishing:
prior positive operational value
→ applicable nullification conditions
→ operational zero-value threshold reached
→ DeMonet™ completed.
The Module determines:
Operational Value Nullification = Established.
However, the machine remains physically intact and retains:
resale value
component value
salvage value
and potentially:
restoration value.
VNDM therefore does not determine:
Total Value = 0.
It determines only:

Operational Value within the defined manufacturing context = Nullified.
This prevents one legitimate zero-value determination from incorrectly eliminating every other value dimension attached to the same object.
Use Case 2 — Digital License Reaches Zero
Current Value but Retains Restoration Potential
An enterprise holds a digital license that historically provided substantial operational value.
The external provider suspends the enterprise's access after a contractual dispute.
The licensed capability becomes completely unusable.
The preceding VNS modules establish:
Positive Functional Value
→ Nullification Conditions
→ Applicable Threshold Reached
→ DeMonet™
→ Zero Functional Value.
VNDM determines:
Functional Value Nullification = Established
for the period in which access is unavailable.
However, contractual negotiations remain active and access may later be restored.
VNDM therefore does not classify the value as extinct.
The governed lifecycle may subsequently become:
Positive Value
→ DeMonet™
→ Value Nullification Determination
→ Zero-Value State
→ ReMonet™
→ Restored Value.
The case demonstrates the architectural necessity of separating:
Value Nullification
from
Value Extinction.
A value can legitimately be zero now without being irrecoverably gone.
Enterprise Application
VNDM provides organizations with a formal governance gate before value is recognized as nullified.
It can be applied to:

physical assets; technologies; digital assets; licenses; contractual rights; intellectual property; infrastructure; organizational capabilities; products; services; data assets; AI systems; autonomous systems; operational capabilities; strategic assets.
Its principal enterprise function is to prevent organizations from collapsing several materially different conditions into the single statement:
“This has no value.”
VNDM instead requires the organization to establish:
What value?
Within what context?
In which dimension?
Against what threshold?
Through what transition?
At what time?
With what evidence?
With what uncertainty?
Only then can Value Nullification be formally determined.
Foundational Principles
Value Nullification requires previously existing positive value.
Value that never emerged cannot be determined as nullified.
Near-zero value is not zero value.
Severely degraded value is not automatically nullified value.
A DeMonet™ transition must not be confused with the determination that nullification has occurred.
Nullification may be contextual, dimensional, partial, temporary, or conditional.
Zero in one value dimension does not establish zero in every value dimension.
Zero in one Value Context does not establish zero everywhere.
Accounting write-off does not automatically establish Value Nullification.
Market price zero does not automatically establish total value zero.
Object destruction and Value Nullification are not methodologically equivalent.

Unknown value is not zero value.
A valid nullification determination may later be followed by legitimate restoration.
Value Nullification ≠ Value Extinction.
Zero Value ≠ Value Extinction.
Canonical Closing Statement
Value Nullification Determination Module establishes the formal determination layer through which VFM® decides whether previously existing positive value has legitimately completed its nullification transition and reached the applicable zero-value condition within a defined Value Object, Value Context, value dimension, scope, and temporal basis. By requiring confirmation of prior positive value, applicable conditions, threshold satisfaction, DeMonet™ completion, contextual and dimensional boundaries, contradictory information, uncertainty, and determination state, VNDM prevents degraded, unknown, narrowly impaired, temporarily unavailable, or merely written-off value from being incorrectly represented as universally nullified. The Module creates the governed determination required before the resulting zero-value condition proceeds into formal state transition, while preserving the fundamental distinction between zero value and terminal loss of recoverability. A Value Nullification Determination establishes that relevant positive value has reached zero; it does not establish that value can never return.

Canonical Definition
Value Nullification Threshold Module (VNTM) is the second Core Module of the Value Nullification Standard (VNS) within VFM® — Value Flow Mechanisms Architecture.
VNTM governs the identification, definition, qualification, contextualization, assessment, crossing, and recording of the threshold at which previously existing positive value ceases to remain positive within a defined Value Context.
The Module establishes the governed boundary between:
Positive Value
and
Zero-Value Condition.

VNTM receives a qualified Value Nullification Condition from VNCM and determines whether that condition has actually brought the relevant governed value to its applicable zero-value boundary.
Its foundational function is:
to prevent decline, impairment, inactivity, obsolescence, withdrawal, or severe loss from being treated as Value Nullification unless the applicable governed zero-value threshold has actually been reached.
Architectural Position
VNTM is the second module within VNS.
It follows:
VNCM — Value Nullification Condition Module
and precedes:
VDMM — DeMonet™ Mechanism Module.
VNCM establishes:
what condition may place existing positive value on a nullification pathway.
VNTM establishes:
whether the governed boundary between positive value and zero value has actually been reached or crossed.
VDMM subsequently governs:
the DeMonet™ mechanism through which the transition into the zero-value condition is represented and governed.
The sequence is therefore:
Condition → Threshold → DeMonet™.
VFM® Governance Flow Position
Value Context → Value Origin
→ Value Emergence → Value Recognition → Value State → Value Change → Value Development → Value Degradation → Value Nullification → Value Restoration
VNTM operates inside the Value Nullification governed space at the decisive boundary between:
remaining positive value
and
zero value.
Internal Module Flow

Governed Nullification Condition → Affected Value Identification → Affected Value Dimension Identification → Applicable Value Context Confirmation → Threshold Basis Identification → Threshold Definition → Threshold Evidence Assessment → Threshold Proximity Assessment → Threshold Crossing Assessment → Threshold State Determination → Governed Nullification Threshold Record → VDMM — DeMonet™ Mechanism Module
The internal logic is:
Which value is threatened → where its zero boundary lies → how that boundary is established → whether it has actually been reached → whether the nullification pathway may continue.
Operational Space
VNTM governs the space between:
qualified Value Nullification Condition
and
established zero-value boundary crossing.
This operational space includes:
threshold identification; threshold basis; threshold definition; threshold qualification; value-dimension specificity; Value Context specificity; threshold measurement; threshold evidence; threshold proximity; threshold crossing; threshold persistence;
threshold duration; threshold reversibility; threshold uncertainty; threshold sensitivity; threshold dependency; compound thresholds; quantitative thresholds; qualitative thresholds; binary thresholds; conditional thresholds; temporal thresholds; contextual thresholds; dynamic thresholds; threshold state assignment; threshold recording.
Threshold Principle

A Value Nullification Threshold is the governed boundary at which the relevant previously existing positive value can no longer legitimately be classified as positive within its defined Value Context.
The threshold answers:
At what governed point does this value cease to remain positive?
The threshold may be numerical.
It may also be functional, operational, temporal, legal, contextual, capability-based, access-based, or otherwise methodologically defined.
VNTM therefore does not assume that every zero-value boundary can be represented by a monetary number.
Positive Value → Zero Boundary
The basic VNTM relationship is:
Positive Value
→ Approaching Nullification Threshold
→ Nullification Threshold Reached
→ Zero-Value Boundary Established.
Until the applicable threshold has been reached:
Positive Value Remains.
This remains true even where the value is:
severely degraded; economically unattractive; technologically obsolete; operationally constrained; rarely used; impaired; declining rapidly; close to zero.
Therefore:
Near Zero ≠ Zero.
Threshold ≠ Condition
VNCM may establish that a critical Nullification Condition exists.
That does not establish that the threshold has been reached.
For example:
Loss of Manufacturer Support
may be a legitimate Nullification Condition.
But if an asset can still be operated, maintained, repaired, substituted, repurposed, or otherwise retain positive governed value, the applicable threshold may remain uncrossed.
Therefore:

Nullification Condition ≠ Nullification Threshold Reached.
Threshold ≠ Nullification Determination
VNTM determines the status of the applicable zero-value boundary.
It does not issue the final Value Nullification Determination.
That responsibility belongs downstream to:
VNDM — Value Nullification Determination Module.
Therefore:
Threshold Reached ≠ Final Nullification Determination.
This separation preserves a controlled sequence between evidence of boundary crossing and formal governance determination.
Threshold ≠ DeMonet™
VNTM identifies and assesses the boundary.
DeMonet™ governs the value transition mechanism associated with movement from positive value into the zero-value condition.
Therefore:
Threshold defines the boundary.
DeMonet™ governs the transition mechanism.
The concepts must not collapse into one another.
Value Dimension Specificity
A Value Nullification Threshold applies to a defined value dimension.
A Value Object may simultaneously carry:
Operational Value
Economic Value
Strategic Value
Functional Value
Knowledge Value
Salvage Value
Historical Value
Informational Value
Option Value
One value dimension may reach its threshold while others remain positive.
For example:
Operational Value = 0
while:
Salvage Value > 0.
VNTM therefore prohibits the automatic inference:
One Value Dimension Reaches Zero
→ Entire Value Object Has Zero Value.
Value Context Specificity
Thresholds exist within defined Value Contexts.
A technology may reach:

Commercial Value = 0 in Market A
while retaining:
Commercial Value > 0 in Market B.
A machine may reach:
Operational Value = 0 in Production Context A
while retaining:
Training Value > 0 in Educational Context B.
VNTM therefore requires every material threshold determination to remain linked to:
Value Object + Value Dimension + Value Context.
Threshold Basis
A legitimate threshold requires an identifiable basis.
The basis may derive from:
defined functional requirements; operational capability requirements; measurable utility; contractual conditions; expiry conditions;
access requirements; economic criteria; technical capability; system availability; recoverable utility; authorized organizational methodology; externally governed determinations; contextual requirements.
The basis must be sufficient to explain:
why this boundary represents zero for this value in this context.
Quantitative Threshold
Some Value Nullification Thresholds may be numerical.
Examples may include:
Remaining governed value ≤ defined zero boundary
or:
Required measurable capability = 0.
A quantitative threshold should identify:
measurement basis; unit; calculation method; relevant value dimension; applicable context; uncertainty; effective period.
A numerical value should not be used merely because it creates an appearance of precision.
Qualitative Threshold
Some value dimensions cannot legitimately be reduced to a single numerical quantity.

A qualitative threshold may therefore be defined through a governed condition such as:
No remaining capability to perform the value-conferring function.
or:
No remaining legitimate use within the defined Value Context.
or:
No remaining accessible benefit attributable to the Value Object within the governed purpose.
Qualitative thresholds must still be explicit and assessable.
Non-Numerical ≠ Undefined.
Binary Threshold
Certain Value Objects may have binary value-conferring properties.
Examples include:
Access Available / Access Unavailable
Right Active / Right Expired
Capability Available / Capability Unavailable
Function Possible / Function Impossible
Where the value dimension legitimately depends on such a binary property, loss of that property may establish the relevant threshold.
But the relationship must be demonstrated rather than assumed.
Temporal Threshold
Some value exists only within a defined time interval.
Examples may include:
expiring rights; temporary access; time-limited licenses; perishable opportunities; event-specific capabilities; deadline-dependent benefits.
The threshold may therefore occur at:
T = Defined Expiry Point.
But expiration of one value dimension does not automatically eliminate every other value dimension attached to the object.
Conditional Threshold
A threshold may become applicable only where specified conditions are simultaneously satisfied.
For example:
Critical Function Unavailable
No Substitute Exists

No Economically or Operationally Viable Recovery Path
may collectively establish a threshold for a defined operational value.
This is a:
Conditional Value Nullification Threshold.
Compound Threshold
Complex Value Objects may require multiple boundary conditions.
A single factor may not be sufficient.
For example:
Market Demand = Near Zero
alone may not establish commercial nullification.
But:
Market Demand = Zero
No Alternative Market
No Internal Use
No Transferable Utility
may establish the applicable commercial-value threshold within the defined context.
VNTM therefore supports:
Single Threshold
and
Compound Threshold.
Dynamic Threshold
A threshold may change when the governed context materially changes.
For example:
A minimum performance capability required for positive operational value may increase after a new production process is introduced.
The Value Object may remain unchanged while the applicable threshold changes.
Therefore:
Value Thresholds may be context-sensitive and temporally dynamic.
Any material threshold change must remain traceable.
Threshold Proximity
VNTM may govern how close existing value is to its applicable nullification threshold.
Possible states may include:
Distant
Approaching
Near
At Threshold
Beyond Threshold
where the governing methodology supports such distinctions.
Threshold proximity is useful for identifying impending nullification without prematurely declaring zero value.
Threshold Crossing

Threshold crossing occurs when the governed evidence establishes that the applicable positive-value boundary has been reached or passed.
The crossing may be:
Progressive
where value gradually declines to the boundary,
or:
Immediate
where an event causes the boundary to be crossed without a prolonged degradation process.
The threshold crossing should identify, where determinable:
when crossing occurred; which value dimension crossed; under which Value Context; what evidence supports the crossing; whether crossing persists; whether uncertainty remains.
Threshold Persistence
A threshold may be reached only temporarily.
For example:
A digital capability may become unavailable for six hours and later be fully restored.
Depending upon the governed Value Context, the functional value may legitimately reach zero during the outage.
VNTM therefore distinguishes:
Threshold Reached Temporarily
from
Threshold Reached Permanently.
This distinction becomes important for downstream:
ZVA™
and
ReMonet™
governance.
Threshold Reversibility
Crossing a zero-value boundary does not necessarily mean that value can never return.
A threshold may be:
Reversible
Conditionally Reversible
Irreversible
or
Indeterminate.
VNTM records this characteristic without governing the restoration itself.
Restoration belongs downstream to:
VRSS — Value Restoration Standard
and its ReMonet™ mechanism.
Threshold Uncertainty
A zero-value boundary may not always be perfectly observable.
Uncertainty may concern:

threshold location; measurement; value dimension; evidence quality; contextual applicability; timing of crossing; persistence; reversibility; compound-condition satisfaction.
VNTM requires uncertainty to remain visible.
Where the evidence cannot establish whether the threshold has been reached, the correct state may be:
Threshold Status Indeterminate
rather than:
Value = 0.
Threshold Sensitivity
VNTM may assess how sensitive the threshold determination is to changes in:
assumptions; measurement; context; value definition; input information; temporal conditions; alternative viable uses.
A threshold determination that changes materially under small reasonable variations may require a conditional or indeterminate state.
Threshold Evidence
Threshold crossing should be supported by evidence appropriate to the governed value.
Evidence may include:
operational records; technical measurements; capability records; access records; market evidence; contractual records; expiry records; system logs;
lifecycle information; physical observations; authorized external determinations; governed value records.
VNTM does not replace evidence validation, integrity, or audit governance.
It determines what the available governed evidence means for the Value Nullification Threshold.
Threshold State Model
VNTM may assign a governed Value Nullification Threshold State.
A minimum state model may include:
1. Not Defined

No legitimate threshold has yet been established for the relevant value dimension and context.
2. Defined
The threshold is established, but the existing value remains materially above it.
3. Approaching
The value is moving materially toward the threshold.
4. At Threshold
Available governed evidence establishes that the applicable zero-value boundary has been reached.
5. Crossed
The relevant value has moved beyond the established positive-value boundary where the methodology permits such representation.
6. Temporarily Reached
The threshold has been reached for a bounded period, but recovery remains possible or has occurred.
7. Indeterminate
Available information is insufficient to determine whether the threshold has been reached.
The threshold state is not itself the final Value State.
No Threshold, No Governed Nullification
Where a Value Nullification Threshold cannot be legitimately defined or determined, VFM® should not manufacture a zero-value conclusion merely to complete the lifecycle.
Therefore:
Undefined Threshold ≠ Zero Value.
and:
Insufficient Threshold Evidence ≠ Nullification.
This creates an important protection against arbitrary declarations of worthlessness.
Boundary with VNCM
VNCM determines:
What condition may lead to nullification?
VNTM determines:
Where is the zero-value boundary, and has that boundary been reached?
Therefore:
Condition ≠ Threshold.
Boundary with VDGS
VDGS governs the weakening, deterioration, or decline of existing positive value.

VNTM governs the boundary at which that positive value ceases to remain positive.
Therefore:
Declining Value > 0 → VDGS
while:
Value reaches governed zero boundary → VNTM/VNS pathway.
Boundary with VDMM — DeMonet™
VNTM establishes whether the applicable zero-value boundary has been reached.
VDMM governs the DeMonet™ mechanism associated with the transition from positive value into a zero-value condition.
Therefore:
Threshold Crossing ≠ DeMonet™ Mechanism.

VNTM establishes threshold status.

Value Nullification Determination.
Therefore:
Threshold State ≠ Nullification Determination.

VSS may subsequently receive the new state resulting from the completed VNS pathway.
Boundary with VCS
VCS governs material changes to existing value.
A Value Change may move value toward, to, or across a Nullification Threshold.
VNTM governs the threshold consequence, not the external change itself.
Boundary with ORA™
ORA™ may govern the Operational Reality relevant to threshold evidence.
VNTM governs what that reality means for the applicable zero-value boundary.
Operational Failure ≠ Zero Value automatically.
Boundary with VALIDOS®

VALIDOS® may validate claims, evidence, methods, or determinations relevant to a threshold.
VNTM owns the methodological governance of the Value Nullification Threshold itself.
Boundary with INTEGROS®
INTEGROS® may govern the integrity of threshold evidence and records.
VNTM governs the meaning of that evidence for determining whether the zero-value boundary has been reached.
Boundary with ADIT®
ADIT® may audit whether threshold evidence, decisions, records, and changes are observable and reconstructable.

A minimum VNTM implementation should establish:

2. Value Dimension Identification

3. Value Context Confirmation

Use Case 1 — Industrial Asset Reaches Zero
Operational Value
A production machine has progressively deteriorated but continues to perform its required manufacturing function.
Its operational value declines substantially.
VNCM identifies:
Loss of critical maintenance capability
as a material Nullification Condition.
VNTM then defines the relevant operational-value threshold:
the machine can no longer perform the required production function within the defined operating context, and no viable supported configuration remains capable of restoring that function under the current operational basis.
Before this point:
Operational Value > 0

even if the machine is inefficient, expensive, or nearing obsolescence.
When the required capability is lost and the threshold evidence establishes that the production function can no longer be performed:
Operational Value → Threshold Reached.
VNTM records:
Operational Value Nullification Threshold State: At Threshold.
This does not declare the entire machine universally valueless.
The machine may retain:
Salvage Value > 0
Material Value > 0
Historical Value > 0
or another positive value dimension.
The threshold applies only to:
Operational Value within the defined production context.
The governed threshold result can then enter the DeMonet™ mechanism.
Use Case 2 — Digital License Reaches Its
Functional Zero-Value Boundary
An organization holds a software license that provides access to a specialized digital capability.
The license has positive functional value while authorized access remains active.
The governing contract establishes a fixed expiration date, after which:
access terminates;
the licensed capability becomes unavailable;
and
no continuing usage right remains.
VNCM identifies:
License Expiration
as the relevant Nullification Condition.
VNTM defines the threshold as:
termination of authorized access to the value-conferring capability.
Before expiration:
Functional Value > 0.
At the defined expiry point:
Authorized Access = Unavailable
→ Functional Threshold Reached.
VNTM records the threshold crossing.
However, it does not infer:
Software = universally valueless.

The organization may still possess:
historical data value;
knowledge value;
migration value;
or other value associated with related assets.
VNTM therefore establishes precisely:
which value reached zero, in which context, and at which governed boundary.
Enterprise Application
VNTM enables organizations to answer a deceptively difficult question:
Where exactly does positive value end?
It can be applied across:
industrial assets; infrastructure; technologies; software; digital capabilities; licenses; contractual rights; datasets; intellectual property; products; services; organizational capabilities; AI systems; autonomous systems; operational systems.
Its primary enterprise value is methodological discipline.
Organizations frequently know that value has declined but lack an explicit basis for determining when that decline becomes zero.
VNTM creates that boundary.
It prevents:
declining
obsolete
unused
impaired
unprofitable
inactive
or
unwanted
from being treated automatically as:
zero value.
Foundational Principles
A nullification condition does not establish that the zero-value threshold has been reached.
Near zero is not zero.
Severe degradation is not automatically nullification.
A threshold must be defined before threshold crossing can be governed.
A zero-value threshold belongs to a defined value dimension and Value Context.
Zero in one value dimension does not establish zero across all value dimensions.

A threshold may be quantitative without requiring all value to be monetary.
A qualitative threshold must still be explicit and assessable.
A threshold may be temporary, contextual, conditional, compound, or dynamic.
Threshold crossing may be progressive or immediate.
Threshold reached does not automatically mean permanently zero.
Threshold reached does not itself constitute the final Value Nullification Determination.
Undefined threshold does not authorize an arbitrary zero-value conclusion.
The zero-value boundary must be governed before the transition through DeMonet™ can be legitimately established.
Canonical Closing Statement
Value Nullification Threshold Module establishes the decisive boundary-control layer of the Value Nullification Standard by defining, contextualizing, assessing, and recording the point at which previously existing positive value ceases to remain positive within a defined value dimension and Value Context. Through explicit governance of threshold basis, threshold type, evidence, proximity, crossing, persistence, reversibility, uncertainty, sensitivity, compound conditions, temporal applicability, and threshold states, VNTM prevents degradation, impairment, inactivity, obsolescence, withdrawal, or severe decline from being prematurely interpreted as zero value. By separating Nullification Conditions from Nullification Thresholds, threshold crossing from DeMonet™, and threshold status from formal Value Nullification Determination, VNTM creates the

methodological boundary required for VFM® to govern the transition from positive value toward a legitimate zero-value condition without erasing remaining value in other dimensions or contexts.
