Canonical Definition
Value Recognition Determination Module (VRDM) is the third Core Module of the Value Recognition Standard (VRS) within VFM® — Value Flow Mechanisms Architecture.
VRDM governs the formal determination of whether existing value is recognized within a defined value context by applying the recognition criteria established through VRCM — Value Recognition Criteria Module to the recognition basis established through VRBM — Value Recognition Basis Module.
Its purpose is to transform an established recognition basis into an explicit, reproducible, bounded, and governable recognition outcome.
VRDM does not determine whether value originally existed.
It does not create value.

It does not determine market price, ownership, legality, accounting treatment, taxation, validation status, or universal acceptance.
Its function is precise:
to determine whether existing value qualifies for recognition within the defined recognition context.
The governing relationship is:
Existing Value + Recognition Context + Recognition Criteria + Recognition Basis → Value Recognition
Determination
Architectural Position
VRDM operates within the fourth governed space of the VFM® lifecycle:
Value Context → Value Origin → Value Emergence → Value Recognition → Value State → Value Change → Value Development / Value Degradation → Value Nullification → Value Restoration / Value Extinction
Within the Value Recognition Standard, VRDM occupies the decision point between the recognition basis and the limitations attached to the resulting recognition.
Internal Module Flow
Existing Value → VRCM — Value Recognition Criteria → VRBM — Value Recognition Basis → VRDM — Value Recognition Determination → VRLM — Value Recognition Limitation → VRRM — Value Recognition Record → Recognized Value
VRDM therefore answers the decisive question in the internal recognition flow:
Given these criteria and this basis, what recognition outcome legitimately follows?
Operational Space
VRDM governs:

recognition determination initiation; recognition context confirmation; criterion applicability confirmation; recognition basis consideration; criterion-to-basis assessment; supporting basis treatment; contradictory basis treatment; conditional recognition; partial recognition; non-recognition; indeterminate recognition; recognition determination reasoning; recognition state assignment; determination consistency; determination reproducibility; determination uncertainty; determination conditions;
determination review triggers; machine-readable recognition outcomes.
The Module converts recognition analysis into a governed determination.
Recognition Determination Principle
Recognition must not arise merely because an institution, organization, model, analyst, or automated system labels something valuable.
A governed recognition determination requires an identifiable methodological chain:
Defined Value → Defined Recognition Context → Applicable Recognition Criteria → Applicable Recognition Basis → Recognition Assessment
→ Recognition Determination
This makes the outcome reconstructable.
A downstream user should be able to determine not merely:
“This value was recognized.”
but:
“This value was recognized under these criteria, on this basis, within this context, subject to these conditions.”
Determination ≠ Value Creation
VRDM enforces one of the most important boundaries in VFM®:
Recognition does not create the underlying value.

Value must already exist before it enters the Value Recognition Standard.
Therefore:
Existing Value → Recognition
not:
Recognition → Value Existence
An institution may recognize value that already exists.
It may fail to recognize value that already exists.
It may change its recognition determination without changing the underlying value.
This prevents institutional recognition systems from silently becoming definitions of value itself.
Determination ≠ Universal Recognition
A VRDM determination applies only within its defined recognition context.
Therefore:
Recognized in Context A ≠ Universally Recognized
For example, a capability may be:
Recognized as Operational Value
while remaining:
Not Recognized as Accounting Value
Not Recognized as Collateral Value
and
Conditionally Recognized as Strategic Value.
These outcomes may coexist without contradiction.
They describe different recognition relationships to the same existing value.
Criterion-to-Basis Determination
VRDM requires each material recognition criterion to be considered against the relevant recognition basis.
The determination chain may be represented as:
Criterion A → Basis A → Assessment A
Criterion B → Basis B → Assessment B
Criterion C → Basis C → Assessment C
↓
Combined Recognition Determination
This prevents recognition from being based upon a general impression when explicit criteria have already been established.
Supporting and Contradictory Basis
VRDM must consider materially relevant basis that:

supports recognition; weakens recognition; contradicts recognition; conditions recognition; limits recognition; leaves recognition unresolved.
A recognition determination that considers only favorable basis is methodologically incomplete.
Therefore:
Recognition Determination ≠ Selection of Supporting Information
VRDM requires material conflicts identified by VRBM to remain visible in the determination.
Recognition Determination States
VRDM may establish a minimum canonical state model.
1. Recognized
The applicable criteria are sufficiently satisfied by the governed recognition basis within the defined context.
2. Conditionally Recognized
Recognition is legitimate only where explicitly defined conditions remain satisfied.
3. Partially Recognized
Only a defined portion, dimension, capability, benefit, period, application, or value relationship satisfies the applicable recognition requirements.
4. Not Recognized
The applicable criteria are not sufficiently satisfied within the defined recognition context.
5. Indeterminate
The available basis does not permit a sufficiently supported recognition or non-recognition determination.
6. Recognition Suspended
A previous recognition determination cannot presently be relied upon because a material change, unresolved contradiction, missing basis, or review condition requires reassessment.
These are recognition states, not value-existence states.
Non-Recognition Principle
VRDM makes a critical distinction:
Not Recognized ≠ No Value

Non-recognition means:
the existing value does not currently satisfy the applicable recognition requirements within this defined context.
It does not establish:
the value does not exist.
This distinction is particularly important where conventional systems recognize only a limited subset of value.
A technological capability, avoided cost, operational advantage, public benefit, strategic resource, unused capacity, or future-use capability may exist as value even where a specific institutional recognition framework does not recognize it.
Indeterminate Recognition
VRDM must permit an indeterminate outcome.
Without an indeterminate state, recognition systems may be forced into false binary conclusions:
Recognized / Not Recognized
even where the available basis is insufficient.
An indeterminate state allows the system to state:
the recognition question remains unresolved on the current basis.
This is methodologically stronger than manufacturing certainty where none exists.
Conditional Recognition
Recognition may depend upon conditions.
Examples include:
continued availability of a capability; continued beneficiary relevance; defined operating conditions; specified technological configuration; defined market conditions; continued resource scarcity; maintained performance; temporal validity; defined regulatory context; continued accessibility.
VRDM must preserve those conditions within the recognition determination.

If a condition disappears, the recognition determination may require reassessment.
Partial Recognition
Some value objects may contain multiple value dimensions.
A single object may provide:
operational value; strategic value; financial value; technological value; resource value; public value; future-use value.
VRDM may therefore recognize one value dimension without recognizing another.
Similarly, only part of a claimed value may be sufficiently supported.
This permits:
Partial Recognition
without forcing the entire value claim into one binary state.
Recognition Across Multiple Beneficiaries
Value may be recognized differently depending upon the beneficiary established through the Value Context Standard (VCXS).
For example, the same infrastructure may create:
Value for Operator
Value for Customer
Value for Government
Value for Community
Value for Future Users
The recognition determination must remain linked to the relevant beneficiary where beneficiary identity materially affects recognition.
Therefore:
Recognition for Beneficiary A ≠ Recognition for Beneficiary B
unless the applicable basis supports both.
Temporal Recognition
Recognition exists in time.
A value recognized today may not remain recognizable indefinitely.
Recognition may change because:

the beneficiary changes; the purpose changes; the capability becomes obsolete; technology advances; resources become more or less scarce; operating conditions change; the recognition basis changes; recognition criteria change; the underlying value changes.
VRDM therefore requires recognition determinations to support temporal applicability and reassessment.
Recognition Change ≠ Value Change
A recognition determination may change even when the underlying value remains unchanged.
For example:
Year 1: value exists but is not institutionally recognized.
Year 2: recognition criteria expand.
Year 3: the same existing value becomes recognized.
The value itself may not have changed.
The recognition relationship changed.
Therefore:
Recognition State Change ≠ Value State Change
This distinction becomes essential when VFM® is used across institutional, economic, technological, governmental, or accounting systems.
Recognition Determination ≠ Valuation
VRDM determines whether value is recognized.
It does not determine the magnitude of that value.
Therefore:
Recognized Value ≠ Valued Amount
A determination such as:
Recognized as Operational Value
does not itself establish:
CHF 10 million of value.
Valuation or value magnitude may require separate methodology.
VRDM protects the architecture from collapsing recognition into pricing.
Recognition Determination ≠ Accounting
Recognition
Accounting systems may use recognition rules appropriate to financial reporting.
VRDM is broader.

It may govern recognition of value in contexts including:
operations; strategy; infrastructure; public systems; science; technology; resource efficiency; resilience; capability; investment analysis; mission planning; digital systems.
Accounting recognition may therefore be one external recognition context.
It is not the universal definition of VFM® value recognition.
Recognition Determination ≠ Market Acceptance
A market may recognize value through demand, exchange, pricing, or liquidity.
But value recognition under VFM® does not depend upon the existence of a market.
A value may be recognized where:
it is internally consumed; it avoids cost; it preserves capability; it reduces resource use; it increases resilience; it creates strategic optionality; it benefits a public system; it cannot be transferred; no market currently exists.
Therefore:
No Market ≠ No Recognizable Value
Recognition Determination ≠ Legal or Tax
Determination
VRDM does not determine whether recognized value:
constitutes property; creates ownership rights; is legally enforceable; is taxable; creates taxable income; creates a taxable event; qualifies as a regulated asset; may be transferred; may be used as collateral.
Those questions belong to their relevant legal, tax, governance, or external architectural systems.
VFM® governs the value lifecycle.
Determination Reproducibility
A governed recognition determination should be capable of reconstruction.
A reviewer should be able to identify:

Value Reference → Recognition Context → Recognition Criteria → Recognition Basis → Criterion Assessments → Material Conflicts → Conditions
→ Recognition Determination
This does not require every evaluator to reach the same conclusion under every methodology.
It requires the reasoning pathway to be explicit enough to understand how the determination was reached.
Determination Consistency
Where materially equivalent value contexts, criteria, and bases are assessed differently, the difference should be identifiable.
VRDM therefore supports consistency analysis across recognition determinations.
This can expose:
inconsistent institutional recognition; undocumented exceptions; criteria drift; arbitrary recognition; algorithmic inconsistency; human decision inconsistency; changes in recognition policy.
Consistency does not require identical outcomes where material facts differ.
It requires differences to have an identifiable basis.
Human and Machine Determination
VRDM may support recognition determinations performed by:
humans; committees; institutions; AI systems; automated rules; hybrid human-machine processes.
The governance requirement remains the same:
the determination must remain connected to the governed criteria, basis, context, conditions, and outcome.
An AI-generated recognition decision does not become governed merely because it is computationally produced.
Machine-Readable Recognition Determination
A machine-readable VRDM implementation may represent:

Value ID → Recognition Context ID → Beneficiary ID / Reference → Criterion Set ID → Recognition Basis ID → Criterion Assessment States → Conflict State → Recognition Conditions → Recognition Determination State → Temporal Applicability → VRLM Limitation Interface → VRRM Record Interface
This allows recognition determinations to become portable across systems without reducing them to a binary label.
Recognition Review Triggers
A recognition determination may require review where there is material change to:
value context; beneficiary; purpose; recognition criteria; recognition basis; underlying capability; resource conditions; technological conditions; operational conditions; temporal relevance; material contradictory information.
Review does not automatically change recognition.
It reopens the determination where its existing basis may no longer be sufficient.
Boundary with VRCM
VRCM — Value Recognition Criteria Module determines:
What must be satisfied for recognition?
VRDM determines:
Given the applicable criteria and basis, what recognition outcome follows?
Therefore:
Criteria ≠ Determination
Boundary with VRBM
VRBM — Value Recognition Basis Module establishes:
What supports the recognition assessment?
VRDM evaluates that basis against the applicable criteria.
Therefore:
Basis ≠ Determination
The same basis may produce different legitimate determinations under different recognition contexts or criteria.
Boundary with VRLM
VRDM determines the recognition outcome.

VRLM — Value Recognition Limitation Module subsequently determines the limitations, boundaries, exclusions, and conditions governing how that recognition may legitimately be interpreted or used.
Therefore:
Recognition Determination ≠ Unlimited Recognition
Boundary with VRRM
VRDM produces the recognition determination.
VRRM — Value Recognition Record Module preserves the recognition outcome and its governed basis as a durable recognition record.
Therefore:
Determination ≠ Record
Boundary with Value State Standard
Recognition is not itself the complete state of value.
The subsequent Value State Standard (VSS) governs the state of the value within the broader VFM® lifecycle.
VRDM must therefore not collapse:
Recognition State
into:
Value State
A value can be recognized while later becoming degraded, nullified, restored, or extinct.
Minimum Implementation Framework
A minimum VRDM implementation should establish:
1. Value Reference
Identify the existing value subject to recognition determination.
2. Recognition Context Confirmation
Confirm the context, beneficiary, and purpose within which recognition is being determined.
3. Applicable Criteria
Receive the applicable recognition criteria from VRCM.
4. Recognition Basis
Receive the governed recognition basis from VRBM.
5. Criterion Assessment
Assess each material criterion against the relevant basis.
6. Conflict Assessment
Consider materially supporting, contradictory, conditional, and limiting basis.
7. Recognition Determination

Determine the legitimate recognition outcome.
8. Recognition State Assignment
Assign the appropriate recognition state.
9. Conditions and Temporal Applicability
Identify conditions and temporal boundaries affecting the determination.
10. Determination Basis
Preserve the reasoning necessary for VRLM and VRRM to govern the resulting recognition.
Governance Outputs
VRDM may produce:
Value Recognition Determination Recognition Determination State Criterion Assessment Record Recognition Context Confirmation Recognition Beneficiary Relationship Recognition Conflict Assessment Conditional Recognition Statement Partial Recognition Statement Non-Recognition Determination
Indeterminate Recognition Determination Recognition Suspension State Recognition Temporal Applicability Recognition Review Trigger Recognition Determination Basis
These outputs provide the governed input for VRLM — Value Recognition Limitation Module.
Use Case 1 — Banking: Recognition Beyond the
Balance Sheet
A bank evaluates a technology company possessing proprietary software, operational datasets, automation capabilities, specialized processes, and internal technological infrastructure.
The relevant value has already emerged.
VRCM establishes criteria for strategic enterprise value recognition.
VRBM establishes basis including:
recurring cost reductions; production improvements; customer retention effects; demonstrated internal dependence; measurable productivity gains; technological capability.

VRDM applies the criteria to that basis.
The outcome might be:
Strategic Value → Recognized
Operational Value → Recognized
Future Capability Value → Conditionally Recognized
Collateral Value → Not Determined within this recognition context
The bank has not magically converted software into collateral.
It has done something methodologically different:
it has established which forms of existing value can legitimately be recognized for the defined analytical purpose.
This enables richer enterprise assessment without confusing strategic recognition with accounting, legal, or collateral status.
Use Case 2 — Space Mission: Recognition of
Avoided Resource Consumption
A space organization deploys a mission-optimization capability.
The capability does not create a new physical asset.
Instead, it reduces:
engineering hours; simulation executions; physical testing;
fuel requirements; hardware consumption; mission preparation time.
The value already exists through these resource effects.
VRCM establishes criteria for Mission Resource Efficiency Value.
VRBM provides the basis:
8,000 engineering hours avoided
35% reduction in computational workload
two physical testing campaigns avoided
measurable fuel requirement reduction
VRDM determines whether those effects satisfy the recognition criteria.
The result may be:
Mission Resource Efficiency Value → Recognized
with specified conditions concerning mission configuration, measurement period, and comparison baseline.

This demonstrates an important VFM® capability:
value can be formally recognized even where its manifestation is not a new asset or new revenue, but resources that no longer need to be consumed.
Enterprise Application
VRDM gives organizations a controlled mechanism for transforming value-related information into explicit recognition determinations.
It can support banking, investment, government, public finance, enterprise management, infrastructure, technology, AI, energy, manufacturing, scientific programs, resource optimization, mission planning, and other environments where organizations need to distinguish:
value that exists
from
value that a particular system recognizes.
This distinction becomes especially powerful where conventional systems recognize only narrow forms of value.
VRDM enables multiple recognition contexts to coexist without forcing operational, strategic, financial, social, technological, resource, and other forms of value into one universal recognition model.
Foundational Principles
Recognition does not create value.
Value may exist before recognition.
Recognition must be based on explicit criteria and an identifiable basis.
Recognition is contextual, not automatically universal.
Not recognized does not mean no value exists.
Indeterminate recognition is legitimate where the basis does not support certainty.
Recognition state is not value state.
Recognition determination is not valuation.
Recognition determination is not accounting treatment.

Recognition determination is not market acceptance.
Recognition determination is not legal or tax determination.
The same existing value may legitimately have different recognition outcomes in different contexts.
A governed recognition determination must be reconstructable from the context, criteria, basis, assessment, and resulting recognition state.
Canonical Closing Statement
**Value Recognition Determination Module establishes the decision layer of the Value Recognition Standard by converting explicit recognition criteria and governed recognition basis into a formal, contextual, conditional, reproducible, and machine-readable recognition outcome. Through governance of criterion assessment, supporting and contradictory basis, recognition states, conditional and partial recognition, non-recognition, indeterminate outcomes, temporal applicability, beneficiary relationships, consistency, review triggers, and determination traceability, VRDM prevents institutional recognition from being confused with value existence itself. By separating recognition determination from value creation, valuation, accounting treatment, market acceptance, legal status, taxation, value state, and downstream recognition limitations, VRDM enables organizations and intelligent systems to state not merely that value is recognized, but precisely what value is recognized, for whom, within what context, against what criteria, on what basis, under what conditions, and with what determination outcome.

Canonical Definition
Value Recognition Limitation Module (VRLM) is the fourth Core Module of the Value Recognition Standard (VRS) within VFM® — Value Flow Mechanisms Architecture.
VRLM governs the explicit boundaries, conditions, exclusions, restrictions, dependencies, uncertainties, temporal limits, beneficiary limits, contextual limits, and prohibited interpretations attached to a Value Recognition Determination.
Its purpose is to prevent legitimate recognition within one defined context from being silently expanded into recognition that the underlying determination does not support.
VRLM does not determine whether value exists.

It does not establish recognition criteria, create the recognition basis, or issue the recognition determination.
Its function begins after a recognition outcome has been established through VRDM — Value Recognition Determination Module.
Its governing function is:
to determine what the recognition determination does not establish, where its legitimate meaning ends, and under what conditions it remains applicable.
The governing relationship is:
Recognition Determination → Recognition Boundary → Recognition Conditions → Recognition Limitations → Bounded Recognition
Architectural Position
VRLM operates within the fourth governed space of the VFM® lifecycle:
Value Context → Value Origin → Value Emergence → Value Recognition → Value State → Value Change → Value Development / Value Degradation → Value Nullification → Value Restoration / Value Extinction
Within the Value Recognition Standard, VRLM follows the recognition determination and precedes the formal recognition record.
Internal Module Flow
Existing Value → VRCM — Value Recognition Criteria → VRBM — Value Recognition Basis → VRDM — Value Recognition Determination → VRLM — Value Recognition Limitation → VRRM — Value Recognition Record → Bounded and Recorded Recognized Value
The internal logic is:
What must be satisfied → what supports the assessment → what recognition outcome follows → where that recognition applies and stops → how the complete recognition is recorded
VRLM therefore establishes the boundary between:

legitimate recognition
and
unsupported recognition expansion.
Operational Space
VRLM governs limitations affecting the legitimate interpretation and downstream use of recognition.
These may include:
recognition-context limitations; beneficiary limitations; purpose limitations; value-dimension limitations; object limitations; capability limitations; geographic limitations; temporal limitations; operational limitations; technological limitations; dependency limitations; assumption limitations; measurement limitations; evidence limitations; uncertainty limitations; comparability limitations; transfer limitations; institutional limitations; downstream-use limitations; prohibited recognition interpretations.
The objective is not to weaken recognition.
It is to preserve its legitimate meaning.
Recognition Limitation Principle
Every recognition determination exists within a boundary.
If the determination establishes:
“Value X is recognized within Context A for Beneficiary B and Purpose C.”
VRLM prevents that statement from silently becoming:
“Value X is universally recognized for every beneficiary and every purpose.”
Therefore:
Recognition ≠ Unlimited Recognition
and:
Recognition Expansion Requires a Governed Basis
Limitation ≠ Non-Recognition
A limitation does not mean that value is not recognized.
For example:
Recognized only for operational efficiency
is still a legitimate recognition determination.
The limitation merely prevents the recognition from being interpreted as:

financial recognition; collateral recognition; accounting recognition; market recognition;
legal recognition; tax recognition; universal recognition.
Therefore:
Bounded Recognition ≠ Weak Recognition
A narrow recognition determination may be extremely strong within its legitimate context.
Context Limitation
Recognition must remain attached to the value context established through the Value Context Standard (VCXS).
A recognition determination made within:
industrial operational efficiency
cannot automatically be transferred into:
financial reporting
or:
taxable economic value.
The underlying value may remain the same.
The recognition context has changed.
A new recognition context may therefore require a new recognition assessment.
Beneficiary Limitation
Value recognized for one beneficiary may not automatically be recognized for another.
For example, a technological system may create substantial value for:
the operator
while creating limited value for:
the customer
and potentially negative value for:
another affected party.
VRLM requires beneficiary boundaries to remain visible where they materially affect recognition.
Therefore:
Recognition for Beneficiary A ≠ Recognition for Beneficiary B
Purpose Limitation
Recognition may be valid only for a defined purpose.
Examples include:
investment analysis; operational planning; strategic assessment;

resource allocation; infrastructure planning; technological capability assessment; public-policy analysis; cost optimization; mission planning.
Recognition for one purpose does not automatically authorize reliance for another.
Value-Dimension Limitation
The same underlying value may possess several dimensions.
For example:
Operational Value Strategic Value Technological Value Financial Value Resource Value Public Value Resilience Value
VRLM ensures that recognition of one dimension does not silently establish recognition of all dimensions.
Therefore:
Recognized Operational Value ≠ Recognized Financial Value
unless a separate governed basis establishes that relationship.
Object and Capability Limitation
Recognition may apply only to a defined object, configuration, capability, version, system, facility, process, technology, resource, or organizational unit.
Recognition attached to:
Technology Configuration V4
must not automatically be transferred to:
Technology Configuration V7
where material changes affect the recognition basis.
Similarly, recognition of one capability within a system does not automatically recognize every capability of the system.
Temporal Limitation
Recognition is not automatically permanent.
A recognition determination may remain legitimate only:

during a defined period; while specific conditions remain satisfied; while the capability remains operational; while the beneficiary relationship exists; while the recognition basis remains current; until material change occurs; until a defined review date; while external conditions remain materially equivalent.
VRLM therefore allows recognition to carry:
Temporal Applicability
rather than assuming perpetual recognition.
Geographic and Jurisdictional Limitation
Recognition may depend upon geography or institutional environment.
A value recognized within:
Region A
may not automatically satisfy the recognition requirements of:
Region B.
Similarly, an institutional recognition determination in one jurisdiction does not automatically create equivalent legal, accounting, regulatory, or tax recognition elsewhere.
VRLM preserves this distinction without attempting to govern those external systems.
Operational Limitation
Recognition may depend upon specific operating conditions.
For example, an optimization system may create recognized value only where:
production exceeds a certain scale; specific infrastructure exists; particular resources are constrained; required data is available; defined process conditions exist; system integration remains functional.
Outside those conditions, the recognition basis may weaken or disappear.
Dependency Limitation

Recognized value may depend upon another capability, system, resource, infrastructure, relationship, right, dataset, workforce, technology, or condition.
VRLM requires material dependencies to remain visible.
For example:
AI capability value
may depend upon:
access to proprietary operational data.
If access disappears, the recognized value may require reassessment.
Therefore:
Recognized Value + Critical Dependency ≠ Independently Sustainable Value
Assumption Limitation
Some recognition determinations rely upon assumptions.
These may concern:
future demand; resource availability; technological continuity; user behavior; cost structures; operational conditions; market conditions; expected utilization; policy continuity.
VRLM requires material assumptions to remain attached to the recognition determination where recognition would materially change if the assumptions fail.
Measurement Limitation
A recognition determination may rely upon measured effects whose measurement itself is bounded.
For example:
18% operating-cost reduction
may apply only to:
one facility; one production period; one product line; one baseline; one operating configuration.
VRLM prevents that measurement from silently becoming evidence of:
18% enterprise-wide permanent cost reduction.
Uncertainty Limitation
Recognition can remain legitimate even where uncertainty exists.
VRLM therefore does not require uncertainty to eliminate recognition.

Instead, it requires material uncertainty to constrain the interpretation of recognition where necessary.
For example:
Strategic Value → Recognized
may coexist with:
Magnitude uncertain
or:
Future persistence uncertain.
This preserves useful recognition without manufacturing false certainty.
Transfer Limitation
A recognition determination may not automatically transfer when value moves between:
entities; beneficiaries; systems; organizations; environments; jurisdictions; technologies; ownership structures; operating contexts.
Transfer of the underlying object does not necessarily transfer the same recognition relationship.
Therefore:
Value Transfer ≠ Recognition Transfer
A new recognition context may require reassessment.
Institutional Limitation
One institution's recognition does not automatically bind another institution.
For example:
Company Recognition
does not automatically establish:
Bank Recognition
which does not automatically establish:
Accounting Recognition
which does not automatically establish:
Tax Recognition
which does not automatically establish:
Regulatory Recognition.
These systems may rely upon different criteria and purposes.
VRLM preserves those institutional boundaries.
Recognition Limitation ≠ Legal Restriction
VRLM uses the term limitation methodologically.
A Value Recognition Limitation is not automatically:
a legal prohibition; regulatory restriction; contractual restriction; ownership restriction; tax limitation.

It defines the boundary of the VFM® recognition determination.
External legal consequences must be established through the relevant system.
Recognition Limitation ≠ Value Limitation
VRLM limits the meaning of the recognition determination, not necessarily the underlying value.
This distinction is fundamental.
For example:
Recognition limited to operational use
does not establish:
the value itself exists only operationally.
Other recognition contexts may later identify additional dimensions of the same value.
Therefore:
Recognition Boundary ≠ Value Boundary
Unsupported Recognition Expansion
VRLM identifies Unsupported Recognition Expansion where recognition is extended beyond its governed basis.
Examples include:
Operational Value Recognized → presented as Financial Value Established
Strategic Capability Recognized → presented as Market Price Established
Cost Avoidance Recognized → presented as Revenue Generated
Public Value Recognized → presented as Taxable Value Established
Technological Value Recognized → presented as Collateral Eligibility Established
Future Capability Recognized → presented as Realized Economic Benefit
These transformations may eventually be legitimate.
But they require their own governed basis.
They cannot be assumed.
Recognition Boundary Statement
VRLM may produce an explicit Recognition Boundary Statement.
A minimum structure may identify:
Recognized Value → Recognition Context → Recognized Dimension → Beneficiary → Purpose → Applicable Conditions

→ Material Dependencies → Temporal Applicability → Exclusions → Unsupported Interpretations
This makes the recognition determination portable without detaching it from its legitimate boundary.
Recognition Limitation States
VRLM may classify recognition limitations using states such as:
1. Unrestricted Within Defined Context
No additional material limitation has been identified beyond the established recognition context.
2. Conditionally Limited
Recognition remains legitimate only while specified conditions remain satisfied.
3. Scope-Limited
Recognition applies only to a defined object, capability, value dimension, beneficiary, purpose, or operational space.
4. Temporally Limited
Recognition applies only within a defined period or until a defined trigger occurs.
5. Dependency-Limited
Recognition materially depends upon another identified capability, resource, relationship, system, or condition.
6. Uncertainty-Limited
Recognition remains legitimate, but material uncertainty constrains its interpretation or downstream use.
7. Transfer-Limited
Recognition cannot automatically be transferred to another context, entity, beneficiary, system, or jurisdiction.
Multiple limitation states may apply simultaneously.
Limitation Combination
A recognition determination may carry several limitations at once.
For example:
Recognized Strategic Value
may be:
Scope-Limited + Dependency-Limited + Temporally Limited + Transfer-Limited
This is not a contradiction.

It is a more precise representation of the recognition relationship.
Limitation Persistence Principle
Material recognition limitations must remain attached to the recognition determination when it is:
recorded; transferred; aggregated; reported; analyzed; reused; exported; consumed by AI; used in another decision process; supplied to another organization.
A limitation that disappears when the recognition result moves downstream no longer functions as a governance control.
Therefore:
Recognition + Detached Limitation = Distorted Recognition
Machine-Readable Recognition Limitation
A machine-readable VRLM implementation may represent:
Recognition Determination ID → Value ID → Recognition Context ID → Beneficiary Reference → Recognized Dimension → Purpose → Limitation Type → Limitation Condition → Dependency Reference → Temporal Boundary → Excluded Interpretation → Transfer Condition → Review Trigger → VRRM Record Interface
This enables AI and automated systems to consume not merely:
“Recognized = Yes”
but:
“Recognized = Yes, within these explicit boundaries.”
Recognition Limitation Review
A limitation may require review when:
the recognition context changes; the beneficiary changes; the purpose changes; a dependency disappears; a dependency becomes stronger; uncertainty decreases; uncertainty increases; new evidence becomes available; operating conditions change;
technology changes; a temporal boundary expires; the underlying value changes.
A review may:

preserve the limitation; narrow it; expand legitimate recognition; remove it; add new limitations; trigger a new recognition determination.
Boundary with VRCM
VRCM — Value Recognition Criteria Module determines the criteria required for recognition.
VRLM does not modify those criteria after determination.
It governs the boundaries attached to the resulting recognition.
Boundary with VRBM
VRBM — Value Recognition Basis Module establishes the basis supporting recognition.
VRLM may use limitations identified in that basis but does not recreate the recognition basis.
Boundary with VRDM
VRDM — Value Recognition Determination Module determines:
whether and how the value is recognized.
VRLM determines:
where that recognition applies, what constrains it, and where its legitimate interpretation ends.
Therefore:
Recognition Determination ≠ Recognition Boundary
Boundary with VRRM
VRLM produces the limitations that must accompany the recognition determination.
VRRM — Value Recognition Record Module preserves the complete recognition record.
Therefore:
Recognition Limitation → Recognition Record Input
The limitation must not disappear when the recognition is recorded.
Boundary with Value State Standard
VRLM does not determine the broader lifecycle state of the underlying value.
A recognition limitation may change without the underlying value state changing.

Likewise, the value may later develop, degrade, become nullified, or be restored without that lifecycle transition being governed by VRLM.
Boundary with VALIDOS®
VRLM does not determine whether evidence or a recognition claim has been formally validated.
Where validation of a recognition claim is required, VALIDOS® may govern that validation process.
VRLM governs the legitimate boundary of the recognition determination itself.
Boundary with AGA™
VRLM does not determine who is accountable for making, accepting, communicating, or relying upon a recognition determination.
Where accountability is required, AGA™ may govern those relationships.
VRLM governs what the recognition means and where that meaning stops.
Minimum Implementation Framework
A minimum VRLM implementation should establish:
1. Recognition Determination Input
Receive the recognition determination from VRDM.
2. Context Boundary
Identify the recognition context within which the determination applies.
3. Beneficiary and Purpose Boundary
Identify who benefits and for what recognition purpose.
4. Scope Boundary
Define applicable value dimensions, objects, capabilities, systems, configurations, or operating spaces.
5. Condition and Dependency Assessment
Identify conditions and dependencies necessary for recognition to remain legitimate.
6. Temporal Boundary
Determine temporal applicability and relevant expiration or review triggers.
7. Uncertainty and Measurement Limits

Preserve material uncertainty and measurement limitations affecting interpretation.
8. Excluded Interpretations
Identify conclusions that the recognition determination does not establish.
9. Transfer Conditions
Determine whether and how recognition may legitimately transfer into another context.
10. Recognition Limitation Record
Create the governed limitation package for VRRM.
Governance Outputs
VRLM may produce:
Value Recognition Boundary Statement Value Recognition Limitation Record Recognition Context Limitation Recognition Beneficiary Limitation Recognition Purpose Limitation Recognition Scope Limitation Recognition Dimension Limitation Recognition Dependency Record Recognition Temporal Limitation Recognition Uncertainty Limitation Recognition Transfer Limitation Recognition Exclusion Statement Unsupported Recognition Expansion Record Recognition Review Trigger Bounded Recognition Object
These outputs provide the governed input for VRRM — Value Recognition Record Module.
Use Case 1 — Banking: Preventing Strategic
Value from Becoming Unsupported Collateral
Value
A bank evaluates a technology company.
VRDM determines that the company's proprietary optimization platform has:
Recognized Operational Value
and:
Recognized Strategic Value.
The recognition basis includes measurable productivity improvement, recurring cost avoidance, deployment across multiple facilities, and dependence of critical operations upon the platform.

Without VRLM, that determination could later be simplified into:
“The platform is recognized as valuable.”
and subsequently interpreted as:
“The platform therefore has established collateral value.”
VRLM prevents that jump.
It may establish:
Recognition Context: enterprise assessment Recognized Dimensions: operational and strategic value Beneficiary: operating company Purpose: enterprise capability assessment Limitation: collateral eligibility not determined Limitation: market price not established Limitation: accounting recognition not established Dependency: continued operational integration and access to required data
The bank can therefore use the recognition legitimately without confusing:
recognized enterprise value
with:
bankable collateral value.
This allows broader forms of value to enter banking analysis while preserving the boundaries necessary for financial discipline.
Use Case 2 — Space Mission: Recognized
Resource Value Without False Universalization
A space organization recognizes substantial value from a mission-optimization capability.
VRDM determines:
Mission Resource Efficiency Value → Recognized
because the capability reduces engineering hours, simulation workload, physical testing, mission preparation time, and projected resource consumption.
VRLM then establishes that the recognition applies only to:

defined mission architecture → specified mission configuration → governed comparison baseline → defined simulation and engineering environment → specified resource categories → current mission-planning period
It also records:
fuel reduction is configuration-dependent
engineering-hour savings are baseline-dependent
future missions require reassessment
avoided resource consumption does not automatically constitute financial revenue
The organization therefore preserves the genuine value of resource reduction without transforming it into claims the recognition basis never established.
This is particularly important for mission, scientific, infrastructure, and public-sector environments where significant value may exist outside conventional revenue-based measurement.
Enterprise Application
VRLM enables organizations to use broader concepts of value without allowing those concepts to become methodologically uncontrolled.
This is particularly important for VFM® because the architecture may recognize forms of value that conventional systems treat separately or fail to represent adequately.
These may include:
avoided cost; preserved capability; resource efficiency; strategic optionality; technological capability; resilience; unused productive capacity; public benefit; future-use capability; infrastructure value; knowledge value.
The broader the recognition system becomes, the more important recognition boundaries become.
VRLM provides that control.
It allows organizations to say:

“Yes, this value is recognized.”
while simultaneously stating:
“This is exactly what that recognition means—and exactly what it does not mean.”
Foundational Principles
Recognition is not unlimited recognition.
A limitation does not negate legitimate recognition.
Bounded recognition may be stronger than ambiguous recognition.
Recognition for one beneficiary does not automatically establish recognition for another.
Recognition for one purpose does not automatically authorize another use.
Recognition of one value dimension does not establish recognition of every value dimension.
Recognition boundary is not value boundary.
Value transfer does not automatically transfer recognition.
Institutional recognition does not automatically create universal recognition.
Operational recognition does not automatically create accounting, tax, market, legal, or collateral recognition.
Material recognition limitations must travel with the recognition determination.
A recognition determination becomes distorted when its limitations are removed from it.
Canonical Closing Statement

Value Recognition Limitation Module establishes the boundary-control layer of the Value Recognition Standard by governing the contextual, beneficiary, purpose, dimensional, operational, temporal, dependency, uncertainty, measurement, transfer, institutional, and interpretive limitations attached to a Value Recognition Determination. Through explicit Recognition Boundary Statements, limitation states, dependency controls, excluded interpretations, temporal applicability, transfer conditions, review triggers, and downstream limitation persistence, VRLM prevents legitimate recognition within one governed context from expanding silently into unsupported financial, accounting, market, legal, tax, collateral, institutional, or universal claims. By separating
the boundary of recognition from the existence and boundary of value itself, VRLM enables VFM® to recognize broad and unconventional forms of value while preserving methodological precision over exactly what each recognition determination establishes, where it applies, under what conditions it remains legitimate, and where its meaning must stop.

Canonical Definition
Value Recognition Record Module (VRRM) is the fifth Core Module of the Value Recognition Standard (VRS) within VFM® — Value Flow Mechanisms Architecture.
VRRM governs the creation, structure, preservation, linkage, versioning, updating, traceability, and machine-readable representation of the governed Value Recognition Record produced through the Value Recognition Standard.
Its purpose is to ensure that a recognition outcome does not survive merely as an isolated statement such as:
“This value is recognized.”

Instead, the recognition must remain connected to the context, criteria, basis, determination, limitations, conditions, beneficiary, purpose, temporal applicability, and other material information that gives the recognition its legitimate meaning.
VRRM therefore transforms the completed recognition process into a persistent governed record capable of supporting downstream value governance.
Its governing relationship is:
Recognition Criteria + Recognition Basis + Recognition Determination + Recognition Limitations → Governed Value Recognition Record
Architectural Position
VRRM operates within the fourth governed space of the VFM® lifecycle:
Value Context → Value Origin → Value Emergence → Value Recognition → Value State → Value Change → Value Development / Value Degradation → Value Nullification → Value Restoration / Value Extinction
It is the final module of the Value Recognition Standard.
VRRM receives the completed recognition basis from the preceding modules and creates the governed recognition record required for transition into the next lifecycle space.
Internal Module Flow
VRCM — Value Recognition Criteria → VRBM — Value Recognition Basis → VRDM — Value Recognition Determination → VRLM — Value Recognition Limitation → VRRM — Value Recognition Record
The internal logic is:
What qualifies for recognition → what supports recognition → what recognition outcome follows → where that recognition applies and stops → how the complete recognition is persistently represented

The output is:
Governed Value Recognition Record
Operational Space
VRRM governs:
recognition record creation; value-reference linkage; context preservation; beneficiary linkage; purpose preservation; criteria linkage; recognition-basis linkage; determination preservation; limitation preservation; condition preservation; uncertainty preservation; temporal applicability; recognition-state recording; record versioning; change history; supersession relationships; review status; record consistency; machine readability; downstream traceability; recognition record retrieval.
The purpose is not simply documentation.
It is governance continuity.
Recognition Record Principle
A recognition determination that becomes detached from the basis that produced it becomes methodologically weaker downstream.
VRRM therefore establishes:
Recognition Outcome Alone ≠ Governed Recognition Record
A governed record must preserve enough information to reconstruct:
what value was recognized, why it was recognized, for whom, for what purpose, within what context, under what criteria, on what basis, subject to what limitations, and during what applicable period.
Minimum Recognition Record Structure
A Value Recognition Record should contain or reference, where materially relevant:

Value Reference → Value Context → Value Object Reference → Beneficiary → Recognition Purpose → Recognition Criteria → Recognition Basis → Recognition Determination → Recognition State → Recognition Conditions → Recognition Limitations → Material Dependencies → Uncertainty → Temporal Applicability → Review Triggers → Record Version → Record Status
This creates a complete recognition object rather than an isolated recognition label.
Record ≠ Recognition Determination
VRDM produces the recognition determination.
VRRM preserves the determination together with the governed structure necessary to interpret it.
Therefore:
Determination ≠ Record
For example:
“Operational Value Recognized”
is a determination.
A governed record may establish:
Value: Process Optimization Capability Beneficiary: Manufacturing Operator Recognition Context: Operational Efficiency Recognition Purpose: Internal Resource Allocation Recognition State: Recognized Basis: Demonstrated production-time and energy reduction Limitation: Applies to Production Configuration C4 Temporal Applicability: Current operating configuration Review Trigger: Material process or configuration change
The second representation can travel downstream without losing its meaning.
Record Completeness
VRRM does not require every recognition record to contain every possible field.
Record completeness is contextual.
The governing requirement is:

the record must preserve the material information necessary to understand and legitimately use the recognition outcome.
A low-consequence internal recognition may require a simpler record.
A recognition used in banking, infrastructure, public finance, investment, AI, critical systems, or major resource allocation may require substantially greater detail.
Context Preservation
The Value Context established through VCXS — Value Context Standard must remain linked to the recognition record.
This prevents:
Recognition in Context A
from becoming:
Recognition in Every Context
when the record moves between systems.
The recognition record must therefore preserve enough contextual information to identify the legitimate recognition environment.
Beneficiary Preservation
Where recognition depends upon a beneficiary, that relationship must remain visible.
For example:
Value Recognized for Manufacturer
must not silently become:
Value Recognized for Customer
or:
Value Recognized for Government
unless the relevant recognition basis supports that conclusion.
VRRM therefore preserves the beneficiary relationship as part of recognition identity.
Criteria Preservation
The recognition record must identify or reference the criteria under which recognition occurred.
This allows downstream users to understand:
what requirements were actually satisfied.
Where criteria later change, the historical recognition record should not be silently rewritten as though the new criteria had always applied.
Instead:

Recognition Criteria Version 1 → Recognition Record Version 1
may later become:
Recognition Criteria Version 2 → New Recognition Assessment → Recognition Record Version 2
This preserves methodological history.
Recognition Basis Preservation
VRRM must preserve or reference the basis upon which the recognition determination was made.
This may include:
measurements; observations; calculations; operational results; resource effects; capability demonstrations; documented relationships; comparisons; analytical outputs; governed evidence; other relevant recognition basis.
The record need not duplicate every underlying evidence object.
It must preserve sufficient linkage to reconstruct the recognition basis.
Determination Preservation
The recognition determination must remain explicit.
The record should not force downstream systems to infer whether value was:
recognized; conditionally recognized; partially recognized; not recognized; indeterminate; recognition suspended.
The recognition state must remain machine-readable where implementation permits.
Limitation Preservation
The outputs of VRLM — Value Recognition Limitation Module are part of the recognition record.
They are not optional annotations.
If the determination states:
Strategic Value → Recognized
while VRLM establishes:
Collateral Value → Not Determined
the record must not preserve the first statement while dropping the second.
Therefore:
Recognition Record − Material Limitation = Distorted Recognition Record

Condition Preservation
Where recognition is conditional, the conditions must remain attached to the record.
For example:
Conditionally Recognized while Dataset D remains available and Production Configuration C remains unchanged.
If those conditions are removed from the record, downstream users may interpret conditional recognition as unconditional recognition.
VRRM prevents that loss of meaning.
Temporal Applicability
Recognition records must support time.
A record may identify:
determination date; effective date; applicable period; review date; expiration condition; material-change trigger; supersession date; suspension date.
This enables organizations to distinguish:
currently applicable recognition
from:
historical recognition.
Historical Recognition Principle
A recognition record should generally preserve historical determinations rather than erase them when recognition changes.
For example:
T1 — Not Recognized → T2 — Conditionally Recognized → T3 — Recognized → T4 — Recognition Suspended
This history can reveal how institutional understanding of value evolved.
It also prevents current recognition states from rewriting the historical record.
Versioning Principle
Material changes to a recognition record should create an identifiable new version or state transition.
Material changes may include:

recognition-context change; beneficiary change; criteria change; recognition-basis change; determination change; limitation change; dependency change; temporal applicability change; newly identified uncertainty; material value change.
VRRM should preserve the relationship between previous and current records.
Supersession
A new recognition record may supersede an earlier record.
Supersession does not mean the earlier record never existed.
VRRM should distinguish:
Current Record
from:
Superseded Record
and preserve the relationship between them.
This enables longitudinal value analysis.
Recognition Record Status
A minimum record-status model may include:
1. Active
The recognition record is currently applicable.
2. Conditional
The record remains applicable only while defined conditions remain satisfied.
3. Under Review
Material change or new information requires reassessment.
4. Suspended
The recognition record should not currently support reliance pending resolution.
5. Superseded
A newer governed recognition record has replaced it.
6. Historical
The record is retained for traceability but no longer represents the current recognition state.
These are record states, not value states.
Record State ≠ Value State
VRRM maintains a critical distinction:
Recognition Record State ≠ Value State
A recognition record may become:
Superseded
while the underlying value continues to exist.
A record may become:
Historical
while the value develops.
A record may remain:
Active

while the value later begins to degrade, triggering downstream lifecycle governance.
The record describes the governed recognition relationship.
It does not own the entire lifecycle state of value.
Recognition Record Update Trigger
A recognition record may require review or update when:
the underlying value materially changes; the value context changes; the beneficiary changes; the recognition purpose changes; recognition criteria change; new basis becomes available; existing basis becomes unreliable; a recognition condition fails; a limitation changes; a dependency disappears; uncertainty materially changes; a temporal boundary expires; downstream value-state governance identifies a material transition.
The trigger does not predetermine the new recognition outcome.
It requires reassessment.
Recognition Record Integrity
VRRM requires the logical integrity of the recognition record to be preserved.
This includes consistency between:
Value Reference Context Criteria Basis Determination Limitations Temporal State
For example, a record should not simultaneously state:
Recognition State: Unconditional Recognition
and:
Recognition Limitation: Valid only if Condition X remains satisfied
without resolving that inconsistency.
General integrity governance may interface with INTEGROS®.
VRRM governs the recognition-specific structural relationship.
Traceability
A recognition record should support traceability backward and forward.
Backward traceability may include:

Recognition Record → Recognition Determination → Recognition Basis → Recognition Criteria → Value Context → Value Emergence Record → Value Origin
Forward traceability may include:
Recognition Record → Value State → Value Change → Value Development / Degradation → Value Nullification → Value Restoration / Extinction
This makes the recognition record an important lifecycle junction inside VFM®.
Recognition Record as Lifecycle Interface
VRRM is not merely the end of Value Recognition.
It is the transition object between:
Value Recognition
and:
Value State Governance.
The recognition record provides the downstream architecture with a governed statement of:
what value has been recognized and under what recognition conditions.
This allows the subsequent lifecycle to operate without reconstructing recognition from the beginning.
Machine-Readable Recognition Record
A machine-readable implementation may represent:
Value ID → Value Context ID → Value Object Reference → Origin Reference → Emergence Reference → Beneficiary Reference → Recognition Purpose ID → Recognition Criteria Set ID → Recognition Basis References → Recognition Determination State → Recognition Limitations → Recognition Conditions → Dependencies → Uncertainty References → Temporal Applicability → Review Triggers → Record Version → Record Status → Superseded Record Reference → Downstream Value-State Interface

This enables VFM® recognition records to be consumed by AI, enterprise software, public systems, analytical engines, financial systems, digital infrastructure, and other machine-readable environments.
Aggregation Principle
Organizations may need to aggregate many recognized values.
VRRM allows recognition records to be aggregated while preserving their individual identity and limitations.
For example:
Value Record A + Value Record B + Value Record C
may contribute to an enterprise-level value view.
But aggregation must not erase:
different beneficiaries; different recognition contexts; different criteria; different limitations; different temporal periods; different recognition states.
Therefore:
Value Record Aggregation ≠ Value Record Homogenization
Interoperability
A recognition record may need to move between systems.
For example:
Operational System → Management System → Investment Analysis → Banking Analysis → Government Analysis
VRRM requires the recognition meaning to remain attached to the record during transfer.
A receiving system may apply a new recognition context.
But it must not silently reinterpret the original recognition as though it had been issued under the receiving system's criteria.
Record Transfer ≠ Recognition Transfer
The recognition record can be transferred technically.
That does not mean the recognition determination automatically transfers institutionally or contextually.
Therefore:
Record Transfer ≠ Recognition Transfer

A bank may receive a company's recognition record without automatically adopting the company's recognition determination.
A government may receive an enterprise recognition record without automatically treating the value as recognized public value.
VRRM preserves the original record so a new system can perform its own governed recognition where required.
Boundary with VRCM
VRCM establishes the recognition criteria.
VRRM records or references those criteria.
It does not redefine them.
Boundary with VRBM
VRBM establishes the recognition basis.
VRRM preserves the linkage to that basis.
It does not recreate the basis.
Boundary with VRDM
VRDM issues the recognition determination.
VRRM preserves the determination and its governed context.
Therefore:
Determination → Record
not:
Record → Determination
Boundary with VRLM
VRLM establishes the boundaries and limitations attached to recognition.
VRRM ensures those limitations remain attached to the recognition record.
Therefore:
Recognition + Limitation → Complete Recognition Record
Boundary with Value State Standard
The subsequent Value State Standard (VSS) governs the state of recognized value within the next VFM® lifecycle space.
VRRM provides the recognition record that enters that process.
The boundary is:
VRS: Is existing value recognized within the defined context?
VRRM: What is the persistent governed record of that recognition?
VSS: What is the current governed state of that value?
Boundary with INTEGROS®

VRRM governs recognition-specific record structure and continuity.
INTEGROS® may govern broader integrity requirements affecting the record.
VRRM does not become a universal information-integrity architecture.
Boundary with ADIT®
VRRM creates and maintains the recognition record structure.
ADIT® may govern auditability, evidence preservation, verification, and reconstruction where applicable.
Therefore:
Recognition Record Governance ≠ Audit Governance
Minimum Implementation Framework
A minimum VRRM implementation should establish:
1. Recognition Record Identity
Create a uniquely identifiable recognition record.
2. Value and Context Linkage
Link the record to the governed value, value object, beneficiary, purpose, and context.
3. Criteria Linkage
Identify the recognition criteria applied.
4. Basis Linkage
Identify the recognition basis supporting the determination.
5. Determination Recording
Record the recognition determination and recognition state.
6. Limitation and Condition Recording
Preserve all material recognition limitations, conditions, dependencies, and uncertainty.
7. Temporal Definition
Define applicable dates, periods, expiration conditions, and review triggers.
8. Version and Status Control
Maintain record version, current status, and supersession relationships.
9. Traceability
Maintain backward traceability to recognition inputs and forward linkage into downstream value governance.
10. Machine-Readable Representation

Represent the record in a structure capable of controlled downstream use where required.
Governance Outputs
VRRM may produce:
Governed Value Recognition Record Recognition Record Identity Recognition Context Record Recognition Beneficiary Link Recognition Criteria Reference Recognition Basis Reference Recognition Determination Record Recognition Limitation Record Recognition Condition Record Recognition Dependency Record Recognition Temporal Applicability Record Recognition Review Trigger Recognition Version History Recognition Supersession Record Recognition Record Status Machine-Readable Recognition Object Value State Interface Record
These outputs complete the Value Recognition Standard and provide the governed input into the next VFM® lifecycle space.
Use Case 1 — Banking: Portable Value
Recognition Without Losing Meaning
A company has identified and recognized substantial operational value generated by a proprietary automation capability.
The recognition process establishes:
Value: Operational Efficiency Value Beneficiary: Manufacturing Company Recognition Purpose: Internal strategic assessment Basis: verified reductions in labor hours, energy use, process time, and production loss Recognition State: Recognized Limitation: recognition does not establish collateral eligibility, market price, accounting recognition, or tax treatment.
The company later provides information about this capability to a bank.
Without VRRM, the bank might receive only:

“The company recognizes significant value in its automation platform.”
That statement carries little methodological structure.
With VRRM, the bank receives a governed recognition record preserving the value context, criteria, basis, determination, limitations, temporal applicability, and dependencies.
The bank can then use that record as an input into its own analysis without being forced either to:
accept the company's recognition universally
or:
discard the underlying value information completely.
VRRM therefore creates a portable value-recognition object while preserving the boundary between:
information transfer
and:
institutional recognition transfer.
Use Case 2 — Space Mission: Preserving the
History of Resource Value
A space organization recognizes resource-efficiency value created by a mission optimization capability.
The initial record establishes:
Mission Resource Efficiency Value → Conditionally Recognized
based on reduced engineering hours, computational workload, testing requirements, fuel consumption, and mission preparation time.
The record preserves:
Mission Configuration M4 Simulation Baseline B7 Engineering Period T1
Defined Resource Categories Recognition Conditions Measurement Limitations Review Trigger: Mission Architecture Change
Six months later, the mission architecture changes.
The organization does not overwrite the original record.
VRRM preserves:
Recognition Record V1 — Historical
and creates:
Recognition Record V2 — Under Review

Following reassessment:
Recognition Record V3 — Active
The organization can now reconstruct how recognized resource value evolved as the mission changed.
This creates something more useful than a single final number:
a governed history of how value was recognized through time.
Enterprise Application
VRRM provides the persistent information structure required to make VFM® operational at organizational scale.
Without governed records, value governance would repeatedly collapse into disconnected assessments, spreadsheets, reports, opinions, and isolated decisions.
VRRM allows recognized value to become a durable governance object capable of being:
stored; retrieved; compared; reviewed; transferred; aggregated; versioned; analyzed; consumed by AI; linked to downstream value states; reassessed after material change.
This is particularly important where organizations need to govern thousands or millions of value relationships across assets, capabilities, processes, technologies, infrastructure, resources, investments, public systems, or digital environments.
The Module therefore establishes the information continuity necessary for VFM® to operate not merely as an analytical framework but as a machine-readable value lifecycle architecture.
Foundational Principles
Recognition outcome alone is not a governed recognition record.
Recognition must remain connected to the context that gives it meaning.
Recognition criteria and basis must remain traceable.

Recognition limitations are part of the recognition record.
Conditional recognition must remain conditional when recorded.
Historical recognition should not be silently rewritten by current recognition.
Record state is not value state.
Record transfer is not recognition transfer.
Aggregation must not erase individual recognition contexts and limitations.
A recognition record must remain interpretable after leaving the system that created it.
Machine-readable recognition must preserve meaning, not merely labels.
A governed recognition record creates continuity between recognition and the downstream value lifecycle.
Canonical Closing Statement

Value Recognition Record Module establishes the persistence and continuity layer of the Value Recognition Standard by transforming recognition criteria, recognition basis, recognition determination, limitations, conditions, dependencies, uncertainty, temporal applicability, and contextual relationships into a structured, traceable, version-controlled, transferable, and machine-readable Governed Value Recognition Record. Through governance of record identity, completeness, contextual preservation, beneficiary relationships, criteria and basis linkage, recognition states, limitation persistence, temporal applicability, historical continuity, supersession, aggregation, interoperability, review triggers, and downstream traceability, VRRM prevents recognized value from becoming detached from the methodological basis that gives recognition its legitimate meaning. By separating record persistence from recognition determination, value state, institutional acceptance, integrity governance, and audit governance, VRRM completes the Value Recognition Standard and creates the governed lifecycle interface through which recognized value can proceed into Value State Governance without losing its origin, context, basis, boundaries, conditions, or recognition history.
