OOF™ The Event Determination Decision Module (EDDM) governs how the results of
The Event Determination Decision Module (EDDM) governs how the results of
OOF™ Origin Open Foundation™
Independent Methodological Authority
Architecture Ecosystem: Structured Reality Standards™
Architecture Family: TREGA™ — Tax-Relevant Event Governance Architecture™
Parent Standard: TREDS — Tax-Relevant Event Determination Standard
Module: EDDM — Event Determination Decision Module
Operational Layer: Event Determination Decision Governance Layer
Category: Governance & Enforcement
Subcategory: Tax-Relevant Event Governance
Type: Core Module
Governed Space: Event Determination Decision
Origin ID: TREGA-TREDS-EDDM-003
Version: 1.0
Status: Canonical · Open Standard
Effective Date: 2 September 2026
AI-Readable: Yes
Authority: OOF®
Protection: MIP® — Methodological Intellectual Property
Canonical Language: UCL — Universal Canonical Language
Canonical Definition
The Event Determination Decision Module (EDDM) governs how the results of Determination Readiness and Determination Conditions governance are converted into a formal Tax-Relevant Event Determination Decision.
EDDM determines the governed Event status that follows from the available readiness, condition, qualification, coherence, uncertainty, and conflict information at the point of decision.
Its principal transition is:
Governed Determination Condition State
↓
Determination Decision Governance
↓
Governed Event Determination Decision

EDDM does not determine legal taxability.
It does not determine tax jurisdiction, taxpayer status, taxable value, Tax Base, Tax Rate, legal tax point, Tax Liability, exemption, deduction, filing obligation, collection, enforcement, or any other jurisdiction-specific tax consequence.
Its foundational distinction is:
Event Determination Decision ≠ Tax Decision.
Operational Role
EDDM is the formal decision layer of TREDS.
EDRDM determines whether the Event is ready for formal Determination.
EDCM determines whether the applicable Determination Conditions are satisfied.
EDDM then answers:
What formal TREGA™ Determination state should this Event receive?
The Decision may be: Positive; Conditional; Deferred; Rejected; Ambiguous; Conflicted; or otherwise qualified.
EDDM transforms prior governance into an explicit and traceable Determination outcome.
Internal Module Flow
TREDS operates through:
EDRDM — Event Determination Readiness
↓
EDCM — Event Determination Conditions
↓
EDDM — Event Determination Decision
↓
EDUM — Event Determination Uncertainty
↓
EDREM — Event Determination Reconsideration
↓
Determined Tax-Relevant Event
EDDM is the third Core Module.
Its output is passed to EDUM for Determination-level uncertainty governance where required.
Operational Transition
The canonical transition is:
Governed Determination Condition State + Readiness State + Relevant Qualifications
↓
Decision Evaluation
↓
Governed Event Determination Decision
Possible outputs include:

Tax-Relevant Event Determined
Conditionally Determined
Determination Deferred
Determination Rejected
Determination Ambiguous
Determination Conflicted
Determination Escalation Required
Determination Reconsideration Flagged
The Decision shall always be explicit.
Operational Space
EDDM governs: decision initiation; decision basis; decision eligibility; decision state selection; positive determination; conditional determination; deferred determination; rejected determination; ambiguous determination; conflicted determination; decision qualification; decision rationale; decision consistency; decision provenance; decision traceability; decision authority reference; decision timing; decision finalization; decision handoff; and decision-level governance control.
Operational Scope
EDDM may govern Event Determination Decisions arising from: commerce; marketplaces; banking; payments; accounting; ERP; logistics; supply chains; digital platforms; digital assets; blockchain systems; smart contracts; AI agents; autonomous systems; industrial systems; energy systems; distributed infrastructure; cross-border operations; machine-to-machine activity; and future machine economies.
The decision logic remains technology-neutral and jurisdiction-neutral.
Decision Object
The Decision Object is the governed Event represented through: the EDRDM Readiness State; the EDCM Condition State; relevant upstream governance references; material qualifications; uncertainty indicators; and conflict indicators.

EDDM decides the TREGA™ status of this governed Event.
It does not decide the legal tax status.
Decision Initiation
Decision governance begins when EDCM establishes a sufficiently governed Determination Condition State.
EDDM shall not begin a formal Decision process where required condition governance remains absent.
Decision Initiation ≠ Positive Determination.
Decision Eligibility
An Event is decision-eligible where the relevant Readiness and Condition governance provides enough basis for EDDM to issue a formal status.
Decision eligibility does not require that the result will be positive.
A Decision may still be: Deferred; Rejected; Conflicted; or Conditional.
Decision Eligible ≠ Determination Positive.
Decision Basis
Every Determination Decision shall be linked to its governance basis.
The Decision basis may include: Readiness State; Condition State; material qualifications; unresolved issues; conflict state; uncertainty state; upstream referrals; governance traceability.
A Decision without a reconstructable basis shall not qualify as a governed Decision.
Decision Output Without Decision Basis ≠ Governed Decision.
Positive Determination
A Positive Determination means that the Event is sufficiently governed to be formally recognized within TREGA™ as a Tax-Relevant Event.
It means:
The Event is eligible for downstream jurisdiction-specific taxation analysis.
It does not mean:
Tax is legally due.
Therefore:
Positive Event Determination ≠ Positive Tax Determination.

Conditional Determination
A Conditional Determination may be issued where the Event is sufficiently governed for controlled downstream use but one or more bounded qualifications remain.
These qualifications shall be explicit.
Conditional Determination ≠ Unqualified Determination.
The downstream system shall be able to identify the conditions attached to the Decision.
Deferred Determination
A Deferred Determination means that the Event cannot yet receive a final Determination state because materially necessary governance remains unresolved.
Deferral may result from: unresolved condition; material uncertainty; material conflict; unstable Event structure; unresolved upstream referral; or pending structural reconsideration.
Deferred Determination ≠ Rejected Determination.
Rejected Determination
A Rejected Determination means that the governed Event structure does not support establishment of a Tax-Relevant Event under TREGA™ at that time.
Rejection may occur where the apparent Event fails a foundational governance requirement.
Examples may include: invalid Event Formation; non-establishable Event Boundary; duplicate technical artifact; purely technical operation incorrectly treated as an Event; or materially incoherent Event structure.
Rejected Determination ≠ Legal Non-Taxability.
Ambiguous Determination
A Determination may remain Ambiguous where more than one materially plausible Event interpretation remains and the available governance does not support a single stable Decision.

Ambiguity shall remain visible.
Ambiguity ≠ Permission to Choose the Convenient Decision.
Conflicted Determination
A Determination may be Conflicted where materially authoritative governance inputs support incompatible outcomes.
The Decision shall preserve the conflict rather than collapse it artificially.
Decision Conflict ≠ Decision Discretion without Governance Basis.
Decision Qualification
A Decision may contain a qualification.
Qualification may relate to: bounded uncertainty; incomplete geographic precision; limited participant certainty; partial Value Association; conditional Relationship structure; provisional source availability; or another materially relevant limitation.
The qualification shall not disappear when the Event moves downstream.
Decision Finality
EDDM may establish operational finality sufficient for downstream processing.
This does not mean absolute or legal finality.
A later correction or reconsideration may change the Decision.
Operational Decision Finality ≠ Legal Finality.
Decision Consistency
EDDM shall apply consistent decision logic across materially comparable Events.
Consistency does not require identical outcomes where Event circumstances differ.
Decision Consistency ≠ Mechanical Uniformity.
The governing principle is methodological consistency.
Decision Rationale
A formal Decision shall be accompanied by sufficient rationale to reconstruct why the Decision state was selected.

The rationale should identify: the Event under review; the Readiness State; the relevant Condition State; material satisfied conditions; material unsatisfied or qualified conditions; material uncertainty; material conflict; and the reason for the resulting Decision.
Decision Provenance
The Decision shall preserve provenance to the governance information from which it arose.
This may include references to: upstream Parent Standards; EDRDM readiness evaluation; EDCM condition evaluation; relevant system or governance-source identifiers; previous Decision states.
Decision Provenance ≠ Identity Provenance.
OBIDENITY® remains authoritative for broader identity and origin governance.
Decision Traceability
The Determination Decision shall remain reconstructable.
A reviewer should be able to identify: what was decided; why; on what governance basis; under which qualifications; with what uncertainty; and whether the Decision later changed.
EDDM owns Decision traceability.
ADIT® may govern broader evidential or audit requirements.
Decision Authority
The Decision process may be: automated; human; hybrid; delegated; rules-based; AI-assisted.
EDDM requires the Decision authority or process reference to remain identifiable.
It does not assign organizational accountability.
AGA™ remains authoritative for accountability governance.
Decision Timing
The time at which the Determination Decision was made should be captured separately from the Event Timing itself.
Decision Time ≠ Event Time.
and:

Decision Time ≠ Legal Tax Point.
Decision Sequence
Where repeated Decision processes occur, Decision sequence may be preserved.
For example:
Initial Decision
↓
Qualification
↓
Correction
↓
Reconsideration
This does not alter the underlying Event Sequence governed by TRERLS.
Decision Sequence ≠ Event Sequence.
Positive Decision Threshold
A Positive Determination should require that: the Event is sufficiently ready; materially required conditions are sufficiently satisfied; remaining qualifications are compatible with downstream use; no unresolved issue fundamentally undermines Event Identity or structure; and the Decision basis is reconstructable.
The threshold is methodological sufficiency.
It is not a jurisdiction-specific tax threshold.
Conditional Decision Threshold
A Conditional Determination may be appropriate where: Event identity is stable; material Event structure is sufficient; remaining limitations are bounded; downstream interpretation remains possible; the qualification is explicit.
Conditional Determination shall not be used to hide a fundamentally unresolved Event.
Deferred Decision Threshold
Deferral is appropriate where material issues remain unresolved but the Event may become determinable later.
Deferral should preserve: reason; required follow-up; affected governance layer; and current Decision state.
Rejected Decision Threshold

Rejection should require a sufficiently governed basis showing that the apparent Event does not qualify as a governed Tax-Relevant Event.
Rejection shall not be based merely on: low tax value; no expected Tax Liability; jurisdictional exemption; or reporting convenience.
Low Tax Relevance under Law ≠ TREGA™ Rejection Criterion.
Decision and Readiness
EDDM consumes the Readiness State.
It does not reperform readiness governance.
Decision ≠ Readiness Assessment.
If Readiness becomes invalid, the matter should be referred back to EDRDM.
Decision and Conditions
EDDM consumes the Condition State.
It does not reperform condition governance.
Decision ≠ Condition Evaluation.
If the Condition basis materially changes, EDCM remains authoritative.
Decision and Uncertainty
EDDM may identify uncertainty affecting the Decision.
EDUM governs Determination-level uncertainty in greater detail.
Therefore:
Decision Uncertainty Recognition ≠ Full Uncertainty Governance.
Decision and Reconsideration
EDDM may flag that reconsideration is required.
EDREM owns the reconsideration process.
Decision Change ≠ Determination Reconsideration by default.
Decision and Event Recognition
TRERS decides whether an occurrence should enter Event governance.
EDDM decides the formal Determination state after the Event has passed through the necessary governance layers.
Recognition Decision ≠ Determination Decision.
Decision and Event Formation
EDDM cannot use a positive Decision to override defective Formation.

Positive Decision ≠ Formation Authority.
TREFS remains authoritative.
Decision and Event Boundary
EDDM cannot redefine Event Boundary.
Decision ≠ Boundary Redetermination.
TREBS remains authoritative.
Decision and Event Timing
EDDM cannot determine legal tax timing.
Event Determination Decision ≠ Legal Tax Point Determination.
TRETS remains authoritative for Event Timing.
Decision and Event Location
EDDM may rely on governed Location information.
It does not determine the taxing jurisdiction.
Positive Determination ≠ Tax Jurisdiction Determination.
Decision and Participation
EDDM may rely on governed Participant structure.
It does not determine who is legally the taxpayer.
Positive Determination ≠ Taxpayer Determination.
Decision and Value
EDDM may rely on governed Value Association.
It does not determine taxable amount.
Positive Determination ≠ Tax Base Determination.
Decision and Relationships
EDDM may rely on a Governed Event Relationship Structure.
It does not merge, split, group, sequence, or otherwise recreate relationships.
Decision ≠ Relationship Governance.
Decision after Merge
Where ERLMM has governed a Merge and the resulting Event has completed relevant upstream governance, EDDM may issue a Decision for the resulting Event.
The resulting Event shall not inherit the prior Decision automatically.
Merged Event ≠ Automatically Determined Event.
Decision after Split
Each resulting Event after a governed Split may require its own Determination Decision.

Split Event ≠ Automatically Determined Event.
Decision after Correction
Where an upstream correction materially changes the Event structure, the existing Decision may become invalid or require reconsideration.
EDDM may identify the Decision impact.
EDREM governs broader reconsideration.
Technical Record Decisions
A system may label a transaction as: taxable; non-taxable; completed; posted; settled; final; reconciled.
These labels do not constitute TREGA™ Determination Decisions.
System Status ≠ Governed Event Determination Decision.
Accounting Decisions
Accounting classification may inform Event governance but does not replace EDDM.
Accounting Classification ≠ Event Determination Decision.
Invoice Decisions
An invoice-status engine cannot determine by itself whether the underlying activity is a governed Tax-Relevant Event.
Invoice Status ≠ Event Determination Decision.
Payment Decisions
Payment completion does not establish Event Determination.
Payment Completion ≠ Event Determination Decision.
Blockchain Finality
Blockchain finality establishes technical ledger state.
It does not establish Tax-Relevant Event Determination.
Blockchain Finality ≠ Event Determination Decision.
Smart-Contract Completion
Smart-contract completion does not establish Determination.
Smart-Contract Completion ≠ Event Determination Decision.
AI Classification
An AI system may propose a Decision state.
That proposal remains subject to EDDM governance.
AI Classification ≠ Governed Determination Decision.

AI Confidence
Model confidence may support the Decision process.
It cannot substitute for the Decision itself.
Model Confidence ≠ Decision.
Autonomous Decisioning
EDDM supports autonomous Determination processes where governance requirements are satisfied.
Autonomy does not remove: Decision basis; Decision rationale; qualification; traceability; or authority reference.
Automated Decision ≠ Ungoverned Decision.
Cross-System Decision
The same governed Event may appear in multiple systems.
EDDM shall seek one governed Determination Decision for the governed Event rather than one Decision per technical record.
Multiple Records ≠ Multiple Determination Decisions by default.
Cross-Organization Decision
The Event may involve several organizations.
Different organizations may hold separate records or internal classifications.
EDDM governs the TREGA™ Event Decision, not organizational tax positions.
Multiple Organizational Views ≠ Multiple Event Realities.
Cross-Border Decision
A cross-border Event may receive a Positive Determination while Tax Jurisdiction remains unresolved downstream.
Cross-Border Positive Determination ≠ Jurisdiction Allocation.
Multi-Jurisdiction Decision Reuse
One governed Determination Decision may support multiple downstream jurisdictional evaluations.
The model is:
One Governed Event Determination Decision
↓
Multiple Jurisdictional Tax Evaluations
This is a core TREGA™ infrastructure function. Jurisdiction-Neutrality

EDDM shall preserve a jurisdiction-neutral Decision.
The Decision states:
This Event is sufficiently governed as Tax-Relevant.
It does not state:
This jurisdiction may tax it.
Jurisdiction-Neutral Determination ≠ Jurisdictional Tax Decision.
Decision and Taxability
This boundary is absolute.
Event Determination Decision ≠ Taxability Determination.
Taxability belongs to downstream law.
Decision and Tax Jurisdiction
Event Determination Decision ≠ Tax Jurisdiction Determination.
Decision and Taxpayer
Event Determination Decision ≠ Taxpayer Determination.
Decision and Tax Base
Event Determination Decision ≠ Tax Base Determination.
Decision and Tax Rate
Event Determination Decision ≠ Tax Rate Determination.
Decision and Tax Period
Event Determination Decision ≠ Tax Period Determination.
Decision and Tax Liability
Event Determination Decision ≠ Tax Liability Determination.
Decision and Legal Characterization
A jurisdiction may later legally characterize the Event differently from TREGA™ operational terminology.
Event Determination Decision ≠ Legal Tax Characterization.
Decision State Preservation
Every materially relevant Decision state shall remain historically traceable.
A later Decision shall not silently erase an earlier one.
Decision Supersession ≠ Decision Erasure.
Decision Correction
Where the Decision itself contains an error that can be corrected without full reconsideration, correction may be recorded.
Decision Correction ≠ Silent Replacement.
Decision Escalation

EDDM may require escalation where: governance basis is materially conflicting; Decision authority is unavailable; conditions are incompatible; automated Decision logic cannot resolve the state; or another governance boundary is reached.
Escalation shall preserve the Event and Decision state.
Governance States
EDDM may represent:
Decision Not Initiated
Decision Eligible
Decision Under Evaluation
Decision Basis Complete
Decision Basis Qualified
Positive Determination
Conditional Determination
Deferred Determination
Rejected Determination
Ambiguous Determination
Conflicted Determination
Decision Escalation Required
Decision Correction Required
Decision Reconsideration Flagged
Decision Finalized
Governed Event Determination Decision Established Governance Requirements

EDDM implementations shall ensure that: Decision governance begins only after suitable condition governance; Decision eligibility remains distinct from Positive Determination; every Decision has a reconstructable basis; Positive Determination remains distinct from legal taxability; Conditional Determination preserves its qualifications; Deferred Determination remains distinct from Rejected Determination; Rejected Determination does not imply legal non-taxability; ambiguous Decisions remain visible; conflicted Decisions remain visible; conflict is not resolved merely by convenience; Decision rationale remains reconstructable; Decision provenance remains available; Decision authority or process reference remains identifiable; Decision time remains distinct from Event Time; operational finality remains distinct from legal finality; Decision logic remains methodologically consistent; AI or automated Decision proposals remain subject to the same governance requirements; technical system status does not substitute for Determination Decision; accounting, invoice, payment, blockchain, and smart-contract status do not substitute for Decision governance; Merge or Split does not automatically transfer a prior Decision; cross-system duplication does not automatically create multiple Decisions; cross-border Determination remains jurisdiction-neutral; Decision does not determine Tax Jurisdiction; Decision does not determine taxpayer status; Decision does not determine Tax Base; Decision do

rmination remains jurisdiction-neutral; Decision does not determine Tax Jurisdiction; Decision does not determine taxpayer status; Decision does not determine Tax Base; Decision does not determine Tax Rate; Decision does not determine Tax Liability; and the resulting Decision state is suitable for EDUM and downstream TREDS governance.

Governance Logic
IF EDCM has not established a sufficient Governed Determination Condition State, THEN EDDM shall not issue a Positive Determination.
IF materially required conditions are sufficiently satisfied and remaining qualifications do not undermine Event Identity or downstream interpretability, THEN EDDM may issue a Positive Determination.
IF the Event is sufficiently governed but bounded qualifications remain, THEN EDDM may issue a Conditional Determination.
IF materially necessary governance remains unresolved but may become resolvable, THEN EDDM shall issue a Deferred Determination rather than a Rejected Determination.
IF the governed structure does not support existence of a valid Tax-Relevant Event, THEN EDDM may issue a Rejected Determination.
IF materially plausible competing Decision outcomes remain unresolved, THEN the Decision shall remain Ambiguous.
IF materially authoritative governance inputs support incompatible outcomes, THEN the Decision shall remain Conflicted or be escalated.
IF the apparent basis for Decision is a technical status, accounting classification, invoice state, payment state, blockchain finality, or model output alone, THEN that basis shall not be sufficient for a governed EDDM Decision.
IF a Merge or Split has materially changed Event structure, THEN the resulting Event shall undergo appropriate Decision governance rather than inherit prior Determination automatically.

IF a Positive Determination is issued, THEN it shall mean only that the Event is sufficiently governed for downstream tax evaluation.
IF later information materially affects the Decision basis, THEN the Decision may be flagged for reconsideration under EDREM.
IF the Decision is sufficiently governed, THEN EDDM shall establish the Governed Event Determination Decision and hand it to EDUM where uncertainty governance is required.
Minimum Implementation Framework
A minimum EDDM implementation should support:
Decision Identifier A stable identifier for the Determination Decision.
Governed Event Reference The Event under Determination.
Readiness State Reference The relevant EDRDM output.
Condition State Reference The relevant EDCM output.
Decision Eligibility State Whether the Event is eligible for formal Decision.
Decision Basis Reference The governance basis supporting the Decision.
Decision State Positive, Conditional, Deferred, Rejected, Ambiguous, Conflicted, or Escalation Required.
Decision Qualification Any bounded qualification attached to the Decision.
Decision Rationale The governed reasoning supporting the selected state.
Material Condition Summary The materially relevant conditions supporting or preventing the Decision.
Unresolved Condition Reference Any unresolved condition affecting the Decision.
Decision Uncertainty State Any uncertainty identified at the Decision stage.
Decision Conflict State Any conflict identified at the Decision stage.

Decision Authority / Process Reference The human, automated, hybrid, delegated, or rule-governed Decision process.
Decision Time The time the Decision was formally established.
Decision Provenance Reference The governance lineage supporting the Decision.
Decision Traceability Reference Information required to reconstruct the Decision.
Prior Decision Reference Any previous Determination Decision for the Event.
Decision Correction Reference Any correction of the Decision.
Decision Escalation Reference Any escalation resulting from the Decision process.
Reconsideration Flag Whether the Decision requires EDREM review.
Jurisdiction-Neutrality State Confirmation that no jurisdiction-specific tax conclusion has been embedded.
Taxability Boundary State Confirmation that the Decision does not determine legal taxability.
Governance State The current EDDM governance state.
Handoff State Whether the Decision may proceed to EDUM or downstream TREDS governance.
Governance Outputs
EDDM may produce: Decision Eligibility State; Decision Basis Record; Positive Determination; Conditional Determination; Deferred Determination; Rejected Determination; Ambiguous Determination; Conflicted Determination; Decision Qualification; Decision Rationale; Decision Provenance Record; Decision Authority Reference; Decision Traceability Record; Decision Correction; Decision Escalation; Reconsideration Flag; Jurisdiction-Neutral Decision State; and the principal output: Governed Event Determination Decision.

Critical Distinctions
Event Determination Decision ≠ Tax Decision.
Decision Initiation ≠ Positive Determination.
Decision Eligible ≠ Determination Positive.
Decision Output Without Decision Basis ≠ Governed Decision.
Positive Event Determination ≠ Positive Tax Determination.
Conditional Determination ≠ Unqualified Determination.
Deferred Determination ≠ Rejected Determination.
Rejected Determination ≠ Legal Non-Taxability.
Ambiguity ≠ Permission to Choose the Convenient Decision.
Decision Conflict ≠ Decision Discretion without Governance Basis.
Operational Decision Finality ≠ Legal Finality.
Decision Consistency ≠ Mechanical Uniformity.
Decision Provenance ≠ Identity Provenance.
Decision Time ≠ Event Time.
Decision Sequence ≠ Event Sequence.
Low Tax Relevance under Law ≠ TREGA™ Rejection Criterion.
Decision ≠ Readiness Assessment.
Decision ≠ Condition Evaluation.
Decision Uncertainty Recognition ≠ Full Uncertainty Governance.
Decision Change ≠ Determination Reconsideration by default.
Recognition Decision ≠ Determination Decision.
Positive Decision ≠ Formation Authority.
Decision ≠ Boundary Redetermination.
Event Determination Decision ≠ Legal Tax Point Determination.
Positive Determination ≠ Tax Jurisdiction Determination.
Positive Determination ≠ Taxpayer Determination.
Positive Determination ≠ Tax Base Determination.
Decision ≠ Relationship Governance.
Merged Event ≠ Automatically Determined Event.
Split Event ≠ Automatically Determined Event.

System Status ≠ Governed Event Determination Decision.
Accounting Classification ≠ Event Determination Decision.
Invoice Status ≠ Event Determination Decision.
Payment Completion ≠ Event Determination Decision.
Blockchain Finality ≠ Event Determination Decision.
Smart-Contract Completion ≠ Event Determination Decision.
AI Classification ≠ Governed Determination Decision.
Model Confidence ≠ Decision.
Automated Decision ≠ Ungoverned Decision.
Multiple Records ≠ Multiple Determination Decisions by default.
Multiple Organizational Views ≠ Multiple Event Realities.
Cross-Border Positive Determination ≠ Jurisdiction Allocation.
Jurisdiction-Neutral Determination ≠ Jurisdictional Tax Decision.
Event Determination Decision ≠ Taxability Determination.
Event Determination Decision ≠ Tax Jurisdiction Determination.
Event Determination Decision ≠ Taxpayer Determination.
Event Determination Decision ≠ Tax Base Determination.
Event Determination Decision ≠ Tax Rate Determination.
Event Determination Decision ≠ Tax Period Determination.
Event Determination Decision ≠ Tax Liability Determination.
Event Determination Decision ≠ Legal Tax Characterization.
Decision Supersession ≠ Decision Erasure.
Decision Correction ≠ Silent Replacement.
Enterprise Application
EDDM provides the formal decision point at which a sufficiently governed Event receives its TREGA™ Determination status.
A typical operational path is:
EDRDM — Governed Determination Readiness State

→ EDCM — Governed Determination Condition State
→ EDDM — Governed Event Determination Decision
→ EDUM — Event Determination Uncertainty Governance
→ EDREM — Event Determination Reconsideration
→ Determined Tax-Relevant Event
This gives enterprises a clear, reviewable answer to whether a governed Event can formally enter downstream tax infrastructure without allowing the Event layer itself to become a tax engine. Use Case 1 — Cross-Border Marketplace Event with Conditional Determination
A marketplace Event has completed Readiness governance and its materially necessary Determination Conditions are satisfied.
However, one bounded digital Location qualification remains.
The uncertainty does not undermine Event Identity, Formation, Boundary, Participation, Value Association, or Event Relationships.
EDDM issues a Conditional Determination and preserves the Location qualification for downstream processing.
The Event becomes eligible for jurisdiction-specific analysis.
EDDM does not determine which jurisdiction has taxing authority. Use Case 2 — Machine-Generated Record Rejected as a Tax-Relevant Event
An autonomous industrial system generates a technical record every time a machine changes operating state.
One record enters TREGA™ because a downstream accounting system incorrectly treats each machine state change as a separate economic event.

Upstream governance establishes that the state change is merely part of an already-governed service Event and does not possess independent Event Formation or Boundary.
EDDM therefore issues a Rejected Determination for the apparent standalone Event.
The rejection does not mean the broader service is non-taxable.
It means only that the technical machine-state record does not qualify as an independent Tax-Relevant Event.
Canonical Boundary
EDDM owns the governance of Decision initiation, Decision eligibility, Decision basis, Positive Determination, Conditional Determination, Deferred Determination, Rejected Determination, Ambiguous Determination, Conflicted Determination, Decision qualification, Decision rationale, Decision consistency, Decision provenance, Decision authority reference, Decision timing, Decision traceability, Decision correction, Decision escalation, and establishment of the Governed Event Determination Decision.
EDDM does not perform Determination Readiness governance, Determination Condition governance, full Determination Uncertainty governance, or Determination Reconsideration.
It does not perform Event Context, Recognition, Formation, Boundary, Timing, Location, Participation, Value Association, or Event Relationship governance.

It does not determine legal taxability, Tax Jurisdiction, taxpayer status, legal tax point, Tax Period, Tax Base, Tax Rate, Tax Liability, exemption, deduction, filing obligation, payment, collection, enforcement, or any other jurisdiction-specific legal tax consequence.
Its governance begins when EDCM establishes a Governed Determination Condition State suitable for Decision.
Its governance ends when a formal Governed Event Determination Decision has been established for handoff to EDUM and the remaining TREDS process.
Canonical Handoff
EDCM — Governed Determination Condition State
↓
EDDM — Governed Event Determination Decision
↓
EDUM — Event Determination Uncertainty Governance
Canonical Closing Statement
EDDM converts governed readiness and explicit determination conditions into a formal Event Determination Decision without allowing that decision to become a legal tax conclusion.
The decision establishes whether TREGA™ recognizes a sufficiently governed Tax-Relevant Event. It does not decide what any jurisdiction must tax.
Event Determination Decision ≠ Tax Decision.
Positive Event Determination ≠ Positive Tax Determination.
TREGA™ governs the event. The jurisdiction governs the tax.

OOF™ The Event Determination Readiness Module (EDRDM) governs whether an event
The Event Determination Readiness Module (EDRDM) governs whether an event
OOF™ Origin Open Foundation™
Independent Methodological Authority
Architecture Ecosystem: Structured Reality Standards™
Architecture Family: TREGA™ — Tax-Relevant Event Governance Architecture™
Parent Standard: TREDS — Tax-Relevant Event Determination Standard
Module: EDRDM — Event Determination Readiness Module
Operational Layer: Event Determination Readiness Governance Layer
Category: Governance & Enforcement
Subcategory: Tax-Relevant Event Governance
Type: Core Module
Governed Space: Event Determination Readiness
Origin ID: TREGA-TREDS-EDRDM-001
Version: 1.0
Status: Canonical · Open Standard
Effective Date: 2 September 2026
AI-Readable: Yes
Authority: OOF®
Protection: MIP® — Methodological Intellectual Property
Canonical Language: UCL — Universal Canonical Language
Canonical Definition
The Event Determination Readiness Module (EDRDM) governs whether an event that has passed through the preceding TREGA™ governance layers is sufficiently prepared to enter formal Tax-Relevant Event Determination.
EDRDM evaluates the availability, material completeness, coherence, accessibility, stability, and governance status of the upstream Event structures required for Determination.
Its principal transition is:
Governed Event Relationship Structure + Upstream Governance States
↓
Determination Readiness Governance
↓

Governed Determination Readiness State
EDRDM does not determine whether the event is a Tax-Relevant Event.
It determines whether the event is ready for that question to be formally evaluated.
The foundational distinction is:
Determination Readiness ≠ Event Determination.
Operational Role
An event should not enter formal Determination merely because a technical record exists or because upstream processing has reached TREDS.
Before Determination Conditions can be evaluated, the system must establish whether the necessary Event governance is actually available and sufficiently mature.
EDRDM provides this entry control.
It prevents formal Determination from beginning where materially necessary upstream governance is: absent; incomplete; inaccessible; structurally inconsistent; materially unstable; unresolved; or not sufficiently traceable.
The module therefore functions as the readiness gate of TREDS.
Internal Module Flow
TREDS operates through:
EDRDM — Event Determination Readiness
↓
EDCM — Event Determination Conditions
↓
EDDM — Event Determination Decision
↓
EDUM — Event Determination Uncertainty
↓
EDREM — Event Determination Reconsideration
↓
Determined Tax-Relevant Event
EDRDM is the first Core Module.
Its principal output is passed to EDCM.
Operational Transition
The canonical operational transition is:
Governed Event Relationship Structure + Relevant Upstream Governance Outputs
↓
Readiness Evaluation
↓
Governed Determination Readiness State
Possible outcomes include:
Ready

Conditionally Ready
Not Ready
Readiness Ambiguous
Readiness Conflicted
Readiness Escalation Required
EDRDM does not convert any of these states into a positive Event Determination.
Operational Space
EDRDM governs: readiness initiation; upstream governance availability; required-input identification; input accessibility; material completeness; governance-state sufficiency; cross-layer coherence screening; unresolved-state screening; upstream conflict screening; upstream uncertainty screening; stability screening; traceability availability; dependency on missing governance; readiness qualification; readiness deferral; readiness ambiguity; readiness conflict; upstream referral; readiness reassessment; and readiness-specific traceability.
Operational Scope
EDRDM may evaluate readiness for events originating from: enterprise systems; ERP environments; commerce; marketplaces; banking; payments; accounting; logistics; supply chains; digital platforms; blockchain infrastructure; digital assets; smart contracts; AI agents; autonomous systems; industrial infrastructure; energy systems; distributed systems; cross-border operations; machine-to-machine activity; and future machine economies.
The readiness principle remains independent of the technology producing the event.
Readiness Object
The Readiness Object is the governed Event representation submitted for Determination Readiness evaluation together with its relevant upstream governance states.

It shall be distinguishable from raw technical records.
Technical Record ≠ Readiness Object by default.
The Readiness Object represents the governed Event structure, not merely its source data.
Readiness Initiation
Readiness governance begins when an event has reached the TREDS entry point and materially relevant upstream outputs are available for evaluation.
Initiation shall not imply readiness.
Readiness Initiation ≠ Readiness Confirmation.
Required Governance Inputs
EDRDM shall identify which upstream governance outputs are materially necessary for the Event under review.
These may include: Event Context; Event Recognition; Event Formation; Event Boundary; Event Timing; Event Location; Event Participation; Value Association; Event Relationship Structure.
Not every Event requires identical information depth.
The relevant requirement depends on the governed Event structure.
Context Readiness
EDRDM may evaluate whether sufficient governed Event Context exists for Determination to proceed.
It does not recreate Context.
TRECS remains authoritative.
Context Readiness ≠ Context Determination.
Recognition Readiness
The event should have a valid Recognition lineage where applicable.
EDRDM may identify an unresolved Recognition problem.
It does not reperform Event Recognition.
Recognition Readiness ≠ Event Recognition.
Formation Readiness
Event Formation must be sufficiently governed for Determination evaluation.

Where it remains materially unclear whether: an Event exists; one or several Events exist; components belong to the same Event;
readiness may fail.
Formation Uncertainty ≠ Determination Readiness by default.
TREFS remains authoritative.
Boundary Readiness
The Event Boundary shall be sufficiently governed where material.
An event whose material scope remains unresolved may not be ready.
Boundary Availability ≠ Boundary Readiness.
A boundary record may exist while still carrying material unresolved conflict.
Timing Readiness
Relevant Event Timing shall be sufficiently governed where timing materially affects Event interpretation.
EDRDM does not determine Event Time or legal tax point.
Timing Readiness ≠ Tax Timing Determination.
Location Readiness
Relevant Event Location information shall be sufficiently governed where location materially contributes to downstream Event interpretation.
EDRDM does not determine Tax Jurisdiction.
Location Readiness ≠ Jurisdiction Determination.
Participation Readiness
Material participants and their Event Participation should be sufficiently represented where required.
EDRDM does not determine taxpayer status.
Participation Readiness ≠ Taxpayer Determination.
Value Association Readiness
Where value is materially associated with the Event, the relevant TRVAS governance should be sufficiently available.
EDRDM does not determine taxable value or Tax Base.
Value Association Readiness ≠ Tax Base Readiness.
Relationship Readiness

The Governed Event Relationship Structure produced by TRERLS is a principal input to TREDS.
EDRDM shall establish whether materially relevant relationships have been sufficiently governed for Determination evaluation.
It does not recreate those relationships.
Relationship Readiness ≠ Relationship Determination.
Input Availability
A governance result cannot support readiness if it is unavailable to the Determination process.
EDRDM shall therefore distinguish between: governance not performed; governance performed but unavailable; governance available but incomplete; governance available but unresolved; governance sufficiently available.
Existing Information ≠ Available Governance.
Input Accessibility
Required governance information should be accessible in a form usable by the Determination process.
Accessibility may be affected by: incompatible systems; inaccessible records; broken references; missing identifiers; unavailable external sources; or failed data exchange.
Technical accessibility shall not be confused with substantive sufficiency.
Accessible Data ≠ Sufficient Governance.
Material Completeness
Readiness does not require every possible field or record.
It requires materially necessary governance.
EDRDM shall distinguish: complete enough for Determination; conditionally complete; materially incomplete; immaterially incomplete.
Material Completeness ≠ Total Data Completeness.
Missing Information
Missing information shall be evaluated according to materiality.

If missing information cannot materially alter Event interpretation, it may not prevent readiness.
If it could materially alter: Event Identity; Formation; Boundary; Participation; Value Association; Relationship structure;
readiness may be blocked.
Missing Data ≠ Automatic Readiness Failure.
Immaterial Missing Information
An event may remain ready where absent information is not necessary for Event Determination.
EDRDM should avoid unnecessary governance burden.
More Data ≠ Greater Readiness by default.
Material Missing Information
Materially missing governance shall be identified explicitly.
Readiness shall not be declared merely because downstream processing expects an answer.
Processing Demand ≠ Readiness.
Governance-State Sufficiency
An upstream governance output may exist but remain in a state unsuitable for Determination.
Examples include: unresolved; conflicted; under reconsideration; structurally incomplete; provisional where finality is materially required.
EDRDM evaluates whether the state is sufficient for entry into Determination Conditions governance.
Cross-Layer Coherence
EDRDM shall screen whether materially relevant upstream outputs are mutually coherent enough to proceed.
Examples of potential conflicts include: Formation inconsistent with Boundary; Timing inconsistent with Event Formation; Participant association outside the governed Boundary; Value associated with another Event; Relationship structure inconsistent with Event Identity.

EDRDM identifies the readiness impact.
It does not assume ownership of the underlying issue.
Coherence Failure
A material contradiction may produce a Not Ready or Conflicted state.
Available Outputs ≠ Coherent Outputs.
The existence of every required governance record does not establish readiness if those records materially contradict one another.
Upstream Uncertainty
Upstream uncertainty shall be evaluated according to its effect on readiness.
Bounded uncertainty may permit Conditional Readiness.
Material unresolved uncertainty may prevent readiness.
Uncertainty ≠ Automatic Not Ready State.
Upstream Conflict
Material conflict shall remain visible.
EDRDM shall not resolve conflicts by selecting whichever result enables Determination.
Readiness Pressure ≠ Permission to Ignore Conflict.
Readiness Stability
The Event structure should be sufficiently stable for formal Determination evaluation.
An event undergoing major Formation, Boundary, Merge, Split, or Relationship reconsideration may not yet be ready.
Readiness Stability ≠ Permanent Finality.
Operationally sufficient stability is enough.
Pending Merge or Split
Where ERLMM identifies an unresolved Merge or Split Candidate that could materially change Event Identity, the Event may not be ready for Determination.
Unresolved Structural Change ≠ Stable Readiness.
Correction in Progress
A minor correction need not always prevent readiness.
The materiality of the correction shall govern the readiness effect.

Correction in Progress ≠ Automatic Readiness Failure.
Traceability Readiness
Sufficient upstream traceability should exist to reconstruct the Event governance relied upon during Determination.
EDRDM does not perform full audit governance.
However, an Event whose governing basis cannot be reconstructed may not be ready.
Governance Result Without Traceability ≠ Reliable Readiness by default.
Identifier Continuity
The Event and relevant upstream outputs should be sufficiently linked through stable references.
Broken or ambiguous identifiers may create readiness problems where they prevent reliable association.
Record Proximity ≠ Identity Continuity.
Cross-System Readiness
An Event may be constructed across multiple systems.
Readiness shall depend on the governed Event representation rather than the number of systems involved.
Multiple Systems ≠ Reduced Readiness by default.
Fragmentation matters only where it prevents sufficient governance.
Cross-Organization Readiness
An Event may involve multiple organizations.
EDRDM may evaluate whether required governance information from those organizations is sufficiently available.
It does not determine accountability or taxpayer status.
Cross-Border Readiness
An Event may span multiple countries.
Cross-border complexity may increase governance requirements but does not prevent readiness by itself.
Cross-Border Event ≠ Not Ready Event.
EDRDM does not determine Tax Jurisdiction.
Multi-Jurisdiction Readiness

An Event should be capable of supporting downstream jurisdiction-specific evaluation without requiring TREGA™ to select a jurisdiction.
The objective is:
One Governed Event
↓
One Determination Readiness Assessment
↓
Multiple Potential Jurisdictional Evaluations
Multi-Jurisdiction Readiness ≠ Jurisdiction Determination.
Blockchain Readiness
Blockchain data may provide strong technical traceability while leaving material Event governance unresolved.
A transaction hash does not establish readiness.
Blockchain Finality ≠ Event Determination Readiness.
Off-chain Formation, Participation, Value, or Relationship governance may still be required.
Smart-Contract Readiness
Completed smart-contract execution does not establish that the resulting Event structure is ready.
Execution Completion ≠ Determination Readiness.
AI-Agent Readiness
An AI agent may produce structured records automatically.
Automation does not eliminate governance requirements.
Machine-Generated Structure ≠ Governed Readiness.
Machine-System Readiness
High-frequency machine activity may produce millions of operational records.
EDRDM evaluates the governed Event, not record volume.
More Machine Records ≠ Greater Readiness.
Automated Readiness Assessment
Readiness assessment may be partially or fully automated.
However, automated processing shall apply the same governance requirements.
Automated Readiness Score ≠ Governed Readiness State.
A score may support the process but does not replace the governed outcome.

Readiness Qualification
Where the Event is sufficiently prepared but bounded limitations remain, EDRDM may establish Conditionally Ready.
The qualification shall identify the remaining limitation.
Conditionally Ready ≠ Fully Ready.
Not Ready State
An Event shall be Not Ready where materially necessary governance is absent, inaccessible, unstable, incoherent, or unresolved to a degree that prevents meaningful Determination Conditions evaluation.
Not Ready ≠ Not Tax-Relevant.
It means only that formal Determination cannot yet proceed reliably.
Readiness Ambiguity
Readiness may be ambiguous where it is unclear whether missing or unresolved governance is materially necessary.
The ambiguity shall remain explicit.
Readiness Ambiguity ≠ Permission to Assume Readiness.
Readiness Conflict
Readiness may be conflicted where materially relevant governance sources support incompatible readiness conclusions.
The conflict shall remain visible until sufficiently resolved.
Upstream Referral
Where readiness fails because of an upstream governance issue, EDRDM shall refer the issue to the appropriate Parent Standard.
Typical routing includes:
Context
↓
TRECS
Recognition
↓
TRERS
Formation
↓
TREFS
Boundary
↓
TREBS
Timing
↓
TRETS
Location
↓
TRELS
Participation
↓
TREPS
Value Association
↓
TRVAS
Event Relationships
↓
TRERLS
EDRDM does not silently repair upstream governance.
Readiness Reassessment

An Event previously classified Not Ready, Conditionally Ready, Ambiguous, or Conflicted may be reassessed when relevant governance changes.
The prior readiness state shall remain traceable.
Readiness Reassessment ≠ Historical Erasure.
Readiness Expiration
Where materially relevant upstream governance changes after readiness was established, the readiness state may cease to be reliable.
EDRDM may require reassessment.
Prior Readiness ≠ Permanent Readiness.
Readiness and Determination Conditions
EDRDM determines whether the Event may enter the next module.
EDCM then governs whether the actual Determination Conditions are satisfied.
This distinction is essential.
Ready for Condition Evaluation ≠ Conditions Satisfied.
Readiness and Determination Decision
EDRDM does not issue: Positive Determination; Rejected Determination; legal tax conclusion; or Taxability Determination.
Those functions remain downstream.
Ready ≠ Determined.
Readiness and Taxability
An Event may be fully Ready and later produce no tax consequence under applicable law.
Conversely, a potentially taxable activity may remain Not Ready because Event governance is insufficient.
Therefore:
Determination Readiness ≠ Taxability.
Readiness and Tax Jurisdiction
Sufficient Location governance may contribute to readiness.
EDRDM does not convert Location into Tax Jurisdiction.
Location Readiness ≠ Tax Jurisdiction.
Readiness and Taxpayer
Sufficient Participation governance may contribute to readiness.

EDRDM does not identify the taxpayer.
Participation Readiness ≠ Taxpayer Readiness.
Readiness and Tax Base
Sufficient Value Association may contribute to readiness.
EDRDM does not establish taxable amount.
Value Readiness ≠ Tax Base Determination.
Readiness and Legal Tax Point
Sufficient Event Timing may contribute to readiness.
EDRDM does not establish a legal tax point.
Timing Readiness ≠ Legal Tax Point.
Governance States
EDRDM may represent:
Readiness Not Initiated
Readiness Governance Initiated
Required Inputs Identified
Inputs Partially Available
Inputs Available
Materially Incomplete
Conditionally Complete
Materially Complete
Coherence Review Required
Coherence Sufficient
Readiness Unstable
Readiness Ambiguous
Readiness Conflicted
Upstream Referral Required
Not Ready
Conditionally Ready
Ready
Readiness Under Reassessment
Governed Determination Readiness State Established Governance Requirements

EDRDM implementations shall ensure that: readiness is evaluated before formal Determination Conditions; readiness remains distinct from Event Determination; materially required upstream governance is identifiable; upstream governance availability is distinguishable from substantive sufficiency; technical accessibility is distinguishable from governance completeness; material completeness is distinguished from total data completeness; immaterial missing information does not automatically block readiness; materially missing governance remains visible; cross-layer coherence is screened; material contradictions are not ignored; upstream uncertainty is evaluated according to material effect; upstream conflict remains visible; unstable Event structures are not automatically declared ready; unresolved Merge or Split issues are considered where material; traceability availability is considered; identifier continuity is considered where necessary; cross-system fragmentation does not automatically prevent readiness; cross-border complexity does not determine Tax Jurisdiction; blockchain finality does not substitute for Event governance; machine-generated information remains subject to the same readiness principles; automated readiness scores do not replace governed readiness states; upstream governance failures are referred to the authoritative layer; readiness reassessment preserves history; readiness remains distinct from Determination Conditions; readiness remains distinct from Dete

es are referred to the authoritative layer; readiness reassessment preserves history; readiness remains distinct from Determination Conditions; readiness remains distinct from Determination Decision; and readiness remains distinct from legal taxability.

Governance Logic
IF materially necessary upstream governance cannot be identified, THEN Determination Readiness shall not be confirmed.
IF required upstream governance is materially unavailable, THEN the Event shall remain Not Ready or otherwise qualified.
IF required governance exists but contains material unresolved contradiction, THEN readiness shall remain Conflicted, Ambiguous, or Not Ready according to impact.
IF missing information is immaterial to Event Determination, THEN its absence shall not automatically prevent readiness.
IF missing information could materially alter Event Identity, Formation, Boundary, Participation, Value Association, or Event Relationships, THEN readiness shall not be confirmed until the issue is sufficiently governed.
IF bounded uncertainty exists but the Event remains sufficiently structured for Determination Conditions evaluation, THEN Conditional Readiness may be established.
IF an unresolved Merge or Split Candidate could materially alter Event Identity, THEN readiness shall be withheld or qualified.
IF upstream governance is sufficiently available, materially complete, coherent, stable, and traceable, THEN the Event may be classified Ready.
IF a readiness failure belongs to an upstream Parent Standard, THEN the issue shall be referred upstream rather than silently resolved inside EDRDM.
IF a previously established readiness state is materially affected by new governance information, THEN readiness shall be reassessed.

IF the Event reaches a sufficient Governed Determination Readiness State, THEN it shall proceed to EDCM for Event Determination Conditions governance.
Minimum Implementation Framework
A minimum EDRDM implementation should support:
Readiness Assessment Identifier A stable identifier for the readiness governance process.
Governed Event Reference The Event entering Determination Readiness governance.
Event Relationship Structure Reference The TRERLS output supplied to TREDS.
Context Governance Reference Relevant TRECS output and governance state.
Recognition Governance Reference Relevant TRERS output and governance state.
Formation Governance Reference Relevant TREFS output and governance state.
Boundary Governance Reference Relevant TREBS output and governance state.
Timing Governance Reference Relevant TRETS output and governance state.
Location Governance Reference Relevant TRELS output and governance state.
Participation Governance Reference Relevant TREPS output and governance state.
Value Association Reference Relevant TRVAS output and governance state.
Relationship Governance Reference Relevant TRERLS output and governance state.
Required Input State Which upstream governance inputs are materially required.
Input Availability State Whether those inputs are available.
Material Completeness State Whether materially necessary governance is sufficiently complete.
Coherence State Whether upstream governance is sufficiently coherent.

Stability State Whether Event structure is sufficiently stable.
Unresolved Governance State Any material unresolved upstream condition.
Upstream Uncertainty State Relevant uncertainty affecting readiness.
Upstream Conflict State Relevant conflict affecting readiness.
Structural Change State Any material pending Merge, Split, or other structural reconsideration.
Traceability Availability State Whether the governance basis can be reconstructed.
Upstream Referral Reference Any referral to another TREGA™ Parent Standard.
Readiness Qualification Any bounded qualification attached to readiness.
Readiness Decision Ready, Conditionally Ready, Not Ready, Ambiguous, Conflicted, or Escalation Required.
Prior Readiness Reference Any previous readiness state.
Reassessment Reference Any later readiness reassessment.
Readiness Traceability Reference Information required to reconstruct the readiness evaluation.
Governance State The current EDRDM governance state.
Handoff State Whether the Event may proceed to EDCM.
Governance Outputs

EDRDM may produce: Required Governance Input Set; Input Availability State; Material Completeness State; Coherence State; Stability State; Upstream Uncertainty State; Upstream Conflict State; Structural Change State; Traceability Readiness State; Upstream Referral; Readiness Qualification; Not Ready Determination; Conditional Readiness State; Ready State; Readiness Ambiguity State; Readiness Conflict State; Readiness Reassessment Record; Readiness Traceability Record; and the principal output: Governed Determination Readiness State.
Critical Distinctions
Determination Readiness ≠ Event Determination.
Technical Record ≠ Readiness Object by default.
Readiness Initiation ≠ Readiness Confirmation.
Context Readiness ≠ Context Determination.
Recognition Readiness ≠ Event Recognition.
Formation Uncertainty ≠ Determination Readiness by default.
Boundary Availability ≠ Boundary Readiness.
Timing Readiness ≠ Tax Timing Determination.
Location Readiness ≠ Jurisdiction Determination.
Participation Readiness ≠ Taxpayer Determination.
Value Association Readiness ≠ Tax Base Readiness.
Relationship Readiness ≠ Relationship Determination.
Existing Information ≠ Available Governance.
Accessible Data ≠ Sufficient Governance.
Material Completeness ≠ Total Data Completeness.
Missing Data ≠ Automatic Readiness Failure.
More Data ≠ Greater Readiness by default.
Processing Demand ≠ Readiness.
Available Outputs ≠ Coherent Outputs.
Uncertainty ≠ Automatic Not Ready State.

Readiness Pressure ≠ Permission to Ignore Conflict.
Readiness Stability ≠ Permanent Finality.
Unresolved Structural Change ≠ Stable Readiness.
Governance Result Without Traceability ≠ Reliable Readiness by default.
Blockchain Finality ≠ Event Determination Readiness.
Execution Completion ≠ Determination Readiness.
Machine-Generated Structure ≠ Governed Readiness.
Automated Readiness Score ≠ Governed Readiness State.
Conditionally Ready ≠ Fully Ready.
Not Ready ≠ Not Tax-Relevant.
Readiness Ambiguity ≠ Permission to Assume Readiness.
Readiness Reassessment ≠ Historical Erasure.
Prior Readiness ≠ Permanent Readiness.
Ready for Condition Evaluation ≠ Conditions Satisfied.
Ready ≠ Determined.
Determination Readiness ≠ Taxability.
Enterprise Application
EDRDM provides the practical entry gate to formal Tax-Relevant Event Determination.
A typical operational path is:
Operational / Digital Systems
→ TREGA™ Upstream Event Governance
→ TRERLS — Governed Event Relationship Structure
→ EDRDM — Governed Determination Readiness State
→ EDCM — Event Determination Conditions
→ EDDM — Event Determination Decision
This allows enterprises to identify incomplete or structurally unstable Event representations before they enter formal Determination or downstream tax infrastructure. Use Case 1 — Cross-Border Marketplace Event with Missing Participation Governance
A marketplace Event has a governed Context, Formation, Boundary, Timing, Location, Value Association, and Relationship Structure.

However, the Event Participation structure remains materially unresolved because two entities may have performed the relevant merchant function.
EDRDM identifies Participation as materially necessary for Determination and establishes a Not Ready state.
The issue is referred to TREPS.
Once Participation governance is sufficiently resolved, EDRDM reassesses the Event and may establish Ready.
The module does not determine which participant is legally the taxpayer. Use Case 2 — Autonomous Service Event with Bounded Location Uncertainty
An autonomous infrastructure service has governed Formation, Boundary, Timing, machine Participation, Value Association, and Event Relationships.
The service spans distributed infrastructure and its exact digital Location contains bounded uncertainty.
EDRDM evaluates whether that uncertainty prevents formal Determination Conditions evaluation.
Where the uncertainty does not alter Event Identity or prevent meaningful downstream jurisdiction-specific analysis, EDRDM may establish Conditionally Ready while preserving the Location qualification.
The module does not determine Tax Jurisdiction.
Canonical Boundary

EDRDM owns the governance of Determination Readiness initiation, required-input identification, upstream governance availability, material completeness, coherence screening, stability screening, unresolved-state screening, uncertainty and conflict impact on readiness, traceability readiness, upstream referral, readiness qualification, readiness reassessment, and establishment of the Governed Determination Readiness State.
EDRDM does not perform Event Context, Recognition, Formation, Boundary, Timing, Location, Participation, Value Association, or Event Relationship governance itself.
It does not determine whether the Event satisfies formal Determination Conditions, does not issue the final Event Determination Decision, and does not determine taxability, Tax Jurisdiction, taxpayer status, legal tax point, Tax Base, Tax Rate, Tax Liability, or another jurisdiction-specific legal consequence.
Its governance begins when a governed Event and materially relevant upstream TREGA™ outputs are presented for Determination Readiness evaluation.
Its governance ends when the Event has received a Governed Determination Readiness State suitable for handoff to EDCM.
Canonical Handoff
TRERLS — Governed Event Relationship Structure
↓
EDRDM — Governed Determination Readiness State
↓
EDCM — Event Determination Conditions Governance
Canonical Closing Statement

EDRDM ensures that formal Event Determination begins only when the Event Reality required to support that determination is sufficiently available, coherent, stable, and reconstructable.
Readiness opens the door to determination. It does not predetermine what the determination will be.
Determination Readiness ≠ Event Determination.
Ready ≠ Determined.
