OOF™ The Event Determination Reconsideration Module (EDREM) governs when and
The Event Determination Reconsideration Module (EDREM) governs when and
OOF™ Origin Open Foundation™
Independent Methodological Authority
Architecture Ecosystem: Structured Reality Standards™
Architecture Family: TREGA™ — Tax-Relevant Event Governance Architecture™
Parent Standard: TREDS — Tax-Relevant Event Determination Standard
Module: EDREM — Event Determination Reconsideration Module
Operational Layer: Event Determination Reconsideration Governance Layer
Category: Governance & Enforcement
Subcategory: Tax-Relevant Event Governance
Type: Core Module
Governed Space: Event Determination Reconsideration
Origin ID: TREGA-TREDS-EDREM-005
Version: 1.0
Status: Canonical · Open Standard
Effective Date: 2 September 2026
AI-Readable: Yes
Authority: OOF®
Protection: MIP® — Methodological Intellectual Property
Canonical Language: UCL — Universal Canonical Language
Canonical Definition
The Event Determination Reconsideration Module (EDREM) governs when and how an existing Tax-Relevant Event Determination is reopened for formal review after materially relevant new information, corrected governance, changed Event structure, resolved uncertainty, new conflict, superseding upstream output, or another legitimate reconsideration trigger emerges.
EDREM governs the transition from an existing Determination state to a reviewed Determination state while preserving the complete history of the prior Decision.

Its principal transition is:
Governed Event Determination Decision + Reconsideration Trigger
↓
Reconsideration Governance
↓
Confirmed, Amended, Replaced, Deferred, Rejected, or Superseded Determination State
EDREM does not silently rewrite the prior Decision.
Its foundational distinction is:
Determination Reconsideration ≠ Historical Erasure.
Operational Role
Tax-Relevant Event Determination occurs at a specific governance state and time.
Operational reality may later change or become better understood.
Examples include: corrected Event Formation; revised Event Boundary; new participant information; corrected Value Association; resolved Event Relationship conflict; new Merge or Split result; newly available evidence; resolved uncertainty; discovery of duplicate Event representation; or material error in the prior Determination basis.
EDREM provides the controlled mechanism for reopening the existing Determination without destroying its historical validity as a prior governance state.
The core question is:
Does new or changed governance materially affect the existing Determination, and if so, what governed Determination state should replace or qualify it?
Internal Module Flow
TREDS operates through:
EDRDM — Event Determination Readiness
↓
EDCM — Event Determination Conditions
↓
EDDM — Event Determination Decision
↓
EDUM — Event Determination Uncertainty
↓
EDREM — Event Determination Reconsideration
↓
Determined Tax-Relevant Event
EDREM is the final Core Module of TREDS.

Its output becomes the final TREDS Determination state for handoff to TREGS.
Operational Transition
The canonical transition is:
Existing Determination State + Material Reconsideration Trigger
↓
Trigger Qualification
↓
Reconsideration Scope
↓
Re-evaluation
↓
Reconsideration Outcome
↓
Final Determination State
Possible outcomes include:
Determination Confirmed
Determination Confirmed with Qualification
Determination Amended
Determination Replaced
Determination Deferred
Determination Rejected
Determination Superseded
Reconsideration Inconclusive
Further Upstream Governance Required Operational Space
EDREM governs: reconsideration trigger identification; trigger legitimacy; trigger materiality; reconsideration initiation; reconsideration scope; affected Decision dimension; upstream-change impact; Decision-basis change; uncertainty-resolution impact; conflict-resolution impact; correction impact; Merge/Split impact; duplicate-event impact; reconsideration qualification; Determination confirmation; Determination amendment; Determination replacement; Determination deferral; Determination rejection; Determination supersession; reconsideration traceability; prior-state preservation; downstream notification; and final TREDS Determination handoff.
Operational Scope

EDREM applies to reconsideration of Determination Decisions arising from: commerce; marketplaces; payments; banking; accounting; ERP systems; logistics; supply chains; digital platforms; digital assets; blockchain systems; smart contracts; AI agents; autonomous systems; industrial systems; distributed infrastructure; cross-border operations; machine-to-machine environments; and future machine economies.
Its governance logic remains technology-neutral and jurisdiction-neutral.
Reconsideration Object
The Reconsideration Object is an existing Governed Event Determination Decision whose continued validity has become materially reviewable.
The Reconsideration Object shall include: the existing Determination Decision; its Decision basis; relevant qualifications; relevant uncertainty state; the new or changed governance information; the reconsideration trigger.
Existing Decision ≠ Immutable Decision.
Reconsideration Trigger
A Reconsideration Trigger is a materially relevant change or discovery capable of affecting the validity, qualification, or status of an existing Determination.

Potential triggers include: corrected upstream governance; newly available information; resolved uncertainty; newly discovered uncertainty; resolved conflict; newly discovered conflict; Event Merge; Event Split; Event correction; duplicate-event discovery; superseded source; materially changed Event Relationship; materially changed Value Association; materially changed Participation; or identified Decision error.
New Information ≠ Automatic Reconsideration Trigger.
The information must be materially relevant to the existing Determination.
Trigger Legitimacy
EDREM shall determine whether the reconsideration trigger is methodologically legitimate.
A Decision shall not be reopened solely because: a different tax result is desired; reporting becomes inconvenient; commercial preference changes; a jurisdiction produces an unfavorable legal interpretation; a technical system wishes to rewrite history.
Preferred Tax Outcome ≠ Reconsideration Basis.
Trigger Materiality
A trigger is material where it could alter: Event Identity; Event Formation; Event Boundary; Determination Conditions; Determination Decision; Determination qualification; Event count; Participation structure; Value Association; Event Relationships; or downstream usability.
Changed Information ≠ Material Change by default.
Reconsideration Initiation
Reconsideration shall begin only after a legitimate material trigger is established.

The prior Decision remains the historical Decision until the reconsideration process produces a governed result.
Reconsideration Initiation ≠ Prior Decision Cancellation.
Reconsideration Scope
EDREM shall define the scope of the reconsideration.
The review may affect: one Decision qualification; one governance dependency; one Decision basis element; the complete Determination Decision; or several related Event Determinations.
Scope should be no broader than materially necessary.
Local Change ≠ Full Determination Reopening by default.
Decision-Basis Change
Where the basis supporting a prior Decision changes materially, EDREM shall assess whether that change affects the Decision.
A changed basis does not automatically require a changed outcome.
Changed Basis ≠ Changed Decision by default.
Upstream Governance Change
An upstream Parent Standard may produce a corrected or superseded governance result.
Examples include: revised Formation; revised Boundary; corrected Timing; corrected Location; changed Participation; corrected Value Association; revised Relationship structure.
EDREM evaluates the effect on Determination.
It does not redo the upstream governance.
Formation Reconsideration Impact
A materially changed Event Formation may require complete Determination reconsideration.
Changed Formation ≠ Automatic Continuity of Prior Determination.
TREFS remains authoritative for Formation.
Boundary Reconsideration Impact

If Event Boundary changes materially, the prior Determination may no longer apply to the same Event structure.
Changed Boundary ≠ Same Determination by default.
TREBS remains authoritative.
Timing Reconsideration Impact
A corrected Event Time may or may not affect the Determination.
EDREM evaluates material impact.
It does not determine legal tax timing.
Corrected Event Time ≠ Legal Tax Point Reconsideration.
Location Reconsideration Impact
Changed Location information may affect Event Determination qualification.
EDREM does not determine Tax Jurisdiction.
Location Reconsideration ≠ Jurisdiction Reconsideration.
Participation Reconsideration Impact
A corrected Participant structure may materially affect the Determination.
EDREM evaluates Determination impact only.
Participant Reconsideration ≠ Taxpayer Reconsideration.
Value Association Reconsideration Impact
Corrected Value Association may require Determination reconsideration.
EDREM does not determine taxable value or Tax Base.
Value Reconsideration ≠ Tax Base Recalculation.
Relationship Reconsideration Impact
Corrected Event Relationships may affect whether prior Determination remains valid.
Examples include: newly established dependency; changed sequence; revised grouping; Event Merge; Event Split.
TRERLS remains authoritative for the relationship structure.
Merge Impact

Where multiple previously determined Events are governed into one Event through ERLMM, the prior Determination states shall not simply collapse into the new Event.
The resulting Event requires appropriate reconsideration.
Merged Determinations ≠ One Determination by automatic inheritance.
Split Impact
Where one previously determined Event is split into multiple governed Events, the prior Decision does not automatically transfer to each resulting Event.
One Prior Determination ≠ Multiple Valid Determinations after Split.
Duplicate-Event Discovery
A previously determined Event may later be identified as a duplicate representation of another governed Event.
EDREM may supersede or reject the duplicate Determination while preserving its historical record.
Duplicate Determination Correction ≠ Historical Deletion.
Uncertainty Resolution Impact
EDUM may resolve uncertainty that previously qualified or deferred a Decision.
EDREM evaluates whether that resolution justifies: confirmation; removal of qualification; amendment; or replacement.
Resolved Uncertainty ≠ Automatic Positive Determination.
New Uncertainty Impact
New material uncertainty may emerge after Determination.
EDREM may reopen the Decision where continued reliance is no longer methodologically justified.
Conflict Resolution Impact
A conflict may later be resolved.
EDREM assesses whether the resolution changes the prior Determination.
Conflict Resolution ≠ Automatic Decision Change.
New Conflict Impact

A new materially authoritative conflict may undermine a previously stable Decision.
EDREM may require reconsideration, qualification, deferral, or upstream referral.
Known Error
If the prior Determination is known to contain a substantive error, EDREM shall distinguish simple correction from full reconsideration.
A minor clerical error may not require reopening the Decision.
A material governance error may.
Clerical Correction ≠ Full Reconsideration by default.
Reconsideration Qualification
Reconsideration may produce a Determination that remains valid but now carries a new qualification.
Any qualification shall remain explicit and traceable.
Determination Confirmation
The prior Determination may be Confirmed where the new information does not materially alter its basis or outcome.
Confirmation should be explicit.
Reconsidered and Confirmed ≠ Never Reconsidered.
Confirmation with Qualification
The prior Determination may remain valid while requiring a new or revised qualification.
This creates:
Determination Confirmed with Qualification
rather than silently altering the original Decision.
Determination Amendment
A Determination may be Amended where part of the Decision state or qualification changes without replacing the entire Determination.
The amendment shall preserve the prior state.
Amendment ≠ Historical Replacement.
Determination Replacement
A Determination may require replacement where the new governance state materially changes the correct Determination outcome.

The new Decision shall reference the replaced Decision.
Replacement ≠ Erasure.
Determination Deferral after Reconsideration
A previously positive or conditional Decision may become Deferred where new information creates a material unresolved governance issue.
Prior Positive Determination ≠ Permanent Positive Determination.
Determination Rejection after Reconsideration
A previously determined Event may ultimately be rejected if new governance establishes that the Event representation was invalid.
For example: duplicate Event; invalid Formation; invalid standalone Event after Merge; technical operation incorrectly treated as independent Event.
Reconsidered Rejection ≠ Legal Non-Taxability.
Determination Supersession
A new Determination may supersede a prior Decision.
Supersession shall preserve: prior Decision; effective sequence; reason for supersession; new Decision; traceability between them.
Supersession ≠ Deletion.
Reconsideration Inconclusive
Where reconsideration cannot establish a sufficiently governed outcome, the state may remain Inconclusive.
Further upstream governance or uncertainty resolution may be required.
Reconsideration ≠ Mandatory Definitive Outcome.
Prior-State Preservation
EDREM shall preserve every materially relevant prior Determination state.
This enables reconstruction of:
What was known
↓
What was determined
↓
What changed
↓
Why reconsideration occurred
↓
What the new Determination became
This lifecycle is central to TREGA™ governance integrity.

Effective-State Management
EDREM shall distinguish: historical Decision state; current effective Determination; pending reconsideration state; superseded Determination.
Historical State ≠ Current Effective State.
Reconsideration Timing
The time of reconsideration shall be distinct from: Event Time; original Decision Time; correction time; legal tax point.
Reconsideration Time ≠ Event Time.
Reconsideration Sequence
Repeated reconsiderations may occur.
For example:
Initial Determination
↓
First Reconsideration
↓
Amended Determination
↓
Second Reconsideration
↓
Superseded Determination
Each material state shall remain traceable.
Reconsideration Frequency
EDREM shall not reopen Determination unnecessarily.
Repeated reconsideration without material trigger may create governance instability.
Frequent Review ≠ Stronger Governance by default.
Reconsideration Stability
After reconsideration, the new Determination should achieve sufficient operational stability for downstream use.
Operational stability does not eliminate the possibility of later reconsideration.
Downstream Reliance Impact
Where downstream systems have already consumed the prior Determination, EDREM should produce a state indicating whether downstream reliance may be affected.
Possible states include: No Downstream Impact; Qualification Update Required; Determination Update Required; Prior Determination Withdrawal Required; Downstream Re-evaluation Required.
EDREM does not perform jurisdiction-specific tax recalculation.

Downstream Notification
A material reconsideration outcome should be capable of notifying downstream consumers that the effective TREGA™ Determination has changed.
The handoff should identify: prior Decision; new Decision; effective state; reason for change; relevant qualification.
Cross-System Reconsideration
The same Event may exist across multiple technical systems.
A reconsideration shall govern the Event Determination itself rather than create independent contradictory Determinations per system.
System Record Update ≠ Event Determination Reconsideration by default.
Cross-Organization Reconsideration
Several organizations may consume the same governed Event.
EDREM may support distribution of the revised Determination state without deciding each organization's legal tax treatment.
Cross-Border Reconsideration
New cross-border information may affect Location, Participation, Value Association, or Event Relationships.
EDREM may reconsider the Event Determination.
It does not reconsider Tax Jurisdiction itself.
Cross-Border Determination Reconsideration ≠ Tax Jurisdiction Reallocation.
Multi-Jurisdiction Continuity
A reconsidered TREGA™ Event may continue to support multiple jurisdictional evaluations.
The model becomes:
One Reconsidered Governed Event
↓
Multiple Updated Jurisdictional Evaluations
Each jurisdiction remains responsible for its own legal treatment.
Blockchain Reconsideration
Immutable ledger records do not make Event Determinations immutable.

Off-chain information may reveal: incorrect participant attribution; invalid Event Formation; duplicate Event representation; changed relationship interpretation.
Immutable Ledger ≠ Immutable Event Determination.
Smart-Contract Reconsideration
A smart contract may execute exactly as coded while the governed Event interpretation later changes.
Immutable Execution ≠ Immutable Determination.
AI-Agent Reconsideration
AI-agent Events may require reconsideration where: agent identity mapping changes; execution role is corrected; newly available logs alter Event Formation; Value Association changes; relationship governance is revised.
Agent Action History ≠ Determination Finality.
Automated Reconsideration
EDREM may be automated.
Automation shall not permit silent rewriting of prior Determinations.
An automated implementation shall preserve: trigger; prior Decision; new governance basis; scope; outcome; effective state; traceability.
Automated Reconsideration ≠ Automatic Historical Rewrite.
Reconsideration and Readiness
A material reconsideration may require return to EDRDM where the revised Event no longer satisfies readiness requirements.
EDREM shall not perform EDRDM functions itself.
Reconsideration ≠ Readiness Reassessment by default.
Reconsideration and Conditions
Changed Event governance may require EDCM conditions to be reevaluated.
EDREM may trigger that process but does not own condition evaluation.
Reconsideration ≠ Condition Re-evaluation Authority.

Reconsideration and Decision
EDDM owns the formal Determination Decision logic.
EDREM owns governance of reopening and transitioning from a prior Decision to a revised governed Decision state.
Initial Decision ≠ Reconsideration Decision Process.
Reconsideration and Uncertainty
EDUM may produce a Reconsideration Required state.
EDREM then governs the reconsideration process.
Uncertainty Trigger ≠ Reconsideration Outcome.
Reconsideration and Lifecycle Governance
EDREM governs reconsideration within TREDS.
Once the Determination is finalized, TREGS governs the Event Record and TRECLS governs longer-term Event continuity, amendment, correction, supersession, and closure.
Determination Reconsideration ≠ Event Lifecycle Governance.
Reconsideration and Taxability
A tax authority or tax engine may later reinterpret the legal treatment of an Event.
That does not automatically require TREGA™ reconsideration unless the underlying Event governance changes.
Changed Tax Treatment ≠ Event Determination Reconsideration by default.
Reconsideration and Tax Jurisdiction
A jurisdiction may change its legal nexus or sourcing rules.
That legal change does not itself alter TREGA™ Event Determination.
Tax Jurisdiction Change ≠ Event Determination Change by default.
Reconsideration and Taxpayer
A legal conclusion about taxpayer identity does not redefine TREGA™ Participation unless new operational facts emerge.
Taxpayer Reclassification ≠ Participation Reconsideration by default.

Reconsideration and Tax Base
A later Tax Base adjustment does not automatically alter Event Determination.
Tax Base Adjustment ≠ Event Determination Reconsideration by default.
Governance States
EDREM may represent:
Reconsideration Not Initiated
Potential Trigger Identified
Trigger Under Review
Trigger Not Material
Material Trigger Confirmed
Reconsideration Initiated
Reconsideration Scope Defined
Upstream Review Required
Determination Under Reconsideration
Determination Confirmed
Determination Confirmed with Qualification
Determination Amended
Determination Replaced
Determination Deferred
Determination Rejected
Determination Superseded
Reconsideration Inconclusive
Further Governance Required
Downstream Update Required
Reconsideration Completed
Final TREDS Determination State Established Governance Requirements

EDREM implementations shall ensure that: reconsideration begins only from an existing Determination; triggers are distinguishable from ordinary new information; triggers are evaluated for legitimacy and materiality; preferred tax outcome is not a valid reconsideration basis; reconsideration initiation does not cancel the prior historical Decision; reconsideration scope is bounded to materially affected areas; changed upstream governance remains governed by its authoritative Parent Standard; Merge and Split do not automatically transfer prior Determinations; duplicate-event correction preserves history; resolved uncertainty does not automatically produce Positive Determination; newly material uncertainty can reopen a Decision; conflict resolution does not automatically require Decision change; clerical correction remains distinct from full reconsideration; confirmation, amendment, replacement, deferral, rejection, and supersession remain distinct states; prior Decision history is preserved; current effective state remains distinguishable from historical state; reconsideration time remains distinct from Event Time; repeated reconsideration requires material basis; downstream impact can be represented; downstream consumers can receive updated Determination state; immutable technical infrastructure does not make Event Determination immutable; automated reconsideration does not silently rewrite history; EDRDM, EDCM, EDDM, and EDUM ownership boundaries remain preserved; tax-law cha

not make Event Determination immutable; automated reconsideration does not silently rewrite history; EDRDM, EDCM, EDDM, and EDUM ownership boundaries remain preserved; tax-law changes do not automatically trigger TREGA™ reconsideration; and the final reconsidered Determination is suitable for handoff to TREGS.

Governance Logic
IF no existing Governed Event Determination Decision exists, THEN EDREM shall not initiate reconsideration.
IF new information is not materially relevant to the existing Determination, THEN reconsideration shall not be required.
IF a proposed trigger exists only because a different tax outcome is preferred, THEN the trigger shall be rejected.
IF a material upstream governance change could alter the Determination basis, THEN EDREM shall initiate or require reconsideration.
IF the new information confirms the original Decision basis, THEN the Determination may be Confirmed.
IF the original Decision remains valid but requires a bounded qualification, THEN the Determination may be Confirmed with Qualification.
IF part of the Decision must change while the Determination remains substantially continuous, THEN the Determination may be Amended.
IF the original Decision no longer represents the governed Event correctly, THEN a Replacement Determination shall be established.
IF material governance remains unresolved, THEN the reconsidered Determination may become Deferred.
IF new governance establishes that the apparent Event should not have been determined as a standalone Tax-Relevant Event, THEN the Determination may be Rejected or Superseded as appropriate.
IF a Merge or Split materially changes Event structure, THEN prior Determinations shall not transfer automatically.

IF reconsideration cannot establish a sufficiently governed outcome, THEN the state shall remain Inconclusive or Further Governance Required.
IF a new Determination supersedes a prior Decision, THEN the historical Decision shall remain traceable.
IF downstream systems relied on the prior Decision and the reconsidered outcome materially changes it, THEN Downstream Update Required shall be established.
IF reconsideration is completed, THEN EDREM shall establish the Final TREDS Determination State for TREGS.
Minimum Implementation Framework
A minimum EDREM implementation should support:
Reconsideration Identifier A stable identifier for the reconsideration process.
Governed Event Reference The Event whose Determination is under reconsideration.
Existing Determination Reference The prior EDDM/TREDS Determination Decision.
Existing Determination State The effective Decision before reconsideration.
Reconsideration Trigger Identifier A stable reference to the triggering change or discovery.
Trigger Type Correction, New Information, Uncertainty Resolution, New Uncertainty, Conflict Resolution, New Conflict, Merge, Split, Duplicate Discovery, Upstream Change, Decision Error, or other governed type.
Trigger Source Reference The governance layer, system, Event, or source producing the trigger.
Trigger Legitimacy State Valid, Invalid, or Under Review.
Trigger Materiality State Immaterial, Material, Critical, or Unresolved.

Reconsideration Scope The Decision dimension or Event structure affected.
Affected Governance Layer Any upstream TREGA™ Parent Standard affected.
Prior Readiness Reference Relevant EDRDM state where required.
Prior Condition Reference Relevant EDCM state where required.
Prior Decision Basis Reference The basis of the earlier EDDM Decision.
Prior Uncertainty Reference Relevant EDUM uncertainty state.
Updated Governance Reference The new or corrected governance information.
Merge / Split Reference Where structural Event transformation triggered reconsideration.
Duplicate Event Reference Where duplicate representation is involved.
Reconsideration Outcome Confirmed, Confirmed with Qualification, Amended, Replaced, Deferred, Rejected, Superseded, Inconclusive, or Further Governance Required.
Updated Determination Qualification Any qualification attached to the reconsidered state.
Reconsideration Rationale The governance basis for the outcome.
Prior State Preservation Reference The record linking the reconsidered state to historical Determination.
Effective Determination State The currently operative TREDS Determination after reconsideration.
Supersession Reference The relationship between prior and superseding Determinations.
Downstream Impact State No Impact, Qualification Update Required, Determination Update Required, Withdrawal Required, or Downstream Re-evaluation Required.

Downstream Notification State Whether relevant consumers have been notified of the changed Determination.
Reconsideration Time The time the reconsideration outcome was established.
Traceability Reference Information required to reconstruct the full reconsideration process.
Governance State The current EDREM governance state.
Handoff State Whether the final TREDS Determination is ready for TREGS.
Governance Outputs
EDREM may produce: Reconsideration Trigger Record; Trigger Legitimacy State; Trigger Materiality State; Reconsideration Scope; Updated Governance Reference; Determination Confirmation; Confirmation with Qualification; Determination Amendment; Determination Replacement; Determination Deferral; Determination Rejection; Determination Supersession; Reconsideration Inconclusive State; Further Governance Requirement; Prior-State Preservation Record; Effective Determination State; Downstream Impact State; Downstream Update Requirement; Reconsideration Traceability Record; and the principal output: Final TREDS Determination State.
Critical Distinctions
Determination Reconsideration ≠ Historical Erasure.
Existing Decision ≠ Immutable Decision.
New Information ≠ Automatic Reconsideration Trigger.
Preferred Tax Outcome ≠ Reconsideration Basis.
Changed Information ≠ Material Change by default.
Reconsideration Initiation ≠ Prior Decision Cancellation.
Local Change ≠ Full Determination Reopening by default.
Changed Basis ≠ Changed Decision by default.

Changed Formation ≠ Automatic Continuity of Prior Determination.
Changed Boundary ≠ Same Determination by default.
Corrected Event Time ≠ Legal Tax Point Reconsideration.
Location Reconsideration ≠ Jurisdiction Reconsideration.
Participant Reconsideration ≠ Taxpayer Reconsideration.
Value Reconsideration ≠ Tax Base Recalculation.
Merged Determinations ≠ One Determination by automatic inheritance.
One Prior Determination ≠ Multiple Valid Determinations after Split.
Duplicate Determination Correction ≠ Historical Deletion.
Resolved Uncertainty ≠ Automatic Positive Determination.
Conflict Resolution ≠ Automatic Decision Change.
Clerical Correction ≠ Full Reconsideration by default.
Reconsidered and Confirmed ≠ Never Reconsidered.
Amendment ≠ Historical Replacement.
Replacement ≠ Erasure.
Prior Positive Determination ≠ Permanent Positive Determination.
Reconsidered Rejection ≠ Legal Non-Taxability.
Supersession ≠ Deletion.
Reconsideration ≠ Mandatory Definitive Outcome.
Historical State ≠ Current Effective State.
Reconsideration Time ≠ Event Time.
Frequent Review ≠ Stronger Governance by default.
System Record Update ≠ Event Determination Reconsideration by default.
Cross-Border Determination Reconsideration ≠ Tax Jurisdiction Reallocation.
Immutable Ledger ≠ Immutable Event Determination.
Immutable Execution ≠ Immutable Determination.
Automated Reconsideration ≠ Automatic Historical Rewrite.
Reconsideration ≠ Readiness Reassessment by default.

Reconsideration ≠ Condition Re-evaluation Authority.
Initial Decision ≠ Reconsideration Decision Process.
Uncertainty Trigger ≠ Reconsideration Outcome.
Determination Reconsideration ≠ Event Lifecycle Governance.
Changed Tax Treatment ≠ Event Determination Reconsideration by default.
Tax Jurisdiction Change ≠ Event Determination Change by default.
Taxpayer Reclassification ≠ Participation Reconsideration by default.
Tax Base Adjustment ≠ Event Determination Reconsideration by default.
Enterprise Application
EDREM provides the controlled mechanism for maintaining Determination integrity when reality, evidence, or upstream governance changes after a Decision has already been issued.
The canonical operational path is:
EDDM — Governed Event Determination Decision
→ EDUM — Governed Determination Uncertainty State
→ EDREM — Final TREDS Determination State
→ TREGS — Governed Tax-Relevant Event Record
This allows organizations to correct Determination without destroying historical governance or confusing Event reconsideration with retroactive tax-law reinterpretation. Use Case 1 — Marketplace Event Reconsidered After Event Merge
A marketplace originally governs two separate Events and EDDM issues a Positive Determination for each.
Later, additional operational evidence establishes that the two apparent Events were technical fragments of one economic Event.
TRERLS and ERLMM govern the Merge and create a revised Event structure.

EDREM identifies the Merge as a material reconsideration trigger.
The two earlier Determinations are preserved historically and superseded.
The merged Event is routed through the necessary TREDS governance and receives a new effective Determination state.
The prior Determinations are not deleted and are not automatically inherited by the merged Event. Use Case 2 — Autonomous Service Determination Confirmed After Uncertainty Resolution
An autonomous service Event received a Conditional Determination because the identity of one machine participant remained uncertain.
EDUM preserved the uncertainty and triggered reconsideration once new authenticated execution records became available.
TREPS updates the governed Participation state.
EDREM evaluates the change and determines that the new information confirms the original Event structure while removing the prior qualification.
The Determination becomes Confirmed without the previous Participation qualification.
The earlier Conditional Determination remains preserved in the Event's governance history.
Canonical Boundary

EDREM owns the governance of Determination reconsideration triggers, trigger legitimacy, materiality, reconsideration initiation, scope, upstream-change impact, uncertainty-resolution impact, conflict-resolution impact, correction impact, Merge/Split impact, confirmation, qualification, amendment, replacement, deferral, rejection, supersession, prior-state preservation, effective-state management, downstream impact, downstream update requirements, reconsideration traceability, and establishment of the Final TREDS Determination State.
EDREM does not perform Event Context, Recognition, Formation, Boundary, Timing, Location, Participation, Value Association, or Relationship governance.
It does not independently perform Determination Readiness, Determination Conditions, initial Determination Decision, or Determination Uncertainty governance.
It does not govern the broader Event lifecycle after TREDS; TREGS and TRECLS remain authoritative for Event Record Governance and Event Lifecycle & Continuity.
It does not determine legal taxability, Tax Jurisdiction, taxpayer status, Tax Base, Tax Rate, legal tax point, Tax Period, exemption, deduction, Tax Liability, filing obligation, collection, enforcement, or any other jurisdiction-specific legal tax consequence.
Its governance begins when a materially legitimate trigger places an existing Determination under reconsideration.

Its governance ends when the effective Final TREDS Determination State is established and ready for handoff to TREGS.
Canonical Handoff
EDUM — Governed Determination Uncertainty State
↓
EDREM — Final TREDS Determination State
↓
TREGS — Governed Tax-Relevant Event Record
Canonical Closing Statement
EDREM ensures that a Tax-Relevant Event Determination can evolve when governed reality changes without allowing the history of prior decisions to disappear.
A Determination may be confirmed, amended, replaced, deferred, rejected, or superseded — but every material transition must remain reconstructable.
Determination Reconsideration ≠ Historical Erasure.
Supersession ≠ Deletion.
Changed Tax Treatment ≠ Event Determination Reconsideration by default.

chunks.text:
OOF™ The Event Determination Uncertainty Module (EDUM) governs how uncertainty
The Event Determination Uncertainty Module (EDUM) governs how uncertainty
OOF™ Origin Open Foundation™
Independent Methodological Authority
Architecture Ecosystem: Structured Reality Standards™
Architecture Family: TREGA™ — Tax-Relevant Event Governance Architecture™
Parent Standard: TREDS — Tax-Relevant Event Determination Standard
Module: EDUM — Event Determination Uncertainty Module
Operational Layer: Event Determination Uncertainty Governance Layer
Category: Governance & Enforcement
Subcategory: Tax-Relevant Event Governance
Type: Core Module
Governed Space: Event Determination Uncertainty
Origin ID: TREGA-TREDS-EDUM-004
Version: 1.0
Status: Canonical · Open Standard
Effective Date: 2 September 2026
AI-Readable: Yes
Authority: OOF®
Protection: MIP® — Methodological Intellectual Property
Canonical Language: UCL — Universal Canonical Language
Canonical Definition
The Event Determination Uncertainty Module (EDUM) governs how uncertainty affecting a Governed Event Determination Decision is identified, classified, bounded, assessed for materiality, represented, qualified, escalated, monitored, and resolved or preserved before the Event proceeds to final Determination completion or reconsideration.
Its principal transition is:
Governed Event Determination Decision + Determination Uncertainty Indicators
↓
Determination Uncertainty Governance
↓
Governed Determination Uncertainty State

EDUM does not recreate Event Readiness, Determination Conditions, or the Determination Decision itself.
It governs what uncertainty means for that Decision.
Its foundational distinction is:
Determination Uncertainty ≠ Determination Failure.
Operational Role
A Determination Decision may be methodologically valid even where some uncertainty remains.
The critical governance question is not whether uncertainty exists.
It is:
Does the uncertainty materially undermine the Event Determination, and if so, how must that uncertainty affect the governed Decision state?
EDUM prevents two opposite failures: treating every uncertainty as fatal; ignoring material uncertainty merely to produce a definitive result.
Its role is to preserve a usable but honest Determination state.
Internal Module Flow
TREDS operates through:
EDRDM — Event Determination Readiness
↓
EDCM — Event Determination Conditions
↓
EDDM — Event Determination Decision
↓
EDUM — Event Determination Uncertainty
↓
EDREM — Event Determination Reconsideration
↓
Determined Tax-Relevant Event
EDUM receives the Governed Event Determination Decision from EDDM.
Its principal output is passed to EDREM where reconsideration becomes necessary.
Operational Transition
The canonical transition is:
Governed Event Determination Decision + Relevant Uncertainty Indicators
↓
Uncertainty Identification
↓
Classification
↓
Materiality Assessment
↓
Qualification / Escalation
↓
Governed Determination Uncertainty State
Possible outcomes include:

No Material Uncertainty
Bounded Uncertainty
Qualified Uncertainty
Material Uncertainty
Critical Uncertainty
Conflicted Uncertainty
Unresolved Uncertainty
Reconsideration Required Operational Space
EDUM governs: uncertainty identification; uncertainty source; uncertainty type; uncertainty scope; uncertainty materiality; uncertainty severity; bounded uncertainty; residual uncertainty; structural uncertainty; factual uncertainty; relationship uncertainty; participation uncertainty; value uncertainty; location uncertainty; timing uncertainty; uncertainty interaction; uncertainty accumulation; uncertainty conflict; uncertainty qualification; uncertainty escalation; uncertainty tolerance; uncertainty threshold; uncertainty traceability; uncertainty reassessment; uncertainty persistence; and uncertainty handoff.
Operational Scope
EDUM may govern uncertainty affecting Events arising from: commerce; marketplaces; banking; payments; ERP environments; digital platforms; blockchain systems; smart contracts; AI agents; autonomous systems; industrial systems; energy infrastructure; distributed systems; machine-to-machine environments; cross-border activity; multi-party economic structures; and future machine economies.
The uncertainty-governance logic remains technology-neutral and jurisdiction-neutral.
Determination Uncertainty
Determination Uncertainty is uncertainty that may affect the reliability, qualification, interpretation, or continued validity of the Event Determination Decision.

It may arise from: incomplete upstream information; conflicting sources; bounded measurement limitations; unstable Event structure; ambiguous Participation; uncertain Value Association; uncertain Event Relationships; incomplete Location precision; timing ambiguity; or subsequent information.
Uncertainty Indicator ≠ Material Determination Uncertainty.
Uncertainty Identification
EDUM shall identify uncertainty that remains materially relevant after EDDM has issued or proposed a Determination Decision.
Uncertainty shall be distinguishable from: missing data; conflict; error; unresolved governance; condition failure; or mere lack of precision.
These states may overlap, but they are not identical.
Uncertainty Source
The source of uncertainty should be identifiable where possible.
Sources may include: Event Context; Event Formation; Event Boundary; Event Timing; Event Location; Event Participation; Value Association; Event Relationships; system interoperability; incomplete records; distributed execution; machine inference; model estimation; or contradictory operational sources.
EDUM governs the uncertainty impact.
It does not seize ownership of the underlying governed space.
Uncertainty Type
EDUM may classify uncertainty as:
Factual Uncertainty Uncertainty over what happened.
Structural Uncertainty Uncertainty over the constitution or structure of the Event.
Identity Uncertainty Uncertainty over which governed Event is under consideration.

Boundary Uncertainty Uncertainty over Event scope.
Temporal Uncertainty Uncertainty over Event timing.
Location Uncertainty Uncertainty over Event location.
Participation Uncertainty Uncertainty over actor participation.
Value Uncertainty Uncertainty over Event–Value Association.
Relationship Uncertainty Uncertainty over relationships among Events.
Decision Uncertainty Uncertainty affecting the validity or qualification of the Determination Decision itself.
Uncertainty Scope
Uncertainty shall be bounded wherever possible.
EDUM should identify whether uncertainty affects: one attribute; one participant; one relationship; one Event segment; one Value Association; the entire Event; or the Determination Decision as a whole.
Local Uncertainty ≠ Global Event Uncertainty by default.
Uncertainty Materiality
The central EDUM question is whether uncertainty is materially significant to Event Determination.
Uncertainty is material where it could materially change: Event Identity; Event Formation; Event Boundary; Determination status; Event count; participant structure; Value Association; relationship structure; or downstream interpretability.
Uncertainty Presence ≠ Material Uncertainty.
Immaterial Uncertainty
Immaterial uncertainty may remain without invalidating the Decision.
For example, minor imprecision in a non-material technical attribute may not affect Event Determination.
EDUM shall avoid transforming trivial imperfection into unnecessary governance failure.

Imprecision ≠ Material Uncertainty by default.
Bounded Uncertainty
Bounded Uncertainty exists where uncertainty remains but its scope and potential impact are sufficiently understood.
A bounded uncertainty may be compatible with a Positive or Conditional Determination.
Bounded Uncertainty ≠ Ungoverned Uncertainty.
Residual Uncertainty
Residual Uncertainty is uncertainty that remains after reasonable governance has been completed.
Its existence may be acceptable where: it is known; bounded; materially limited; traceable; and does not invalidate the Event structure.
Residual Uncertainty ≠ Governance Failure.
Material Uncertainty
Material Uncertainty exists where the uncertainty could materially alter the meaning or validity of the Event Determination.
This may require: Decision qualification; Decision deferral; escalation; upstream referral; or reconsideration.
Critical Uncertainty
Critical Uncertainty exists where Event Determination cannot be responsibly relied upon without further governance.
Examples may include uncertainty over: whether the Event exists; whether one or several Events exist; which Event Boundary applies; whether the principal participant is correctly associated; or whether the Value Association belongs to another Event.
Critical Uncertainty ≠ Permission to Maintain an Unqualified Decision.
Uncertainty Severity
EDUM may govern uncertainty severity through states such as:
Low
Moderate
Material
High
Critical

Severity shall reflect governance impact rather than arbitrary scoring.
Higher Score ≠ Greater Materiality by default.
Uncertainty Confidence
Confidence may be recorded as supporting information.
However:
Confidence ≠ Certainty.
and:
Confidence Score ≠ Determination Validity.
A high-confidence model output may still be methodologically unsupported.
Uncertainty Qualification
Where uncertainty does not invalidate the Decision but materially limits its interpretation, EDUM may attach an explicit qualification.
Qualification may specify: affected governance dimension; uncertainty scope; known limitation; potential Decision impact; required downstream caution; reassessment condition.
Qualification ≠ Concealment of Uncertainty.
Uncertainty Interaction
Multiple small uncertainties may interact and create material combined impact.
For example: moderate Location uncertainty; moderate Participation uncertainty; moderate Value uncertainty
may together undermine downstream interpretability.
EDUM shall therefore consider cumulative impact where material.
Several Immaterial Uncertainties ≠ Automatically Immaterial in Combination.
Uncertainty Accumulation
Uncertainty may accumulate across Event governance layers.
EDUM shall identify whether cumulative uncertainty has reached a threshold where the Determination Decision requires qualification or reconsideration.
Uncertainty and Conflict
Uncertainty and conflict shall remain distinct.
Uncertainty means the correct state is not fully known.

Conflict means materially relevant sources support incompatible states.
Uncertainty ≠ Conflict.
A Determination may contain both.
Conflicted Uncertainty
Where uncertainty exists because authoritative inputs conflict, EDUM may establish a Conflicted Uncertainty state.
It shall preserve: competing positions; source references; material effect; unresolved status.
Conflict Resolution by Convenience ≠ Governed Uncertainty Resolution.
Uncertainty Tolerance
A governed system may define tolerance for bounded uncertainty.
Tolerance shall be based on Event-governance materiality.
It shall not be determined solely by: commercial pressure; reporting deadlines; tax advantage; processing cost; system limitations.
Operational Pressure ≠ Uncertainty Tolerance Criterion.
Uncertainty Threshold
EDUM may establish thresholds determining when uncertainty requires: qualification; escalation; Decision deferral; upstream referral; or reconsideration.
Thresholds shall remain methodological rather than jurisdiction-specific tax thresholds.
Uncertainty Escalation
Escalation may be required where: uncertainty is critical; uncertainty cannot be bounded; material conflict remains unresolved; automated evaluation cannot reliably classify impact; or downstream reliance would be unsafe.
Escalation does not itself resolve the uncertainty.
Upstream Referral
Where uncertainty originates in an upstream governed space, EDUM may route the substantive issue to the authoritative Parent Standard.

Typical routing includes:
Context
↓
TRECS
Recognition
↓
TRERS
Formation
↓
TREFS
Boundary
↓
TREBS
Timing
↓
TRETS
Location
↓
TRELS
Participation
↓
TREPS
Value Association
↓
TRVAS
Event Relationships
↓
TRERLS
EDUM governs the Determination impact of the uncertainty.
The authoritative upstream layer governs the underlying issue.
Uncertainty and Readiness
EDRDM may already identify uncertainty affecting Readiness.
EDUM does not repeat that function.
At EDUM level, the question is whether uncertainty affects an existing Determination Decision.
Readiness Uncertainty ≠ Determination Uncertainty.
Uncertainty and Conditions
EDCM may identify uncertainty attached to individual Determination Conditions.
EDUM evaluates the consolidated impact on the Determination Decision.
Condition Uncertainty ≠ Determination-Level Uncertainty by default.
Uncertainty and Decision
EDDM establishes the Decision.
EDUM governs how uncertainty qualifies, constrains, destabilizes, or preserves that Decision.
Uncertainty Governance ≠ Decision Issuance.
Uncertainty and Reconsideration
EDUM may conclude that uncertainty is significant enough to trigger reconsideration.
EDREM owns the reconsideration process.
Reconsideration Trigger ≠ Reconsideration Decision.
Uncertainty and Correction
An uncertainty is not automatically an error.
Correction is appropriate where a governed state is known to be wrong.
Uncertainty exists where the correct state remains insufficiently established.
Uncertainty ≠ Error.

Uncertainty Persistence
Some uncertainty may persist legitimately over time.
Persistent uncertainty shall remain governed, visible, and traceable.
Persistent Uncertainty ≠ Permission to Ignore Uncertainty.
Uncertainty Resolution
Uncertainty may be resolved through: additional governance; better source information; corrected Event structure; participant clarification; Value reassociation; Event Relationship correction; reconciliation of conflicting sources; or later evidence.
Resolution shall preserve prior uncertainty history where material.
Uncertainty Reassessment
EDUM shall support reassessment when: new information appears; upstream governance changes; the Event is corrected; Merge or Split occurs; a conflict is resolved; or downstream reliance reveals material inconsistency.
Uncertainty Reassessment ≠ Historical Erasure.
Uncertainty State Supersession
A later uncertainty state may supersede an earlier one.
Historical states shall remain traceable.
Resolved Uncertainty ≠ Never-Existing Uncertainty.
Machine-Generated Uncertainty
Machine-generated Events may carry uncertainty resulting from: probabilistic classification; incomplete sensor data; inferred participation; distributed execution; asynchronous systems; model estimation.
Machine processing does not reduce the requirement for explicit uncertainty governance.
Machine Confidence ≠ Governed Certainty.
AI-Generated Uncertainty

AI systems may propose: Event classification; Event association; participant mapping; relationship interpretation; Value mapping.
Where such conclusions are probabilistic, EDUM shall preserve relevant uncertainty rather than convert probability into certainty automatically.
AI Probability ≠ Governed Determination Certainty.
Blockchain Uncertainty
Blockchain infrastructure may provide strong certainty about ledger state while leaving uncertainty about: off-chain Event Formation; participant role; Value meaning; legal or operational context; Event Relationship.
Therefore:
Ledger Certainty ≠ Event Determination Certainty.
Distributed-System Uncertainty
Distributed systems may contain: asynchronous timestamps; replicated records; delayed updates; differing system states; partial visibility.
EDUM shall evaluate their effect on the governed Decision rather than assuming technical inconsistency equals Event failure.
Cross-System Uncertainty
The same Event may appear differently across systems.
EDUM may classify whether those differences are: harmless representation differences; bounded uncertainty; material uncertainty; or conflict.
Representation Difference ≠ Event Uncertainty by default.
Cross-Organization Uncertainty
Different organizations may possess incomplete or inconsistent views of the same Event.
EDUM may govern the resulting Determination uncertainty without assigning accountability.
Cross-Border Uncertainty

Cross-border Events may contain uncertain operational location, participant roles, or distributed execution.
These uncertainties may affect Event governance.
They do not authorize EDUM to determine Tax Jurisdiction.
Cross-Border Uncertainty ≠ Tax Jurisdiction Determination.
Multi-Jurisdiction Neutrality
EDUM shall preserve uncertainty in jurisdiction-neutral Event terms.
A jurisdiction may later interpret the same uncertainty differently under law.
Determination Uncertainty ≠ Jurisdictional Tax Uncertainty.
Uncertainty and Taxability
EDUM does not govern uncertainty over legal tax interpretation.
It governs uncertainty over the Tax-Relevant Event Determination.
Event Determination Uncertainty ≠ Taxability Uncertainty.
Uncertainty and Taxpayer
Participant uncertainty may affect Event Determination.
EDUM does not determine taxpayer status.
Participant Uncertainty ≠ Taxpayer Determination.
Uncertainty and Tax Base
Value uncertainty may affect Event Determination.
EDUM does not calculate Tax Base.
Value Uncertainty ≠ Tax Base Determination.
Uncertainty and Legal Tax Point
Timing uncertainty may affect Event representation.
EDUM does not determine legal tax timing.
Temporal Uncertainty ≠ Legal Tax Point Determination.
Governance States
EDUM may represent:
Uncertainty Governance Not Initiated
Uncertainty Indicator Identified
Uncertainty Under Evaluation
No Material Uncertainty
Immaterial Uncertainty
Bounded Uncertainty
Residual Uncertainty
Qualified Uncertainty
Material Uncertainty

Critical Uncertainty
Ambiguous Uncertainty
Conflicted Uncertainty
Unresolved Uncertainty
Uncertainty Escalation Required
Upstream Referral Required
Uncertainty Reassessment Required
Reconsideration Required
Uncertainty Resolved
Governed Determination Uncertainty State Established Governance Requirements

EDUM implementations shall ensure that: uncertainty remains distinct from Determination failure; uncertainty indicators remain distinct from material uncertainty; uncertainty source is identifiable where possible; uncertainty type is distinguishable; uncertainty scope can be bounded where possible; materiality is explicitly assessed; immaterial uncertainty does not automatically invalidate the Decision; bounded uncertainty may be preserved without forcing false certainty; residual uncertainty remains visible; critical uncertainty cannot support an unqualified Decision; uncertainty severity reflects governance impact; confidence scores do not replace uncertainty governance; qualifications remain visible downstream; interacting uncertainties are evaluated where materially relevant; cumulative uncertainty can be represented; uncertainty remains distinguishable from conflict; conflicted uncertainty preserves competing governance states; operational pressure does not determine uncertainty tolerance; escalation remains available; upstream issues are referred to the authoritative governance layer; uncertainty does not recreate Readiness, Conditions, or Decision governance; reconsideration triggers remain distinct from reconsideration itself; uncertainty remains distinct from known error; persistent uncertainty remains governed; resolution preserves historical traceability; AI or machine probability does not become certainty automatically; blockchain finality does not eliminate off-c

inty remains governed; resolution preserves historical traceability; AI or machine probability does not become certainty automatically; blockchain finality does not eliminate off-chain Event uncertainty; cross-border uncertainty does not determine Tax Jurisdiction; and the resulting uncertainty state is suitable for EDREM or final TREDS completion.

Governance Logic
IF an uncertainty indicator exists, THEN EDUM shall evaluate its scope and materiality before modifying the Determination state.
IF uncertainty is immaterial to Event Identity, structure, or downstream interpretability, THEN the Determination Decision may remain unchanged.
IF uncertainty is bounded and materially limited, THEN the Decision may remain valid with an explicit uncertainty qualification.
IF several individually limited uncertainties combine into a material Determination risk, THEN EDUM shall govern their cumulative effect rather than evaluate them only in isolation.
IF uncertainty materially undermines Event Identity, Formation, Boundary, Participation, Value Association, or Event Relationships, THEN the Decision shall be qualified, escalated, deferred, or referred for reconsideration as appropriate.
IF uncertainty results from conflicting materially relevant sources, THEN EDUM shall preserve the conflict rather than select the most convenient representation.
IF the underlying uncertainty belongs to an upstream TREGA™ governed space, THEN EDUM shall preserve Determination impact and refer the substantive issue to the authoritative layer.
IF uncertainty cannot be sufficiently bounded and downstream reliance would be materially unsafe, THEN Reconsideration Required shall be established.
IF new information resolves the uncertainty, THEN the new uncertainty state shall supersede the prior state without erasing historical uncertainty.

IF the Determination Decision remains sufficiently reliable after uncertainty governance, THEN EDUM shall establish the Governed Determination Uncertainty State for downstream TREDS processing.
Minimum Implementation Framework
A minimum EDUM implementation should support:
Uncertainty Governance Identifier A stable identifier for the uncertainty-governance process.
Governed Event Reference The Event affected by uncertainty.
Determination Decision Reference The EDDM Decision under uncertainty governance.
Uncertainty Identifier A stable identifier for each uncertainty.
Uncertainty Source The governance layer, system, record, process, or condition from which uncertainty arises.
Uncertainty Type Factual, Structural, Identity, Boundary, Temporal, Location, Participation, Value, Relationship, Decision, or other governed type.
Uncertainty Scope The part of the Event or Decision affected.
Uncertainty Materiality State Immaterial, Bounded, Material, Critical, or Unresolved.
Uncertainty Severity State The relative governance impact.
Uncertainty Confidence Reference Any supporting confidence or probability measure where used.
Affected Governance Dimension The Event governance area influenced by the uncertainty.
Decision Impact State No Impact, Qualification Required, Escalation Required, Deferral Required, or Reconsideration Required.
Uncertainty Qualification Any explicit limitation attached to the Determination Decision.

Cumulative Uncertainty Reference Any interaction with other uncertainty states.
Conflict Reference Any materially conflicting governance source.
Upstream Referral Reference Any referral to another TREGA™ Parent Standard.
Uncertainty Tolerance State Whether the uncertainty remains within an acceptable governance tolerance.
Uncertainty Resolution State Unresolved, Partially Resolved, Resolved, or Persistent.
Resolution Basis Reference The basis for any uncertainty resolution.
Prior Uncertainty State Any earlier governed uncertainty state.
Reassessment Reference Any later uncertainty reassessment.
Reconsideration Trigger State Whether EDREM review is required.
Uncertainty Traceability Reference Information required to reconstruct the uncertainty assessment.
Governance State The current EDUM governance state.
Handoff State Whether the Event may proceed to EDREM or final TREDS completion.
Governance Outputs

EDUM may produce: Uncertainty Identification Record; Uncertainty Source Record; Uncertainty Classification; Uncertainty Scope; Materiality State; Severity State; Bounded Uncertainty State; Residual Uncertainty State; Material Uncertainty State; Critical Uncertainty State; Conflicted Uncertainty State; Uncertainty Qualification; Cumulative Uncertainty State; Decision Impact State; Upstream Referral; Uncertainty Escalation; Uncertainty Reassessment Record; Uncertainty Resolution Record; Reconsideration Trigger; Uncertainty Traceability Record; and the principal output: Governed Determination Uncertainty State.
Critical Distinctions
Determination Uncertainty ≠ Determination Failure.
Uncertainty Indicator ≠ Material Determination Uncertainty.
Local Uncertainty ≠ Global Event Uncertainty by default.
Uncertainty Presence ≠ Material Uncertainty.
Imprecision ≠ Material Uncertainty by default.
Bounded Uncertainty ≠ Ungoverned Uncertainty.
Residual Uncertainty ≠ Governance Failure.
Critical Uncertainty ≠ Permission to Maintain an Unqualified Decision.
Confidence ≠ Certainty.
Confidence Score ≠ Determination Validity.
Qualification ≠ Concealment of Uncertainty.
Several Immaterial Uncertainties ≠ Automatically Immaterial in Combination.
Uncertainty ≠ Conflict.
Conflict Resolution by Convenience ≠ Governed Uncertainty Resolution.
Operational Pressure ≠ Uncertainty Tolerance Criterion.
Readiness Uncertainty ≠ Determination Uncertainty.

Condition Uncertainty ≠ Determination-Level Uncertainty by default.
Uncertainty Governance ≠ Decision Issuance.
Reconsideration Trigger ≠ Reconsideration Decision.
Uncertainty ≠ Error.
Persistent Uncertainty ≠ Permission to Ignore Uncertainty.
Uncertainty Reassessment ≠ Historical Erasure.
Resolved Uncertainty ≠ Never-Existing Uncertainty.
Machine Confidence ≠ Governed Certainty.
AI Probability ≠ Governed Determination Certainty.
Ledger Certainty ≠ Event Determination Certainty.
Representation Difference ≠ Event Uncertainty by default.
Cross-Border Uncertainty ≠ Tax Jurisdiction Determination.
Determination Uncertainty ≠ Jurisdictional Tax Uncertainty.
Event Determination Uncertainty ≠ Taxability Uncertainty.
Enterprise Application
EDUM provides the uncertainty-control layer between formal Event Determination and later reconsideration or final downstream use.
A canonical enterprise path is:
EDCM — Governed Determination Condition State
→ EDDM — Governed Event Determination Decision
→ EDUM — Governed Determination Uncertainty State
→ EDREM — Event Determination Reconsideration Governance
→ Determined Tax-Relevant Event
This enables systems to preserve usable Determination results while exposing the exact uncertainty that remains rather than forcing every Event into a misleading binary state. Use Case 1 — Distributed Digital Service with Bounded Location Uncertainty

A distributed digital service has stable Formation, Boundary, Participation, Value Association, and Event Relationship governance.
EDDM issues a Positive Determination.
However, infrastructure execution occurred across several geographically distributed systems and the exact operational Location of one component cannot be established with full precision.
EDUM determines that the Location uncertainty is bounded and does not alter Event Identity or prevent downstream jurisdiction-specific analysis.
The Determination remains valid with an explicit Bounded Location Uncertainty qualification.
EDUM does not determine which jurisdiction may tax the Event. Use Case 2 — Autonomous Settlement with Material Participation Uncertainty
An autonomous settlement Event receives a provisional Determination Decision.
Two materially authoritative systems disagree over which autonomous participant executed the decisive settlement function.
The uncertainty could materially change the governed Participation structure and downstream interpretation.
EDUM classifies the uncertainty as Material and Conflicted, preserves both participant representations, refers the substantive Participation issue to TREPS, and establishes Reconsideration Required.
The module does not select the participant that produces the preferred tax result.
Canonical Boundary

EDUM owns the governance of Determination-level uncertainty identification, source, classification, scope, materiality, severity, bounded uncertainty, residual uncertainty, cumulative uncertainty, conflict interaction, qualification, tolerance, escalation, persistence, reassessment, resolution, traceability, and Determination-level reconsideration triggers.
EDUM does not perform Event Readiness governance, Determination Condition governance, Determination Decision issuance, or Determination Reconsideration itself.
It does not recreate Event Context, Recognition, Formation, Boundary, Timing, Location, Participation, Value Association, or Event Relationships.
It does not determine legal taxability, Tax Jurisdiction, taxpayer status, legal tax point, Tax Period, Tax Base, Tax Rate, Tax Liability, exemption, deduction, filing obligation, or any other jurisdiction-specific tax consequence.
Its governance begins when a Governed Event Determination Decision contains or encounters materially relevant uncertainty.
Its governance ends when uncertainty has been sufficiently governed for continued reliance, qualification, escalation, or handoff to EDREM.
Canonical Handoff
EDDM — Governed Event Determination Decision
↓
EDUM — Governed Determination Uncertainty State
↓
EDREM — Event Determination Reconsideration Governance
Canonical Closing Statement
EDUM ensures that uncertainty is governed according to its material impact rather than hidden, exaggerated, or converted into false certainty.

A Determination may remain valid while uncertainty exists, but only when that uncertainty is understood, bounded, visible, and compatible with continued reliance.
Determination Uncertainty ≠ Determination Failure.
Uncertainty ≠ Error.
