chunks.text:
OOF™ The Event Relationship Identification Module (ERLIM) governs how
The Event Relationship Identification Module (ERLIM) governs how
OOF™ Origin Open Foundation™
Independent Methodological Authority
Architecture Ecosystem: Structured Reality Standards™
Architecture Family: TREGA™ — Tax-Relevant Event Governance Architecture™
Parent Standard: TRERLS — Tax-Relevant Event Relationship Standard
Module: ERLIM — Event Relationship Identification Module
Operational Layer: Event Relationship Identification Governance Layer
Category: Governance & Enforcement
Subcategory: Tax-Relevant Event Governance
Type: Core Module
Governed Space: Event Relationship Identification
Origin ID: TREGA-TRERLS-ERLIM-001
Version: 1.0
Status: Canonical · Open Standard
Effective Date: 1 September 2026
AI-Readable: Yes
Authority: OOF®
Protection: MIP® — Methodological Intellectual Property
Canonical Language: UCL — Universal Canonical Language
Canonical Definition
The Event Relationship Identification Module (ERLIM) governs how materially relevant relationships among already-governed Tax-Relevant Events are discovered, screened, distinguished, qualified, and admitted into Event Relationship governance.
ERLIM determines whether sufficient indications exist that two or more governed events may possess a relationship requiring further governance under TRERLS.
Its principal transition is:
Governed Value-Associated Events
↓
Event Relationship Identification
↓
Governed Event Relationship Candidate Set

ERLIM does not determine the final type, dependency structure, sequence, grouping, merge, or split of the relationship.
It identifies which events require relationship governance.
The foundational distinction is:
Relationship Indicator ≠ Established Event Relationship.
Operational Role
Modern systems may contain thousands or millions of governed events.
It is neither methodologically valid nor operationally efficient to assume that every event relates to every other event.
At the same time, important relationships may be missed when systems consider events only as isolated records.
ERLIM provides the entry mechanism into TRERLS.
It identifies potentially meaningful Event Relationships based on governed information such as: shared context; shared participants; shared value; operational linkage; temporal proximity; common source structures; contractual association; technical references; settlement linkage; reversal references; machine-generated relationships; or other materially relevant indicators.
These indicators initiate relationship governance.
They do not complete it.
Relationship Discovery ≠ Relationship Determination.
Internal Module Flow
TRERLS operates through:
ERLIM — Event Relationship Identification
↓
ERLDM — Event Relationship Dependency
↓
ERLSM — Event Relationship Sequence
↓
ERLGM — Event Relationship Grouping
↓
ERLMM — Event Relationship Merge & Split
↓
Governed Event Relationship Structure
ERLIM is the entry point.

Its output becomes the governed candidate structure consumed by ERLDM and subsequent TRERLS modules.
Operational Transition
The canonical ERLIM transition is:
One or More Governed Value-Associated Events + Relationship Indicators
↓
Relationship Identification Governance
↓
Governed Event Relationship Candidate Set
The output establishes that relationship governance is warranted.
It does not establish the final relationship structure.
Operational Space
ERLIM governs: relationship candidate discovery; event-pair identification; multi-event candidate identification; relationship-indicator identification; indicator differentiation; shared-context screening; shared-participant screening; shared-value screening; temporal-proximity screening; operational-linkage screening; technical-reference screening; contractual-link screening; settlement-link screening; reversal and correction reference screening; cross-system relationship discovery; cross-organization relationship discovery; machine-generated relationship discovery; duplicate candidate detection; candidate inclusion; candidate exclusion; candidate qualification; candidate uncertainty; candidate conflict; and relationship-governance readiness.
Operational Scope

ERLIM may identify potential Event Relationships across: commerce; banking; payments; ERP systems; accounting infrastructure; marketplaces; logistics; supply chains; digital platforms; blockchain systems; smart contracts; digital assets; industrial infrastructure; energy systems; AI agents; autonomous systems; machine-to-machine environments; cross-border operations; and other governed economic or operational systems.
The technology generating the event does not determine whether a relationship exists.
Relationship Candidate
A Relationship Candidate is a governed indication that two or more events may possess a materially relevant relationship requiring further TRERLS governance.
A candidate may be created because one or more relationship indicators are present.
However:
Relationship Candidate ≠ Established Event Relationship.
Candidate status means the relationship deserves governance.
It does not mean the relationship has already been proven.
Eligible Events
ERLIM operates on already-governed events.
An occurrence that has not entered sufficient TREGA™ governance shall not become an Event Relationship merely because another record refers to it.
Referenced Occurrence ≠ Governed Related Event by default.
Where ERLIM discovers information indicating a possible ungoverned event, that issue should be referred to the relevant upstream TREGA™ governance layer.
Event Pair Identification
The simplest relationship candidate involves two events.
The structure is:
Event A ↔ Event B

ERLIM identifies whether sufficient indicators exist to place the pair under relationship governance.
It does not determine the final direction or type of relationship.
Multi-Event Candidate Identification
Relationships may involve more than two events.
ERLIM shall support candidate structures such as:
Event A ↔ Event B ↔ Event C
or broader multi-event candidate sets.
Relationship Identification ≠ Pairwise-Only Governance.
Complex activity may require several events to enter governance together.
Relationship Indicator
A Relationship Indicator is information suggesting that events may possess a meaningful relationship.
Indicators may include: common participants; common value; common context; temporal proximity; shared source references; operational dependencies; process linkage; contractual linkage; common settlement; reversal references; replacement references; machine instructions; smart-contract references; or other governed information.
Indicator Presence ≠ Relationship Proof.
Multiple Indicators
Several indicators may support the same Relationship Candidate.
For example:
Shared Participant + Shared Value + Temporal Proximity + Common Order Reference
may provide stronger reason for relationship governance than any single indicator.
However:
More Indicators ≠ Established Relationship by default.
Indicator quantity and indicator quality are separate considerations.
Shared Context Screening

Events occurring within the same governed Event Context may warrant relationship evaluation.
However:
Shared Event Context ≠ Established Event Relationship.
Thousands of independent events may occur within the same commercial or operational context.
TRECS remains authoritative for Event Context.
Shared Participant Screening
Events involving the same participant may warrant relationship evaluation.
Examples may include the same: customer; supplier; platform; bank; AI agent; autonomous machine; organization; or service provider.
However:
Same Participant ≠ Related Event by default.
TREPS remains authoritative for Event Participation.
Shared Value Screening
Events associated with the same governed value, Value Reference, Value Change, or Value State may warrant relationship evaluation.
For example, one payment may relate to several purchases.
A refund may reference value associated with an earlier event.
An asset may participate in several events.
However:
Shared Value ≠ Established Event Relationship by default.
TRVAS remains authoritative for Value Association.
Temporal Proximity Screening
Events occurring close together in time may warrant relationship evaluation.
However:
Temporal Proximity ≠ Event Relationship.
Two independent events may occur simultaneously.
Two strongly related events may occur months apart.
TRETS remains authoritative for Event Timing.
Shared Location Screening

Events occurring at the same physical, digital, or distributed location may warrant relationship evaluation.
However:
Same Location ≠ Event Relationship.
TRELS remains authoritative for Event Location.
Operational Linkage Screening
Operational systems may explicitly link events.
For example: an order references fulfillment; a refund references purchase; settlement references payment; machine execution references instruction; delivery references shipment; resource consumption references allocation.
These links may provide strong Relationship Indicators.
However:
Operational Link ≠ Governed Event Relationship by default.
The operational system may contain incomplete, incorrect, or technically convenient linkage.
Technical Reference Screening
Events may share technical identifiers.
Examples include: transaction IDs; session IDs; order IDs; invoice references; settlement IDs; API correlation IDs; ledger references; blockchain hashes; smart-contract identifiers; machine-job identifiers.
These references may support candidate identification.
However:
Shared Technical Reference ≠ Same Event.
and:
Shared Technical Reference ≠ Established Event Relationship by default.
Contractual Link Screening
Events may arise under the same contract or commercial arrangement.
This may be relevant to relationship identification.
However:
Same Contract ≠ Same Event.
and:
Same Contract ≠ Established Event Relationship by default.
A long-term agreement may produce thousands of independent events.

Invoice Link Screening
Several events may appear on one invoice.
One event may also appear across several invoice records.
Therefore:
Same Invoice ≠ Same Event.
Invoice linkage may become a Relationship Indicator but not a final Event Relationship determination.
Payment Link Screening
A payment may provide an important relationship indicator.
However: one payment may settle several events; several payments may settle one event; a payment may be unrelated to a nearby event; a later payment may settle an earlier activity.
Therefore:
Same Payment ≠ Same Event.
and:
Payment Link ≠ Established Event Relationship by default.
Settlement Link Screening
Settlement systems frequently aggregate multiple underlying activities.
A settlement reference may therefore identify a multi-event candidate structure.
One Settlement ≠ One Event by default.
ERLIM may admit the relevant events into relationship governance without deciding their eventual relationship structure.
Refund Reference Screening
A refund may explicitly refer to an earlier transaction.
This is a strong relationship indicator.
However, ERLIM does not determine whether the refund is: part of the original event; a separate related event; a reversal event; or another relationship structure.
That determination belongs downstream.
Refund Reference ≠ Relationship Type Determination.
Reversal Reference Screening
A reversal may explicitly reference an earlier event.
ERLIM may identify the two events as Relationship Candidates.

It does not determine the full reversal structure.
Reversal Reference ≠ Established Reversal Relationship.
Correction Reference Screening
A later event may refer to an earlier event as part of a correction.
ERLIM may admit that relationship into governance.
It does not determine whether the later activity represents correction, replacement, continuation, or another relationship type.
Common Source Screening
Two or more events may originate from a common operational source.
For example, one customer request may produce several events.
A machine instruction may generate several operational events.
A smart contract may trigger several executions.
A common source can therefore be relevant.
However:
Common Source ≠ Same Event by default.
Common Destination Screening
Several events may converge on the same operational destination.
For example, several commercial events may settle into one payment or resource pool.
This may create a Relationship Candidate.
Common Destination ≠ Event Merger.
Cross-System Relationship Discovery
Related events may exist in different systems.
For example:
Commerce Event
↓
Payment Event
↓
Banking Event
↓
Logistics Event
ERLIM shall support discovery across system boundaries.
Different Systems ≠ Independent Events by default.
Likewise:
Same System ≠ Related Events by default.
System architecture and Event Relationship architecture are separate.
Cross-Organization Relationship Discovery
Related events may be distributed across several organizations.

One organization may hold only part of the relationship information.
ERLIM may therefore use governed cross-organizational references where available.
Different Organizations ≠ Unrelated Events by default.
Cross-Border Relationship Discovery
Potentially related events may occur across different countries.
Geographic separation does not invalidate relationship candidacy.
Likewise, shared geography does not prove relationship.
Different Countries ≠ Unrelated Events.
Same Country ≠ Related Events by default.
ERLIM does not determine tax jurisdiction.
Blockchain Relationship Discovery
Blockchain systems may contain technical relationships through: transaction references; wallet interactions; smart-contract calls; token movements; bridge operations; settlement structures; or protocol execution.
ERLIM may use these as Relationship Indicators.
However:
On-Chain Link ≠ Governed Event Relationship by default.
and:
One Blockchain Transaction ≠ One Tax-Relevant Event by default.
Off-chain information may also be necessary.
AI-Agent Relationship Discovery
AI agents may initiate, coordinate, or respond to multiple governed events.
Agent-generated references may identify potential relationships.
For example:
Agent Instruction
↓
Resource Allocation Event
↓
Service Event
↓
Settlement Event
ERLIM may identify these as Relationship Candidates.
It does not determine dependency, sequence, or grouping.
Machine-to-Machine Relationship Discovery

Autonomous machines may exchange instructions, resources, services, energy, or value.
Machine-generated correlation data may support relationship discovery.
Machine Correlation ≠ Governed Event Relationship by default.
Machine-generated activity remains subject to the same governance requirements as human-mediated activity.
Direct Relationship Indicator
Some indicators explicitly connect two events.
Examples include: refund-of reference; correction-of reference; replacement-of reference; settlement-of reference.
These may constitute Direct Relationship Indicators.
However:
Direct Indicator ≠ Final Relationship Determination.
Indirect Relationship Indicator
Some relationships become visible only through intermediate information.
For example:
Event A
↓
Shared Value Reference
↓
Settlement Record
↓
Event B
ERLIM may identify an indirect candidate relationship.
Indirect Indicator ≠ Weak Relationship by default.
The quality of the relationship depends on the governed information, not merely on whether the indicator is direct.
Candidate Relevance
Not every detectable connection deserves continued governance.
ERLIM shall evaluate whether the potential relationship is materially relevant to Tax-Relevant Event governance.
A technically detectable but economically or operationally meaningless correlation may be excluded.
Detectable Connection ≠ Material Relationship Candidate.
Candidate Inclusion

A Relationship Candidate may be included where sufficient materially relevant indicators justify further TRERLS governance.
Inclusion means:
Further Relationship Governance Required.
It does not mean:
Relationship Established.
Candidate Exclusion
A potential relationship may be excluded where available information does not support material relevance.
Exclusion should remain traceable where materially important.
Candidate Exclusion ≠ Proof of Permanent Unrelatedness.
New information may justify reconsideration.
Duplicate Relationship Candidates
Multiple systems may independently identify the same potential relationship.
ERLIM shall support duplicate detection.
Multiple Candidate Records ≠ Multiple Relationships by default.
Duplicate consolidation shall preserve source traceability.
Candidate Overlap
Several Relationship Candidates may partially overlap.
For example: Candidate 1: Events A and B; Candidate 2: Events B and C; Candidate 3: Events A, B, and C.
ERLIM shall preserve these structures without prematurely deciding whether they form one group or network.
Grouping belongs to ERLGM.
Candidate Confidence
ERLIM may qualify confidence that further relationship governance is warranted.
Possible states may include:
High · Qualified · Limited · Ambiguous · Conflicted · Unresolved
Confidence applies to candidacy.
It does not represent final Relationship Confidence.
Candidate Ambiguity

Information may indicate that a relationship exists while leaving uncertainty about which events are involved.
For example, a payment may clearly settle one of several earlier events but available records may not identify which one.
ERLIM shall preserve that ambiguity.
Candidate Ambiguity ≠ Permission to Select a Convenient Event.
Candidate Conflict
Different systems may identify incompatible Relationship Candidates.
For example: ERP links settlement to Event A; bank metadata links it to Event B; marketplace records link it to Events A and B.
ERLIM shall preserve the conflict.
Candidate Conflict ≠ Permission for Convenient Relationship Selection.
Missing Relationship Information
Absence of an explicit relationship reference does not prove that events are unrelated.
No Explicit Link ≠ No Event Relationship.
ERLIM may use other governed indicators where appropriate.
Excessive Relationship Generation
Systems may generate large numbers of weak correlations.
ERLIM shall prevent indiscriminate admission of every detectable connection.
Correlation ≠ Relationship.
This is particularly important for large-scale AI, graph, banking, marketplace, and machine systems.
Relationship Identification and Event Formation
ERLIM identifies potential relationships among already-governed events.
It does not form new events.
Relationship Discovery ≠ New Event Formation.

Where relationship analysis reveals a possible previously unrecognized event, the matter shall be referred to TREFS and relevant upstream governance.
Relationship Identification and Event Boundary
ERLIM shall not alter Event Boundaries merely because two events appear strongly related.
Strong Relationship Indicator ≠ Shared Event Boundary.
TREBS remains authoritative.
Relationship Identification and Dependency
ERLIM may detect information suggesting dependency.
It does not govern dependency.
Dependency Indicator ≠ Governed Event Dependency.
ERLDM owns dependency governance.
Relationship Identification and Sequence
ERLIM may detect temporal or operational ordering.
It does not establish governed sequence.
Sequence Indicator ≠ Governed Event Sequence.
ERLSM owns sequence governance.
Relationship Identification and Grouping
ERLIM may identify several events that appear structurally connected.
It does not create an Event Group.
Multi-Event Candidate ≠ Event Group.
ERLGM owns grouping governance. Relationship Identification and Merge / Split
ERLIM may detect indications that event structure requires reconsideration.
It does not merge or split events.
Merge Indicator ≠ Governed Event Merge.
Split Indicator ≠ Governed Event Split.
ERLMM owns Merge & Split governance while respecting TREFS and TREBS boundaries.
Relationship Identification and Taxation
ERLIM shall not identify relationships based solely on a desired tax result.

A relationship must arise from governed operational or economic information.
Desired Tax Outcome ≠ Relationship Indicator.
ERLIM does not determine whether related events should be legally aggregated.
Relationship Candidate ≠ Tax Aggregation Candidate by default.
Governance States
ERLIM may represent:
Relationship Screening Ready
Relationship Screening Active
Potential Relationship Detected
Direct Relationship Indicator Detected
Indirect Relationship Indicator Detected
Multi-Event Candidate Detected
Relationship Candidate Qualified
Relationship Candidate Included
Relationship Candidate Excluded
Duplicate Relationship Candidate
Relationship Candidate Ambiguous
Relationship Candidate Conflicted
Relationship Candidate Unresolved
Governed Event Relationship Candidate Established Governance Requirements

ERLIM implementations shall ensure that: relationship identification operates on governed event references; Relationship Indicators remain distinct from established Event Relationships; event pairs and multi-event candidates can be represented; shared context can be screened without establishing Event Identity; shared participants can be screened without establishing Event Identity; shared value can be screened without establishing Event Identity; temporal proximity can be considered without being treated as proof; shared location can be considered without being treated as proof; operational and technical references can support candidacy; contractual, invoice, payment, and settlement links remain indicators rather than automatic conclusions; refund, reversal, and correction references can initiate governance; cross-system relationships can be discovered; cross-organization relationships can be discovered; cross-border relationships can be discovered; blockchain and machine-generated indicators can be consumed; direct and indirect indicators remain distinguishable; materially irrelevant correlations can be excluded; candidate inclusion and exclusion remain governable; duplicate candidates can be identified; candidate overlap can remain visible; ambiguity remains visible; conflict remains visible; missing explicit linkage does not automatically establish unrelatedness; Event Formation remains under TREFS; Event Boundary remains under TREBS; dependency remains under ERLDM; seque

sing explicit linkage does not automatically establish unrelatedness; Event Formation remains under TREFS; Event Boundary remains under TREBS; dependency remains under ERLDM; sequence remains under ERLSM; grouping remains under ERLGM; Merge & Split remains under ERLMM; and jurisdiction-specific tax interpretation remains downstream.

Governance Logic
IF two or more governed events possess one or more materially relevant Relationship Indicators, THEN ERLIM shall evaluate whether a Relationship Candidate should be established.
IF an indicator is merely technical and lacks material relationship relevance, THEN the candidate may be excluded.
IF multiple indicators support the same potential relationship, THEN those indicators may strengthen candidacy without establishing the final relationship.
IF multiple systems produce duplicate candidates, THEN duplication shall be identified without creating multiple Event Relationships.
IF the candidate remains ambiguous or conflicted, THEN the corresponding governance state shall remain visible.
IF relationship discovery suggests an ungoverned event may exist, THEN the matter shall be referred to appropriate upstream Event governance rather than creating the event within ERLIM.
IF indicators suggest dependency, sequence, grouping, merge, or split, THEN ERLIM shall preserve those indications for the appropriate downstream TRERLS module without determining them.
IF the candidate possesses sufficient material relevance, THEN it shall enter the Governed Event Relationship Candidate Set for downstream Relationship governance.
Minimum Implementation Framework
A minimum ERLIM implementation should support:
Primary Governed Event Reference The governed event from which relationship screening is performed.

Related Event Candidate Reference The other governed event potentially involved.
Relationship Candidate Identifier A stable identifier for the candidate relationship.
Candidate Cardinality Whether the candidate contains two or multiple events.
Relationship Indicator Type The category of information suggesting the relationship.
Relationship Indicator Reference The underlying governed reference supporting candidacy.
Indicator Source The system or governance source from which the indicator originates.
Indicator Directness Direct or indirect.
Shared Context Reference Where Event Context contributes to candidacy.
Shared Participant Reference Where Event Participation contributes to candidacy.
Shared Value Reference Where governed value contributes to candidacy.
Temporal Relationship Indicator Where Event Timing contributes to candidacy.
Location Relationship Indicator Where Event Location contributes to candidacy.
Operational Link Reference Where operational systems explicitly connect the events.
Technical Link Reference Where technical identifiers contribute to candidacy.
Candidate Material Relevance State Whether the potential relationship warrants further governance.
Duplicate State Whether the candidate duplicates another Relationship Candidate.
Candidate Confidence The qualified confidence that further relationship governance is warranted.
Ambiguity State Whether candidate membership or relevance remains ambiguous.

Conflict State Whether materially conflicting candidate information exists.
Inclusion / Exclusion State Whether the candidate enters further TRERLS governance.
Traceability Reference Information required to reconstruct the identification decision.
Governance State The current ERLIM state.
Handoff State Whether the candidate is ready for ERLDM.
Governance Outputs
ERLIM may produce: Event Pair Candidate; Multi-Event Relationship Candidate; Direct Relationship Indicator; Indirect Relationship Indicator; Shared Context Relationship Indicator; Shared Participant Relationship Indicator; Shared Value Relationship Indicator; Temporal Relationship Indicator; Operational Relationship Indicator; Technical Relationship Indicator; Cross-System Relationship Candidate; Cross-Organization Relationship Candidate; Machine-Generated Relationship Candidate; Candidate Inclusion Record; Candidate Exclusion Record; Duplicate Candidate Record; Candidate Confidence State; Candidate Ambiguity State; Candidate Conflict State; Relationship Identification Traceability Record; and the principal output: Governed Event Relationship Candidate Set.
Critical Distinctions
Relationship Indicator ≠ Established Event Relationship.
Relationship Discovery ≠ Relationship Determination.
Relationship Candidate ≠ Established Event Relationship.
Referenced Occurrence ≠ Governed Related Event by default.
Relationship Identification ≠ Pairwise-Only Governance.
Indicator Presence ≠ Relationship Proof.

More Indicators ≠ Established Relationship by default.
Shared Event Context ≠ Established Event Relationship.
Same Participant ≠ Related Event by default.
Shared Value ≠ Established Event Relationship by default.
Temporal Proximity ≠ Event Relationship.
Same Location ≠ Event Relationship.
Operational Link ≠ Governed Event Relationship by default.
Shared Technical Reference ≠ Same Event.
Same Contract ≠ Same Event.
Same Invoice ≠ Same Event.
Same Payment ≠ Same Event.
One Settlement ≠ One Event by default.
Refund Reference ≠ Relationship Type Determination.
Reversal Reference ≠ Established Reversal Relationship.
Common Source ≠ Same Event by default.
Common Destination ≠ Event Merger.
Different Systems ≠ Independent Events by default.
On-Chain Link ≠ Governed Event Relationship by default.
Machine Correlation ≠ Governed Event Relationship by default.
Detectable Connection ≠ Material Relationship Candidate.
Candidate Exclusion ≠ Proof of Permanent Unrelatedness.
Multiple Candidate Records ≠ Multiple Relationships by default.
Candidate Ambiguity ≠ Permission to Select a Convenient Event.
No Explicit Link ≠ No Event Relationship.
Correlation ≠ Relationship.
Relationship Discovery ≠ New Event Formation.
Dependency Indicator ≠ Governed Event Dependency.
Sequence Indicator ≠ Governed Event Sequence.
Multi-Event Candidate ≠ Event Group.
Merge Indicator ≠ Governed Event Merge.
Split Indicator ≠ Governed Event Split.
Desired Tax Outcome ≠ Relationship Indicator.

Relationship Candidate ≠ Tax Aggregation Candidate by default.
Enterprise Application
ERLIM provides the discovery layer required to identify meaningful Event Relationships across fragmented enterprise and digital infrastructures.
A typical operational path is:
ERP / Marketplace / Bank / Payment Network / Blockchain / AI Agent / Machine Systems
→ Governed Value-Associated Events
→ ERLIM — Relationship Identification
→ Governed Event Relationship Candidate Set
→ ERLDM — Relationship Dependency Governance
→ ERLSM — Relationship Sequence Governance
→ ERLGM — Relationship Grouping Governance
→ ERLMM — Merge & Split Governance
→ Governed Event Relationship Structure
This enables large systems to identify which events require relationship governance without assuming that every technical correlation represents an economically meaningful relationship. Use Case 1 — Multi-System Commerce Relationship Discovery
A marketplace processes thousands of purchases, payments, settlements, deliveries, returns, and refunds each day.
The events exist across several independent systems and use different identifiers.
A later settlement covers multiple merchant transactions, while several refunds refer to earlier purchases through different technical references.
ERLIM uses governed indicators such as shared Value References, participant information, order references, payment records, settlement identifiers, and refund references to identify which events should enter Relationship governance.

It does not decide whether those events are dependent, sequential, grouped, merged, or split.
The output is a Governed Event Relationship Candidate Set for further TRERLS processing. Use Case 2 — Autonomous and Blockchain Relationship Discovery
An AI agent initiates a resource request that causes machine allocation, energy consumption, digital service execution, smart-contract activity, and several blockchain transfers.
The infrastructure produces numerous governed events and many more technical records.
ERLIM identifies materially relevant relationship candidates using agent references, resource identifiers, machine execution records, Value References, smart-contract links, and settlement information.
It filters technical correlations that do not justify further Event Relationship governance while preserving ambiguous or conflicting candidates.
The result allows subsequent TRERLS modules to determine the actual dependency, sequence, grouping, and structural relationships without treating every autonomous or blockchain operation as an independent economic event.
Canonical Boundary
ERLIM owns the discovery, screening, differentiation, qualification, inclusion, exclusion, duplication control, uncertainty, conflict, and identification-level traceability of potential relationships among already-governed Tax-Relevant Events.

ERLIM does not establish final Event Relationships, govern dependency, determine sequence, create Event Groups, determine Event Chains or Networks, merge events, split events, form new events, redefine Event Boundaries, determine Event Timing, Event Location, Event Participation, Value Association, Event Determination, tax aggregation, Tax Liability, or another jurisdiction-specific legal conclusion.
Its governance ends when materially relevant Event Relationship Candidates are sufficiently identified for downstream Relationship Dependency governance under ERLDM.
Canonical Handoff
Governed Value-Associated Events
↓
ERLIM — Governed Event Relationship Candidate Set
↓
ERLDM — Event Relationship Dependency Governance
Canonical Closing Statement
ERLIM determines which governed events require relationship governance without treating every shared record, technical correlation, common participant, or nearby occurrence as proof that a relationship has already been established.
The discovery of a possible relationship and the governance of that relationship are separate operations.
Relationship Indicator ≠ Established Event Relationship.
Correlation ≠ Relationship.

OOF™ The Event Record Linkage Module (ERLKM) governs how a structurally
The Event Record Linkage Module (ERLKM) governs how a structurally
OOF™ Origin Open Foundation™
Independent Methodological Authority
Architecture Ecosystem: Structured Reality Standards™
Architecture Family: TREGA™ — Tax-Relevant Event Governance Architecture™
Parent Standard: TREGS — Tax-Relevant Event Record Governance Standard
Module: ERLKM — Event Record Linkage Module
Operational Layer: Event Record Linkage Governance Layer
Category: Governance & Enforcement
Subcategory: Tax-Relevant Event Governance
Type: Core Module
Governed Space: Event Record Linkage
Primary Governed Object: Governed Event Record Linkage State
Origin ID: TREGA-TREGS-ERLKM-003
Version: 1.0
Status: Canonical · Open Standard
Effective Date: 3 September 2026
AI-Readable: Yes
Authority: OOF®
Protection: MIP® — Methodological Intellectual Property
Canonical Language: UCL — Universal Canonical Language
Canonical Definition
The Event Record Linkage Module (ERLKM) governs how a structurally governed Tax-Relevant Event Record is linked to the Event, related Event Records, upstream governance states, supporting records, predecessor or successor representations, and other materially relevant references required to preserve reconstructability and downstream usability.
Its principal transition is:
Governed Event Record Structure
↓
Event Record Linkage Governance
↓
Governed Event Record Linkage State

ERLKM governs the relationship between records and references.
It does not recreate the substantive Event Relationships governed by TRERLS.
Its foundational distinction is:
Record Linkage ≠ Event Relationship Governance.
Operational Role
A structurally complete Event Record may still be operationally weak if it cannot be reliably connected to the objects and governance states that give it meaning.
ERLKM answers:
Which records, Events, governance states, and materially relevant references must this Event Record remain linked to in order to preserve its governed meaning?
Its role is to prevent: isolated records; broken Event references; lost predecessor or successor relationships; detached Determination states; disconnected supporting records; ungoverned duplicate links; ambiguous cross-system associations; and silent link loss during transformation.
Internal Module Flow
TREGS operates through:
ERIDM — Event Record Identification
↓
ERSTM — Event Record Structure
↓
ERLKM — Event Record Linkage
↓
ERTM — Event Record Traceability
↓
ERINM — Event Record Interoperability
↓
Governed Tax-Relevant Event Record
ERLKM receives:
Governed Event Record Structure
and produces:
Governed Event Record Linkage State
for ERTM.
Operational Transition
The canonical transition is:
Governed Event Record Structure
↓
Link Requirement Identification
↓
Link Establishment
↓
Link Qualification
↓
Link Validation State
↓
Governed Event Record Linkage State Operational Space

ERLKM governs: Event-to-Record linkage; Record-to-Record linkage; upstream governance references; Determination references; qualification references; uncertainty references; reconsideration references; predecessor links; successor links; related-record links; supporting-record links; duplicate-record associations; Merge/Split references; cross-system references; link type; link direction; link scope; link materiality; link validity state; link continuity; link conflict; link correction; link supersession; and linkage handoff.
Operational Scope
ERLKM may govern Record Linkage across: ERP systems; commerce platforms; accounting systems; banking infrastructure; payment systems; marketplaces; logistics; tax infrastructure; blockchain systems; smart contracts; AI agents; autonomous systems; distributed platforms; industrial systems; machine-to-machine environments; cross-border infrastructures; and future machine economies.
The linkage logic remains technology-neutral and jurisdiction-neutral.
Linkage Object
The linkage object is a governed association between the Event Record and another materially relevant governed object or reference.
A link may connect the Record to: the underlying Event; another Event Record; an upstream governance result; a supporting technical record; a predecessor representation; a successor representation; or another relevant reference.
Link Object ≠ Event Relationship by default.
Link Requirement Identification

ERLKM shall identify which links are materially required for the Event Record to remain reconstructable and usable.
Not every available connection belongs in the canonical Record linkage layer.
Available Connection ≠ Required Governed Link.
Event-to-Record Link
The Record shall remain linked to the Determined Tax-Relevant Event it represents.
This link is foundational.
It allows downstream systems to move from:
Record
↓
Governed Event
without reconstructing Event identity independently.
Event-to-Record Link ≠ Record Identity itself.
ERIDM owns Record identity.
Record-to-Record Link
Event Records may require association with other governed Event Records.
Examples include: predecessor/successor Record relationships; duplicate representations; derived representations; superseding Records; records corresponding to related Events.
ERLKM governs these associations at the Record layer.
Upstream Governance Linkage
The Record may preserve links to relevant upstream TREGA™ outputs, including: TRECS Context; TRERS Recognition; TREFS Formation; TREBS Boundary; TRETS Timing; TRELS Location; TREPS Participation; TRVAS Value Association; TRERLS Event Relationships; TREDS Determination.
ERLKM does not reproduce these governance functions.
Determination Linkage
The Event Record shall remain linked to the applicable TREDS Determination result.

Where reconsideration has occurred, linkage should support identification of: prior Determination; reconsideration process; current effective Determination.
Determination Link ≠ Determination Decision.
Qualification Linkage
Material qualifications may be linked directly or through governed references.
The Record shall not lose qualification merely because the underlying qualification is stored elsewhere.
Referenced Qualification ≠ Missing Qualification.
Uncertainty Linkage
Where material uncertainty remains relevant to downstream reliance, ERLKM shall support a durable link to the governed uncertainty state.
Uncertainty Link ≠ Uncertainty Governance.
EDUM remains authoritative.
Reconsideration Linkage
Where EDREM changes the effective Determination, the Event Record should preserve relevant linkage between:
Prior Determination
↓
Reconsideration
↓
Current Determination
Detailed chronological reconstruction belongs to ERTM.
Predecessor Link
A Record may require linkage to an earlier representation from which it developed.
Predecessor linkage supports continuity without implying that both records represent different Events.
Predecessor Record ≠ Prior Event by default.
Successor Link
A Record may link to a later representation that replaces or supersedes it.
This linkage preserves continuity while keeping identities distinct where required.
Successor Record ≠ Same Record by default.
Supporting Record Linkage

A canonical Event Record may link to supporting technical records such as: invoices; payment records; ledger entries; logs; sensor records; contracts; API messages; transaction receipts.
These support or represent aspects of the Event.
They do not automatically become governed Event Records.
Supporting Record ≠ Canonical Event Record.
Invoice Linkage
An invoice may be linked to a governed Event Record where materially relevant.
This does not make the invoice authoritative over the Event.
Invoice Link ≠ Event Definition.
Payment Linkage
A payment record may be linked to the Event Record.
The payment may represent: settlement; consideration; transfer; or partial execution.
Payment Link ≠ Event Identity.
Blockchain Linkage
A blockchain transaction may be linked as a supporting or operational representation.
A transaction hash may provide strong technical reference quality without defining the Event itself.
Blockchain Link ≠ Event Equivalence.
Smart-Contract Linkage
A smart-contract execution log may be linked where relevant.
The link preserves technical execution association.
It does not determine full Event meaning.
Machine-Generated Linkage
Autonomous systems may create large numbers of technical references.
ERLKM shall avoid creating canonical links merely because records are technically adjacent.
Machine Correlation ≠ Governed Linkage by default.
Link Type
Every material governed link should possess a distinguishable type.

Possible link types include: Represents; Supports; Derived From; References; Supersedes; Precedes; Succeeds; Corresponds To; Duplicate Of; Qualification Reference; Determination Reference; Uncertainty Reference; Governance State Reference.
Link semantics should remain explicit.
Link Direction
Where direction matters, the governed Record should distinguish source and target.
For example:
Record B Supersedes Record A
is not equivalent to:
Record A Supersedes Record B.
Link Presence ≠ Directional Meaning.
Link Scope
A link may apply to: the entire Record; one Record component; one Determination state; one qualification; one supporting object; or one lifecycle transition.
The scope should be explicit where material.
Link Materiality
Not every link requires canonical preservation.
A link is materially relevant where its absence could impair: Event reconstruction; Record meaning; Determination interpretation; downstream reliance; lifecycle continuity; or auditability.
More Links ≠ Better Governance by default.
Link Validity
ERLKM shall represent whether a link is: Proposed; Established; Qualified; Ambiguous; Conflicted; Invalid; Superseded; or Closed.
A stored reference is not necessarily a valid governed link.
Stored Reference ≠ Governed Link.
Link Qualification
A link may exist with qualification.
For example: probable source association; bounded duplicate association; unresolved cross-system mapping.
Qualification shall remain visible.
Link Conflict

Link conflict exists where materially relevant sources support incompatible associations.
Examples include: one Record linked to two mutually exclusive Events; conflicting predecessor references; incompatible duplicate-record conclusions; inconsistent Determination references.
Link Conflict ≠ Permission to Preserve Both as Equally Valid without Qualification.
Link Ambiguity
Ambiguous linkage exists where the correct association cannot be established sufficiently.
Ambiguous links should remain explicitly governed rather than silently treated as established.
Duplicate Linkage
Where multiple technical records represent the same governed Event Record, ERLKM may establish duplicate or corresponding-record associations.
This supports deduplication and traceability.
Duplicate Representation ≠ Duplicate Event.
Merge Linkage
Where TRERLS establishes an Event Merge, TREGS Records may require links among: pre-Merge Event Records; merged Event; resulting governed Record.
ERLKM represents these associations.
It does not govern the Merge itself.
Merge Linkage ≠ Merge Decision.
Split Linkage
Where an Event is split, Record linkage may preserve association between: original Event Record; resulting Event Records; Split governance reference.
Split Linkage ≠ Split Governance.
Record Supersession Linkage
Where one Record supersedes another, ERLKM shall preserve explicit linkage.

Supersession linkage should support: prior Record identity; successor Record identity; effective transition; reason reference.
TRECLS owns broader lifecycle supersession.
Correction Linkage
Where a corrected Record exists, ERLKM may preserve the association between prior and corrected representations.
Correction Link ≠ Event Correction Decision.
Cross-System Linkage
Different systems may maintain independent local representations associated with the same governed Record.
ERLKM may link these representations through the canonical Record identity.
Cross-System Link ≠ Full Interoperability.
ERINM governs interoperability.
Cross-Organization Linkage
Where several organizations exchange or consume the same Event Record, linkage may preserve associations among: canonical Record; local organizational representation; downstream processing object.
This supports continuity without requiring identical local schemas.
Cross-Border Linkage
Cross-border Event Records may link to several jurisdiction-specific evaluations.
These downstream links shall remain distinguishable from the canonical Event Record.
Jurisdictional Evaluation Link ≠ Tax Jurisdiction Determination.
Multi-Jurisdiction Linkage
The same Event Record may support:
Governed Event Record
↓
Jurisdiction A Evaluation
Governed Event Record
↓
Jurisdiction B Evaluation
Governed Event Record
↓
Jurisdiction C Evaluation
Each downstream evaluation may be linked without becoming part of the canonical Event definition.
Linkage Cardinality

ERLKM shall support one-to-one, one-to-many, many-to-one, and where necessary many-to-many Record associations.
Cardinality shall reflect governed reality rather than database convenience.
Database Relationship Type ≠ Governed Linkage Meaning.
Linkage Persistence
Material links should persist as long as they are necessary for reconstructability or lifecycle continuity.
Deletion of a technical reference shall not automatically erase a materially relevant governed linkage.
Linkage Continuity
Links may remain continuous across: Record transformation; system migration; identifier change; schema change; lifecycle state change.
Continuity shall preserve semantic meaning.
Linkage Change
A link may change because: a prior association was incorrect; a new supporting record appeared; a Record was superseded; a Duplicate was resolved; Merge/Split changed Event structure.
Material changes should remain governable and traceable.
Linkage Correction
Where a link is known to be incorrect, it may be corrected.
Correction shall preserve prior link state where materially relevant.
Link Correction ≠ Silent Historical Rewrite.
Linkage Supersession
A newer link may supersede an older link.
Superseded links should remain reconstructable where materially necessary.
Linkage Closure
Some links may cease to be operationally active while remaining historically relevant.
Closed linkage does not mean the association never existed.
Closed Link ≠ Erased Link.
Linkage and Traceability

ERLKM establishes governed associations.
ERTM uses those associations to reconstruct lineage and governance history.
Therefore:
Linkage ≠ Traceability.
A network of links may exist without sufficient traceability logic.
Linkage and Interoperability
ERLKM establishes what is linked.
ERINM governs whether those links and their meanings remain usable across systems.
Linkage ≠ Interoperability.
Linkage and Event Relationships
TRERLS governs substantive relationships among Events.
ERLKM may represent those relationships at the Record level.
It does not create, merge, split, sequence, group, or dependency-govern Events.
Record Relationship Representation ≠ Event Relationship Determination.
Linkage and Identity
ERIDM establishes Record identity.
ERLKM may use that identity to establish links.
It does not re-identify the Record.
Link Establishment ≠ Record Identification.
Linkage and Structure
ERSTM establishes structural capacity for links.
ERLKM governs actual linkage.
Link Field ≠ Governed Link.
Linkage and Tax Law
Links to jurisdictional evaluations, assessments, returns, or filings do not cause TREGA™ to own those legal outcomes.
Tax Assessment Link ≠ Tax Assessment Governance.
Governance States
ERLKM may represent:
Linkage Governance Not Initiated
Link Requirement Identified
Link Candidate Identified
Link Under Evaluation
Link Established
Link Qualified
Link Ambiguous
Link Conflicted
Link Invalid
Duplicate Link Established
Predecessor Link Established
Successor Link Established

Supersession Link Established
Correction Link Established
Cross-System Link Established
Link Superseded
Link Closed
Linkage Sufficient
Governed Event Record Linkage State Established
Ready for Traceability Governance Governance Requirements

ERLKM implementations shall ensure that: a valid Governed Event Record Structure exists; materially required links are identified; Event-to-Record linkage remains preserved; Record Linkage remains distinct from Event Relationship governance; upstream governance references can be maintained where material; Determination, qualification, uncertainty, and reconsideration references remain governable; predecessor and successor links remain distinguishable; supporting technical records remain distinct from canonical Event Records; link type is explicit where material; link direction is preserved where relevant; link scope is identifiable; link materiality is assessed; stored references do not automatically become governed links; ambiguous and conflicted links remain visible; Duplicate representations do not become duplicate Events; Merge/Split links do not recreate Merge/Split governance; correction and supersession links preserve materially relevant prior states; cross-system linkage remains distinct from interoperability; jurisdiction-specific evaluation links remain downstream; materially relevant links persist sufficiently for reconstructability; link changes remain traceable; and the resulting Governed Event Record Linkage State is suitable for ERTM.
Governance Logic
IF no valid Governed Event Record Structure exists, THEN ERLKM shall not establish canonical Record Linkage.

IF a link is materially necessary to reconstruct or interpret the Event Record, THEN the link shall be represented or reliably referenced.
IF a connection is technically present but has no governed semantic meaning, THEN it shall not automatically qualify as a canonical Record Link.
IF multiple technical records correspond to the same canonical Record, THEN duplicate or corresponding-record linkage may be established without creating multiple Events.
IF a link is materially ambiguous, THEN it shall remain qualified or unresolved rather than treated as established.
IF materially authoritative sources support incompatible links, THEN Link Conflict shall be established and governed explicitly.
IF one Record supersedes another, THEN predecessor/successor or supersession linkage shall preserve continuity.
IF a link changes because of correction, Merge, Split, or reconsideration, THEN prior materially relevant linkage shall remain reconstructable.
IF a jurisdiction-specific evaluation is linked, THEN the linkage shall not redefine the canonical Event Record.
IF materially required links are sufficiently established and qualified, THEN ERLKM shall produce the Governed Event Record Linkage State for ERTM.
Minimum Implementation Framework
A minimum ERLKM implementation should support:
Linkage Governance ID A stable identifier for the ERLKM governance process.
Canonical Record Identifier The ERIDM-established Record identity.

Record Structure Reference The ERSTM-governed Record Structure.
Link Identifier A stable identifier for each governed link.
Link Type Represents, Supports, References, Derived From, Precedes, Succeeds, Supersedes, Duplicate Of, Qualification Reference, Determination Reference, Uncertainty Reference, or other governed type.
Source Object Reference The source side of the link.
Target Object Reference The target side of the link.
Link Direction The governed directional meaning where relevant.
Link Scope Record-wide, Component-Level, Determination-Level, Qualification-Level, Lifecycle-Level, or other governed scope.
Link Materiality State Immaterial, Material, Critical, or Unresolved.
Link Validity State Proposed, Established, Qualified, Ambiguous, Conflicted, Invalid, Superseded, or Closed.
Event Reference Link The canonical association to the governed Event.
Determination Link Reference The applicable TREDS Determination link.
Qualification Link Reference Any material qualification link.
Uncertainty Link Reference Any EDUM uncertainty link.
Reconsideration Link Reference Any EDREM reconsideration association.
Predecessor Record Reference Any prior Record representation.
Successor Record Reference Any later Record representation.
Supporting Record Reference(s) Invoices, payments, ledger records, logs, contracts, or other supporting objects.
Duplicate Representation Reference Any governed duplicate or corresponding technical representation.

Merge / Split Reference Any relevant TRERLS structural transition.
Cross-System Reference Any materially relevant local-system representation.
Cross-Organization Reference Any organizational representation associated with the Record.
Jurisdictional Evaluation Reference Any downstream tax evaluation linked to the canonical Record.
Prior Link State The previous materially relevant link state.
Link Correction Reference Any governed link correction.
Link Supersession Reference Any superseding linkage.
Link Qualification Any limitation attached to the link.
Link Conflict State Whether materially incompatible link conclusions exist.
Link Trace Reference Minimum reference required for later ERTM reconstruction.
Governance State The current ERLKM governance state.
Handoff State Whether linkage is sufficiently governed for ERTM.
Governance Outputs
ERLKM may produce: Event-to-Record Link; Record-to-Record Link; Determination Link; Qualification Link; Uncertainty Link; Reconsideration Link; Predecessor Link; Successor Link; Supporting Record Link; Duplicate Representation Link; Merge/Split Reference; Cross-System Link; Cross-Organization Link; Jurisdictional Evaluation Link; Link Validity State; Link Materiality State; Link Conflict State; Link Correction State; Link Supersession State; Link Continuity State; and the principal output: Governed Event Record Linkage State.
Critical Distinctions
Record Linkage ≠ Event Relationship Governance.
Link Object ≠ Event Relationship by default.

Available Connection ≠ Required Governed Link.
Event-to-Record Link ≠ Record Identity itself.
Determination Link ≠ Determination Decision.
Referenced Qualification ≠ Missing Qualification.
Uncertainty Link ≠ Uncertainty Governance.
Predecessor Record ≠ Prior Event by default.
Successor Record ≠ Same Record by default.
Supporting Record ≠ Canonical Event Record.
Invoice Link ≠ Event Definition.
Payment Link ≠ Event Identity.
Blockchain Link ≠ Event Equivalence.
Machine Correlation ≠ Governed Linkage by default.
Link Presence ≠ Directional Meaning.
More Links ≠ Better Governance by default.
Stored Reference ≠ Governed Link.
Link Conflict ≠ Permission to Preserve Both as Equally Valid without Qualification.
Duplicate Representation ≠ Duplicate Event.
Merge Linkage ≠ Merge Decision.
Split Linkage ≠ Split Governance.
Correction Link ≠ Event Correction Decision.
Cross-System Link ≠ Full Interoperability.
Jurisdictional Evaluation Link ≠ Tax Jurisdiction Determination.
Database Relationship Type ≠ Governed Linkage Meaning.
Link Correction ≠ Silent Historical Rewrite.
Closed Link ≠ Erased Link.
Linkage ≠ Traceability.
Linkage ≠ Interoperability.
Record Relationship Representation ≠ Event Relationship Determination.
Link Establishment ≠ Record Identification.
Link Field ≠ Governed Link.
Tax Assessment Link ≠ Tax Assessment Governance.
Enterprise Application

ERLKM creates the governed association layer that allows a canonical Event Record to remain connected to the Event, its governance basis, related representations, and downstream processing objects.
The canonical enterprise path is:
ERIDM — Governed Event Record Identity
→ ERSTM — Governed Event Record Structure
→ ERLKM — Governed Event Record Linkage State
→ ERTM — Governed Event Record Traceability
→ ERINM — Governed Event Record Interoperability
→ Governed Tax-Relevant Event Record
This prevents the Event Record from becoming an isolated data object after it enters complex system infrastructure. Use Case 1 — Cross-Border Marketplace Event Linked Across Commerce, Payment, and Tax Systems
A marketplace Event has one canonical Governed Event Record.
The marketplace maintains an order record, the payment provider maintains a settlement record, the ERP maintains an accounting object, and three jurisdictions later create separate tax-evaluation objects.
ERLKM links the canonical Event Record to the relevant supporting technical records and downstream jurisdictional evaluations while preserving their distinct roles.
The payment record does not become the Event.
The tax evaluations do not redefine the canonical Record.
One governed Record remains the common reference across the infrastructure. Use Case 2 — Event Record Supersession After Merge
Two Events previously possessed separate governed Event Records.

TRERLS later determines that the Events must be merged into one governed Event.
TREDS produces the appropriate reconsidered Determination, and a resulting Event Record is created.
ERLKM preserves links from the new Record to the predecessor Records and the relevant Merge governance reference.
The prior Records remain historically reconstructable while the new Record becomes the effective canonical representation.
Record continuity is preserved without pretending that supersession erased the prior Record state.
Canonical Boundary
ERLKM owns the governance of Event-to-Record links, Record-to-Record links, upstream governance references, Determination/qualification/uncertainty/reconsideration links, predecessor and successor links, supporting-record associations, duplicate-representation links, Merge/Split references, link type, direction, scope, materiality, validity, ambiguity, conflict, continuity, correction, supersession, and establishment of the Governed Event Record Linkage State.
ERLKM does not establish Record identity; ERIDM owns that space.
It does not define Record Structure; ERSTM owns that space.
It does not govern full Record lineage reconstruction; ERTM owns Traceability.
It does not govern semantic preservation across systems; ERINM owns Interoperability.
It does not recreate Event Relationships; TRERLS owns Event Relationship Governance.
It does not govern Event lifecycle amendment, correction, supersession, or closure; TRECLS owns those lifecycle functions.

It does not determine legal taxability, Tax Jurisdiction, taxpayer status, Tax Base, Tax Rate, legal tax point, Tax Period, Tax Liability, or other jurisdiction-specific tax consequences.
Its governance begins when a valid Governed Event Record Structure exists.
Its governance ends when materially required Record links are sufficiently governed and the Governed Event Record Linkage State is ready for Traceability Governance.
Canonical Handoff
ERSTM — Governed Event Record Structure
↓
ERLKM — Governed Event Record Linkage State
↓
ERTM — Event Record Traceability Governance
Canonical Closing Statement
ERLKM ensures that a governed Event Record remains connected to the Event, governance states, records, and representations that give it operational meaning without confusing those links with the Event relationships themselves.
A Record can be richly connected and still remain one canonical representation of one governed Event.
Record Linkage ≠ Event Relationship Governance.
Linkage ≠ Traceability.
