chunks.text:
OOF™ The Event Relationship Merge & Split Module (ERLMM) governs how
The Event Relationship Merge & Split Module (ERLMM) governs how
OOF™ Origin Open Foundation™
Independent Methodological Authority
Architecture Ecosystem: Structured Reality Standards™
Architecture Family: TREGA™ — Tax-Relevant Event Governance Architecture™
Parent Standard: TRERLS — Tax-Relevant Event Relationship Standard
Module: ERLMM — Event Relationship Merge & Split Module
Operational Layer: Event Relationship Merge & Split Governance Layer
Category: Governance & Enforcement
Subcategory: Tax-Relevant Event Governance
Type: Core Module
Governed Space: Event Relationship Merge & Split Governance
Origin ID: TREGA-TRERLS-ERLMM-005
Version: 1.0
Status: Canonical · Open Standard
Effective Date: 1 September 2026
AI-Readable: Yes
Authority: OOF®
Protection: MIP® — Methodological Intellectual Property
Canonical Language: UCL — Universal Canonical Language
Canonical Definition
The Event Relationship Merge & Split Module (ERLMM) governs how already-related Tax-Relevant Events are evaluated for justified consolidation into one governed Event representation or separation into multiple governed Event representations when accumulated relationship governance reveals that the existing Event structure no longer faithfully represents operational reality.
ERLMM governs the conditions, justification, decision path, historical preservation, and downstream relationship consequences of Event Merge and Event Split.

Its principal transition is:
Governed Event Group Structure
↓
Merge & Split Governance
↓
Governed Event Relationship Structure
ERLMM does not create Event Formation or Event Boundary authority independently.
Where a Merge or Split changes what the event itself is, ERLMM coordinates the relationship-level restructuring with the authoritative upstream governance of TREFS — Tax-Relevant Event Formation Standard and TREBS — Tax-Relevant Event Boundary Standard.
The foundational distinction is:
Relationship Convenience ≠ Permission to Merge or Split Events.
Operational Role
Event structures may initially appear correct and later prove incomplete, fragmented, duplicated, over-aggregated, or incorrectly bounded.
Several records may have been treated as separate events even though subsequent governance establishes that they represent one materially coherent event.
Conversely, one governed event may later prove to contain several independently meaningful events.
ERLMM provides a controlled mechanism for addressing those situations.
Its role is not to optimize the Event structure for: tax outcome; reporting convenience; database architecture; billing convenience; system migration; reconciliation convenience; or computational simplicity.
Its role is to preserve the most faithful governed representation of operational reality.
Internal Module Flow
TRERLS operates through:
ERLIM — Event Relationship Identification
↓
ERLDM — Event Relationship Dependency
↓

ERLSM — Event Relationship Sequence
↓
ERLGM — Event Relationship Grouping
↓
ERLMM — Event Relationship Merge & Split
↓
Governed Event Relationship Structure
ERLMM is the final Core Module within TRERLS.
It receives the Governed Event Group Structure and produces the final Governed Event Relationship Structure for handoff to TREDS.
Operational Transition
The canonical transition is:
Governed Event Group Structure + Formation Evidence + Boundary Evidence + Relationship History
↓
Merge & Split Governance
↓
Governed Event Relationship Structure
ERLMM may determine that: no structural change is required; Merge review is required; Split review is required; a Merge is justified; a Split is justified; the issue must be referred upstream; or the structure remains unresolved.
Operational Space

ERLMM governs: Merge candidate identification; Split candidate identification; Merge qualification; Split qualification; Merge justification; Split justification; Merge decision; Split decision; Event preservation during Merge; Event preservation during Split; source-event mapping; resulting-event mapping; historical relationship preservation; Merge lineage; Split lineage; partial Merge; partial Split; duplicate-event consolidation; artificial-fragmentation correction; artificial-aggregation correction; relationship reassignment; group restructuring; Event Chain restructuring; Event Network restructuring; Merge uncertainty; Split uncertainty; Merge conflict; Split conflict; reconsideration; supersession; and Merge/Split-specific traceability.
Operational Scope
ERLMM may operate across: enterprise transactions; commerce; payments; banking; accounting; marketplaces; logistics; supply chains; ERP environments; digital platforms; distributed systems; blockchain infrastructures; digital assets; AI agents; autonomous machines; industrial systems; energy systems; cross-border operations; and future machine economies.
Merge Candidate
A Merge Candidate exists where two or more governed Event representations may in fact represent one materially coherent Tax-Relevant Event.
A candidate does not authorize Merge.
Merge Candidate ≠ Governed Event Merge.
The candidate shall be evaluated against Formation, Boundary, Relationship, and historical information.
Split Candidate

A Split Candidate exists where one governed Event representation may contain two or more materially independent events.
A candidate does not authorize Split.
Split Candidate ≠ Governed Event Split.
Merge Purpose
Event Merge exists to correct structural over-fragmentation where several Event representations incorrectly represent what governance establishes as one event.
Merge is therefore corrective, not convenient.
Merge ≠ Aggregation for Convenience.
Split Purpose
Event Split exists to correct structural over-aggregation where one Event representation incorrectly contains several independently meaningful events.
Split is therefore corrective, not a mechanism for generating preferred downstream results.
Split ≠ Fragmentation for Convenience.
Merge Preconditions
A Merge shall require sufficient governed basis indicating that separate Event representations should not remain independently constituted.
Relevant considerations may include: common Event Formation; overlapping or identical Event Boundary; inseparable operational substance; duplicated Event representation; duplicate technical capture; relationship evidence indicating one underlying occurrence; shared participant structure where materially relevant; integrated Value Association; and consistent historical reconstruction.
No single indicator establishes Merge automatically.
Split Preconditions

A Split shall require sufficient governed basis indicating that one Event representation contains materially distinct Event structures.
Relevant considerations may include: independently formed occurrences; separable Event Boundaries; independent participants; independent Value Associations; materially distinct timing; materially distinct location; independent operational purpose; independent dependency or sequence paths; or materially independent downstream relationships.
Again:
Additional Detail ≠ Split Requirement by default.
Duplicate Event Consolidation
Two records may represent the same governed event because of: duplicate ingestion; system synchronization; mirrored infrastructure; replicated ledger entries; platform duplication; or migration artifacts.
ERLMM may govern consolidation of duplicate Event representations.
Duplicate Record ≠ Additional Event.
Artificial Fragmentation
Artificial fragmentation occurs when one materially coherent event is represented as multiple events without sufficient Event Formation or Boundary justification.
Examples may arise from: technical process steps; API calls; accounting line items; blockchain operations; machine instructions; internal workflow stages.
ERLMM shall prevent technical structure from becoming Event structure by default.
Technical Fragmentation ≠ Economic Event Fragmentation.
Artificial Aggregation

Artificial aggregation occurs when several independently meaningful events are represented as one event merely because they share: one contract; one invoice; one payment; one participant; one platform; one settlement; one technical workflow; or one reporting record.
ERLMM shall prevent convenience-based Event collapse.
Shared Record ≠ Permission to Merge.
Merge Basis
A valid Merge basis shall arise from governed Event reality.
It shall not arise solely from: desired tax treatment; desired accounting treatment; lower reporting complexity; database design; reconciliation preference; system limitations.
Desired Outcome ≠ Merge Basis.
Split Basis
A valid Split basis shall likewise arise from governed Event reality.
It shall not be created solely because separating the event produces: preferred tax rates; different jurisdictional treatment; different taxable periods; exemptions; reduced tax exposure; reporting convenience.
Desired Outcome ≠ Split Basis.
Tax Advantage and Merge
ERLMM shall explicitly reject tax advantage as an Event Merge criterion.
Tax Advantage ≠ Event Merge Criterion.
Whether tax law later aggregates events is a separate downstream legal question.
Tax Exposure and Split
Likewise:
Tax Exposure ≠ Event Split Criterion.
Event structure shall not be redesigned merely because different representation changes potential tax liability.
Merge and Event Formation
A Merge may reveal that multiple Event records resulted from one underlying Event Formation.

TREFS remains authoritative for Event Formation.
ERLMM shall not silently override TREFS.
Where Formation must be reconsidered, the issue shall be referred upstream.
Event Merge ≠ Independent Formation Authority.
Split and Event Formation
A Split may reveal that one original representation contained several independently formed events.
Where this changes Event Formation, TREFS authority applies.
Event Split ≠ Independent Formation Authority.
Merge and Event Boundary
Merge may require reconsideration of individual Event Boundaries.
TREBS remains authoritative.
ERLMM governs the relationship-level restructuring resulting from that determination.
Event Merge ≠ Independent Boundary Authority.
Split and Event Boundary
A Split may require creation of distinct governed Event Boundaries.
TREBS remains authoritative for those boundaries.
Event Split ≠ Independent Boundary Authority.
Merge Direction
A Merge may combine:
Event A + Event B
↓
Event AB
or:
Event A + Event B + Event C
↓
Event ABC
The resulting representation must preserve traceability to all contributing Event representations.
Split Direction
A Split may produce:
Event A
↓
Event A1 + Event A2
or a broader structure where several new Event representations emerge from one previously over-aggregated record.
Each resulting event shall remain traceable to the pre-Split representation.
Many-to-One Merge
Several Event representations may merge into one governed Event representation.

Many-to-One Representation ≠ Automatic Merge Justification.
The Merge requires substantive governance basis.
One-to-Many Split
One Event representation may split into several governed events.
One-to-Many Representation ≠ Automatic Split Justification.
Partial Merge
Only part of an Event structure may require consolidation.
Where supported, ERLMM may govern a partial Merge without collapsing unrelated Event structure.
Partial Relationship Overlap ≠ Full Merge by default.
Partial Split
Only one portion of an event may prove independently constituted.
A partial Split may be required while the remaining event continues.
Partial Independence ≠ Full Event Split by default.
Merge and Event Identity
A governed Merge changes how Event Identity is represented.
The original source records shall not disappear from history.
They become traceably associated with the resulting governed event.
Event Merge ≠ Historical Erasure.
Split and Event Identity
A governed Split creates or recognizes multiple independently governed Event representations.
The prior representation shall remain part of the historical lineage.
Event Split ≠ Historical Erasure.
Source Event Preservation
All events participating in Merge or Split governance shall remain historically referenceable.
Historical records may be marked as: merged; superseded; split; replaced; reconstituted; or otherwise structurally transformed.
They shall not simply disappear.
Resulting Event Preservation

Each resulting Event representation shall receive sufficient identity and traceability to support future governance.
The resulting structure shall clearly indicate its relationship to predecessor representations.
Merge Lineage
Merge lineage shall preserve:
Source Event(s)
↓
Merge Decision
↓
Resulting Event
The basis, decision, authority, and transformation history shall remain reconstructable.
Split Lineage
Split lineage shall preserve:
Source Event
↓
Split Decision
↓
Resulting Event(s) Relationship Reassignment
Merge or Split may require existing relationships to be reassigned.
For example: dependencies; sequences; group memberships; settlement links; reversal links; Value Associations.
Reassignment shall be explicit.
Structural Change ≠ Permission to Lose Relationship History.
Dependency After Merge
Where events merge, prior dependency relationships may become internal to the resulting event or may cease to represent relationships between independent events.
ERLMM shall preserve the historical distinction.
ERLDM remains authoritative for dependency itself.
Dependency After Split
A Split may reveal new dependencies among the resulting events.
Those dependencies may require renewed ERLDM governance.
Split Result ≠ Automatically Governed Dependency.
Sequence After Merge
Merge may alter how prior Event Sequences are represented.
Historic sequence shall remain reconstructable even where several earlier event records become one Event representation.
Sequence After Split

Split may create multiple events requiring distinct sequence relationships.
Those relationships shall be governed through ERLSM where necessary.
Grouping After Merge
A merged Event representation may replace several group members.
Group membership shall be updated without losing prior history.
Grouping After Split
A Split may create several new group members or may distribute resulting events across different Event Groups.
ERLGM authority remains applicable.
Event Chain Restructuring
Merge or Split may alter an Event Chain.
For example:
A
↓
B
↓
C
may become:
AB
↓
C
or:
A
↓
B1
↓
B2
↓
C
ERLMM shall preserve structural lineage.
Event Network Restructuring
Complex Event Networks may require relationship-edge reassignment after Merge or Split.
No relationship should disappear merely because Event representation changes.
Reversal and Merge
A reversal event shall not normally be merged into the original event merely because it reverses it.
Reversal Relationship ≠ Merge Requirement.
The events may remain separately governed and related.
Refund and Merge
A refund may remain a separate event related to an earlier purchase or payment.
Refund Relationship ≠ Merge Requirement.
Correction and Merge
A correction record may or may not constitute an independent event.
ERLMM shall not assume Merge or independence solely from the label “correction.” Replacement and Merge
A replacement event may remain separate from the original event while preserving a replacement relationship.

Replacement Relationship ≠ Merge Requirement.
Continuation and Split
A long-running event shall not be split merely because it contains several operational phases.
Operational Phases ≠ Multiple Events by default.
TRECLS remains authoritative for lifecycle continuity.
System Migration
Migration from one platform to another may create duplicate Event representations.
This may justify duplicate consolidation.
However:
System Migration ≠ New Event Formation.
and:
System Migration ≠ Event Split.
Database Consolidation
Combining database records does not establish Event Merge.
Database Consolidation ≠ Event Merge.
Likewise, separating a database record does not establish Event Split.
Database Separation ≠ Event Split.
Accounting Structure
Accounting systems may aggregate or separate activity according to ledger requirements.
Those structures do not automatically define TREGA™ Event structure.
Accounting Aggregation ≠ Event Merge.
Accounting Disaggregation ≠ Event Split.
Invoice Structure
Several events may appear on one invoice.
One event may span several invoice lines or documents.
Therefore:
Invoice Consolidation ≠ Event Merge.
Invoice Separation ≠ Event Split.
Payment Structure
One payment may settle multiple events, and several payments may relate to one event.
Therefore:
Payment Aggregation ≠ Event Merge.
Multiple Payments ≠ Event Split.
Blockchain Merge & Split

Blockchain infrastructure may represent one economic activity through several technical transactions or combine many operations inside one transaction.
ERLMM shall not derive Merge or Split mechanically from ledger structure.
Multiple Blockchain Transactions ≠ Event Split Requirement.
Single Blockchain Transaction ≠ Event Merge Requirement.
Smart-Contract Structure
One smart contract may execute several independent events.
Several contracts may participate in one event.
Therefore:
Smart-Contract Boundary ≠ Event Boundary.
AI-Agent Workflow
An AI agent may generate hundreds of technical actions in executing one governed event or several independent events within one workflow.
ERLMM shall rely on Event governance rather than agent workflow structure.
One Agent Workflow ≠ One Event by default.
Machine Operations
Machine systems may generate high-frequency technical actions.
Those operations shall not be split into independent Tax-Relevant Events without appropriate Formation and Boundary governance.
Machine Operation Count ≠ Event Count.
Cross-System Merge
Records from several systems may represent the same event.
ERLMM may govern consolidation where Event Formation and Boundary support one Event Identity.
Different Systems ≠ Different Events by default.
Cross-Organization Merge
Different organizations may hold records referring to the same governed event.
Their separate records do not automatically mean separate events.

However, separate organizational participation also does not automatically justify Merge.
Cross-Border Merge & Split
An event may cross national borders.
Geographic distribution does not by itself justify Event Split.
Likewise, shared jurisdiction does not justify Event Merge.
Multiple Countries ≠ Multiple Events by default.
One Country ≠ One Event by default.
Multi-Jurisdiction Neutrality
ERLMM shall preserve a jurisdiction-neutral Event structure.
Different tax systems may later aggregate or separate the events differently for legal purposes.
The TREGA™ representation shall remain stable unless Event reality itself changes.
Jurisdictional Tax Treatment ≠ TREGA™ Merge/Split Authority.
Merge Uncertainty
Available information may suggest Merge without providing sufficient basis.
ERLMM shall preserve that uncertainty.
Merge Uncertainty ≠ Permission to Merge.
Split Uncertainty
Likewise:
Split Uncertainty ≠ Permission to Split.
Merge Conflict
Different systems or governance sources may disagree on whether events constitute one event.
ERLMM shall preserve the conflict.
Merge Conflict ≠ Permission for Convenient Consolidation.
Split Conflict
Conflicting evidence regarding Event independence shall remain explicit.
Split Conflict ≠ Permission for Convenient Fragmentation.
Merge Reconsideration
A prior Merge may later be reconsidered if materially relevant information changes.
Historical Merge state shall remain reconstructable.
Split Reconsideration

A prior Split may likewise be reconsidered.
Reconsideration shall not erase previous governance states. Supersession
A new Event representation resulting from Merge or Split may supersede prior Event representations for current governance purposes.
However:
Supersession ≠ Historical Deletion.
Governance States
ERLMM may represent:
Merge & Split Governance Ready
Merge & Split Under Governance
No Structural Change Required
Merge Candidate
Split Candidate
Merge Qualification Required
Split Qualification Required
Merge Qualified
Split Qualified
Merge Rejected
Split Rejected
Merge Referred Upstream
Split Referred Upstream
Merge Approved
Split Approved
Partial Merge
Partial Split
Duplicate Event Consolidation
Artificial Fragmentation Corrected
Artificial Aggregation Corrected
Merge Ambiguous
Split Ambiguous
Merge Conflicted
Split Conflicted
Merge Under Reconsideration
Split Under Reconsideration
Relationship Structure Reconstituted
Governed Event Relationship Structure Established Governance Requirements

ERLMM implementations shall ensure that: Merge and Split operate only on governed Event structures; Merge Candidate remains distinct from Merge Decision; Split Candidate remains distinct from Split Decision; Event Merge is supported by substantive Event governance; Event Split is supported by substantive Event governance; technical fragmentation does not automatically create Split; technical aggregation does not automatically create Merge; duplicate records can be distinguished from separate events; desired tax outcome does not govern Merge or Split; tax advantage is not a Merge criterion; tax exposure is not a Split criterion; Event Formation authority remains under TREFS; Event Boundary authority remains under TREBS; source Event representations remain historically traceable; resulting Event representations remain traceable to source events; Merge lineage can be reconstructed; Split lineage can be reconstructed; dependency relationships can be reassigned where necessary; sequence relationships can be reassigned where necessary; group memberships can be updated where necessary; Event Chains can be restructured without losing history; Event Networks can be restructured without losing history; ambiguity remains visible; conflict remains visible; reconsideration remains traceable; supersession does not erase historical states; system migration does not redefine Event structure automatically; accounting, invoicing, payment, blockchain, AI-agent, and machine-system structures do

t erase historical states; system migration does not redefine Event structure automatically; accounting, invoicing, payment, blockchain, AI-agent, and machine-system structures do not independently determine Merge or Split; and jurisdiction-specific tax aggregation remains downstream.

Governance Logic
IF several governed Event representations appear to represent one materially coherent event, THEN ERLMM shall establish a Merge Candidate rather than automatically merging them.
IF one governed Event representation appears to contain several materially independent events, THEN ERLMM shall establish a Split Candidate rather than automatically splitting it.
IF Merge would alter Event Formation or Event Boundary, THEN the relevant matter shall be coordinated with TREFS and TREBS before final structural change.
IF Split would alter Event Formation or Event Boundary, THEN the relevant matter shall be coordinated with TREFS and TREBS before final structural change.
IF records are merely technical duplicates of one governed event, THEN duplicate consolidation may be performed while preserving source lineage.
IF several technical operations belong to one materially coherent event, THEN technical fragmentation alone shall not justify multiple Event Identities.
IF several independently meaningful events share one invoice, payment, contract, workflow, or settlement, THEN that shared structure alone shall not justify Event Merge.
IF tax advantage is the only material basis for Merge, THEN Merge shall be rejected.
IF tax exposure is the only material basis for Split, THEN Split shall be rejected.
IF Merge or Split remains ambiguous or conflicted, THEN the corresponding governance state shall remain visible.

IF Merge or Split is approved, THEN source Event representations, resulting Event representations, relationship reassignment, and historical lineage shall remain reconstructable.
IF the final relationship structure is sufficiently governed, THEN ERLMM shall produce the Governed Event Relationship Structure for TREDS.
Minimum Implementation Framework
A minimum ERLMM implementation should support:
Event Group Structure Reference The ERLGM output entering Merge & Split governance.
Structural Review Identifier A stable identifier for the Merge/Split governance process.
Review Type Merge, Split, Duplicate Consolidation, or No Structural Change.
Candidate Event References The governed events under structural review.
Merge Candidate State Whether Merge is under consideration.
Split Candidate State Whether Split is under consideration.
Formation Reference Relevant TREFS governance supporting or constraining structural change.
Boundary Reference Relevant TREBS governance supporting or constraining structural change.
Relationship Basis The TRERLS relationship information supporting structural review.
Merge Basis The governed substantive basis for Merge where applicable.
Split Basis The governed substantive basis for Split where applicable.
Duplicate State Whether candidate records represent duplicated Event capture.
Fragmentation State Whether artificial Event fragmentation has been identified.
Aggregation State Whether artificial Event aggregation has been identified.

Source Event References All Event representations preceding structural change.
Resulting Event References All Event representations resulting from approved Merge or Split.
Transformation Direction Many-to-one, one-to-many, partial Merge, partial Split, or other governed transformation.
Relationship Reassignment Record How dependencies and other Event Relationships are reassigned.
Sequence Reassignment Record How Event Sequence is affected.
Grouping Reassignment Record How group membership is affected.
Value Association Reference Any material TRVAS reference affected by the structural change.
Historical Lineage Record The complete relationship between source and resulting Event representations.
Merge/Split Justification Record The governed rationale for the decision.
Decision State Approved, Rejected, Referred Upstream, Ambiguous, Conflicted, or Unresolved.
Uncertainty State Any remaining structural uncertainty.
Conflict State Any materially conflicting governance information.
Reconsideration Reference Where a prior Merge or Split decision has been reopened.
Supersession Reference Where a resulting Event representation supersedes an earlier representation.
Traceability Reference Information required to reconstruct the full Merge/Split decision.
Governance State The current ERLMM state.
Handoff State Whether the Governed Event Relationship Structure is ready for TREDS.
Governance Outputs

ERLMM may produce: No Structural Change Determination; Merge Candidate Record; Split Candidate Record; Merge Qualification Record; Split Qualification Record; Merge Decision; Split Decision; Duplicate Event Consolidation Record; Artificial Fragmentation Correction; Artificial Aggregation Correction; Partial Merge Record; Partial Split Record; Source Event Mapping; Resulting Event Mapping; Merge Lineage Record; Split Lineage Record; Relationship Reassignment Record; Sequence Reassignment Record; Group Reassignment Record; Merge Uncertainty State; Split Uncertainty State; Merge Conflict State; Split Conflict State; Merge Reconsideration Record; Split Reconsideration Record; Supersession Record; Merge/Split Traceability Record; and the principal output: Governed Event Relationship Structure.
Critical Distinctions
Relationship Convenience ≠ Permission to Merge or Split Events.
Merge Candidate ≠ Governed Event Merge.
Split Candidate ≠ Governed Event Split.
Merge ≠ Aggregation for Convenience.
Split ≠ Fragmentation for Convenience.
Additional Detail ≠ Split Requirement by default.
Duplicate Record ≠ Additional Event.
Technical Fragmentation ≠ Economic Event Fragmentation.
Shared Record ≠ Permission to Merge.
Desired Outcome ≠ Merge Basis.
Desired Outcome ≠ Split Basis.
Tax Advantage ≠ Event Merge Criterion.
Tax Exposure ≠ Event Split Criterion.
Event Merge ≠ Independent Formation Authority.
Event Split ≠ Independent Formation Authority.
Event Merge ≠ Independent Boundary Authority.

Event Split ≠ Independent Boundary Authority.
Many-to-One Representation ≠ Automatic Merge Justification.
One-to-Many Representation ≠ Automatic Split Justification.
Partial Relationship Overlap ≠ Full Merge by default.
Partial Independence ≠ Full Event Split by default.
Event Merge ≠ Historical Erasure.
Event Split ≠ Historical Erasure.
Structural Change ≠ Permission to Lose Relationship History.
Split Result ≠ Automatically Governed Dependency.
Reversal Relationship ≠ Merge Requirement.
Refund Relationship ≠ Merge Requirement.
Replacement Relationship ≠ Merge Requirement.
Operational Phases ≠ Multiple Events by default.
System Migration ≠ New Event Formation.
Database Consolidation ≠ Event Merge.
Database Separation ≠ Event Split.
Accounting Aggregation ≠ Event Merge.
Accounting Disaggregation ≠ Event Split.
Invoice Consolidation ≠ Event Merge.
Invoice Separation ≠ Event Split.
Payment Aggregation ≠ Event Merge.
Multiple Payments ≠ Event Split.
Multiple Blockchain Transactions ≠ Event Split Requirement.
Single Blockchain Transaction ≠ Event Merge Requirement.
Smart-Contract Boundary ≠ Event Boundary.
One Agent Workflow ≠ One Event by default.
Machine Operation Count ≠ Event Count.
Different Systems ≠ Different Events by default.
Multiple Countries ≠ Multiple Events by default.
Jurisdictional Tax Treatment ≠ TREGA™ Merge/Split Authority.
Merge Uncertainty ≠ Permission to Merge.
Split Uncertainty ≠ Permission to Split.
Merge Conflict ≠ Permission for Convenient Consolidation.

Split Conflict ≠ Permission for Convenient Fragmentation.
Supersession ≠ Historical Deletion.
Enterprise Application
ERLMM provides the final structural-control layer of TRERLS.
A typical enterprise path is:
ERLIM — Governed Event Relationship Candidate Set
→ ERLDM — Governed Event Dependency Structure
→ ERLSM — Governed Event Sequence Structure
→ ERLGM — Governed Event Group Structure
→ ERLMM — Merge & Split Governance
→ Governed Event Relationship Structure
→ TREDS — Tax-Relevant Event Determination
This allows enterprises and digital infrastructures to correct duplicated, fragmented, or over-aggregated Event representations while preserving operational reality, historical lineage, and jurisdiction neutrality. Use Case 1 — ERP, Payment, and Marketplace Duplicate Event Reconciliation
A marketplace, merchant ERP, and payment infrastructure each create separate records for the same purchase activity.
Initial integration produces three apparent Tax-Relevant Events.
Relationship governance later establishes that two of those records are duplicate representations of one underlying governed event, while the payment event remains independently constituted and related.
ERLMM evaluates the Merge Candidate, coordinates the relevant Event Formation and Boundary references, consolidates the duplicate Event representations, preserves all source-record lineage, and retains the independent payment Event Relationship.

The resulting structure corrects technical duplication without collapsing materially distinct activity. Use Case 2 — Autonomous Workflow Incorrectly Aggregated as One Event
An autonomous industrial platform records an entire multi-stage service workflow as one event.
Subsequent governance establishes that resource allocation, machine service delivery, and later digital settlement possess independent Formation, Boundaries, participants, and Value Associations.
ERLMM establishes a Split Candidate and coordinates the required Formation and Boundary governance.
The original over-aggregated Event representation is preserved historically while three independently governed Event representations are established and linked through dependency, sequence, and grouping relationships.
The Split is justified by operational reality rather than tax treatment.
Canonical Boundary
ERLMM owns relationship-level governance of Merge Candidates, Split Candidates, duplicate consolidation, artificial-fragmentation correction, artificial-aggregation correction, Merge/Split qualification, decision structure, source-to-result mapping, relationship reassignment, lineage, uncertainty, conflict, reconsideration, supersession, and Merge/Split-specific traceability.

ERLMM does not independently create Event Formation authority, redefine Event Boundaries without TREBS governance, determine Event Timing, Event Location, Event Participation, underlying Value governance, taxpayer status, tax aggregation, tax jurisdiction, Tax Base, Tax Liability, or another jurisdiction-specific legal consequence.
Where Merge or Split changes Event Formation or Event Boundary, TREFS and TREBS remain authoritative.
ERLMM governance ends when the final relationship structure among the relevant governed events is sufficiently represented for downstream Tax-Relevant Event Determination under TREDS.
Canonical Handoff
ERLGM — Governed Event Group Structure
↓
ERLMM — Governed Event Relationship Structure
↓
TREDS — Tax-Relevant Event Determination
Canonical Closing Statement
ERLMM corrects the structure of related events when governance establishes that reality has been fragmented or aggregated incorrectly, while preserving every material step in the history of that correction.
Events should be merged or split because the governed reality requires it — never because a technical system, reporting structure, or preferred tax outcome makes another representation more convenient.
Event Merge ≠ Historical Erasure.
Event Split ≠ Historical Erasure.
Tax Advantage ≠ Event Merge Criterion.
Tax Exposure ≠ Event Split Criterion.
