OOF™ TREGA™ Architecture Map
TREGA™ Architecture Map
Tax-Relevant Event Governance Architecture — Tax-Relevant Event Governance Layer
TREGA™ serves as the official OOF® Tax-Relevant Event Governance reference map used to identify, define, classify, navigate, govern, evaluate, and understand governable Tax-Relevant Event spaces across physical transactions, digital services, financial systems, platforms, AI agents, autonomous systems, machine-to-machine environments, distributed systems, cross-border activity, organizations, and future taxation environments.
The purpose of TREGA™ is not to define taxation itself.
The purpose of TREGA™ is to identify, define, separate, and map the governable spaces through which a real-world, economic, operational, digital, transactional, machine-generated, autonomous, or value-affecting occurrence is contextualized, recognized, formed into a governed Event, bounded, temporally and spatially situated, associated with participants and Value, related to other Events, formally determined as tax-relevant, represented as a governed Event Record, and maintained throughout its lifecycle before jurisdiction-specific taxation rules are applied.
TREGA™ serves as the official Tax-Relevant Event Governance reference map for:
Physical Transactions
Digital Transactions
Digital Services
Commercial Activity
Financial Systems
Banking Systems
Commerce Platforms
Digital Platforms
Cross-Border Activity
Distributed Systems
Digital Assets
AI Agents
Autonomous Systems

Machine-to-Machine Transactions
Robotics and Machine Economies
Industrial Systems
Multi-Party Events
Multi-Jurisdiction Environments
Future Taxation Ecosystems
Core Architectural Principle
Every Tax-Relevant Event Governance space answers one primary governance question.
No Tax-Relevant Event Governance space duplicates the purpose of another Tax-Relevant Event Governance space.
Every Tax-Relevant Event Governance space has a defined beginning, a defined operational purpose, and a defined governance boundary.
Every Tax-Relevant Event Governance space begins where the preceding Event Governance requirement has been sufficiently established.
Together, these Tax-Relevant Event Governance spaces form the official Tax-Relevant Event Governance reference map of TREGA™.
Official Tax-Relevant Event Governance Flow
Real-World / Digital Event
↓
Event Context
↓
Event Recognition
↓
Event Formation & Root Association
↓
Event Boundary
↓
Event Timing
↓
Event Location
↓
Event Participation
↓
Value Association
↓
Event Relationships
Event Determination
↓
Governed Tax-Relevant Event Record
↓
Event Continuity
& Lifecycle
↓
Jurisdiction-Ready Tax-Relevant Event
1. Tax-Relevant Event Context Standard (TRECS)
Governed Space: Tax-Relevant Event Context
Core Question
Within what governed operational, economic, digital, transactional, organizational, or machine context does the occurrence exist, and which contextual boundaries and relationships are relevant to its Event governance?
Canonical Definition

Tax-Relevant Event Context Standard (TRECS) defines the governance conditions under which the operational, economic, digital, transactional, organizational, machine, platform, infrastructural, or other materially relevant context surrounding an occurrence is formally identified, scoped, related, updated, and maintained as the contextual basis for Tax-Relevant Event Governance.
Governance Boundary
Begins when a real-world or digital occurrence requires a governed contextual basis before Tax-Relevant Event Recognition can legitimately proceed.
Ends when the Event Context has been sufficiently identified, scoped, related, and governed to support recognition of whether the occurrence should enter Tax-Relevant Event Governance.
2. Tax-Relevant Event Recognition Standard (TRERS)
Governed Space: Tax-Relevant Event Recognition
Core Question
Which occurrence should enter Tax-Relevant Event Governance, under what recognition conditions, and with what confidence, qualification, or escalation state?
Canonical Definition
Tax-Relevant Event Recognition Standard (TRERS) defines the governance conditions under which an occurrence is recognized as requiring Tax-Relevant Event Governance through explicit recognition rules, relevance screening, confidence assessment, qualification, and escalation where recognition remains uncertain.
Governance Boundary
Begins when an occurrence exists within a sufficiently governed Event Context and must be assessed for entry into Tax-Relevant Event Governance.

Ends when the occurrence has been sufficiently recognized, qualified, rejected, or escalated to support Event Formation Governance.
3. Tax-Relevant Event Formation Standard (TREFS)
Governed Space: Tax-Relevant Event Formation
Core Question
How must a recognized occurrence be assembled into a governed Event, which components constitute it, and what operational root relationship supports its formation?
Canonical Definition
Tax-Relevant Event Formation Standard (TREFS) defines the governance conditions under which a recognized occurrence is formed into a governed Event by identifying its constituent components, assembling their relevant relationships, establishing formation dependencies, associating the Event with its operational root, and maintaining Formation Integrity.
Governance Boundary
Begins when an occurrence has been sufficiently recognized as requiring Tax-Relevant Event Governance.
Ends when the occurrence has been sufficiently formed into a governed Event with identifiable components, dependencies, assembly structure, and Root Association to support explicit Event Boundary Governance.
Event Root ≠ Identity Origin.
4. Tax-Relevant Event Boundary Standard (TREBS)
Governed Space: Tax-Relevant Event Boundary
Core Question
Where does the governed Event begin and end, what belongs inside or outside it, and how must it remain distinguishable from adjacent or related Events?
Canonical Definition

Tax-Relevant Event Boundary Standard (TREBS) defines the governance conditions under which the inclusion, exclusion, scope, separation, and revision boundaries of a Tax-Relevant Event are established so that the Event remains distinguishable from adjacent occurrences, related Events, supporting activity, and external operational conditions.
Governance Boundary
Begins when an Event has been sufficiently formed and its governed extent must be explicitly established.
Ends when the Event Boundary has been sufficiently identified, scoped, separated, excluded where necessary, and governed to support Event Timing.
5. Tax-Relevant Event Timing Standard (TRETS)
Governed Space: Tax-Relevant Event Timing
Core Question
When does the Event begin, continue, complete, and relate temporally to other Events without converting operational Event Timing into a jurisdiction-specific legal tax point or Tax Period?
Canonical Definition
Tax-Relevant Event Timing Standard (TRETS) defines the governance conditions under which the temporal identity, start, completion, duration, and temporal ordering of a Tax-Relevant Event are established and maintained as operational Event Timing.
Governance Boundary
Begins when a sufficiently formed and bounded Event requires explicit temporal positioning.
Ends when Event Timing has been sufficiently established through Event Time identification, Start, Completion, Duration, and Temporal Order to support Event Location Governance.

Operational Event Time ≠ Legal Tax Point.
Event Timing ≠ Tax Period Determination.
6. Tax-Relevant Event Location Standard (TRELS)
Governed Space: Tax-Relevant Event Location
Core Question
Where does the Event occur physically, digitally, operationally, or across distributed environments without converting Event Location into Tax Jurisdiction determination?
Canonical Definition
Tax-Relevant Event Location Standard (TRELS) defines the governance conditions under which the physical, digital, distributed, operational, or correlated locations associated with a Tax-Relevant Event are identified, represented, related, and maintained without converting those locations into jurisdiction-specific tax conclusions.
Governance Boundary
Begins when Event Timing has been sufficiently established and the Event requires governed spatial or operational positioning.
Ends when materially relevant physical, digital, distributed, and correlated Event Locations have been sufficiently established to support Event Participation Governance.
Event Location ≠ Tax Jurisdiction.
7. Tax-Relevant Event Participation Standard (TREPS)
Governed Space: Tax-Relevant Event Participation
Core Question
Which human, organizational, digital, machine, or autonomous actors materially participate in the Event, in what roles, and with what continuity without determining taxpayer status?
Canonical Definition

Tax-Relevant Event Participation Standard (TREPS) defines the governance conditions under which human, organizational, digital, machine, autonomous, or other actors are identified for Event Participation, associated with the Event, assigned materially relevant participation roles, and governed for participation continuity.
Governance Boundary
Begins when a sufficiently contextualized, recognized, formed, bounded, timed, and located Event requires identification of the actors materially participating in it.
Ends when materially relevant Event Participants, their participation roles, actor associations, machine or autonomous participation, and participation continuity have been sufficiently governed to support Value Association.
Participant ≠ Taxpayer.
Identified Actor ≠ Governed Event Participant.
8. Tax-Relevant Value Association Standard (TRVAS)
Governed Space: Tax-Relevant Value Association
Core Question
Which governed Value states, changes, transfers, or relationships belong to the Event, and how must they remain associated without duplicating Value lifecycle governance itself?
Canonical Definition
Tax-Relevant Value Association Standard (TRVAS) defines the governance conditions under which governed Value references, Value states, Value changes, and materially relevant Value relationships are associated with a Tax-Relevant Event and remain traceable as Event-specific Value Associations.
Governance Boundary

Begins when Event Participation has been sufficiently established and governed Value results must be associated with the Event.
Ends when materially relevant Value references, states, changes, and traceability relationships have been sufficiently associated with the Event to support Event Relationship Governance.
Value Association ≠ Value Governance.
9. Tax-Relevant Event Relationship Standard (TRERLS)
Governed Space: Tax-Relevant Event Relationships
Core Question
How is the Event related to other Events through dependency, sequence, grouping, Merge, Split, or other materially relevant relationships?
Canonical Definition
Tax-Relevant Event Relationship Standard (TRERLS) defines the governance conditions under which Tax-Relevant Events are identified as related through dependency, sequence, grouping, Merge, Split, or other materially relevant Event relationships without collapsing distinct Events into one undifferentiated activity.
Governance Boundary
Begins when an Event has sufficient Context, Formation, Boundary, Timing, Location, Participation, and Value Association to determine materially relevant relationships with other Events.
Ends when those relationships have been sufficiently identified and governed to support formal Event Determination.
One economic activity ≠ necessarily one Event.
Multiple technical operations ≠ necessarily multiple economically independent Events.
10. Tax-Relevant Event Determination Standard (TREDS)

Governed Space: Tax-Relevant Event Determination
Core Question
When is an Event sufficiently governed to be formally determined as tax-relevant and eligible for downstream taxation analysis without determining whether the Event is legally taxable?
Canonical Definition
Tax-Relevant Event Determination Standard (TREDS) defines the governance conditions under which a governed Event is assessed for Determination Readiness, evaluated against Event Determination conditions, assigned a formal Tax-Relevant Event Determination, qualified for uncertainty where required, and reconsidered when materially relevant conditions change.
Governance Boundary
Begins when the Event has been sufficiently governed across Context, Recognition, Formation, Boundary, Timing, Location, Participation, Value Association, and Event Relationships.
Ends when the Event has been sufficiently determined as tax-relevant, not tax-relevant, qualified, uncertain, or requiring reconsideration to support Event Record Governance.
Event Determination ≠ Taxability Determination.
11. Tax-Relevant Event Record Governance Standard (TREGS)
Governed Space: Tax-Relevant Event Record Governance
Core Question
How can a Determined Tax-Relevant Event be represented as a stable, identifiable, structured, linked, traceable, and interoperable governed record without allowing the record to redefine the Event or determine its legal tax consequence?
Canonical Definition

Tax-Relevant Event Record Governance Standard (TREGS) defines the governance conditions under which a Determined Tax-Relevant Event is transformed into an identifiable, structured, linked, traceable, and interoperable Governed Tax-Relevant Event Record while preserving the governed meaning established by preceding TREGA™ standards.
Governance Boundary
Begins when an Event has received a sufficiently governed Tax-Relevant Event Determination.
Ends when the Determined Event has been sufficiently represented as a Governed Tax-Relevant Event Record capable of supporting lifecycle governance and downstream jurisdiction-specific taxation analysis.
Governed Event Record ≠ Tax Assessment.
12. Tax-Relevant Event Lifecycle & Continuity Standard (TRECLS)
Governed Space: Tax-Relevant Event Lifecycle & Continuity
Core Question
How can a governed Tax-Relevant Event remain continuous, reconstructable, correctable, and jurisdiction-ready throughout change without erasing historical reality or converting Event lifecycle governance into tax-law administration?
Canonical Definition
Tax-Relevant Event Lifecycle & Continuity Standard (TRECLS) defines the governance conditions under which a Governed Tax-Relevant Event Record remains methodologically continuous, historically reconstructable, and governably current as the Event is amended, corrected, superseded, maintained, closed, reopened, or referred for New Event Formation when continuity can no longer legitimately be preserved.

Governance Boundary
Begins when a Governed Tax-Relevant Event Record enters continuing use, maintenance, downstream reliance, lifecycle change, or closure consideration.
Continues throughout the remaining Event lifecycle while the Event remains relevant for downstream taxation analysis, reporting, compliance, audit, reconstruction, or other legitimate use.
Where material change invalidates the existing Event continuity basis, Tax-Relevant Event Lifecycle & Continuity Standard may trigger governed re-entry into the appropriate earlier TREGA™ governance space rather than forcing the existing Event to absorb a materially different occurrence.
Event Continuity ≠ Tax Obligation Lifecycle.
Core Governed Tax-Relevant Event Spaces
Tax-Relevant Event Context
Tax-Relevant Event Recognition
Tax-Relevant Event Formation
Tax-Relevant Event Boundary
Tax-Relevant Event Timing
Tax-Relevant Event Location
Tax-Relevant Event Participation
Tax-Relevant Value Association
Tax-Relevant Event Relationships
Tax-Relevant Event Determination
Tax-Relevant Event Record Governance
Tax-Relevant Event Lifecycle & Continuity
Recursive Tax-Relevant Event Lifecycle
TREGA™ does not end when a Governed Tax-Relevant Event Record is created.
Once a governed Event remains in use, downstream reliance, reporting, analysis, maintenance, or jurisdictional processing, the architecture becomes recursive:
Governed Tax-Relevant Event Record
↓
Event Continuity
↓
Event Amendment
↓
Event Correction
↓
Event Supersession
↓

Event Closure
↓
Jurisdiction-Ready
Tax-Relevant Event
Where materially relevant information emerges after Closure:
Closed Event
↓
Reopening Review
↓
Lifecycle Re-Entry
↓
Updated Governed Event
↓
Reclosure
Where Event continuity becomes materially invalid:
Material Change
↓
Continuity Reassessment
↓
Continuity Break
↓
New Event
Formation Referral
↓
Lifecycle Re-Entry
Lifecycle re-entry occurs at the earliest materially affected governance space.
A changed Event Context may require re-entry into Tax-Relevant Event Context Standard.
A previously unrecognized material occurrence may require re-entry into Tax-Relevant Event Recognition Standard.
A materially changed Event constitution may require re-entry into Tax-Relevant Event Formation Standard.
A changed Event Boundary may require re-entry into Tax-Relevant Event Boundary Standard.
Changed operational Timing may require re-entry into Tax-Relevant Event Timing Standard.
Changed or corrected Location may require re-entry into Tax-Relevant Event Location Standard.
Changed Participation may require re-entry into Tax-Relevant Event Participation Standard.
Changed Value Association may require re-entry into Tax-Relevant Value Association Standard.
A newly established dependency, sequence, Merge, Split, or grouping relationship may require re-entry into Tax-Relevant Event Relationship Standard.
A materially changed Event basis may require reconsideration under Tax-Relevant Event Determination Standard.

The architecture therefore supports targeted governed Event lifecycle re-entry rather than uncontrolled reconstruction of the entire Event.
Architectural Position
TREGA™ governs the complete Tax-Relevant Event Governance lifecycle before jurisdiction-specific tax determination begins.
The architecture progresses through:
Real-World / Digital Event
↓
Event Context
↓
Event Recognition
↓
Event Formation & Root Association
↓
Event Boundary
↓
Event Timing
↓
Event Location
↓
Event Participation
↓
Value Association
↓
Event Relationships
Event Determination
↓
Governed Tax-Relevant Event Record
↓
Event Continuity
& Lifecycle
↓
Jurisdiction-Ready Tax-Relevant Event
Together, these Tax-Relevant Event Governance spaces govern how the context of an occurrence is established, whether the occurrence should enter Event Governance, how it becomes a governed Event, where its boundaries lie, when and where it occurs, which actors materially participate, which governed Value results belong to it, how it relates to other Events, when it becomes formally tax-relevant, how it is represented as a governed Event Record, and how that Event remains continuous, reconstructable, correctable, supersedable, closable, and jurisdiction-ready throughout its lifecycle.
TREGA™ therefore provides a complete governance path from the first identification of the context in which something happened to the determination of whether the resulting governed Event is ready to enter jurisdiction-specific taxation analysis.

What TREGA™ Defines
TREGA™ defines:

- where Tax-Relevant Event Governance begins, - how Event Context is identified and scoped, - which occurrences should enter Event Governance, - how a recognized occurrence is formed into a governed Event, - how Event components and Root Associations are established, - where the Event begins and ends, - what belongs inside and outside the Event Boundary, - when the Event begins, continues, and completes, - how Event Duration and Temporal Order are governed, - where the Event occurs physically, digitally, operationally, or across distributed environments, - which human, organizational, digital, machine, or autonomous actors materially participate, - what participation roles those actors hold, - which governed Value references, states, and changes belong to the Event, - how Event Value Associations remain traceable, - how Events relate through dependency, sequence, grouping, Merge, or Split, - when the Event is sufficiently governed for Tax-Relevant Event Determination, - how Event Determination uncertainty and reconsideration are governed, - how a Determined Tax-Relevant Event becomes an identifiable governed Event Record, - how Event Records remain structured, linked, traceable, and interoperable, - how Event Continuity is maintained, - how Events are amended, - how incorrect Event states are corrected without historical erasure, - how successor states supersede prior states without deleting history, - how Event Closure is governed, - when a Closed Event may require reopening

ted without historical erasure, - how successor states supersede prior states without deleting history, - how Event Closure is governed, - when a Closed Event may require reopening, - when material transformation requires New Event Formation, - and when the Event becomes Jurisdiction-Ready for downstream tax-rule application.

TREGA™ provides the official Tax-Relevant Event Governance language used for Event-space identification, lifecycle navigation, governance classification, structural diagnosis, jurisdiction-readiness, Event Record interoperability, and Tax-Relevant Event architecture design across complex physical, digital, distributed, autonomous, and cross-border environments.
Critical Architectural Distinctions
Operational Reality ≠ Tax-Relevant Event Governance
Tax-Relevant Event ≠ Legally Taxable Event
Event Recognition ≠ Taxability Determination
Event Formation ≠ Event Boundary
Event Root ≠ Identity Origin
Operational Event Time ≠ Legal Tax Point
Event Timing ≠ Tax Period Determination
Event Location ≠ Tax Jurisdiction
Participant ≠ Taxpayer
Participant Identification ≠ Event Participation
Identified Actor ≠ Governed Event Participant
Value Association ≠ Value Governance
Event Relationship ≠ Event Identity
Event Determination ≠ Tax Liability Determination
Governed Event Record ≠ Tax Assessment
Event Amendment ≠ Event Correction
Correction ≠ Historical Erasure
Record Correction ≠ Event Correction by default
Supersession ≠ Historical Deletion
Successor State ≠ New Event by default
Event Continuity ≠ Tax Obligation Lifecycle
Event Closure ≠ Tax Obligation Closure
Jurisdiction-Ready ≠ Jurisdiction-Determined Cross-Architecture Governance Boundaries TREGA™ ↔ ORA™ — Operational
Reality Architecture

ORA™ — Operational Reality Architecture governs what exists and occurs in actual Operational Reality.
TREGA™ — Tax-Relevant Event Governance Architecture™ governs how occurrences from Operational Reality become structured and governed as Tax-Relevant Events.
Operational Reality ≠ Tax-Relevant Event Governance. TREGA™ ↔ OBIDENITY® — Origin-Bound Identity Governance Architecture®
OBIDENITY® — Origin-Bound Identity Governance Architecture® governs identity, origin, ownership, authority, permission, responsibility, provenance, transfer, and continuity.
TREGA™ — Tax-Relevant Event Governance Architecture™ governs whether and how an identified actor materially participates in a specific governed Event.
Identity ≠ Event Participation. TREGA™ ↔ VFM® — Value Flow Mechanism
VFM® — Value Flow Mechanism governs what happens to Value throughout its lifecycle.
TREGA™ — Tax-Relevant Event Governance Architecture™ governs which governed Value state, change, reference, or relationship belongs to a specific Tax-Relevant Event.
Value Governance ≠ Event Value Association. TREGA™ ↔ VALIDOS™ — Validation Governance Architecture
TREGA™ — Tax-Relevant Event Governance Architecture™ determines when an Event has become sufficiently governed to support downstream taxation analysis.
VALIDOS™ — Validation Governance Architecture determines whether a complete validation basis is sufficient to support a Validation Determination and intended reliance.

Event Determination ≠ Validation Determination. TREGA™ ↔ INTEGROS® — Integrity Governance Architecture
TREGA™ — Tax-Relevant Event Governance Architecture™ governs Event-specific context, formation, boundary, timing, location, participation, Value Association, relationships, Determination, Record Governance, and lifecycle.

ADIT® — Audit in Real Time Architecture governs evidential observation, preservation, verification, traceability, examination, and auditability of what occurred where applicable.

AGA™ — Accountability Governance Architecture governs who holds authority, responsibility, accountability, attribution, and decision ownership surrounding relevant actions, decisions, and failures.

TREGA™ — Tax-Relevant Event Governance Architecture™ governs the Tax-Relevant Event lifecycle.
HALIA™ — Harm & Liability Architecture governs the lifecycle of harm and liability arising from relevant occurrences.

TREGA™ ↔ Jurisdictional Tax Systems
TREGA™ — Tax-Relevant Event Governance Architecture™ governs the Event before jurisdiction-specific tax rules are applied.

Jurisdiction-Ready ≠ Jurisdiction-Determined.

TREGA™ does not define legal Taxability, Tax Jurisdiction, taxpayer determination, tax nexus, legal tax point, Tax Period, Tax Base, Tax Rate, exemptions, deductions, Tax Liability, filing obligations, payment, collection, enforcement, or other jurisdiction-specific legal tax consequences. TREGA™ governs the conditions under which a real-world or digital occurrence is contextualized, recognized, formed into a governed Event, bounded, temporally and spatially situated, associated with participants and Value, related to other Events, formally determined as tax-relevant, represented as a governed Event Record, and maintained through Continuity, Amendment, Correction, Supersession, Closure, and lifecycle re-entry until it becomes Jurisdiction-Ready for downstream tax-rule application.
Canonical Closing Statement

TREGA™ serves as the official Tax-Relevant Event Governance reference map for physical transactions, digital services, financial systems, platforms, AI agents, autonomous systems, machine-to-machine economies, distributed environments, cross-border activity, and future taxation ecosystems. By defining the primary governable spaces of the complete Tax-Relevant Event lifecycle, TREGA™ provides the architecture used to establish the context in which an occurrence exists, determine whether it should enter Event Governance, form and bound the Event, govern when and where it occurs, identify who or what materially participates, associate governed Value with the Event, establish relationships between Events, determine when the Event has become tax-relevant, convert that Event into a governed and interoperable Record, and preserve its continuity through Amendment, Correction, Supersession, Closure, reopening, and material lifecycle change. TREGA™ therefore establishes taxation-relevant Event Governance as a distinct methodological layer between Operational Reality and jurisdiction-specific taxation systems, enabling one governed Event Reality to remain structurally coherent, historically reconstructable, and Jurisdiction-Ready before different jurisdictions determine what that Event legally means under tax law.

ETOM — Event Temporal Order Module

TREGA™ ↔ Jurisdictional Tax Systems

TREGA™: determines whether an occurrence has become a sufficiently governed Tax-Relevant Event suitable for downstream analysis.
Jurisdictional Tax System: determines what that Event legally means under applicable tax law.
Tax-Relevant Event ≠ Legally Taxable Event.
Jurisdiction-Ready ≠ Jurisdiction-Determined.
Architectural Origin
TREGA™ evolved from the foundational methodological problem that taxation systems require a reliable Event layer between operational reality and legal tax determination.
Traditional taxation infrastructure often moves directly from:
Transaction Data
↓
Tax Rules
without explicitly governing what the underlying Event actually is.
As digital platforms, distributed systems, autonomous agents, machine-to-machine activity, cross-border services, and future machine economies expand, the Event itself becomes increasingly difficult to identify, bound, locate, associate with participants and Value, relate to other Events, and preserve through time.
TREGA™ therefore establishes a dedicated governance architecture between:
Operational Reality
and:
Jurisdiction-Specific Tax Determination
Its foundational principles are distributed primarily across:
Event Context
↓
Event Recognition
↓
Event Formation
↓
Event Boundary
↓
Event Timing
↓
Event Location
↓
Event Participation
↓
Value Association
↓
Event Relationships
↓
Event Determination
↓
Event Record Governance
↓
Event
Lifecycle & Continuity

The architecture establishes the governed Tax-Relevant Event as an independent methodological object before downstream tax law determines legal consequence.
Architectural Structure
Architecture: TREGA™ — Tax-Relevant Event Governance Architecture™
Category: Governance & Enforcement
Subcategory: Tax-Relevant Event Governance
Core Parent Standards: 12
Core Modules: 60
Architecture Model: Lifecycle-Based · Modular · Jurisdiction-Neutral
Primary Governance Domain: Tax-Relevant Event Governance
The architecture deliberately separates governable spaces that can independently fail.
A taxation-relevant occurrence may:
- be placed in the wrong Context; - fail to be recognized; - be incorrectly formed; - contain an incorrect Event Boundary; - have inaccurate Timing; - have incomplete or misleading Location information; - associate the wrong participants; - associate the wrong Value result; - be incorrectly related to other Events; - be prematurely determined as tax-relevant; - become an incomplete or semantically unstable Event Record; - lose lifecycle continuity through uncontrolled Amendment, Correction, Supersession, or Closure.
TREGA™ treats these not as one generic tax data problem, but as distinct Event Governance spaces requiring distinct methodological controls.
Recursive Lifecycle Principle
TREGA™ does not end when a Tax-Relevant Event Record is first created.
A governed Event may continue to change after its initial Determination and Record Governance.
During that period:

New information may emerge.
Event attributes may require Amendment.
Previously governed information may require Correction.
A successor state may Supersede a prior state.
Continuity may become uncertain.
An Event may close.
A Closed Event may require reopening.
Material transformation may require New Event Formation.
TREGA™ therefore closes recursively through TRECLS:
Governed Tax-Relevant Event Record
↓
Event Continuity
↓
Event Amendment
↓
Event Correction
↓
Event Supersession
↓
Event Closure
↓
Jurisdiction-Ready
Tax-Relevant Event
Where materially relevant new information emerges:
Closed Event
↓
Reopening Review
↓
Lifecycle Re-Entry
↓
Updated Governed Event
↓
Reclosure
Where continuity can no longer legitimately be preserved:
Material Transformation
↓
Continuity Break
↓
New Event Formation Referral
This makes Event change part of Tax-Relevant Event Governance rather than an uncontrolled downstream data-maintenance problem.
Foundational Architecture Principles
TREGA™ governs the event. The jurisdiction governs the tax.
Tax-Relevant Event ≠ Legally Taxable Event.
Tax relevance means eligibility for taxation analysis, not legal taxability.
Operational Reality must not become tax interpretation before the Event itself has been governed.
Recognition ≠ Taxability Determination.
Formation ≠ Boundary.
Event Root ≠ Identity Origin.
Operational Event Time ≠ Legal Tax Point.
Event Timing ≠ Tax Period Determination.
Event Location ≠ Tax Jurisdiction.
Participant ≠ Taxpayer.

Identified Actor ≠ Governed Event Participant.
Value Association ≠ Value Governance.
Event Determination ≠ Tax Liability Determination.
Governed Event Record ≠ Tax Assessment.
Correction ≠ Historical Erasure.
Amendment ≠ New Event by default.
Material Transformation May Require New Event Formation.
Event Continuity ≠ Tax Obligation Lifecycle.
Jurisdiction-Ready ≠ Jurisdiction-Determined.
One governed Event can support multiple legitimate jurisdictional evaluations without becoming multiple different Event realities.
Canonical Principle
TREGA™ does not govern legal Taxability, Tax Jurisdiction, taxpayer determination, tax nexus, legal tax point, Tax Period, Tax Base, Tax Rate, exemptions, deductions, Tax Liability, filing obligations, payment, collection, enforcement, or other jurisdiction-specific legal tax consequences. TREGA™ governs the methodological conditions under which real-world and digital occurrences become contextualized, recognized, formed, bounded, temporally and spatially situated, associated with participants and Value, related to other Events, formally determined as tax-relevant, represented as governed Event Records, and maintained through Amendment, Correction, Supersession, Closure, and continuity governance until they become Jurisdiction-Ready for downstream tax-rule application.
TREGA™ governs the event. The jurisdiction governs the tax.

chunks.text:
OOF™ The Value Change Association Module (VACM) governs how governed changes
The Value Change Association Module (VACM) governs how governed changes
OOF™ Origin Open Foundation™
Independent Methodological Authority
Architecture Ecosystem: Structured Reality Standards™
Architecture Family: TREGA™ — Tax-Relevant Event Governance Architecture™
Parent Standard: TRVAS — Tax-Relevant Value Association Standard
Module: VACM — Value Change Association Module
Operational Layer: Value Change Association Governance Layer
Category: Governance & Enforcement
Subcategory: Tax-Relevant Event Governance
Type: Core Module
Governed Space: Value Change Association
Origin ID: TREGA-TRVAS-VACM-003
Version: 1.0
Status: Canonical · Open Standard
Effective Date: 1 September 2026
AI-Readable: Yes
Authority: OOF®
Protection: MIP® — Methodological Intellectual Property
Canonical Language: UCL — Universal Canonical Language
Canonical Definition
The Value Change Association Module (VACM) governs how governed changes affecting value are materially associated with a specific Tax-Relevant Event through the Governed Value References established by VARM.
VACM determines whether a governed Value Change legitimately belongs to the event, how that relationship is qualified, and how multiple, partial, direct, indirect, sequential, or conflicting Value Change Associations are represented.

VACM does not determine whether value actually changed, how the change occurred within the Value Lifecycle, or what economic, accounting, legal, or tax consequence follows from that change.
VFM® remains authoritative for the underlying Value Change.
Its principal task is:
Governed Value Reference + Governed Value Change
↓
Governed Event–Value Change Association
The foundational distinction is:
Value Change Association ≠ Value Change Governance.
Operational Role
Events frequently coincide with changes in value.
Value may be: created; increased; decreased; transferred; transformed; consumed; developed; degraded; impaired; nullified; restored; or otherwise materially changed.
But temporal proximity between an event and a Value Change does not establish that the event and change belong together.
VACM provides the governance mechanism for determining whether an already-governed Value Change is materially associated with the event.
It therefore protects TREGA™ from making a common methodological error:
observing a Value Change and automatically attributing that change to the event.
Internal Module Flow
TRVAS operates through:
VAIM — Value Association Identification
↓
VARM — Value Reference
↓
VACM — Value Change Association
↓
VASM — Value State Association
↓
VATM — Value Association Traceability
↓
Governed Value-Associated Event
VACM receives the Governed Value Reference Set from VARM together with relevant governed Value Change information.
Its output proceeds to VASM.

Operational Transition
The canonical VACM transition is:
Governed Value Reference Set + Governed Value Change Information
↓
Value Change Association Governance
↓
Governed Value Change Association Set
VACM associates change with the event.
It does not create the Value Change.
Operational Space
VACM governs: Event–Value Change Association; Value Change relevance; change-association basis; direct and indirect association; partial association; multiple Value Changes; sequential Value Changes; concurrent Value Changes; positive and negative changes; transfer-related changes; transformation-related changes; consumption-related changes; machine-generated changes; association materiality; association qualification; association uncertainty; association conflict; association correction; and Value Change Association readiness for downstream TRVAS governance.
Operational Scope
VACM may operate across Value Changes associated with: commercial events; payments; banking; digital assets; goods; services; rights; resources; energy; computational capacity; industrial production; marketplaces; blockchain systems; AI-agent activity; autonomous systems; machine-to-machine activity; infrastructure operations; and other governed economic or operational environments.
The form of value does not determine the validity of the association.
Governed Value Change
A Governed Value Change is an upstream governance result describing a material change affecting a governed value.
VACM may consume such a result.

It does not recreate it.
The architecture boundary is explicit:
VFM® governs what changed in the value. VACM governs whether that governed change belongs to the event. Event–Value Change Association
An Event–Value Change Association represents a sufficiently governed relationship between: a Governed Tax-Relevant Event; a Governed Value Reference; and a Governed Value Change.
The existence of all three does not automatically establish the relationship.
Event + Value + Change ≠ Established Value Change Association by default.
The association itself requires governance.
Association Basis
VACM shall preserve the basis supporting the relationship between the event and the Value Change.
The basis may derive from operational, transactional, temporal, participant-related, system-generated, contractual, technical, or other legitimate governed information.
The existence of one indicator does not automatically establish the association.
Association Evidence ≠ Association Determination by default.
Direct Value Change Association
A Value Change may occur directly through the governed event.
For example, an event may directly transfer, consume, transform, increase, or decrease a governed value.
Where sufficient support exists, VACM may establish a Direct Value Change Association.
However:
Direct Value Change Association ≠ Taxable Event Determination.
Indirect Value Change Association
A Value Change may be materially related through intermediate operations.
For example:
Governed Event
↓

Platform Operation
↓
Settlement Process
↓
Governed Value Change
The presence of an intermediary does not automatically invalidate the relationship.
Indirect Association ≠ Irrelevant Change by default.
VACM shall preserve the actual association structure where sufficiently supported.
Partial Value Change Association
Only part of a governed Value Change may belong to the event.
For example, one settlement may cover several events, or one resource-consumption record may aggregate several operations.
VACM shall support partial association without forcing the entire change onto one event.
Partial Association ≠ Complete Value Change Association.
Multiple Value Changes
One event may legitimately be associated with multiple Value Changes.
For example:
Event
↓
Payment Change + Asset Change + Service Value Change + Resource Consumption Change
Therefore:
One Event ≠ One Value Change by default.
VACM shall preserve materially distinct changes.
One Value Change Across Multiple Events
A single governed Value Change may also relate to several events.
For example, one settlement may resolve several transactions.
VACM shall permit qualified multi-event association where operational reality supports it.
One Value Change ≠ One Event by default.
TRERLS remains authoritative for relationships among the events themselves.
Sequential Value Changes
An event may be associated with Value Changes occurring in a governed sequence.
For example:
Authorization
↓
Reservation
↓
Transfer
↓
Settlement
↓
Refund

VACM may preserve the association sequence where materially relevant.
However:
Sequential Value Changes ≠ Separate Events by default.
Whether separate events exist belongs to Event Formation, Boundary, and Relationship governance.
Concurrent Value Changes
Several Value Changes may occur simultaneously or within the same operational stage.
VACM shall support concurrent associations without forcing an artificial sequence.
Concurrent Value Changes ≠ Same Value Change.
Value Increase Association
An event may be associated with an increase in governed value.
VACM may establish the association where the increase is already governed upstream.
It does not determine the amount, cause, legal recognition, or tax consequence of the increase.
Value Increase Association ≠ Taxable Gain.
Value Decrease Association
An event may be associated with a reduction in governed value.
VACM may preserve this relationship without determining whether the decrease constitutes an expense, loss, deduction, impairment, or other legal or accounting category.
Value Decrease Association ≠ Tax Deduction.
Value Transfer Association
A governed event may be associated with movement or transfer of value.
VACM may establish the relationship between the event and the governed transfer result.
However:
Value Transfer Association ≠ Ownership Transfer Determination.
Ownership remains outside VACM.
Value Transformation Association
Value may change form while remaining part of a governed lifecycle.

An event may be associated with such transformation.
VACM may represent the association without determining whether the transformed value constitutes a new asset, legal object, accounting item, or taxable category.
Value Transformation Association ≠ Legal Reclassification.
Value Consumption Association
Events may consume value such as: energy; materials; computational capacity; machine time; service capacity; infrastructure resources; or other productive inputs.
VACM may associate a governed consumption change with the event.
Value Consumption ≠ Deductible Cost by default.
Value Creation and Development Association
An event may contribute to emergence or development of value.
Where VFM® has governed the relevant result, VACM may associate that change with the event.
VACM does not determine Value Origin or Value Development itself.
Value Development Association ≠ Value Ownership.
Value Degradation and Nullification Association
An event may contribute to degradation, impairment, destruction, or nullification of value.
VACM may associate the governed result with the event without determining responsibility or liability.
Value Degradation Association ≠ Liability Determination.
HALIA™ remains authoritative for harm and liability where applicable.
Value Restoration Association
An event may restore previously degraded or nullified value.
VACM may preserve this relationship where the restoration result is governed upstream.

Value Restoration Association ≠ Legal Compensation Determination. Reversal
A Value Change may later be reversed.
A payment may be reversed.
A digital-asset transfer may be returned.
A resource allocation may be cancelled.
VACM shall preserve the relationship between the original and reversal-associated changes without assuming that the original event never occurred.
Value Change Reversal ≠ Historical Erasure. Refund
A refund may be associated with an earlier governed event or may itself participate in a separate event structure.
VACM shall not automatically collapse the refund into the original Value Change.
Refund ≠ Original Value Change Erasure.
Whether the refund constitutes part of the same event or another related event belongs to the appropriate TREGA™ governance layers. Correction
A Value Change Association may later be shown to be incorrect.
VACM shall support governed correction while preserving reconstructability.
Association Correction ≠ Historical Erasure.
Value Change Timing
A Value Change may occur, be recorded, recognized, settled, or observed at times different from the governed Event Timing.
VACM shall not redefine Event Timing from a Value Change timestamp.
Value Change Timestamp ≠ Event Time by default.
TRETS remains authoritative for Event Timing.
Value Change Location
A Value Change may be recorded or technically executed in a location different from the governed Event Location.

For example, a digital transfer may be processed through infrastructure in several countries.
Therefore:
Value Change Location ≠ Event Location by default.
TRELS remains authoritative for Event Location.
Value Change and Participation
A participant may be associated with a Value Change.
That relationship does not automatically establish ownership, entitlement, responsibility, or taxpayer status.
Participant Associated with Value Change ≠ Value Owner.
Participant Associated with Value Change ≠ Taxpayer.
TREPS remains authoritative for Event Participation.
Value Change and Ownership
VACM does not determine whether ownership changes because value changes or transfers.
Value Change ≠ Ownership Change by default.
OBIDENITY® remains authoritative for ownership governance where applicable.
Value Change and Accountability
The association of a Value Change with an event does not establish which participant caused or is accountable for that change.
Value Change Association ≠ Accountability Determination.
AGA™ remains authoritative for accountability governance.
Value Change and Liability
A negative Value Change may represent loss, degradation, destruction, or impairment.
VACM does not determine who is liable.
Negative Value Change ≠ Liability by default.
HALIA™ remains authoritative where applicable.
Value Change and Taxation
A governed Value Change may later be important to taxation.

However, VACM does not determine whether the change constitutes: taxable income; taxable gain; deductible loss; taxable consideration; taxable benefit; realization; disposal; acquisition; taxable transfer; customs value; or another jurisdiction-specific tax concept.
Therefore:
Governed Value Change Association ≠ Taxable Value Change.
A jurisdiction may later apply its own legal rules to the governed event-value structure.
Multi-Jurisdiction Governance
The same governed Value Change Association may support different interpretations across jurisdictions.
The model is:
One Governed Value Change Association
↓
Multiple Jurisdictional Evaluations
Jurisdiction A may treat the change as taxable.
Jurisdiction B may classify it differently.
Jurisdiction C may not recognize a taxable consequence.
TREGA™ preserves one governed operational reality while allowing legal interpretation to remain jurisdiction-specific.
Machine and Autonomous Value Changes
AI agents, robots, software systems, and autonomous machines may initiate or produce Value Changes without contemporaneous human execution.
Examples include: autonomous asset transfer; resource consumption; energy allocation; computational exchange; machine-generated production; autonomous procurement; service execution; or digital settlement.
VACM shall support association of such governed changes with the event.
Machine-Generated Value Change ≠ Human Value Change by default.
Likewise:
Autonomous Value Change ≠ Autonomous Tax Liability.

Association Materiality
VACM shall determine whether the relationship between the governed Value Change and event is sufficiently material to require association.
Materiality concerns the event-change relationship.
It does not determine legal, accounting, audit, or tax materiality.
Association Materiality ≠ Tax Materiality.
Association Confidence
A Value Change Association may possess different levels of support.
VACM may represent the association as:
Established · Qualified · Partial · Ambiguous · Conflicted · Unresolved
A downstream need for a deterministic value shall not override governance uncertainty.
Association Uncertainty
It may be unclear whether the event caused, contributed to, coincided with, or merely preceded a Value Change.
VACM shall preserve that uncertainty.
Temporal Proximity ≠ Value Change Association.
and:
Association Uncertainty ≠ Permission to Assume Causation.
VACM governs association, not universal causality.
Association Conflict
Different sources may disagree about whether a Value Change belongs to the event.
VACM shall preserve materially relevant conflict until sufficiently resolved.
Association Conflict ≠ Permission for Convenient Attribution.
Governance States
VACM may represent states including:
Change Association Ready
Change Association Under Governance
Direct Change Association
Indirect Change Association
Partial Change Association
Multi-Change Association
Sequential Change Association
Concurrent Change Association

Change Association Qualified
Change Association Ambiguous
Change Association Conflicted
Change Association Unresolved
Governed Value Change Association Established
These states describe Event–Value Change Association only.
Governance Requirements

VACM implementations shall ensure that: Value Changes are associated only through governed Value References; upstream governed Value Changes are consumed without being redefined; direct and indirect associations can be distinguished; partial association can be represented; multiple Value Changes can belong to one event; one Value Change can relate to multiple events where legitimate; sequential and concurrent changes can be represented; increases and decreases remain distinct from tax conclusions; transfers remain distinct from ownership determination; transformations remain distinct from legal reclassification; consumption remains distinct from deductibility; degradation remains distinct from liability; restoration remains distinct from compensation; reversals do not erase historical changes; refunds do not automatically erase original Value Changes; corrections remain traceable; Value Change timestamps do not redefine Event Timing; Value Change location does not redefine Event Location; participant association does not establish ownership or taxpayer status; accountability and liability remain separate; uncertainty remains visible; conflict remains visible; VFM® ownership of Value Change governance remains preserved; and tax determination remains downstream.
Governance Logic
IF VARM establishes a Governed Value Reference and a relevant governed Value Change exists, THEN VACM shall evaluate whether the change materially belongs to the governed event.

IF the association is sufficiently supported, THEN a Governed Value Change Association may be established.
IF only part of a Value Change belongs to the event, THEN partial association shall be preserved rather than assigning the complete change.
IF multiple Value Changes belong to the event, THEN materially distinct associations shall remain separately governable.
IF one Value Change relates to several events, THEN exclusivity shall not be assumed.
IF a reversal, refund, or correction occurs, THEN historical Value Change Association shall remain reconstructable.
IF the association remains uncertain or conflicted, THEN the corresponding governance state shall remain visible.
IF information indicates a possible Event Formation, Event Boundary, Event Timing, or Event Relationship issue, THEN VACM shall refer the issue to the appropriate TREGA™ layer rather than redefining those spaces.
IF Value Change Association is sufficiently governed, THEN the result shall proceed to VASM for Value State Association governance.
Minimum Implementation Framework
A minimum VACM implementation should support:
Governed Event Reference The governed event to which the Value Change may be associated.
Governed Value Reference The VARM-governed value reference.
Governed Value Change Reference The upstream governed Value Change being associated.
Change Association Identifier The stable identifier for the Event–Value Change Association.

Change Type Reference The relevant upstream governed change classification where available.
Association Basis The basis supporting the relationship between event and change.
Association Directness Direct, indirect, or otherwise qualified.
Association Extent Complete, partial, or otherwise qualified.
Sequence State Whether the change forms part of a materially relevant sequence.
Concurrency State Whether the change occurs concurrently with another associated change.
Reversal Reference Any materially relevant reversal relationship.
Refund Reference Any materially relevant refund relationship.
Correction Reference Any governed correction affecting the association.
Association Confidence The qualified confidence attached to the association.
Ambiguity State Whether the association remains ambiguous.
Conflict State Whether materially conflicting associations exist.
Traceability Reference The information required to reconstruct the association.
Governance State The current VACM state.
Handoff State Whether the result is ready for VASM.
Governance Outputs

VACM may produce: Governed Direct Value Change Association; Governed Indirect Value Change Association; Governed Partial Value Change Association; Governed Multi-Change Association Structure; Governed Sequential Value Change Association; Governed Concurrent Value Change Association; Value Transfer Association; Value Transformation Association; Value Consumption Association; Value Development Association; Value Degradation Association; Value Restoration Association; Value Change Reversal Relationship; Value Change Association Correction; Value Change Association Confidence State; Value Change Association Ambiguity State; Value Change Association Conflict State; and the principal output: Governed Value Change Association Set.
Critical Distinctions
Value Change Association ≠ Value Change Governance.
VFM® governs what changed in value. VACM governs whether that governed change belongs to the event.
Event + Value + Change ≠ Established Value Change Association by default.
Association Evidence ≠ Association Determination by default.
Direct Value Change Association ≠ Taxable Event Determination.
Indirect Association ≠ Irrelevant Change by default.
Partial Association ≠ Complete Value Change Association.
One Event ≠ One Value Change by default.
One Value Change ≠ One Event by default.
Sequential Value Changes ≠ Separate Events by default.
Concurrent Value Changes ≠ Same Value Change.
Value Increase Association ≠ Taxable Gain.
Value Decrease Association ≠ Tax Deduction.

Value Transfer Association ≠ Ownership Transfer Determination.
Value Transformation Association ≠ Legal Reclassification.
Value Consumption ≠ Deductible Cost by default.
Value Development Association ≠ Value Ownership.
Value Degradation Association ≠ Liability Determination.
Value Restoration Association ≠ Legal Compensation Determination.
Value Change Reversal ≠ Historical Erasure.
Value Change Timestamp ≠ Event Time by default.
Value Change Location ≠ Event Location by default.
Value Change ≠ Ownership Change by default.
Value Change Association ≠ Accountability Determination.
Governed Value Change Association ≠ Taxable Value Change.
Temporal Proximity ≠ Value Change Association.
Enterprise Application
VACM enables businesses, banks, digital platforms, blockchain infrastructures, ERP systems, AI agents, and machine systems to connect governed Value Changes to the correct event without turning operational change into premature legal or tax conclusions.
The operational path is:
VARM — Governed Value Reference Set
↓
Governed Value Change Information
↓
VACM — Governed Value Change Association Set
↓
VASM — Value State Association
↓
VATM — Value Association Traceability
↓
Governed Value-Associated Event
This enables downstream systems to understand not merely that value changed, but which governed event the change materially belongs to. Use Case 1 — Cross-Border Commerce with Settlement, Refund, and Multiple Value Changes

A multinational marketplace processes a commercial event involving goods, platform services, payment processing, logistics, and currency conversion.
The customer payment creates several operational records. The merchant later receives settlement after platform fees are deducted. A partial refund subsequently occurs.
VFM® governs the relevant Value Changes.
VACM determines which of those governed changes materially belong to the event, distinguishes direct, partial, sequential, and refund-related associations, and preserves the original change history.
It does not determine whether the settlement constitutes taxable income, whether the refund creates a deduction, or which jurisdiction may tax any resulting amount.
The result is a governed Event–Value Change structure suitable for subsequent tax analysis without rewriting operational value reality. Use Case 2 — Autonomous Infrastructure and Digital-Asset Settlement
An autonomous industrial system obtains computational capacity and energy from distributed providers.
AI agents coordinate allocation, machine systems consume resources, and settlement occurs through digital assets.
Several governed Value Changes occur: resource consumption, service-value change, energy consumption, digital-asset transfer, and potentially later settlement adjustments.
VACM associates the relevant governed Value Changes with the event while keeping the underlying Value Lifecycle under VFM®.

It does not treat the blockchain transfer as the complete economic change, attribute ownership from wallet movement, or determine whether any change is taxable.
The resulting association structure allows different jurisdictions to evaluate the same governed operational reality according to their own tax rules.
Canonical Boundary
VACM owns the association of already-governed Value Changes with a specific Tax-Relevant Event, including directness, indirectness, partial association, multiple changes, sequence, concurrency, reversals, refunds, correction, qualification, uncertainty, conflict, and association-specific traceability.
VACM does not own Value Change creation or determination, the Value Lifecycle, Value Reference establishment, Value State governance, Value State Association, complete Value Association traceability, Event Formation, Event Boundary, Event Timing, Event Location, Event Participation, Event Relationships, ownership, entitlement, accountability, liability, taxable value, Tax Base, Tax Liability, or another jurisdiction-specific tax conclusion.
Its governance ends when relevant governed Value Changes are sufficiently associated with the event for Value State Association governance.
Canonical Handoff
VARM — Governed Value Reference Set
↓
VACM — Governed Value Change Association Set
↓
VASM — Value State Association Governance
Canonical Closing Statement

VACM connects governed Value Change to governed Event Reality without taking ownership of the Value Change itself.
A change in value may be real without belonging to the event, and a change belonging to the event may have different legal consequences across jurisdictions.
Value Change Association ≠ Value Change Governance.
Governed Value Change Association ≠ Taxable Value Change.
