chunks.text:
OOF™ The Value Association Identification Module (VAIM) governs how
The Value Association Identification Module (VAIM) governs how
OOF™ Origin Open Foundation™
Independent Methodological Authority
Architecture Ecosystem: Structured Reality Standards™
Architecture Family: TREGA™ — Tax-Relevant Event Governance Architecture™
Parent Standard: TRVAS — Tax-Relevant Value Association Standard
Module: VAIM — Value Association Identification Module
Operational Layer: Value Association Identification Governance Layer
Category: Governance & Enforcement
Subcategory: Tax-Relevant Event Governance
Type: Core Module
Governed Space: Value Association Identification
Origin ID: TREGA-TRVAS-VAIM-001
Version: 1.0
Status: Canonical · Open Standard
Effective Date: 1 September 2026
AI-Readable: Yes
Authority: OOF®
Protection: MIP® — Methodology Intellectual Property Protection
Canonical Language: UCL — Universal Canonical Language
Canonical Definition
The Value Association Identification Module (VAIM) governs how value-related information potentially relevant to a Governed Participatory Event is discovered, distinguished, screened, qualified, and admitted into Tax-Relevant Value Association governance.
VAIM establishes which available governed value results possess a sufficiently plausible and materially relevant relationship to the event to become Value Association Candidates.
Its principal task is: Available Governed Value Information
↓
Governed Value Association Candidate Set

VAIM does not establish the complete Value Association.
It identifies the value results that are eligible to proceed through TRVAS governance.
The foundational distinction is: Value Presence ≠ Event Value Association Operational Role
Modern events may be surrounded by large quantities of value-related information.
A single event may generate or interact with: prices; payments; invoices; accounting entries; asset transfers; balances; commissions; discounts; refunds; service values; resource consumption; digital assets; energy use; computational resources; rights; benefits; losses; and non-monetary value.
Not all such information necessarily belongs to the event.
VAIM prevents surrounding value data from being automatically absorbed into the governed event merely because it appears in the same system, transaction chain, account, ledger, platform, wallet, process, or operational environment.
Internal Module Flow
TRVAS operates through:
VAIM — Value Association Identification
→ VARM — Value Reference
→ VACM — Value Change Association
→ VASM — Value State Association
→ VATM — Value Association Traceability
→ Governed Value-Associated Event
VAIM is the entry point into this flow.
Its output becomes the governed input to VARM.
Operational Transition
The canonical VAIM transition is:
Governed Participatory Event + Available Governed Value Information
→ Value Association Identification Governance
→ Governed Value Association Candidate Set

A Value Association Candidate is a governed value result or value-related reference whose potential relationship to the event is sufficiently supported to require further TRVAS governance. Value Association Candidate ≠ Established Value Association Operational Space
VAIM governs: value-information discovery; potential value-association identification; candidate differentiation; value-source screening; event-relevance screening; material relevance; candidate inclusion; candidate exclusion; duplicate candidate detection; multi-value candidate identification; monetary and non-monetary candidate recognition; direct and indirect candidate recognition; candidate uncertainty; candidate conflict; and candidate readiness for subsequent Value Reference governance.
VAIM does not determine the legal tax treatment of any candidate.
Operational Scope
VAIM may process value-related information originating from: ERP systems; accounting systems; banking infrastructure; payment systems; invoices; procurement systems; commerce platforms; marketplaces; blockchain networks; digital-asset systems; smart contracts; industrial systems; logistics systems; energy systems; AI agents; autonomous systems; machine networks; digital services; operational databases; or governed outputs from VFM®.
The source of value information does not by itself establish event relevance.
Value Association Candidate

A Value Association Candidate is a sufficiently distinguishable value result or value-related reference that may materially belong to the governed event and therefore requires further Value Association governance.
Candidate status means:
Potentially relevant to the event.
It does not mean:
Established as belonging to the event.
Therefore: Candidate Value ≠ Governed Event Value Candidate Identification
VAIM shall identify value information only where a plausible relationship to the governed event exists.
Possible indicators may include: event-generated value information; participant-linked value information; event-linked payment; asset movement; resource consumption; service delivery; value-state information; governed Value Change; contractual or operational value reference; machine-generated value activity; or another sufficiently supported event-value connection.
These indicators initiate governance.
They do not prove the final association.
Event Relevance
Value information may be economically real while still being irrelevant to the specific event.
VAIM therefore distinguishes:
Value existence
from:
Event relevance
and:
Established Event Value Association.
The sequence is:
Value Information
↓
Potential Event Relevance
↓
Value Association Candidate
↓
Subsequent TRVAS Governance
Therefore: Economic Relevance ≠ Event Relevance by Default Material Relevance
VAIM shall determine whether the potential relationship is sufficiently material to require governance.

Material relevance concerns the relationship between the value information and the event.
It does not determine whether the amount is materially significant under accounting, tax, audit, or securities law.
Therefore:
Value Association Materiality ≠ Legal Materiality.
A small monetary amount may be operationally essential to an event.
A large amount appearing nearby may be unrelated.
Monetary Value Candidates
VAIM may identify monetary value information including: payments; prices; fees; commissions; settlements; refunds; deposits; credits; debits; currency amounts; or other monetary records.
However: Monetary Record ≠ Event Value Association by Default
A payment record may relate to another event, several events, an earlier obligation, a later settlement, or a bundled economic structure.
Non-Monetary Value Candidates
VAIM shall support non-monetary value information.
Candidates may include: goods; services; rights; access; resources; energy; computational capacity; productive capacity; digital assets; operational benefits; value loss; or other governed value results.
Therefore: No Monetary Amount ≠ No Value Association Candidate
This is essential for digital and machine economies.
Governed Value Results
Where VFM® or another legitimate governance source has already established a governed value result, VAIM may consume that result as an input.
VAIM shall not independently recreate its Value Lifecycle governance.
The boundary is:
VFM® establishes what happened to value.

VAIM establishes whether that governed value result should enter Event Value Association governance.
Recorded Amount
A numeric amount may be present in an operational system.
Its presence alone does not establish that it belongs to the event.
Therefore:
Recorded Amount ≠ Value Association Candidate by Default.
VAIM requires an event-relevance basis.
Invoice Information
An invoice may contain strong evidence of an economic relationship.
But invoice information may contain: several items; several events; taxes; fees; discounts; bundled services; adjustments; historical charges; or later corrections.
Therefore:
Invoice Presence ≠ Complete Event Value.
and:
Invoice Amount ≠ Taxable Value.
VAIM may identify individual value candidates without treating the invoice total as a single authoritative event value.
Payment Information
Payment information may support Value Association Identification.
However, payment timing and economic-event timing may differ.
One payment may settle several events.
Several payments may settle one event.
A payment may be reversed.
A deposit may precede the event.
Therefore: Payment ≠ Event Value by Default
VAIM identifies the potential relationship.
It does not resolve the complete Value Association.
Digital-Asset Information
Blockchain and distributed-ledger systems may expose highly visible asset movements.
Visibility does not establish event meaning.

A digital-asset transfer may represent: payment; internal transfer; collateral; settlement; exchange; liquidity movement; staking; protocol interaction; asset migration; or another activity.
Therefore: On-Chain Transfer ≠ Tax-Relevant Event Value by Default
VAIM may identify the transfer as a candidate while preserving the need for subsequent governance.
Resource Consumption
An event may consume economically relevant resources without generating a conventional transaction record.
Examples include: energy; computing capacity; storage; bandwidth; machine time; production capacity; materials; or infrastructure resources.
VAIM may identify such governed value information as candidates where materially related to the event.
Resource Consumption ≠ Taxable Value by Default.
Value Creation
An event may create or develop value without an immediate payment or transfer.
VAIM may identify governed value-creation results where they materially relate to the event.
Therefore:
No Transfer ≠ No Value Candidate.
The existence and lifecycle of the value remain governed by VFM®.
Value Loss and Degradation
An event may be associated with value loss, degradation, impairment, destruction, or nullification.
Such outcomes may be relevant even where the event contains no positive value transfer.
Therefore:
Value Loss ≠ Absence of Value Association.
VAIM may admit the relevant governed value result as a candidate without determining liability or tax treatment.
Direct Candidate Relationship

A value result may possess an apparent direct relationship to the event.
Examples include: payment specifically generated for the event; goods transferred during the event; service delivered through the event; or resource directly consumed by the event.
Directness strengthens potential relevance.
It does not establish final association.
Therefore:
Direct Value Connection ≠ Established Value Association.
Indirect Candidate Relationship
Some value results may relate through intermediate operations or systems.
For example:
Event
↓
Platform
↓
Settlement System
↓
Value Transfer
The value may remain materially relevant despite the indirect path.
Therefore:
Indirect Value Connection ≠ Irrelevant Value by Default.
VAIM may admit such information for subsequent governance.
Participant-Linked Value
Value information may be linked to an Event Participant.
That linkage may support candidate identification.
It does not establish ownership or final event association.
Therefore:
Participant-Linked Value ≠ Participant-Owned Value.
and:
Participant-Linked Value ≠ Event Value by Default.
TREPS remains authoritative for Event Participation.
Multiple Value Candidates
One event may produce many legitimate candidates.
VAIM shall not force them into a single value representation.
The candidate structure may therefore be:
Governed Event
↓
Candidate A + Candidate B + Candidate C + Candidate N
Therefore: One Event ≠ One Value Candidate

Subsequent TRVAS modules determine how those candidates are governed.
One Candidate Across Multiple Events
The same governed value reference may potentially relate to several events.
VAIM shall not automatically assign exclusivity.
Therefore:
One Value Candidate ≠ One Event by Default.
Event Relationship governance may later become relevant under TRERLS.
Duplicate Candidate Detection
Different systems may expose multiple references to the same underlying value result.
For example:
Invoice Record + Payment Record + ERP Record + Bank Record
may represent overlapping information rather than four independent values.
VAIM shall support detection of potential duplication.
However: Multiple Value Records ≠ Multiple Values by Default
VAIM shall not merge candidates where equivalence remains uncertain.
Candidate Differentiation
Conversely, similar amounts or descriptions do not prove that two records represent the same value.
Therefore:
Same Amount ≠ Same Value
Same Currency ≠ Same Value
Same Participant ≠ Same Value
Similar Description ≠ Value Equivalence
Candidate differentiation must remain evidence-based.
Source Reliability
A value candidate may originate from one or more sources.
Source reliability may influence candidate qualification.
However:
Trusted Source ≠ Event Relevance by Default.
A highly reliable bank record may still describe value unrelated to the event under governance.
VAIM separates source quality from event relationship.
Source Conflict

Different sources may identify incompatible value information.
VAIM shall preserve materially relevant conflicts.
For example:
ERP: CHF 10,000
Invoice: CHF 9,500
Settlement: CHF 9,200
VAIM does not select a taxable amount.
It identifies and preserves the candidate structure and conflict for subsequent governance.
Therefore: Value Data Conflict ≠ Permission for Convenient Value Selection Candidate Uncertainty
A value relationship may remain uncertain.
VAIM shall not convert uncertainty into artificial certainty merely because a downstream system requires a value field.
Therefore: Required Value Field ≠ Permission to Invent Event Value
Candidate uncertainty must remain visible.
Candidate Exclusion
Value information may be excluded from further TRVAS governance where sufficient evidence establishes that it does not materially relate to the governed event.
Exclusion should itself remain traceable where materially relevant.
Therefore:
Candidate Exclusion ≠ Value Nonexistence.
The value may exist but belong elsewhere.
Candidate Reconsideration
New information may justify reconsideration of previously included or excluded value information.
VAIM shall permit governed reconsideration without silently rewriting historical decisions.
Candidate Reconsideration ≠ Historical Erasure.
Value Identification and Event Boundary
VAIM operates inside the governed Event Boundary.
Value information shall not automatically enlarge that boundary.

Therefore: Value Candidate Discovery ≠ Event Boundary Expansion
If candidate information indicates a possible Event Boundary problem, VAIM shall refer the issue to TREBS rather than redefine the event itself.
Value Identification and Event Participation
A value candidate may reveal information about an actor.
VAIM shall not independently establish Event Participation from that information.
Therefore:
Value Candidate ≠ Participant Determination.
TREPS remains authoritative for participation.
Value Identification and Ownership
VAIM does not determine who owns the candidate value.
Therefore: Value Candidate ≠ Ownership Determination
OBIDENITY® remains authoritative for governed ownership where applicable.
Value Identification and Value Lifecycle
VAIM does not determine: Value Origin; Value Emergence; Value State; Value Change; Value Development; Value Degradation; Value Nullification; Value Restoration; or Value Extinction.
Those belong to VFM®.
VAIM only determines whether available governed value information should enter TRVAS Value Association governance.
Value Identification and Taxation
Candidate identification occurs before jurisdiction-specific tax evaluation.
VAIM does not determine: taxable value; Tax Base; taxable income; taxable gain; consideration under tax law; customs value; transfer-pricing value; deductible amount; exemption; or Tax Liability.
Therefore: Value Association Candidate ≠ Taxable Value Machine and Autonomous Events

Machine and autonomous systems may generate value information without traditional commercial records.
Examples may include: autonomous resource allocation; machine-to-machine service exchange; computational consumption; energy exchange; autonomous procurement; digital-resource transfer; or machine-generated production.
VAIM shall permit these value signals to enter candidate governance where materially relevant.
Therefore: No Invoice ≠ No Value Candidate
and: No Human Transaction ≠ No Value Candidate Candidate Governance States
VAIM may represent states including:
Value Information Detected
Candidate Screening
Candidate Qualified
Candidate Included
Candidate Excluded
Candidate Duplicated
Candidate Ambiguous
Candidate Conflicted
Candidate Unresolved
Value Association Candidate Established
These states govern admission into Value Association governance.
They do not establish final Value Association.
Governance Requirements

VAIM implementations shall ensure that: available value information can be discovered; event relevance is evaluated before candidate admission; monetary and non-monetary value can be recognized; governed VFM® outputs can be consumed without being redefined; payments are not automatically treated as complete Event Value; invoice amounts are not automatically treated as taxable value; digital-asset transfers are not automatically treated as Event Value; resource consumption can be identified where materially relevant; value creation and value loss can enter candidate governance; direct and indirect relationships can be recognized; multiple candidates can exist for one event; one candidate can potentially relate to multiple events; duplicate records are not automatically treated as distinct values; similar records are not automatically merged; participant-linked value is not automatically treated as participant-owned value; source reliability remains distinct from Event Relevance; uncertainty remains visible; conflicts remain visible; exclusions remain traceable where required; candidate reconsideration does not erase governance history; Event Boundary remains protected; Event Participation remains governed by TREPS; ownership remains separate; the Value Lifecycle remains governed by VFM®; and tax valuation remains downstream.
Governance Logic
IF a Governed Participatory Event exists, THEN available governed value information may enter VAIM screening.

IF value information has a plausible relationship to the event, THEN Event Relevance shall be evaluated.
IF the relationship is sufficiently material to require further governance, THEN a Value Association Candidate may be established.
IF multiple materially distinct candidates exist, THEN they shall remain distinguishable.
IF multiple records may describe the same underlying value, THEN potential duplication shall be preserved until sufficiently resolved.
IF a candidate relationship remains uncertain or conflicted, THEN the corresponding governance state shall remain visible.
IF value information is sufficiently shown to be unrelated to the event, THEN it may be excluded without denying the existence of the value itself.
IF candidate information indicates an Event Boundary problem, THEN VAIM shall refer the issue upstream rather than redefine the event.
IF candidate status is sufficiently governed, THEN the candidate shall proceed to VARM for Value Reference governance.
Minimum Implementation Framework
A minimum VAIM implementation should support:
Governed Event Reference
The Governed Participatory Event under Value Association governance.
Candidate Identifier
A stable identifier for the Value Association Candidate.
Value Information Type
The type of value-related information being evaluated.
Value Source Reference
The source from which the candidate information originates.
Upstream Governed Value Reference
The relevant VFM® or other governed value reference where available.

Candidate Form
Monetary, non-monetary, digital, resource-based, service-based, asset-based, or another governed form.
Event Relevance Basis
The basis supporting possible association with the event.
Material Relevance State
Whether the relationship is sufficiently material for further governance.
Direct / Indirect State
The apparent relationship path between candidate and event.
Participant Link Reference
Relevant TREPS participant reference where applicable.
Duplicate State
Whether the candidate may duplicate another value record.
Candidate Confidence
The qualified confidence attached to candidate identification.
Ambiguity State
Whether the candidate relationship remains ambiguous.
Conflict State
Whether materially conflicting value information exists.
Inclusion / Exclusion State
Whether the candidate proceeds through TRVAS governance.
Traceability Reference
The information required to reconstruct candidate identification.
Governance State
The current VAIM state.
Handoff State
Whether the candidate is ready for VARM.
Governance Outputs

VAIM may produce: Value Association Candidate; Monetary Value Candidate; Non-Monetary Value Candidate; Digital-Asset Value Candidate; Resource Value Candidate; Governed Value Result Candidate; Direct Value Candidate; Indirect Value Candidate; Multi-Value Candidate Structure; Potential Duplicate Value Candidate; Candidate Exclusion Record; Candidate Confidence State; Candidate Ambiguity State; Candidate Conflict State; Candidate Traceability Record; and the principal output:
Governed Value Association Candidate Set
This output proceeds to VARM.
Critical Distinctions
Value Presence ≠ Event Value Association
Value Association Candidate ≠ Established Value Association
Candidate Value ≠ Governed Event Value
Economic Relevance ≠ Event Relevance by Default
Value Association Materiality ≠ Legal Materiality
Monetary Record ≠ Event Value Association by Default
No Monetary Amount ≠ No Value Association Candidate
Recorded Amount ≠ Value Association Candidate by Default
Invoice Presence ≠ Complete Event Value
Invoice Amount ≠ Taxable Value
Payment ≠ Event Value by Default
On-Chain Transfer ≠ Tax-Relevant Event Value by Default
Resource Consumption ≠ Taxable Value by Default
No Transfer ≠ No Value Candidate
Direct Value Connection ≠ Established Value Association
Indirect Value Connection ≠ Irrelevant Value by Default
Participant-Linked Value ≠ Participant-Owned Value
Participant-Linked Value ≠ Event Value by Default
One Event ≠ One Value Candidate
One Value Candidate ≠ One Event by Default

Multiple Value Records ≠ Multiple Values by Default
Same Amount ≠ Same Value
Trusted Source ≠ Event Relevance by Default
Required Value Field ≠ Permission to Invent Event Value
Candidate Exclusion ≠ Value Nonexistence
Value Candidate Discovery ≠ Event Boundary Expansion
Value Candidate ≠ Participant Determination
Value Candidate ≠ Ownership Determination
Value Association Candidate ≠ Taxable Value
No Invoice ≠ No Value Candidate
No Human Transaction ≠ No Value Candidate Enterprise Application
VAIM provides the first operational gateway into TRVAS:
ERP / Banking / Commerce / Blockchain / Platform / AI Agent / Machine System
→ Available Value Information TREPS — Governed Participatory Event
→ VAIM — Value Association Identification
→ Governed Value Association Candidate Set
→ VARM — Value Reference Governance
→ VACM — Value Change Association
→ VASM — Value State Association
→ VATM — Value Association Traceability
→ Governed Value-Associated Event
This allows organizations to separate potentially relevant value from surrounding operational data before downstream tax interpretation begins. Use Case 1 — Multi-System Commercial Event
A multinational business processes a customer transaction through an ERP system, payment provider, marketplace, invoicing platform, and logistics system.
The available records include a product price, platform commission, payment-processing fee, shipping charge, discount, currency-conversion amount, tax field, settlement amount, and later refund.

Several systems contain overlapping records of the same underlying value relationships.
VAIM identifies which value information plausibly belongs to the governed event, distinguishes materially different candidates, detects possible duplication, and excludes unrelated surrounding records.
It does not decide which amount is taxable.
The resulting Governed Value Association Candidate Set can proceed through TRVAS for structured Value Association governance. Use Case 2 — Autonomous Machine Economy
An autonomous industrial system allocates excess computational and production capacity through a machine-accessible marketplace.
An AI agent initiates the allocation, another autonomous system consumes the resource, energy is used, productive capacity is transferred, and settlement later occurs through a digital asset.
There may be no conventional invoice when the operational event occurs.
VAIM identifies computational capacity, energy consumption, service output, digital-asset movement, and other governed value results that plausibly belong to the event.
It does not assume that the digital-asset transfer represents the entire event value and does not determine the tax treatment of any candidate.
The resulting candidate structure allows subsequent TREGA™ governance to represent the economic event before jurisdiction-specific tax rules are applied.
Canonical Boundary

VAIM owns the discovery, differentiation, screening, qualification, inclusion, exclusion, duplicate detection, uncertainty, conflict, and readiness governance of value information that may materially belong to a Governed Participatory Event.
VAIM does not establish the complete Value Association, create the definitive Value Reference, govern Value Change, govern Value State, own Value Association Traceability as a complete downstream mechanism, govern the Value Lifecycle, determine ownership or entitlement, redefine Event Participation or Event Boundary, determine accountability or liability, or establish taxable value, Tax Base, Tax Liability, or any jurisdiction-specific tax consequence.
Its governance ends when the relevant value information has been sufficiently identified and qualified to enter Value Reference governance.
Canonical Handoff
Governed Participatory Event + Available Governed Value Information
→ VAIM — Governed Value Association Candidate Set
→ VARM — Value Reference Governance
Canonical Closing Statement
VAIM establishes which value information deserves to enter Event Value Association governance without treating the presence of money, assets, resources, or value records as proof that they belong to the event.
Finding value and associating value are separate governance operations. Value Presence ≠ Event Value Association. Value Association Candidate ≠ Taxable Value.

chunks.text:
OOF™ The Value Reference Module (VARM) governs how Value Association
The Value Reference Module (VARM) governs how Value Association
OOF™ Origin Open Foundation™
Independent Methodological Authority
Architecture Ecosystem: Structured Reality Standards™
Architecture Family: TREGA™ — Tax-Relevant Event Governance Architecture™
Parent Standard: TRVAS — Tax-Relevant Value Association Standard
Module: VARM — Value Reference Module
Operational Layer: Value Reference Governance Layer
Category: Governance & Enforcement
Subcategory: Tax-Relevant Event Governance
Type: Core Module
Governed Space: Value Reference
Origin ID: TREGA-TRVAS-VARM-002
Version: 1.0
Status: Canonical · Open Standard
Effective Date: 1 September 2026
AI-Readable: Yes
Authority: OOF®
Protection: MIP® — Methodological Intellectual Property
Canonical Language: UCL — Universal Canonical Language
Canonical Definition
The Value Reference Module (VARM) governs how Value Association Candidates identified by VAIM are connected to stable, distinguishable, reconstructable, and interoperable value references within a Tax-Relevant Event.
VARM establishes the reference structure through which TREGA™ can consistently identify which governed value object, value result, or value representation is being associated with the event without redefining the value itself.
Its principal task is: Governed Value Association Candidate
↓
Governed Value Reference
VARM does not determine what happened to value.

It does not determine whether value increased, decreased, transferred, developed, degraded, was nullified, restored, or extinguished.
It does not determine the legal or tax meaning of the referenced value.
Its foundational distinction is: Value Reference ≠ Value DeterminationOperational Role
Once VAIM identifies potentially relevant value information, TREGA™ requires a stable method for referring to that value throughout subsequent governance.
Without a governed reference layer, the same value may appear under: different transaction identifiers; different invoice lines; different account entries; different currencies; different blockchain transaction references; different asset identifiers; different ERP records; different system-specific IDs; different machine-generated references; or different representations across organizations.
Conversely, similar references may represent different values.
VARM creates the governed reference structure needed to keep these representations distinguishable and traceable.
Internal Module Flow
TRVAS operates through:
VAIM — Value Association Identification
→ VARM — Value Reference
→ VACM — Value Change Association
→ VASM — Value State Association
→ VATM — Value Association Traceability
→ Governed Value-Associated Event
VARM receives the Governed Value Association Candidate Set from VAIM.
Its output provides the stable reference structure required by the downstream TRVAS modules.
Operational Transition
The canonical VARM transition is:

Governed Value Association Candidate Set
→ Value Reference Governance
→ Governed Value Reference Set
A Governed Value Reference establishes which value object, result, or representation subsequent TRVAS governance is referring to.
It does not establish the legal meaning or tax treatment of that value.
Operational Space
VARM governs: Value Reference establishment; reference differentiation; reference normalization; source-reference preservation; multi-source reference linkage; reference equivalence qualification; reference non-equivalence; reference hierarchy; reference granularity; reference stability; reference substitution; reference versioning; reference ambiguity; reference conflict; reference interoperability; and reference readiness for downstream TRVAS governance.
Operational Scope
VARM may govern value references originating from: VFM®; ERP systems; accounting systems; banking systems; payment infrastructure; invoices; procurement systems; marketplaces; digital platforms; blockchain networks; digital-asset systems; smart contracts; industrial systems; energy systems; logistics; AI agents; autonomous systems; machine networks; and other legitimate operational or governed sources.
VARM remains neutral to the technology or data model producing the reference.
Governed Value Reference
A Governed Value Reference is a stable governance-level reference through which a specific value object, value result, or value representation can be distinguished within TRVAS.

It permits subsequent governance to answer:
Which value are we referring to?
without answering:
What is the final legal or tax meaning of that value?
Therefore: Governed Value Reference ≠ Tax ValuationSource Value Reference
Operational systems may already provide value identifiers.
Examples include: transaction ID; invoice-line ID; asset ID; ledger-entry ID; payment ID; wallet transaction reference; token identifier; accounting reference; product reference; resource-allocation reference; or machine-generated value identifier.
VARM may preserve these as Source Value References.
However: Source Value Reference ≠ Governed Value Reference by Default
A source identifier becomes part of the governed reference structure only through appropriate qualification.
Canonical Reference
Where several operational references describe the same governed value, VARM may establish a common governance-level reference through which those representations remain linked.
The purpose is not to erase the source identifiers.
The canonical reference provides a stable governance anchor while preserving the underlying source references.
Therefore:
Canonical Reference ≠ Source Reference Replacement.
Reference Differentiation
VARM shall distinguish separate value references where available information supports their independence.
Similar numeric values or descriptions do not establish equivalence.
Therefore:
Same Amount ≠ Same Value Reference
Same Currency ≠ Same Value Reference

Same Participant ≠ Same Value Reference
Same Timestamp ≠ Same Value Reference
Similar Description ≠ Same Value Reference
Reference equivalence must be governed rather than assumed.
Reference Equivalence
Multiple records may legitimately represent the same underlying value.
VARM may establish governed reference equivalence where sufficient support exists.
For example:
ERP Record A Invoice Line B Bank Settlement C
may refer to the same underlying value relationship.
However: Multiple References ≠ Multiple Values by Default
Equivalence must remain qualified where uncertainty exists.
Reference Non-Equivalence
Records that appear similar may represent distinct values.
Two payments of the same amount may relate to separate events.
Two identical digital assets may represent separate governed value objects.
Two invoice lines may contain identical descriptions but refer to different economic components.
Therefore: Reference Similarity ≠ Value Equivalence
VARM shall preserve distinction where equivalence cannot legitimately be established.
Reference Granularity
Value may be represented at different levels.
For example:
Invoice
→ Invoice Component
→ Invoice Line
→ Line Component
or:
Digital Asset Portfolio
→ Asset Class
→ Asset
→ Asset Unit
VARM shall preserve the level of reference necessary for the governed Value Association.
Therefore: Aggregate Reference ≠ Component Reference
A reference shall not be treated as more granular than the underlying information supports.

Composite Value Reference
One event may involve a value structure composed of several distinct components.
VARM may establish a composite reference structure where the components legitimately belong together while remaining individually distinguishable.
The canonical structure may be:
Composite Value Reference
→ Component A
→ Component B
→ Component C
However:
Composite Reference ≠ Single Indivisible Value by Default.
Reference Hierarchy
Where value references exist at multiple levels, VARM may preserve their relationship.
For example:
Settlement Reference
→ Transaction References
→ Value Components
or:
Asset Bundle
→ Individual Asset References
The hierarchy represents reference structure.
It does not determine Value Ownership, Tax Base, or legal classification.
Multi-Source Reference Linkage
The same value may be represented across several systems.
VARM shall permit governed linkage among those representations.
Example:
Commerce Platform Reference
↔ ERP Reference
↔ Payment Reference
↔ Bank Reference
↔ Governed Value Reference
This can create interoperability without requiring every system to use the same internal identifier.
Reference Normalization
Different systems may use incompatible reference formats.
VARM may normalize those representations for governance purposes while preserving their original forms.
Normalization shall not alter the substantive meaning of the underlying value.
Therefore: Reference Normalization ≠ Value TransformationReference Stability

A Governed Value Reference should remain sufficiently stable throughout TRVAS governance.
Changes in surrounding system identifiers shall not automatically create a new governed value reference.
Therefore:
Source Identifier Change ≠ New Governed Value by Default.
The continuity of the reference must be assessed independently.
Reference Substitution
An operational source may replace one identifier with another.
VARM shall preserve the relationship between prior and subsequent references where they represent the same underlying value.
Therefore:
Reference Substitution ≠ Value Replacement by Default.
Historical reference paths should remain reconstructable.
Reference Versioning
Some value representations evolve.
An estimate may later be updated.
A provisional settlement reference may become final.
A digital record may receive a subsequent version.
VARM may preserve version relationships without treating every version as a separate value.
Therefore:
New Reference Version ≠ New Value by Default.
Whether the underlying value itself changed belongs to the appropriate value-governance mechanism.
Reference Correction
A source reference may be corrected because of error.
VARM shall support correction without silently erasing the prior reference history. Reference Correction ≠ Historical Erasure
The corrected structure should remain reconstructable where governance requires it.
Reference Ambiguity
It may be unclear which value a source identifier represents.

VARM shall preserve ambiguity rather than arbitrarily linking the reference.
Therefore: Reference Ambiguity ≠ Permission to Assume Equivalence
Where ambiguity cannot be sufficiently resolved, the governance state shall remain qualified or unresolved.
Reference Conflict
Different sources may assert incompatible reference relationships.
For example:
one system may associate a settlement with Invoice A while another associates it with Invoice B.
VARM shall preserve material conflict until sufficiently resolved.
Therefore: Reference Conflict ≠ Permission for Convenient LinkageMissing Reference
Economically relevant value may exist even where no usable operational identifier is available.
VARM shall not assume that missing source identification means absence of value.
Therefore: Missing Source Reference ≠ No Value
Where permitted by governance, a governance-level reference may be established from sufficiently supported information while preserving the missing-source condition.
Technical Identifier
A technical identifier may assist reference governance.
However, technical uniqueness does not establish economic uniqueness.
Therefore: Unique Technical ID ≠ Unique Economic Value by Default
This distinction is particularly important in blockchain, tokenized, machine-generated, and distributed systems.
Blockchain References

Blockchain systems may provide: transaction hashes; wallet addresses; token IDs; contract addresses; block references; output references; or protocol-specific identifiers.
VARM may consume these references.
However:
Transaction Hash ≠ Economic Value Reference by Default.
One transaction may contain several value relationships.
One economic value relationship may also span multiple transactions.
VARM therefore preserves the distinction between technical ledger references and governed value references.
Token Reference
A token identifier may identify a digital representation.
It does not automatically establish the complete economic value being governed.
Therefore:
Token ID ≠ Governed Economic Value by Default.
Likewise:
Wallet Address ≠ Value Owner.
Ownership remains outside VARM.
Banking and Payment References
Banks and payment systems may provide highly reliable transaction identifiers.
VARM may use them as source references.
However:
Payment Identifier ≠ Complete Event Value Reference by Default.
A payment may settle: one event; several events; part of an event; an earlier obligation; or a composite value structure.
The reference relationship must therefore remain governed.
Invoice References
An invoice number may represent an aggregate commercial document rather than one value.
VARM shall permit references below the invoice level where necessary.
Therefore:
Invoice Reference ≠ Single Value Reference by Default.

Invoice lines and components may require separate governed references.
Machine-Generated References
Autonomous systems may create value-related references without human involvement.
Examples include: resource-allocation IDs; machine-service IDs; compute-consumption references; autonomous procurement references; energy-exchange identifiers; agent transaction IDs; or machine settlement references.
VARM shall support these references without requiring a human-created invoice or account entry.
Therefore: Machine-Generated Reference ≠ Invalid Value Reference
The reference must still satisfy normal governance requirements.
Reference and Value State
VARM establishes which value is being referenced.
It does not determine the state of that value.
Therefore: Value Reference ≠ Value State
VASM owns Event–Value State Association within TRVAS.
VFM® owns the underlying Value State governance.
Reference and Value Change
A stable Value Reference may persist while value changes.
Therefore: Value Reference ≠ Value Change
VACM governs the association between governed Value Changes and the event.
VFM® owns the underlying Value Change governance.
Reference and Event Participation
A Value Reference may contain or be linked to participant information.
VARM shall not infer participation solely from the reference.
Therefore:
Value Reference ≠ Participant Determination.
TREPS remains authoritative for Event Participation.
Reference and Ownership

A Value Reference may be associated with an actor, account, wallet, organization, or machine.
This does not establish legal ownership.
Therefore: Value Reference ≠ Ownership
OBIDENITY® remains authoritative for governed ownership where applicable.
Reference and Event Boundary
A Value Reference may reveal information outside the current Event Boundary.
VARM shall not independently expand the event.
Therefore:
Reference Linkage ≠ Event Boundary Expansion.
Potential Event Boundary issues shall be referred to TREBS.
Reference and Event Relationship
The same Value Reference may appear across several governed events.
This does not establish that the events are identical.
Therefore: Shared Value Reference ≠ Same Event
TRERLS remains authoritative for Event Relationships.
Reference and Taxation
A governed reference identifies the value under subsequent governance.
It does not determine its tax treatment.
Therefore:
Governed Value Reference ≠ Taxable Value
Governed Value Reference ≠ Tax Base
Governed Value Reference ≠ Tax Liability
A jurisdiction may later interpret the referenced value according to applicable law.
Multi-Jurisdiction Reference Stability
A principal benefit of a jurisdiction-neutral Value Reference is that multiple taxation systems can evaluate the same governed value without TREGA™ redefining it for each jurisdiction.
The model is:
One Governed Value Reference
→ Jurisdiction A Evaluation
→ Jurisdiction B Evaluation
→ Jurisdiction C Evaluation

The legal conclusions may differ.
The governed reference remains stable.
Reference Interoperability
VARM should enable different operational systems to refer consistently to the same governed value structure without requiring identical internal data models.
This supports: ERP integration; banking interoperability; payment reconciliation; blockchain integration; tax-engine integration; marketplace interoperability; AI-agent systems; machine economies; auditability; and cross-border data exchange.
Interoperability concerns the reference.
It does not require uniform legal interpretation.
Reference Traceability
VARM shall preserve sufficient information to reconstruct: where a reference originated; which source identifiers exist; how references were linked; which equivalence decisions were made; which hierarchy exists; whether normalization occurred; whether substitution occurred; whether versioning occurred; whether corrections occurred; whether ambiguity existed; and whether conflicts remain.
VATM later governs the complete Value Association traceability structure.
VARM owns traceability necessary specifically for the integrity of the Value Reference.
Governance States
VARM may represent states including:
Reference Ready
Reference Under Governance
Reference Distinguished
Reference Linked
Reference Normalized
Reference Equivalent
Reference Non-Equivalent
Reference Composite
Reference Substituted
Reference Versioned
Reference Ambiguous
Reference Conflicted
Reference Unresolved

Governed Value Reference Established
These states describe reference governance only.
Governance Requirements
VARM implementations shall ensure that: every admitted Value Association Candidate can be referenceable; source references remain preserved; governance-level references can be distinguished from source identifiers; multiple source references can be linked where legitimate; reference equivalence is not assumed from superficial similarity; reference non-equivalence can remain visible; aggregate and component references can be distinguished; composite value structures can be represented; reference hierarchies can be preserved; normalization does not alter underlying value meaning; reference stability can survive source-identifier changes; substitutions remain traceable; version relationships remain reconstructable; corrections do not erase governance history; ambiguity remains visible; conflicts remain visible; missing source references do not automatically eliminate legitimate value; technical uniqueness is not treated as economic uniqueness; blockchain identifiers are not automatically treated as complete economic references; machine-generated references can be governed; Value State remains separate; Value Change remains separate; Event Participation remains separate; ownership remains separate; Event Boundary remains protected; Event Relationships remain separate; and tax valuation remains downstream.
Governance Logic

IF VAIM establishes a Value Association Candidate, THEN VARM shall determine how the relevant value can be stably referenced.
IF a valid upstream governed Value Reference already exists, THEN VARM should preserve and consume that reference rather than unnecessarily recreate it.
IF multiple source identifiers represent the same underlying governed value, THEN they may be linked under a common Governed Value Reference where equivalence is sufficiently supported.
IF similar references cannot be shown to represent the same value, THEN they shall remain distinct.
IF one aggregate reference contains materially distinct value components, THEN appropriate reference granularity shall be preserved.
IF a source identifier changes while the underlying value remains continuous, THEN a new governed value shall not be created solely because of the identifier change.
IF reference equivalence remains ambiguous or conflicted, THEN that state shall remain visible.
IF a reference reveals a possible Event Boundary problem, THEN VARM shall refer the issue upstream rather than expand the event independently.
IF the Value Reference is sufficiently governed, THEN it shall proceed to VACM for Value Change Association governance.
Minimum Implementation Framework
A minimum VARM implementation should support:
Governed Event Reference
The governed event to which the Value Reference structure relates.
VAIM Candidate Reference
The originating Value Association Candidate.
Governed Value Reference Identifier

The stable governance-level reference.
Source Value Reference
The original operational or governed identifier.
Source System
The system or governance source providing the reference.
Reference Type
The applicable reference category.
Reference Granularity
The level at which the value is being referenced.
Parent Reference
A higher-level reference where a hierarchy exists.
Component Reference
A lower-level reference where components exist.
Equivalent Reference Set
Other references governed as representing the same underlying value.
Reference Equivalence State
The qualification of equivalence.
Normalization State
Whether reference normalization occurred.
Substitution State
Whether one reference replaced another.
Prior Reference
The historical reference where substitution or versioning occurs.
Version State
The applicable reference version relationship.
Reference Confidence
The qualified confidence attached to the reference structure.
Ambiguity State
Whether reference meaning or equivalence remains ambiguous.
Conflict State
Whether materially conflicting reference relationships exist.
Traceability Reference
The information required to reconstruct the reference governance.
Governance State
The current VARM state.
Handoff State
Whether the reference is ready for VACM.
Governance Outputs

VARM may produce: Governed Value Reference; Source Value Reference Map; Multi-Source Value Reference Link; Governed Reference Equivalence; Governed Reference Non-Equivalence; Composite Value Reference; Value Reference Hierarchy; Value Component Reference; Normalized Value Reference; Reference Substitution Record; Reference Version Record; Reference Correction Record; Reference Confidence State; Reference Ambiguity State; Reference Conflict State; Reference Traceability Structure; and the principal output:
Governed Value Reference Set
This output proceeds to VACM.
Critical Distinctions
Value Reference ≠ Value Determination
Governed Value Reference ≠ Tax Valuation
Source Value Reference ≠ Governed Value Reference by Default
Canonical Reference ≠ Source Reference Replacement
Same Amount ≠ Same Value Reference
Same Currency ≠ Same Value Reference
Same Participant ≠ Same Value Reference
Same Timestamp ≠ Same Value Reference
Similar Description ≠ Same Value Reference
Multiple References ≠ Multiple Values by Default
Reference Similarity ≠ Value Equivalence
Aggregate Reference ≠ Component Reference
Composite Reference ≠ Single Indivisible Value by Default
Reference Normalization ≠ Value Transformation
Source Identifier Change ≠ New Governed Value by Default
Reference Substitution ≠ Value Replacement by Default
New Reference Version ≠ New Value by Default
Reference Correction ≠ Historical Erasure
Reference Ambiguity ≠ Permission to Assume Equivalence

Reference Conflict ≠ Permission for Convenient Linkage
Missing Source Reference ≠ No Value
Unique Technical ID ≠ Unique Economic Value by Default
Transaction Hash ≠ Economic Value Reference by Default
Token ID ≠ Governed Economic Value by Default
Wallet Address ≠ Value Owner
Payment Identifier ≠ Complete Event Value Reference by Default
Invoice Reference ≠ Single Value Reference by Default
Machine-Generated Reference ≠ Invalid Value Reference
Value Reference ≠ Value State
Value Reference ≠ Value Change
Value Reference ≠ Participant Determination
Value Reference ≠ Ownership
Reference Linkage ≠ Event Boundary Expansion
Shared Value Reference ≠ Same Event
Governed Value Reference ≠ Taxable Value Enterprise Application
VARM creates a stable reference layer across fragmented economic systems:
VAIM — Governed Value Association Candidate Set
→ ERP Reference / Banking Reference / Payment Reference / Blockchain Reference / Machine Reference / VFM® Reference
→ VARM — Value Reference Governance
→ Governed Value Reference Set
→ VACM — Value Change Association
→ VASM — Value State Association
→ VATM — Value Association Traceability
→ Governed Value-Associated Event
This allows multiple systems and later jurisdictional tax engines to refer to the same governed value structure without requiring identical source identifiers or identical legal interpretations. Use Case 1 — Banking, ERP, and Commerce Reference Reconciliation
A multinational merchant completes a commercial event.

The ERP system records an order ID and several invoice lines.
The payment provider records a payment transaction ID.
The bank records a settlement reference.
The marketplace uses its own transaction identifier.
The same economic value is therefore represented differently across four systems.
At the same time, the invoice contains several value components that must not be collapsed into one reference.
VARM establishes governed links between the relevant source references, preserves component-level granularity, distinguishes genuinely separate values, and creates stable Governed Value References for subsequent TRVAS governance.
The result can be consumed by tax, audit, compliance, and reconciliation systems without treating any single operational identifier as the complete economic truth. Use Case 2 — Blockchain and Autonomous Machine Transaction
An AI agent purchases computational capacity from an autonomous digital service.
The event produces an agent transaction ID, smart-contract call, blockchain transaction hash, token-transfer reference, compute-allocation ID, and settlement record.
These technical references describe different parts of the same economic activity, while one blockchain transaction may also contain unrelated protocol operations.
VARM preserves each source reference, determines which references can legitimately be linked, maintains appropriate granularity, and establishes the Governed Value Reference structure required by TREGA™.

It does not treat the transaction hash as the economic value itself, determine who owns the digital asset, or decide the tax treatment of the transaction.
Canonical Boundary
VARM owns the establishment, differentiation, normalization, linkage, equivalence, non-equivalence, hierarchy, granularity, stability, substitution, versioning, correction, ambiguity, conflict, interoperability, and reference-specific traceability of value references admitted into TRVAS governance.
VARM does not identify initial Value Association Candidates, govern the underlying Value Lifecycle, determine Value State, determine Value Change, establish Value Change Association, establish Value State Association, own complete Value Association traceability, determine Event Participation, redefine Event Boundary, determine Value Ownership or entitlement, establish accountability or liability, or determine taxable value, Tax Base, Tax Liability, or another jurisdiction-specific tax consequence.
Its governance ends when the relevant value possesses a sufficiently stable, distinguishable, and reconstructable Governed Value Reference for subsequent Value Change Association governance.
Canonical Handoff
VAIM — Governed Value Association Candidate Set
→ VARM — Governed Value Reference Set
→ VACM — Value Change Association Governance
Canonical Closing Statement

VARM establishes a stable reference to value without allowing identifiers, records, transaction hashes, invoice numbers, or system-specific representations to become substitutes for the governed value itself.
Different systems may describe the same value differently, and similar records may describe different values. Reference governance preserves that distinction. Value Reference ≠ Value Determination.
Governed Value Reference ≠ Taxable Value.

OOF™ The Value State Association Module (VASM) governs how already-governed
The Value State Association Module (VASM) governs how already-governed
OOF™ Origin Open Foundation™
Independent Methodological Authority
Architecture Ecosystem: Structured Reality Standards™
Architecture Family: TREGA™ — Tax-Relevant Event Governance Architecture™
Parent Standard: TRVAS — Tax-Relevant Value Association Standard
Module: VASM — Value State Association Module
Operational Layer: Value State Association Governance Layer
Category: Governance & Enforcement
Subcategory: Tax-Relevant Event Governance
Type: Core Module
Governed Space: Value State Association
Origin ID: TREGA-TRVAS-VASM-004
Version: 1.0
Status: Canonical · Open Standard
Effective Date: 1 September 2026
AI-Readable: Yes
Authority: OOF®
Protection: MIP® — Methodological Intellectual Property
Canonical Language: UCL — Universal Canonical Language
Canonical Definition
The Value State Association Module (VASM) governs how already-governed Value States are materially associated with a specific Tax-Relevant Event through Governed Value References and relevant Value Change Associations.
VASM establishes which Value State is relevant to the event, at which governed point or phase that state applies, how multiple or changing states are represented, and how uncertainty or conflict in State Association is preserved.
VASM does not determine the Value State itself.

It does not define whether value is active, developed, degraded, nullified, restored, extinct, available, restricted, transferred, or otherwise situated within its lifecycle.
VFM® remains authoritative for the underlying Value State.
Its principal task is:
Governed Value Reference + Governed Value State + Relevant Event Context
↓
Governed Event–Value State Association
The foundational distinction is:
Value State Association ≠ Value State Governance.
Operational Role
A Tax-Relevant Event may involve value that exists in different governed states before, during, or after the event.
For example, value may be: available; transferred; consumed; restricted; developed; degraded; restored; nullified; or otherwise governed within its lifecycle.
The existence of a Value State does not automatically establish that the state is the relevant state for the event.
VASM therefore governs the relationship between: the event; the Governed Value Reference; and the applicable upstream-governed Value State.
It prevents downstream systems from assuming that the latest, most visible, or most convenient Value State necessarily represents the state relevant to the governed event.
Internal Module Flow
TRVAS operates through:
VAIM — Value Association Identification
↓
VARM — Value Reference
↓
VACM — Value Change Association
↓
VASM — Value State Association
↓
VATM — Value Association Traceability
↓
Governed Value-Associated Event

VASM receives: the Governed Value Reference Set from VARM; relevant Governed Value Change Associations from VACM; and upstream Governed Value State information.
Its output proceeds to VATM.
Operational Transition
The canonical VASM transition is:
Governed Value Reference Set + Governed Value State Information + Relevant Value Change Association
↓
Value State Association Governance
↓
Governed Value State Association Set
VASM associates state with the event.
It does not create the state.
Operational Space
VASM governs: Event–Value State Association; state relevance; state applicability; state-point association; pre-event state; event-phase state; post-event state; state transition relevance; multiple State Associations; concurrent State Associations; partial State Association; state persistence; state supersession; state correction; state uncertainty; state conflict; and State Association readiness for complete TRVAS traceability.
Operational Scope
VASM may operate across Value States associated with: goods; services; money; financial assets; digital assets; rights; access; resources; energy; computational capacity; productive capacity; inventories; industrial assets; AI-agent activity; autonomous systems; machine-generated value; and other governed forms of value.
The module remains neutral to the specific Value State taxonomy used by the upstream authoritative architecture.
Governed Value State

A Governed Value State is an upstream governance result describing the state of a governed value at a relevant point in its lifecycle.
VASM may consume this result.
It shall not recreate or reinterpret it.
The architectural rule is:
VFM® governs the state of value. VASM governs whether that state belongs to the event representation. Event–Value State Association
An Event–Value State Association represents a governed relationship between: a Tax-Relevant Event; a Governed Value Reference; and a Governed Value State.
The coexistence of those elements does not automatically establish association.
Event + Value + State ≠ Established Value State Association by default.
The relationship must be governed.
State Relevance
A Value State may exist but be irrelevant to the specific event.
For example, a later restored state may not represent the state of value when the event occurred.
VASM therefore evaluates which state is materially relevant to the event.
Existing Value State ≠ Event-Relevant Value State by default.
Pre-Event State
The state of value immediately before an event may be material to understanding the event.
VASM may associate that state where relevant.
However:
Pre-Event Value State ≠ Event Outcome.
It represents the starting governed condition, not the result of the event.
Event-Phase State
Some events unfold across multiple operational phases.
The relevant Value State may change during those phases.
VASM may preserve distinct State Associations where necessary.

For example:
Initial State
↓
Intermediate State
↓
Completion State
may all belong to one governed event.
Therefore:
One Event ≠ One Value State by default.
Post-Event State
A state observed after event completion may represent the resulting condition of the value.
VASM may associate that state where sufficiently linked to the event.
However:
Post-Event Value State ≠ Tax Consequence.
A jurisdiction may later interpret that state differently.
State Transition Relationship
A Value Change governed under VFM® may connect two Value States.
VACM governs whether that change belongs to the event.
VASM may then associate the relevant states surrounding that change.
The conceptual structure may be:
Governed Value State A
↓
Governed Value Change
↓
Governed Value State B
within the context of a governed event.
However:
State Transition Representation ≠ Value Change Governance.
VACM owns Event–Value Change Association.
VFM® owns the underlying Value Change and Value State governance.
Multiple Value States
One event may involve multiple governed Value States.
This may occur because: different values are involved; one value changes state during the event; several components possess different states; or value exists in parallel states across different structures.
VASM shall preserve materially distinct State Associations.
Multiple Value States ≠ Multiple Events by default.
Concurrent Value States

Different values associated with the same event may simultaneously possess different governed states.
VASM shall support concurrent states without forcing them into one aggregate state.
Concurrent Value States ≠ Same Value State.
Partial State Association
A governed Value State may apply to only part of a referenced value structure.
For example, one component of an asset bundle may be degraded while another remains unchanged.
VASM shall support partial association.
Partial Value State Association ≠ Complete Value State Association.
Composite Value Structures
Where VARM establishes a composite Value Reference, VASM may associate different states with different components.
Therefore:
Composite Value Reference ≠ Uniform Value State by default.
Each component may require separate governed State Association.
State Persistence
A Value State may persist across several events.
VASM shall not assume that a continuing state was created by the current event.
Therefore:
State Persistence ≠ Event Causation.
The state may predate the event and continue afterward.
State Supersession
A later governed Value State may supersede an earlier state.
VASM shall preserve historical relevance rather than overwriting the state associated with the event.
Later Value State ≠ Historical Event Value State.
and:
State Supersession ≠ Historical Erasure.
State Correction
An earlier State Association may later be shown to be incorrect.

VASM shall support governed correction while preserving the prior governance record where required.
State Association Correction ≠ Historical Erasure.
State and Value Change
A Value State may exist without a Value Change occurring during the current event.
Likewise, a Value Change may occur without the downstream system having complete State information.
Therefore:
Value State Association ≠ Value Change Association.
VACM and VASM remain separate governance mechanisms.
State and Event Timing
The time at which a Value State is recorded may differ from the governed Event Timing.
A state may be measured later but still describe an earlier condition.
Therefore:
Value State Timestamp ≠ Event Time by default.
TRETS remains authoritative for Event Timing.
VASM may preserve temporal linkage necessary to establish the relevant state.
State and Event Location
The location where a Value State is recorded, stored, or observed does not necessarily represent Event Location.
Therefore:
Value State Location ≠ Event Location by default.
TRELS remains authoritative for Event Location.
State and Participation
A participant may interact with value in a particular state.
That relationship does not establish that the participant owns, controls, or is legally entitled to the value.
Therefore:
Participant–Value State Relationship ≠ Ownership.
TREPS remains authoritative for participation.
OBIDENITY® remains authoritative for ownership where applicable.
State and Ownership

A change in Value State does not automatically change ownership.
Likewise, the same Value State may persist across ownership changes.
Therefore:
Value State ≠ Ownership State.
Ownership and Value State remain distinct governance spaces.
State and Availability
A value may be available operationally without being legally disposable or transferable.
Likewise, restricted value may still possess material economic significance.
Therefore:
Operational Availability ≠ Legal Availability.
VASM preserves the governed Value State without converting it into a legal entitlement conclusion.
State and Recognition
A value may exist in a governed state before an accounting, regulatory, or tax system legally recognizes that value.
Therefore:
Governed Value State ≠ Accounting Recognition.
Governed Value State ≠ Tax Recognition.
Those interpretations remain outside VASM.
State and Valuation
A Value State may influence downstream valuation.
For example, degraded, restricted, restored, or incomplete value may later be valued differently.
VASM does not determine the amount.
Therefore:
Value State Association ≠ Valuation Determination.
State and Tax Base
A jurisdiction may use a Value State as one factor in determining taxable amount or legal classification.
VASM does not make that determination.
Therefore:
Governed Value State ≠ Tax Base.
and:
Value State Association ≠ Taxable Value Determination.
Digital-Asset States

Digital assets may exist in operational states such as: locked; transferred; escrowed; staked; bridged; restricted; burned; redeemable; frozen; or otherwise governed.
VASM may associate an upstream-governed state with the event without treating protocol terminology as a tax conclusion.
Protocol State ≠ Tax State.
Machine and Autonomous Value States
Autonomous systems may create, consume, reserve, transform, or release resources.
The associated value may move through several governed states without human action.
VASM shall support these State Associations.
For example:
Available Capacity
↓
Reserved Capacity
↓
Consumed Capacity
may be associated with a machine-generated event.
However:
Machine-Generated Value State ≠ Human-Owned Value State by default.
Ownership remains separate.
State Uncertainty
It may be unclear which Value State applied at the relevant event point.
VASM shall preserve that uncertainty.
For example: records may be incomplete; state changes may occur between observations; distributed systems may disagree; or retrospective reconstruction may be required.
Therefore:
State Uncertainty ≠ Permission to Select the Most Convenient State.
State Conflict
Different authoritative or operational sources may report conflicting Value States.
VASM shall preserve materially relevant conflict until sufficiently resolved.
Value State Conflict ≠ Permission for Convenient State Selection.
State Confidence

VASM may qualify State Associations according to the degree of support available.
Possible states include:
Established · Qualified · Partial · Ambiguous · Conflicted · Unresolved
The confidence applies to the Event–Value State Association.
It does not alter the upstream governance status of the Value State itself.
State Association Traceability
VASM shall preserve sufficient information to reconstruct: which Governed Value Reference is involved; which Governed Value State is associated; which upstream source governed that state; which event phase the state relates to; what association basis was used; whether the state was pre-event, event-phase, or post-event; whether multiple states existed; whether supersession occurred; whether correction occurred; whether ambiguity existed; and whether conflict existed.
VATM subsequently integrates this into the complete TRVAS Value Association traceability structure.
Governance States
VASM may represent states including:
State Association Ready
State Association Under Governance
Pre-Event State Associated
Event-Phase State Associated
Post-Event State Associated
Multi-State Association
Concurrent State Association
Partial State Association
State Association Qualified
State Association Ambiguous
State Association Conflicted
State Association Unresolved
Governed Value State Association Established
These states describe Event–Value State Association only.
Governance Requirements

VASM implementations shall ensure that: Value States are consumed from legitimate upstream governance sources; VASM does not independently redefine Value State; state relevance to the event is evaluated; pre-event, event-phase, and post-event states can be distinguished; multiple State Associations can be represented; concurrent states can remain distinct; partial State Association can be represented; composite Value References can carry component-level states; state persistence does not automatically imply event causation; later states do not overwrite historical Event–Value State Associations; corrections remain traceable; State Association remains separate from Value Change Association; Value State timestamps do not redefine Event Timing; Value State location does not redefine Event Location; participant relationships do not establish ownership; Value State remains distinct from Ownership State; operational availability remains distinct from legal availability; accounting and tax recognition remain downstream; Value State does not determine valuation; Value State does not determine Tax Base; digital-asset protocol states are not automatically treated as tax states; machine-generated states can be governed; uncertainty remains visible; conflict remains visible; and VFM® ownership of Value State governance remains preserved.
Governance Logic

IF a Governed Value Reference exists and a relevant upstream Governed Value State is available, THEN VASM shall evaluate whether that state materially belongs to the governed event representation.
IF the relevant state differs across event phases, THEN materially distinct State Associations shall remain separately representable.
IF several values possess different states within one event, THEN the states shall not be collapsed into one aggregate state unless governance supports such aggregation.
IF a later state supersedes an earlier state, THEN the earlier Event–Value State Association shall remain historically reconstructable.
IF the State Association remains uncertain or conflicted, THEN the corresponding governance state shall remain visible.
IF a State Association depends on a Value Change already governed through VACM, THEN that dependency shall remain traceable without VASM redefining the change.
IF State information indicates a possible Event Timing, Event Boundary, or Event Relationship problem, THEN VASM shall refer the issue to the relevant TREGA™ layer rather than redefine those spaces.
IF the relevant Value States are sufficiently associated with the event, THEN the result shall proceed to VATM for complete Value Association traceability governance.
Minimum Implementation Framework
A minimum VASM implementation should support:
Governed Event Reference The governed event to which the Value State may be associated.

Governed Value Reference The VARM-governed value reference.
Governed Value State Reference The upstream governed Value State being associated.
State Association Identifier The stable reference for the Event–Value State Association.
State Type Reference The upstream governed State classification where available.
Association Basis The basis supporting the Event–Value State relationship.
Event Phase Reference Pre-event, event-phase, post-event, or another governed phase relationship.
State Applicability Point The governed point or interval at which the state applies.
State Extent Complete, partial, component-level, or otherwise qualified.
Prior State Reference Relevant earlier Value State where continuity or transition matters.
Subsequent State Reference Relevant later Value State where applicable.
Value Change Association Reference The related VACM association where a change connects relevant states.
Supersession State Whether the state has subsequently been superseded.
Correction Reference Any governed correction affecting the association.
Association Confidence The qualified confidence attached to the State Association.
Ambiguity State Whether the association remains ambiguous.
Conflict State Whether materially conflicting State Associations exist.
Traceability Reference The information required to reconstruct the association.
Governance State The current VASM state.
Handoff State Whether the result is ready for VATM.
Governance Outputs

VASM may produce: Governed Pre-Event Value State Association; Governed Event-Phase Value State Association; Governed Post-Event Value State Association; Governed Multi-State Association Structure; Governed Concurrent Value State Association; Governed Partial Value State Association; Governed Component Value State Association; Value State Transition Reference; Value State Supersession Record; Value State Association Correction; Value State Association Confidence State; Value State Association Ambiguity State; Value State Association Conflict State; and the principal output: Governed Value State Association Set.
Critical Distinctions
Value State Association ≠ Value State Governance.
VFM® governs the state of value. VASM governs whether that state belongs to the event representation.
Event + Value + State ≠ Established Value State Association by default.
Existing Value State ≠ Event-Relevant Value State by default.
Pre-Event Value State ≠ Event Outcome.
One Event ≠ One Value State by default.
Post-Event Value State ≠ Tax Consequence.
State Transition Representation ≠ Value Change Governance.
Multiple Value States ≠ Multiple Events by default.
Concurrent Value States ≠ Same Value State.
Partial Value State Association ≠ Complete Value State Association.
Composite Value Reference ≠ Uniform Value State by default.
State Persistence ≠ Event Causation.
Later Value State ≠ Historical Event Value State.
State Supersession ≠ Historical Erasure.

Value State Association ≠ Value Change Association.
Value State Timestamp ≠ Event Time by default.
Value State Location ≠ Event Location by default.
Participant–Value State Relationship ≠ Ownership.
Value State ≠ Ownership State.
Operational Availability ≠ Legal Availability.
Governed Value State ≠ Accounting Recognition.
Governed Value State ≠ Tax Recognition.
Value State Association ≠ Valuation Determination.
Governed Value State ≠ Tax Base.
Value State Association ≠ Taxable Value Determination.
Protocol State ≠ Tax State.
State Uncertainty ≠ Permission to Select the Most Convenient State.
Enterprise Application
VASM enables organizations to preserve the relevant state of value at the correct point in an event without converting that state into legal valuation or tax treatment.
The operational path is:
VAIM — Governed Value Association Candidate Set
↓
VARM — Governed Value Reference Set
↓
VACM — Governed Value Change Association Set
↓
VASM — Governed Value State Association Set
↓
VATM — Value Association Traceability
↓
Governed Value-Associated Event
This allows banks, ERP systems, digital platforms, blockchain infrastructures, AI agents, autonomous systems, and tax technology to understand not only which value changed, but also what governed state of that value is relevant to the event. Use Case 1 — Digital Asset with Multiple Operational States
A digital asset is associated with a cross-border platform event.
Before the event, the asset is available.

During the event, it becomes temporarily locked through a protocol.
A transfer then occurs, followed by a later release into another operational state.
VFM® governs the relevant Value States and Value Changes.
VACM associates the relevant Value Changes with the event.
VASM determines which pre-event, event-phase, and post-event Value States materially belong to the event representation and preserves them without interpreting “locked,” “transferred,” or “released” as jurisdiction-specific tax states.
A downstream tax system can then evaluate the governed event without rewriting the operational history of the asset. Use Case 2 — Autonomous Resource Consumption and Capacity State
An autonomous production system has available computational and manufacturing capacity.
An AI agent reserves part of that capacity for an external service request.
During execution, part of the capacity becomes consumed while another portion remains reserved but unused.
The event therefore involves several materially different Value States across the same resource structure.
VASM associates those governed states with the correct event phases and value components without treating available, reserved, and consumed capacity as the same economic condition.
It does not determine who owns the capacity, whether consumption is deductible, or whether the resulting service creates taxable income.
The result provides downstream governance with a precise and reconstructable Value State structure.
Canonical Boundary

VASM owns the association of already-governed Value States with a specific Tax-Relevant Event, including state relevance, applicability, pre-event, event-phase and post-event association, multiple and concurrent states, partial association, persistence, supersession, correction, qualification, uncertainty, conflict, and State Association-specific traceability.
VASM does not own Value State creation or determination, Value Change governance, Value Change Association, Value Reference establishment, complete Value Association traceability, Event Formation, Event Boundary, Event Timing, Event Location, Event Participation, Event Relationships, ownership, entitlement, accountability, liability, valuation, taxable value, Tax Base, Tax Liability, or any other jurisdiction-specific legal conclusion.
Its governance ends when the relevant Governed Value States are sufficiently associated with the event for complete Value Association traceability governance under VATM.
Canonical Handoff
VACM — Governed Value Change Association Set
↓
VASM — Governed Value State Association Set
↓
VATM — Value Association Traceability Governance
Canonical Closing Statement
VASM connects the relevant governed state of value to the governed event without taking ownership of the Value State itself.
The state in which value exists during an event and the legal or tax meaning later assigned to that state are separate governance questions.
Value State Association ≠ Value State Governance.
Governed Value State ≠ Taxable Value.
