Origin ID: TREGA-TRVAS-VATM-005
Version: 1.0
Status: Canonical · Open Standard
Effective Date: 1 September 2026
AI-Readable: Yes
Authority: OOF®
Protection: MIP® — Methodological Intellectual Property
Canonical Language: UCL — Universal Canonical Language
Canonical Definition
The Value Association Traceability Module (VATM) governs how the complete relationship between a Tax-Relevant Event and its associated governed value results remains reconstructable, attributable, qualified, reviewable, interoperable, and historically traceable throughout the Value Association governance process.
VATM integrates the traceability outputs produced across VAIM, VARM, VACM, and VASM into a coherent Value Association traceability structure.
Its principal task is:

Governed Value Association Candidate Set + Governed Value Reference Set + Governed Value Change Association Set + Governed Value State Association Set
↓
Governed Value Association Traceability Structure
VATM does not recreate or redetermine the underlying Value Association decisions.
It preserves how those decisions were reached and how they relate.
The foundational distinction is:
Value Association Traceability ≠ Value Association Redetermination.
Operational Role
A governed Event–Value relationship is not sufficiently robust merely because a final association exists.
The association must also remain reconstructable.
A downstream system, auditor, regulator, tax authority, enterprise system, AI system, or later governance process may need to understand: which value information entered governance; which candidates were included or excluded; which references were used; how equivalent or non-equivalent references were distinguished; which Value Changes were associated; which Value States were associated; which sources supported those decisions; which uncertainties existed; which conflicts existed; which corrections occurred; and whether the final Value Association remains historically coherent.
VATM provides the traceability layer required to answer those questions.

Operational Scope
VATM may preserve traceability across: ERP systems; banking systems; payment networks; accounting platforms; commerce systems; marketplaces; blockchain networks; digital-asset platforms; industrial infrastructure; energy systems; AI agents; autonomous systems; machine-to-machine systems; tax technology; reporting systems; audit systems; and other operational or governance environments.

VATM remains neutral to the technology producing the underlying records.
Traceability Object
A Value Association Traceability Object is a governed representation of the information required to reconstruct one or more parts of the Event–Value Association.
It may refer to: a candidate; a source; a reference; a Value Change Association; a Value State Association; a decision; a correction; a conflict; an uncertainty; or a handoff.
Traceability Object ≠ Evidence Conclusion.
Traceability preserves the path.
It does not automatically prove that every upstream decision was correct.

This path shall remain reconstructable to the degree required by the governed context.
Final Association ≠ Sufficient Traceability by default.
Source Lineage
VATM shall preserve the sources that contributed to the Value Association.
Sources may include: system records; governed VFM® outputs; transaction records; banking data; blockchain data; invoices; machine-generated records; operational systems; participant-linked records; or other legitimate sources.
The source chain should remain distinguishable.
Source Presence ≠ Source Authority by default.
Candidate Lineage
VATM shall preserve which value information entered VAIM and what happened to it.

This includes: candidate creation; candidate qualification; candidate inclusion; candidate exclusion; candidate duplication; candidate ambiguity; candidate conflict; and candidate reconsideration.
Excluded Candidate ≠ Erased Candidate.
Where materially relevant, the fact that a candidate was considered and excluded should remain reconstructable.
Reference Lineage
VATM shall preserve the reference structure established by VARM.
This includes: source references; governed references; equivalent references; non-equivalent references; composite references; hierarchy; normalization; substitution; versioning; and correction.
Reference Change ≠ Traceability Break by default.
Value Change Association Lineage
VATM shall preserve how governed Value Changes became associated with the event.
This includes: direct association; indirect association; partial association; sequential association; concurrent association; reversals; refunds; corrections; uncertainty; and conflict.
The traceability record shall distinguish the Value Change itself from the decision to associate it with the event.
Value Change Traceability ≠ Value Change Governance.
Value State Association Lineage
VATM shall preserve how governed Value States became associated with the event.
This may include: pre-event State Association; event-phase State Association; post-event State Association; multiple states; concurrent states; partial states; supersession; correction; uncertainty; and conflict.

State History ≠ Current State Only.
Historical Event–Value State relationships shall remain reconstructable where governance requires it.
Decision Provenance
A Value Association may involve governance decisions at several stages.
VATM shall preserve sufficient information to identify: what decision was made; which module made it; which inputs were used; what qualification applied; what uncertainty existed; and what later change affected the decision.
Decision Provenance ≠ Decision Justification by itself.
It enables the decision to be reviewed.
Inclusion Traceability
Where value information is included in the final association structure, VATM shall preserve how it moved from candidate status into the governed association.
The trace should permit reconstruction of:
Candidate

Final Value Association Exclusion Traceability
Where materially relevant value information is excluded, VATM should preserve: what was excluded; why it was excluded; at which stage; based on what information; and whether the exclusion was later reconsidered.
Exclusion ≠ Nonexistence.
Qualification Traceability
An association may be qualified rather than absolute.
VATM shall preserve qualifications such as: direct; indirect; partial; estimated; provisional; uncertain; conflicted; or otherwise constrained.
Qualified Association ≠ Defective Association by default.
Qualification may accurately represent incomplete or complex operational reality.

Uncertainty Traceability
Uncertainty shall remain visible across the governance chain.
VATM shall preserve: where uncertainty arose; what it affected; whether it changed; whether it was resolved; and what downstream decisions consumed the uncertain result.
Uncertainty Resolution ≠ Historical Uncertainty Erasure.
Conflict Traceability
Conflicting sources or associations shall remain reconstructable.
VATM should preserve: the competing records; the affected governance object; the conflict state; any resolution; and any residual uncertainty.
Resolved Conflict ≠ Conflict Never Existed.
Correction Traceability
Corrections may occur at any TRVAS stage.
VATM shall preserve: the original representation; the corrected representation; the reason for correction where governed; the effective correction point; and downstream dependencies affected by the change.
Correction ≠ Historical Erasure.
Supersession Traceability
A later reference, State Association, or Value Association representation may supersede an earlier one.
VATM shall preserve the relationship between prior and subsequent representations.
Superseded ≠ Deleted.
Traceability Continuity
Traceability shall remain continuous where references, systems, actors, or representations change.

System Migration ≠ Traceability Reset.

Cross-Organization Traceability
An event may involve several organizations.
No single participant may possess the full Value Association record.
VATM may therefore support federated or distributed traceability where governance permits.
Distributed Traceability ≠ Centralized Data Ownership Requirement.
The traceability model may preserve relationships without requiring all source data to be physically centralized.
Blockchain Traceability
Blockchain systems provide strong technical transaction lineage.
However, technical ledger history does not automatically equal complete Value Association traceability.
Blockchain Traceability ≠ Economic Event Traceability by default.
VATM may incorporate blockchain references while also preserving off-chain and governance-layer relationships.
Banking Traceability
Bank records may strongly establish movement of money.
But bank lineage alone may not explain: which event the payment belongs to; which components it settles; whether it covers several events; or whether the amount represents the full Event Value.
Therefore:
Payment Traceability ≠ Complete Value Association Traceability.
Machine and Autonomous Traceability

AI agents and autonomous systems may create Value Associations across several machine-generated actions.
VATM shall support traceability of: machine-originated value candidates; agent references; autonomous transactions; resource-consumption records; digital settlement; machine-generated corrections; and human intervention where relevant.
Machine-Generated Traceability ≠ Untraceable Activity.
Autonomous execution should not remove the requirement for reconstructable governance.
Traceability and Identity
Traceability may contain actor references.
VATM does not establish origin-bound identity, ownership, authority, or permission.
Traceability Reference to Actor ≠ Identity Governance.
OBIDENITY® remains authoritative where applicable.
Traceability and Participation
VATM may preserve participant references supplied by TREPS.
It does not redetermine whether the actor participated.
Participation Traceability ≠ Participation Determination.
Traceability and Event Boundary
Traceability may reveal information that suggests an Event Boundary problem.
VATM shall not independently redefine the boundary.
Traceability Discovery ≠ Event Boundary Expansion.
Potential issues shall be referred to TREBS.
Traceability and Event Relationships
A Value Association trace may show that the same value interacts with multiple events.
VATM preserves that information.
It does not determine how those events relate.
Shared Value Trace ≠ Event Relationship Determination.

TRERLS remains authoritative for Event Relationships.
Traceability and Evidence
Traceability may support evidence governance, auditability, or validation.
However:
Traceability ≠ Evidence Sufficiency.
Traceability ≠ Validation.
Traceability ≠ Audit Conclusion.
ADIT® and VALIDOS™ remain authoritative for their respective governance spaces.
Traceability and Taxation
VATM may provide jurisdictional tax systems with a reconstructable Value Association record.
It does not determine: taxable value; taxable income; taxable gain; Tax Base; tax rate; tax liability; deduction; exemption; taxable person; jurisdiction; or legal tax consequence.
Therefore:
Traceable Value Association ≠ Taxable Value.
Multi-Jurisdiction Traceability
A major purpose of VATM is to allow multiple jurisdictions to consume the same governed Event–Value history.
The model is:
One Governed Value Association Traceability Structure
↓
Multiple Jurisdictional Evaluations
Each jurisdiction may apply different legal rules.
The underlying governance history remains stable.
This improves comparability and reduces the need to reconstruct operational reality separately for each jurisdiction.
Historical Reconstruction
VATM shall support reconstruction of the Value Association as it existed at a relevant historical point.
A later corrected or superseded state should not prevent an authorized governance process from understanding the earlier representation.

Current Value Association ≠ Complete Historical Value Association. Reproducibility
Where sufficient source information remains available, VATM should support reproduction of the governance path that generated the Value Association.
This does not require that every decision be automatically repeated with the same outcome under changed information.
Reproducibility ≠ Immutable Conclusion.
Traceability Completeness
A traceability structure should be sufficiently complete to reconstruct the material Value Association governance path.
Completeness does not require preserving every technically available data point.
Traceability Completeness ≠ Total Data Capture.
The requirement is governed sufficiency, not indiscriminate accumulation.
Traceability Integrity
VATM shall protect the relationship between traceability records and the governance objects they represent.
A record should not be silently detached, reassigned, overwritten, or merged in a manner that destroys reconstructability.
Traceability Integrity ≠ Data Immutability by default.
Corrections may be legitimate if their history remains governed.
Traceability Interoperability
VATM should permit traceability structures to move across systems without losing their core governance meaning.
This may support: enterprise interoperability; tax-engine integration; audit workflows; cross-border reporting; banking; blockchain infrastructure; digital platforms; AI systems; and regulatory technology.

Interoperability does not require identical technical implementation.

Governed Value-Associated Event Ready Governance Requirements

VATM implementations shall ensure that: the complete material Value Association governance chain can be reconstructed; source lineage is preserved; candidate inclusion and exclusion history can remain reconstructable; reference lineage is preserved; Value Change Association lineage is preserved; Value State Association lineage is preserved; governance decisions remain attributable to their appropriate module; qualifications remain visible; uncertainty remains visible; conflict remains visible; corrections remain traceable; supersession does not erase prior governed representations; system migration does not automatically break traceability; cross-system relationships can be preserved; cross-organization traceability can be supported where required; blockchain records are not treated as complete economic traceability by default; banking records are not treated as complete Value Association traceability by default; autonomous and machine-generated activity remains reconstructable; identity governance remains separate; participation determination remains separate; Event Boundary remains protected; Event Relationships remain separate; evidence sufficiency remains separate; validation remains separate; tax determination remains downstream; and the final Governed Value-Associated Event retains a sufficiently reconstructable Value Association history.
Governance Logic

IF VAIM, VARM, VACM, and VASM produce governed outputs, THEN VATM shall preserve the material lineage connecting those outputs.
IF an upstream governance object is corrected, THEN the original and corrected traceability states shall remain reconstructable where required.
IF an upstream object is superseded, THEN the relationship between prior and subsequent representations shall remain visible.
IF uncertainty or conflict existed during governance, THEN later resolution shall not silently erase the historical state.
IF multiple systems describe the same governed Value Association, THEN cross-system relationships shall be preserved where sufficiently established.
IF one system identifier changes, THEN traceability continuity shall not be broken solely because of the identifier change.
IF traceability information reveals a possible upstream governance issue, THEN VATM shall refer the issue to the appropriate module or Parent Standard rather than redetermine that space.
IF the Value Association governance chain is sufficiently reconstructable, qualified, and internally coherent, THEN the event may be represented as a Governed Value-Associated Event and handed to TRERLS.

Enterprise Application
VATM provides the final traceability layer connecting fragmented value information into one reconstructable TREGA™ Event–Value governance chain.
The operational path is:
VAIM — Value Association Identification
↓
VARM — Value Reference
↓
VACM — Value Change Association
↓
VASM — Value State Association
↓
VATM — Value Association Traceability
↓
Governed Value-Associated Event
↓
TRERLS — Event Relationship Governance

For enterprises, banks, marketplaces, blockchain platforms, ERP systems, tax technology, AI agents, autonomous systems, and public-sector infrastructure, this creates a structured record of not only what value is associated with an event, but also how that conclusion was governed and how it can later be reconstructed. Use Case 1 — Cross-Border Banking and Enterprise Audit
A multinational group records one commercial event across an ERP system, payment provider, bank, accounting platform, and tax engine.
The underlying value passes through several references, a partial settlement, a currency conversion, and a later correction.
Several years later, the event must be reviewed in another jurisdiction.
VATM preserves the chain from the original candidate information through Value References, Value Change Associations, Value State Associations, corrections, and final Value Association.
The reviewing system can reconstruct how the governed Event–Value relationship was established without relying solely on the current ERP record or final bank settlement.
The jurisdiction may then apply its own tax rules to the same governed historical event. Use Case 2 — Blockchain and Autonomous Economic Infrastructure
An AI agent purchases computational resources through a decentralized platform.
The event includes an agent instruction, resource-allocation record, smart-contract call, token transfer, machine consumption record, later settlement adjustment, and several upstream Value State changes.

No single system contains the complete economic history.
VATM links the relevant governance records across the AI platform, machine infrastructure, blockchain network, and Value Association modules while preserving uncertainty, corrections, and source distinctions.
The result is a reconstructable Governed Value-Associated Event that can be consumed by downstream audit, compliance, or jurisdiction-specific tax systems without assuming that the blockchain ledger alone represents the complete economic reality.
Canonical Boundary
VATM owns the end-to-end traceability, lineage, reconstructability, qualification history, uncertainty history, conflict history, correction history, supersession history, cross-system continuity, and traceability integrity of the Value Association governed under TRVAS.
VATM does not recreate Value Association Candidates, establish Value References, govern Value Changes, determine Value Change Associations, govern Value States, determine Value State Associations, establish Event Participation, redefine Event Boundary, determine Event Relationships, govern identity or ownership, determine evidence sufficiency, perform validation, conduct audit conclusions, or determine taxable value, Tax Base, Tax Liability, or any other jurisdiction-specific legal or tax consequence.

Its governance ends when the complete material Event–Value Association is sufficiently reconstructable and the Governed Value-Associated Event is ready for Event Relationship governance under TRERLS.

Canonical Closing Statement
VATM preserves how value became associated with the event without allowing traceability to become a substitute for the governance decisions it records.
A governed Value Association should remain understandable not only at the moment it is created, but also when it is reviewed, corrected, transferred between systems, or evaluated years later.
Value Association Traceability ≠ Value Association Redetermination.
Traceable Value Association ≠ Taxable Value.
